entry.summary: This position paper reviews critical open problems in the use of general-purpose chatbots for emotional and mental health support, including sycophancy, reinforcement of delusional beliefs, and poor crisis response. It lays out tractable research directions in evaluation, such as establishing construct and ecological validity, assessing multi-turn interactions, and connecting evaluations to behavior improvements.

entry.title: MIRIX-2.0: Multi-Agent Memory System

author.name: Wei-Chieh Huang, Weizhi Zhang, Jiayan Nan, Peng Xia, Yu Wang

entry.summary: MIRIX-2.0 is a multi-agent memory system for LLM agents aiming to be practical, accurate, and efficient simultaneously, avoiding the costs of parametric memory training, lossy consolidation, and unbounded record stores. It reports strong benchmark results, including 91.4 percent on LoCoMo and 72.6 percent on LongMemEval-S with a 14.3-point lead over the strongest baseline, plus top procedural-memory performance on ALFWorld and WebShop. This suggests meaningfully better long-term memory for agents.

entry.title: Task-adaptive anonymisation enables privacy-preserving sharing of clinical speech data

author.name: Ziyun Cui, Haoyu Niu, Wen Wu, Hao Sun, Sihan Zhang, Chang Lei, Yun Zhang, Chunyun Sun, Yang Luo, Liangliang Cao, Ji Wu, Runsen Chen, Lian Zhou, Yongsheng Tong, Chao Zhang

entry.summary: The paper introduces CASA, a clinically adaptive speech anonymisation agent that reframes anonymisation as a task-guided optimization process rather than a fixed pipeline, dynamically balancing removal of speaker-identifying voiceprints against preservation of clinical utility. This addresses the fact that different clinical tasks rely on different speech characteristics. It matters for enabling privacy-safe sharing of clinical speech data used in disease screening and assessment.

entry.title: MaRiO: Multi-agent Collaborative Reasoning via Shared Observations in MLLMs

author.name: Nathaniel Redmond, Fidel Omar Tito Cruz, Devansh Sharma, Shehreen Azad, Sirshapan Mitra, Shruti Vyas, Yogesh S. Rawat

entry.summary: Introduces MaRiO, a benchmark for multi-agent collaborative reasoning in multimodal LLMs where multiple agents observe a shared environment from independent viewpoints, and evaluates 23 state-of-the-art MLLMs on it. Findings include that static perception tasks are generally easier than tasks requiring transforming observations into a shared decision, highlighting a gap in current MLLM evaluation.

entry.title: SoftPAT3D: Physics-Augmented Text-to-3D Scene Generation with Deformables

author.name: Lei Shu, Alberta Longhini, Leonidas Guibas, Gordon Wetzstein, Jeannette Bohg

entry.summary: SoftPAT3D extends physics-augmented text-to-3D scene generation to deformable objects such as cloth, stuffed toys, and ropes, producing simulation-ready bodies placed in intersection-free contact with furniture, each other, and themselves. The key contribution is constructing the rest shape, material model, and admissible initial state that deformable simulation requires but text-to-3D meshes lack, all from information already in the generation pipeline. Prior physics-augmented pipelines handled only rigid bodies.

entry.title: From Game Generation to Game Playing: Fully Automated Ability Training for Vision-Language-Action Models

author.name: Changran Liu, Qi Wu, Wenchao Ma, Sharon X. Huang, Haomiao Jiang

entry.summary: The authors introduce a fully automated pipeline where an LLM-powered agent builds game environments and programmatic experts generate aligned demonstrations, producing 150.3 hours of synthetic Minecraft and Roblox gameplay. A 4B vision-language model post-trained via behavior cloning (Script2Play) learns to follow gameplay instructions without human demonstrations or reinforcement learning.

entry.title: SAFE-Hair: Scalp-Anchored Fields for Exportable Single-View Hair Reconstruction

author.name: Yucheng Wang, Zedong Wang, Yuetong Wu, Yue Ma, Dan Xu

entry.summary: SAFE-Hair reconstructs explicit, editable strand-level hair grooms from a single portrait image by decoding hair geometry from persistent follicles in a canonical scalp-UV domain. It uses a conditional Rectified Flow model to generate latent scalp fields, then decodes occupancy, direction, and length attributes at fixed follicle locations, producing assets directly usable in grooming and simulation pipelines rather than just visually plausible geometry.

entry.title: Beyond Modality Preference: Controlling Multimodal Arbitration under Modality Conflict in MLLMs

author.name: Zhaoying Pan, Shenyu Lu, Jun Hui Wong, Junyi Chai, Xiaoqian Wang

entry.summary: This work identifies a small set of attention heads, termed arbitration heads, that causally influence whether multimodal LLMs follow visual or textual evidence under conflicting inputs, and introduces a training-free intervention that biases these heads toward a designated trusted modality at inference time. The heads are stable across calibration sizes and generalize across settings.

entry.title: Dataset Collections: Challenges of Large-Scale Data Aggregation in 3D Medical Image Datasets

author.name: Yannick Kirchhoff, Saikat Roy, Elisa Stegmeier, Hamideh Haghiri, Constantin Ulrich, Maximilian Rouven Rokuss, Tassilo Wald, Karol Gotkowski, Benjamin Hamm, Raphael Stock, Nico Disch, Michael Baumgartner, Dimitrios Bounias, Anand Deshpande, Stefan Dinkelacker, Stefan Dvoretskii, Katharina Eckstein, Selen Erkan, Jessica K\"achele, Kim-Celine Kahl, Balint Kovacs, Lucas Kulla, Moritz Langenberg, Philipp Schader, Stephen Schaumann, Dasha Trofimova, Shuhan Xiao, Sebastian Ziegler, David Zimmerer, Marco Nolden, Fabian Isensee, Klaus Maier-Hein, Ralf Floca

entry.summary: The paper studies the risks of aggregating public datasets into large-scale collections, including reuse propagation, leakage, bias amplification, and distorted distributions, on a collection of 565k 3D radiological images across 1034 public datasets. It formalizes these problems and provides practical resources, including tools for provenance and leakage detection.

entry.title: HARP-Bench: Benchmarking Robot Manipulation Around Active Humans

author.name: Qinhong Zhou, Riley Zong, Chunru Lin, Diyi Hu, Shivraj Singh Bhatti, Hongxin Zhang, Lin Qiu, Hanqing Zeng, Chuang Gan

entry.summary: HARP-Bench addresses a gap in robot manipulation benchmarks, which typically assume the robot is the only active agent. It evaluates manipulation policies in workspaces shared with active humans who may reveal implicit goals, complete part of tasks, or constrain robot motion, enabling more realistic human-robot interaction evaluation.

entry.title: SimDuoReal: Object-Centric Bimanual Policy for Emergent Dexterity

author.name: Qiyang Yan, Yulin Liu, Akash Sharma, Haozhi Qi, Guanya Shi, C. Karen Liu

entry.summary: SimDuoReal shows that complex bimanual dexterous behaviors such as pre-grasp manipulation, regrasping, in-hand adjustment, and handover can emerge from a simple shared object-centric reward under varied training environments, without hand-designed motion sequences. The authors refine the resulting experts and distill them into a single policy via DAgger and RL.

entry.title: DexForesight: Grounding Dexterous Policies with Implicit Spatial Foresight

author.name: Zhongxi Chen, Yi Yang, Xinyi Chen, Mingzhe Ye, Yaping Li, Zhihong Liu, Congsheng Xu, Haonan Wang, Zhijie Deng

entry.summary: DexForesight learns implicit spatial foresight for dexterous manipulation by injecting an action-conditioned 3D world model into the latent space of a dexterous policy, predicting hand-point motion and visual feature changes including occluded fingers. Rather than explicit future prediction, dynamics-aware representations are learned from depth, hand kinematics, and demonstrations. This targets a core limitation of dexterous policies: lack of anticipatory scene and hand dynamics.

entry.title: Learning Heterogeneous Tactile Representation for General Dexterous Manipulation

author.name: Bing Han, Yichuan Peng, Haoyu Dong, Yuanmeng Hu, Yongyi Jia, Fangjing Wang, Kecheng Zheng, Yiming Zhang, Yanhong Zeng, Xiaoqing Zhang, Chen Song, Rundong Zou, Anqi Dong, Yuan Guan, Ka Leong Cheng, Xing Zhu, Yujun Shen, Nan Xue, Wei Ning

entry.summary: LingBot-Touch is a tactile foundation model that yields a unified representation across different tactile sensor types (piezoresistive, magnetic, and visuotactile), freeing tactile understanding from sensor-specific physics. The work enables embodied models to leverage heterogeneous tactile data, supporting general dexterous manipulation.

entry.title: LEGION: Benchmarking Language Agents on Sparse-Signal Investigation Under Adversarial Noise

author.name: Samuel Joseph Amouyal, Ofek Glick, Yaniv Menasherov, Eyal Fisher, Ohav Barbi

entry.summary: LEGION is a benchmark framework for language agents on discovery tasks with sparse signal and mostly irrelevant retrieved information, coupling a stochastic enterprise-telemetry simulator with 74 expertly crafted adversarial scenarios. It scores investigation efficiency alongside detection accuracy and independently controls confounder density and event volume, evaluated across five agent architectures.

entry.title: Hibana: Fast Agentic Inference on Unified-Memory Devices

author.name: Yahya Emara, Chi-Chih Chang, Anthony Fei, Ahmed F. AbouElhamayed, Chong-Yan Chen, Hung-Yueh Chiang, Kai-Chiang Wu, Mohamed S. Abdelfattah

entry.summary: Hibana is an inference engine optimized for unified-memory devices (like laptops and edge machines) that co-optimizes model representation, memory management, and decoding strategy, using model surgery to shrink memory footprint and data movement where engines like vLLM and SGLang underperform. It enables capable open-weight agentic models to run locally and privately. This addresses the growing demand for efficient on-device agentic inference.

entry.title: BAPLe++: Cross-Model Transferability and Prompt-Level Defense of Backdoors in Medical Foundation Models

author.name: Ufaq Khan, Umair Nawaz, Satyajit Tourani, Awais Rauf, Fahad Shamshad, Asif Hanif, Rao Muhammad Anwer, Muhammad Haris Khan, Mohammad Yaqub

entry.summary: BAPLe++ studies backdoors implanted via jointly optimized learnable prompts and noise triggers during few-shot adaptation of medical foundation models. It presents the first study of cross-model transferability of backdoored prompts, examining whether a backdoored prompt remains effective on a different Med-FM, and whether it can be repaired at the prompt level without retraining the backbone.

entry.title: Where Should a Gate Look? Input vs. State Gating in Diagonal State Space Models

author.name: Riccardo Zattra, Giacomo Baggio, Leonardo De Marchi, Augusto Ferrante, Francesco Ticozzi, Marco Del Pr\`a, Antonio Orvieto

entry.summary: Investigates whether state feedback through a simple gate regulating memory updates can enhance the expressivity of diagonal state-space models, comparing gates that depend on current input, recurrent state, or both. It establishes a strict expressivity separation: for scalar models, state gating solves induction-head tasks for arbitrary vocabulary and sequence length whereas input gating fails on a finite instance.

entry.title: Regularization Amplifies Subliminal Learning

author.name: Lawrence Feng, Jacob Mitchell Springer, Gaurav R. Ghosal, Ziqian Zhong, Aditi Raghunathan

entry.summary: The paper systematically studies whether regularization can suppress subliminal learning, where hidden biases transfer through data with no apparent semantic relationship, and finds the opposite: regularization amplifies the transfer. Low-rank adaptation or explicit penalties can induce strong subliminal transfer that is typically absent under full fine-tuning, and similar effects appear in phantom transfer and logit-linear selection.

entry.title: Online Imitation Learning for Stabilizing Vlasov--Poisson Plasmas

author.name: Xiaofan Xia, Qin Li, Wenlong Mou

entry.summary: The authors study imitation learning for controlling instability in Vlasov-Poisson plasma systems, a problem relevant to nuclear fusion control under partial observability. They prove a separation between online and offline imitation learning - behavior cloning errors compound exponentially while online imitation loss controls rollout stability polynomially - and propose a DAgger-style algorithm that learns stabilizing control from macroscopic measurements.

entry.title: Streaming Failure Forecasting: VLA Failure Monitors That Keep Learning After Deployment

author.name: Amit Jadhav, Shaurya Beriwala, David Q. Liu, Yanfei Liu

entry.summary: This paper identifies that failure monitors for vision-language-action (VLA) robot policies degrade to near-chance performance when tasks or policy versions change after deployment. It proposes Streaming Failure Forecasting (SFF), which keeps the monitor's network fixed and refits only its last linear layer after each episode using the success/failure label, at 2.18 ms per policy call on a Jetson CPU. The alarm threshold only moves after successes, keeping false alarms near target in simulation.

entry.title: Curbside Chatbots: Auditing the Mental Health Interventions Large Language Models Recommend to Clinicians, Caregivers, and Patients

author.name: Matthew Flathers, Jill Noorily, Phuong Anh Nguyen, Mark Kalinich, Mina Fallah, Victoria Lisowski, Christine Shi, Rebekah M. Bodner, Anna Simms, Mihika Hete, Meiting Chen, Samuel K. Powell, Tatum Williamson, Laura Ospina-Pinillos, Haruka Notsu, Julian Herpertz, John Torous

entry.summary: This large audit examines what 41 language models recommend when the same clinical information arrives from a clinician, caregiver, or patient footing, across 19 vignettes and five questions, yielding 35,055 free-text responses. Models largely recommend interventions they rate well, differ recommendations by user footing, and adapt response style (consultation-style for clinicians, hedged simplification for lay users). It matters as a systematic safety-relevant audit of LLM behavior in high-stakes mental health contexts.

entry.title: Is Recursive Self-Improvement Safe?

author.name: Vincent Conitzer

entry.summary: Vincent Conitzer argues that recursive self-improvement (RSI), long an abstract futuristic idea, is becoming plausible given frontier AI abilities in programming, mathematics, research, and long-horizon coherence, and that AI companies are beginning to pursue it. The paper discusses whether humanity should set RSI in motion, arguing that existing frameworks for assessing RSI safety are inadequate.

entry.title: Improving Analytic Constants via Interpretable AI-Guided Lean Proof Refinement

author.name: Rahul Saha, Alan Li, Anton Xue, Swarat Chaudhuri, Adam Klivans, Pravesh K. Kothari, Raghu Meka

entry.summary: The paper introduces an interpretable framework for AI-guided mathematical discovery where proofs are represented as partially-formalized Lean blueprints (dependency graphs of definitions and lemmas), and an AI agent iteratively tightens slack in intermediate lemmas to improve quantitative bounds on analytic constants. This preserves the overall proof structure while enabling local, verifiable improvements. It addresses the interpretability and verifiability problems of AI-discovered mathematics.

entry.title: Measuring Generative AI Content in Political Campaigns: Evidence of Rising Adoption and Non-Disclosure

author.name: Anna-Maria Gueorguieva, Nic Weber

entry.summary: This study develops measures of both magnitude and modality of AI-generated content (AIGC) used by political campaigns, applied to a novel dataset of campaign text and imagery during an election cycle. It documents rising adoption and widespread non-disclosure even as nearly half of U.S. states have enacted laws targeting deceptive AIGC in elections.

entry.title: ChainCheck: Near-Perfect Evidence-Sufficiency Scores Can Conceal Sensitivity to Construction Artifacts -- Paired Conditional Contrasts that Expose an Evaluation Confound

author.name: Hyojung Han, Ryangkyung Kang, Youngeun Kim, Seung-Hun Jeon

entry.summary: This paper introduces ChainCheck, an audit methodology showing that near-perfect scores on evidence-sufficiency benchmarks can be matched or exceeded by scorers that never read the reasoning chain, exposing construction artifacts in how broken passage sets are created. On 2,214 HotpotQA pairs, a chain-ignoring scorer achieves a nominal AUC of 0.997, revealing that popular benchmarks may not measure multi-hop reasoning at all.

entry.title: AutoBuddy: Evaluating Proactive, Always-On Agents on Task Discovery and Execution in a Simulated Workplace

author.name: Shiqi Chen, Daniel Madrigal Diaz, Wei-Ning Chen, Gbola Afonja, Fangkai Yang, Rujia Wang, Chetan Bansal, Victor R\"uhle, Saravan Rajmohan, Dongge Han

entry.summary: AutoBuddy studies proactive task discovery, where an always-on agent must infer pending tasks from a user's mail, chat, documents, and records and then execute them in the systems where the work lives. Existing benchmarks hand the agent its task, so this work addresses a gap in evaluating agents' ability to recognize obligations themselves. The authors include Microsoft-affiliated researchers (Fangkai Yang, Victor Ruhle, Saravan Rajmohan), suggesting industrial grounding.

entry.title: Autonomy Is Absent, Not Eroded: An Observational Study of User Autonomy in Multi-Turn LLM Conversations

author.name: Chaoran Chen (University of Notre Dame), Isabel Barber\'a (Independent Researcher), Yuhuai Wei (Independent Researcher)

entry.summary: This observational study tests the hypothesis that prolonged LLM interaction erodes user autonomy, scoring 2,877 multi-turn conversations (46,952 turns) from WildChat and validating on 500 conversations from LMSYS-Chat-1M. The core finding is a null result: population-level autonomy is stable, and the apparent decline is survivorship bias; the dominant pattern is absence of autonomy engagement (80.8% of conversations), and when autonomy occurs it is self-reinforcing. This is a valuable empirical correction to an influential narrative.

entry.title: Micius-Flash: Lightweight Agentic Intelligence for Engineering

author.name: Hongcheng Gao, Weiheng Li, Yipeng Wei, Yu Lei, Shuo Sun, Yi Li, Yajiao Wang, Jie Luo, Jianwei Wen, Xinyi Zhou, Hongda Li, Yibing Zhang, Henghui Sun, Yufan Zhou, Tianfang Hao, Naihao Xue, Hailong Qu, Jingjing Zhou, Peng Xu, Yongzheng Wei, Yichen Zhu, Ziying Wang, Yibo Wang, Jianshu Zeng, Yuhang Lei, Zeqiang Wang

entry.summary: Introduces Micius-Flash, a 27-billion-parameter engineering-focused model with native multimodal input, deep reasoning, and a 256K-token context window, trained via a knowledge-tree-driven data flywheel and expert models for semiconductor knowledge, hardware coding, and multimodal understanding. Multi-Teacher On-Policy Distillation integrates the experts into one unified model, suggesting strong specialized agentic capability at modest scale.

entry.title: How Much Skill Orchestration Can LLM Agents Compile Away? Execution-Grounded Specialization for Token-Efficient Skill Use

author.name: Jiayi Ni, Zac Wang, Alex Zhang, Zheng Liu, Roopa Prabhu

entry.summary: The paper investigates whether LLM agents can automatically compile reusable skill orchestration into executable fast paths, showing that zero-shot compilation without execution evidence produces brittle plans due to wrong assumptions about runtime bindings. The proposed SkillCache compiles a completed invocation trace into a parameterized capsule, replays it before reuse, and grounds specialization in execution evidence for token efficiency.

entry.title: Jais 3: Introducing Arabic-centric Agentic AI

author.name: Team IFM, Haonan Li, Hadi Abdine, Nikhil Ranjan, Mohamed Anwar, Ahmad Chamma, Amr Mohamed, Ahmed Frikha, Dani Bouch, Maaz Maqsood, George Ibrahim, Mostafa Awad, Nurkhan Laiyk, Hasan Iqbal, Abhishek Maiti, Bilal Bouardi, Shivam Chauhan, Ahmer Tabassum, Owais Aijaz, Omar Arbi, Neha Sengupta, Aaryamonvikram Singh, Abdelhakim Freihat, Sarath Chandran, Rahul Pal, Mohammed Bellam, Sajid Siddiki, Sarah AlBarri, Debopriyo Banerjee, Ali El Filali, Samta Kamboj, Rifo Genadi, Ahmed Attia, Go Inoue, Shuonan Dong, Amine Khelif Khelif, Evan Dufraisse, Florian Valade, Tapas Sen, Guowei He, Sunil Sahu, Onkar Pandit, Kareem Magdy, Sheikh Khalid bin Khalifa Al Nahyan, Samujjwal Ghosh, Zainul Abedien, Ahmed Quraishi, Larry Murray, Avraham Sheinin, Natalia Vassilieva, Preslav Nakov, Guokan Shang, Xuguang Hector Ren, Zhengzhong Liu, Eric Xing

entry.summary: Jais 3 is a fleet of six open Arabic-centric agentic language models ranging from 0.9B to 375B parameters, adapted from the fully open K2 Horizon fleet via continual pretraining, SFT, FTPO, and RLVR. The models are trained for agentic behavior in Arabic: planning multi-step tasks, tool and MCP server calls, terminal operation, web search, and document manipulation. This represents a significant step for underrepresented-language agentic AI with open weights.

entry.title: HexIt: Learning Hexahedral Block Decomposition with Expert Iteration on Combinatorial Maps

author.name: Arjun Narayanan, Per-Olof Persson

entry.summary: HexIt frames the long-standing mesh generation problem of decomposing a polyhedral solid into well-shaped hexahedral blocks as a sequential decision problem on 3D generalized maps, with a policy convolving over the map's involutions choosing split operations. After policy cloning and expert iteration, the learned policy solves 94.4% of held-out chamfered solids sharing no boundary topology with training data. A novel RL application to a classic computational geometry challenge.

entry.title: Beyond Discrete Ancestry Groups: Distribution-Aware In-Context Learning for Cancer Outcome Prediction Across the Genetic Ancestry Continuum

author.name: Weizhi Li, Yan Cui

entry.summary: This paper addresses a known weakness in omics-based cancer outcome prediction: models built on discrete ancestry groups lose accuracy as genetic distance from training samples grows, because genetic variation shifts continuously rather than falling into fixed categories. The authors propose distribution-aware in-context learning (DA-ICL), extending conventional ancestry-discrete modeling to a continuum formulation so predictions degrade more gracefully across the genetic ancestry spectrum. The work matters because it tackles health-equity concerns in genomic ML, where current approaches systematically underserve populations distant from training data.

entry.title: Pixels over Symbols: Sensory Realism Improves Behavioral Alignment in Models of Cognition

author.name: Hao Yuan Bai, Xiaoxuan Lei, Zihan Weng, Motahareh Pourrahimi, Lucas Gomez, Pouya Bashivan

entry.summary: A large-scale empirical comparison of abstract versus sensory-realistic neural network models trained on memory-dependent decision-making tasks finds that sensory realism meaningfully improves behavioral alignment with cognitive processes. This challenges the long-standing assumption that symbolic input approximations are incidental to modeling cognition.

entry.title: EndoSCOP-V: A Multi-Turn Video Understanding Evaluation Framework for Multimodal Models in Endoscopy Reporting and Clinical Reasoning

author.name: Abhishek Tyagi, Tanmay Jain, Vilas Biradar, Krithi Krishna Koduri, Misba Hul Bashir Masoodi, Swetha Rapolu, Hardik Rughwani, Rachana Kotha, Anjan Kumar Kaipa, Anudeep Katrevula, Rakesh Garlapati, Aniruddha Pratap Singh, Rajendra Patel, Abhay Tyagi, Sundeep Lakhtakia, Mohan Ramchandani, Rakesh Kalapala, D. Nageshwar Reddy

entry.summary: EndoSCOP-V is a video-grounded multi-turn evaluation framework for structured endoscopy reporting and clinical reasoning, containing 1,307 real-world endoscopy and colonoscopy videos (63.2 hours) with 20,274 question-answer turns derived deterministically from clinician-filled structured reports. It captures the temporal, multi-minute reasoning chains that real-world endoscopy reporting demands, unlike static-image benchmarks.

entry.title: STABLE: A Continual Learning Optimizer with Adaptive Drift Control

author.name: Xiaoyan Li, Lanpei Li, Massimo Coppola, Vincenzo Lomonaco, Antonio Carta

entry.summary: STABLE treats catastrophic forgetting as a consequence of unstable learning dynamics and proposes an optimizer-level solution. The authors formally prove that for distance-based classifiers, bounded parameter drift guarantees bounded margin erosion under a local score-stability condition, and build a primal-dual optimizer with adaptive drift control to exploit this.

entry.title: REINS: A Self-Evolving Agent Harness for Real-Time Trajectory Planning

author.name: Zhihong Cui, Hengyu Liu, Haoran Tang, Shijun Liu, Amir Taherkordi, Tor Skeie

entry.summary: REINS applies the agent harness paradigm (runtime scaffolds wrapping the LLM reasoning loop with tool dispatch, verification, and persistent memory) to trajectory planning, where existing LLM planners either exceed millisecond control budgets or offload the model to offline rules. The paper proposes a runtime harness that lets an LLM planner meet real-time constraints while self-evolving.

entry.title: Zero-Shot VLA Adaptation with Retrieved Guidance

author.name: Subin Kim, Anh-Quan Pham, Dinesh Jayaraman

entry.summary: Motivated by retrieval-augmented generation in language models, the paper introduces RAGu, which retrieves guidance from domain-mismatched in-the-wild demonstration datasets like DROID to improve vision-language-action model behavior in new target domains. This addresses VLA fragility under small domain shifts such as camera viewpoint, background, object identity, or robot morphology changes.

entry.title: Horizon-Scalable Q-Learning

author.name: Haoran Xu, Pragya Srivastava, Xinjie Liu, Siddhant Agarwal, Amy Zhang

entry.summary: This paper introduces HQL, a method for learning accurate off-policy Q-functions on long-horizon tasks by automatically balancing one-step TD bootstrapping against multi-step TD returns along the dataset trajectory. The goal is to avoid the error accumulation of one-step TD and the bias growth of naively following suboptimal behavior-policy actions over many steps.

entry.title: SGA-Sparse: Training Native SwiGLU Gates for Activation-Sparse and Low-Bit LLMs

author.name: Ruokai Yin, Steven Li

entry.summary: Shows that training-free routing with the native SwiGLU gate performs worse than routing with the up activation at high sparsity, but this reverses after sparsity-aware training. SGA-Sparse converts pretrained SwiGLU LLMs into fixed-budget activation-sparse models by training the existing gate projection as a top-k router end-to-end, with no auxiliary router parameters, and also supports low-bit settings.

entry.title: Does Predictive Performance Translate to Causal Performance? Evaluating tabular foundation models as nuisance learners for causal effect estimation

author.name: Andrew R Weckstein, Issa J Dahabreh, Marinka Zitnik, Sonia Hern\'andez-D\'iaz, Sebastian Schneeweiss

entry.summary: The authors evaluate whether tabular foundation models based on prior-data fitted networks (PFNs) can serve as nuisance learners (propensity scores and outcome regressions) inside doubly robust causal estimators. Using synthetic and semi-synthetic benchmarks with varying confounding and effect heterogeneity, they probe whether strong predictive accuracy translates into accurate causal effect estimates and calibrated uncertainty.

entry.title: Perturbing Inputs Improves Pretraining Distillation

author.name: Ziyang Cai, Yihe Dong, Dimitris Papailiopoulos, Shivam Garg

entry.summary: The paper investigates whether training a distilled student LM to match its teacher on perturbed inputs (token noise, document blending, token blending) improves generalization beyond the training text. Allocating part of the pretraining budget to perturbed distillation improves on standard distillation at both 135M and 0.5B parameter scales, with consistent gains across seeds.

entry.title: Attention Is Only as Good as Its Witnesses: When Higher-Order Layers Help, and When They Do Not

author.name: Mostafa 'Neo' Mohsenvand

entry.summary: Analyzes why transformers fail at graph search and the card game SET despite attention being expressive enough, framing each layer as computing a partition function over a family of witnesses. It derives a depth law matching a logical result (L layers over two-step walks reach exactly 2^L - 1 steps), verifies a matching construction in Lean, and characterizes when higher-order attention helps.

entry.title: Say Shibboleth: Fingerprinting the LLMs and Harnesses Behind Agentic Attacks

author.name: Dario Pasquini, Reworr, Giuseppe Ateniese, Manish Bhatt, Sergej Epp

entry.summary: The paper introduces shibboleth traps, modular honeypot services that elicit discriminative behaviors from agentic attackers to fingerprint the LLM version and harness behind cyberattacks. Probes reveal characteristic harness behaviors such as secret masking and execution patterns, enabling attribution from telemetry without successful prompt injection.

entry.title: A Clinical Evaluation of Conformal Prediction for Chest Radiograph Report Generation

author.name: Nikolaos Kontogeorgis, Pascal Krezer, Klaus-Rudolf Kladny, Arne Estler, Christian F. Baumgartner, Lisa Koch, Saif Afat, Michael Muehlebach

entry.summary: This work introduces CLARITY, a framework of clinical admissibility criteria that distinguishes clinically consequential errors from minor deviations in radiology report generation, backed by radiologist annotations of MLLM-generated reports. It benchmarks conformal prediction strategies against these human-annotated criteria rather than uncalibrated automatic judges.

entry.title: MACaQ: Fast, Model Agnostic Calibrated Quantization for Low-Precision Weights and Activations

author.name: Lorenz K. Muller, Philippe Bich, Chiara Boretti, Hyun-Min Chang, Jiawei Zhuang, Lukas Cavigelli

entry.summary: MACaQ is a post-training quantization method achieving W4A4 (MXFP4) by treating each linear layer independently: it applies a per-channel scale and block-Hadamard transform to activations online while absorbing the inverse transform into the weights. This avoids cross-layer dependencies, enabling a streaming implementation where only one layer needs to be in memory at a time. The work addresses a practical barrier to low-precision LLM inference deployment.

entry.title: Prune to Probe: Causal Decision-Stability Probes for Efficient Reasoning

author.name: Yufei Qi, Chonghe Jiang

entry.summary: Prune-to-Probe is an inference-time controller that decides when a reasoning model should stop generating by probing answer stability through causal activation interventions. It identifies late-MLP coordinates that drive post-answer continuation, temporarily suppresses them once an answer is stated, and measures the response relative to matched random interventions as a stopping signal.

entry.title: The Race Is Decided Early! A Kernel Law Predicts Lock-In in Majority-Vote Test-Time RL

author.name: Jaeho Hwang, Sehong Park, Daejin Choi, Uiwon Hwang

entry.summary: This paper analyzes test-time reinforcement learning with majority-vote rewards on unlabeled questions, where each question locks into one answer during training, sometimes a wrong one. The authors show the lock-in outcome is determined early by a short race among close answers driven by sampling noise, and derive closed-form probabilities for which answer wins, including a normal tail probability scaled by a noise constant. This provides the first predictive theory for a failure mode of label-free RL fine-tuning.

entry.title: A Stability Analysis of AdamW: Unstable Equilibria and Non-Convergence

author.name: Baiyu Su, Lizhang Chen, Qiang Liu

entry.summary: This paper analyzes AdamW's training dynamics through dynamical-systems theory, showing that its fixed points coincide with stationary points of a constrained, regularized objective but that many of these fixed points are unstable depending on curvature, weight decay, and momentum. Even in one dimension, equilibria can be unstable with persistent oscillations rather than convergence. The authors derive sufficient conditions for local stability of the continuous-time dynamics.

entry.title: Tropical Gaussian Anticoncentration: Optimal Instance-Dependent Bounds for Online Learning in Extensive-Form Games

author.name: Ashkan Soleymani, Zhiyuan Fan, Lillian J. Ratliff, Patrick Jaillet, Gabriele Farina

entry.summary: The paper proves that the logarithmic dependence on the number of reduced normal-form strategies in regret bounds for extensive-form games, achieved by algorithms like KOMWU and dilated entropy mirror descent, is minimax optimal. The analysis handles the key difficulty that pure plans in a treeplex are correlated experts whose rewards are not independent.

entry.title: On the Global Convergence of Stochastic Adam for Physics-Informed Neural Networks

author.name: Yihang Gao

entry.summary: This paper establishes linear convergence guarantees for the Adam optimizer when training sufficiently wide two-layer neural networks, using neural tangent kernel (NTK) analysis extended to handle Adam's momentum coupling and adaptive second-moment preconditioner. It covers both full-batch and minibatch settings, addressing a gap in the theoretical understanding of why Adam drives training loss near zero.

entry.title: Do Time-Series Foundation Models Forecast Index-Futures Returns? A Preregistered Evaluation of Models, Metrics, and Input Representations

author.name: Rishabh Upadhyay

entry.summary: A preregistered evaluation asks whether apparent skill of frozen time-series foundation models (Chronos-Bolt, Chronos-2, TimesFM 2.5, Moirai 2.0, TiRex, plus Kronos) on intraday index-futures returns is real incremental skill. Across NQ and ES futures, a common panel tested against no-change forecasts at 5-120 minute horizons found that 0 of 160 model-representation-horizon-market cells beat no-change on a blind set, with a Hansen SPA test p = 1.000 on both markets. The rigorous preregistration and null result matter for the field of financial ML, where overfitting and backtest bias are rampant.

entry.title: Harnessing Vision-Language Models for Federated Unsupervised Visual Recognition

author.name: Jian Liang, Kuangpu Guo, Ran He, Tieniu Tan

entry.summary: The paper introduces FedUR, the first framework for unsupervised visual recognition in federated learning, leveraging the zero-shot capabilities of pre-trained vision-language models such as CLIP. It handles data heterogeneity via pseudo-labeling with class-aware data selection, filling a gap left by prior unsupervised FL work focused on clustering and self-supervised learning.

entry.title: Two-Phase Rapid Simulation-Based Inference with Differentiable Simulators

author.name: Uros Zivanovic, Rahul Srinivasan, Roberto Trotta, Andre Scaffidi

entry.summary: RSBI is a diffusion-based variational approach to likelihood-free Bayesian inference combining Schrodinger Bridge sampling with a differentiable simulator to supply an efficient initial surrogate likelihood. The two-phase design replaces sequential rounds of other methods with a one-shot proposal followed by refinement, handling multi-modal posteriors under large prior-to-posterior volumes.

entry.title: UniHam: A Large-Scale SOC-Complete Dataset and Benchmark for Hamiltonian Learning in Materials

author.name: Yuewen Huang, Pin Chen, Yutong Lu

entry.summary: UniHam is a large-scale dataset and benchmark of 100,000+ DFT-computed complex-valued Hermitian Hamiltonians with full spin-orbit coupling, covering 72 elements and diverse crystal geometries and symmetries. It addresses a key data bottleneck for general-purpose materials foundation models that predict electronic Hamiltonians to avoid costly DFT.

entry.title: What the Loss Curve Misses: FP4 Pretraining Slows the Acquisition of Rare Facts

author.name: Chang Lu, Mengjiao Zhang

entry.summary: The authors train transformers from scratch with emulated 4-bit matrix multiplications on synthetic biographies with controlled fact-exposure counts, showing that NVFP4 pretraining needs about 1.2-1.5x more exposures than BF16 to match rare-fact recall even when validation loss is nearly identical. Gradient-noise analysis suggests backward-pass quantization noise is a key driver of the gap. The result warns that loss-matched evaluations understate the cost of low-precision pretraining for factual knowledge acquisition.

entry.title: Done Is Not Correct: Measuring Silent Failures and Self-Verification Calibration When LLM Agents Take CAD Actions

author.name: Carson Rodrigues, Clive Rodrigues, Aravind Reddy G

entry.summary: This paper releases a benchmark of 13 CAD specification tasks where every requirement maps to machine-checkable properties of the produced boundary representation, measured against tolerance bands by a geometry kernel. It isolates two previously unreported quantities for agentic LLMs: silent-failure rate (a valid solid plus an explicit completion claim plus at least one failed semantic check) and completion-claim calibration, evaluated across four models from four vendors.

entry.title: Sparse Predict and Demote: Optimal Scheduling with Minimal Size Advice

author.name: Chengyi Liu, Thodoris Lykouris, Junxuan Shen, Adam Wierman

entry.summary: This paper introduces Sparse Predict and Demote, a scheduling policy that achieves order-optimal mean response time in heavy traffic while requiring only one-bit job-size predictions for a vanishing fraction of arrivals. It proves robustness to inexact predictions up to fixed multiplicative error and to costly predictions where the server must be used to obtain them.

entry.title: Sampling-based Model Predictive Control as Sequential Monte Carlo Inference

author.name: Austin Garrett, Muyang Yan, Zachary Kingston

entry.summary: The authors show that a family of seemingly distinct sampling-based MPC algorithms, including predictive sampling, MPPI, cross-entropy method, and their biased, colored-noise, and annealed variants, are all instances of a single Sequential Monte Carlo inference algorithm. The unifying framework is specified by three independent axes: proposal, update rule, and effective-sample-size threshold for resampling. They validate on MuJoCo control, navigation, 7-DoF motion planning, and push-T both in simulation and on a physical Franka FR3 robot.

entry.title: Amortized Bayesian Experimental Design with In-Context Knowledge Conditioning

author.name: Zhanghu Zhao, Daolang Huang, Xinyi Wen, Samuel Kaski

entry.summary: Introduces IMBUE, an amortized Bayesian experimental design framework that accepts external knowledge at deployment time - user-specified priors and observations from prior experiment instances - through a unified in-context Transformer interface without retraining. Enables real-time design strategies that go beyond the training prior.

entry.title: AI-Driven Discovery of Entanglement Witness in Spin Hamiltonians

author.name: Jiwei Tian, Mouyang Cheng, Mingda Li

entry.summary: This paper introduces EntNet, an AI framework that discovers compact combinations of spin observables distinguishing entangled from fully separable many-body mixed states in one-dimensional spin-1/2 chains. It constructs local-unitary-invariant representations of Pauli correlators up to four-body order and learns their spatial structure with a Transformer using rotary positional embeddings. The approach uses only low-order expectation values accessible in experiments.

entry.title: Watching Itself Watch: Self-Auditing Visual Reliance for Video Reasoning

author.name: Rohan Dugad, Mi Luo, Kristen Grauman

entry.summary: The paper introduces VIOS, a post-training framework for video reasoning models that uses the divergence between next-token distributions with and without video input to self-audit where the model under-uses visual evidence. Learning is concentrated at those positions via on-policy self-distillation, avoiding coarse trajectory-level rewards, multiple rollouts, and expensive external judges common in GRPO-style training.

entry.title: Learning Rate Decay Can Exponentially Accelerate SGD for Global Optimization of Nonconvex Functions

author.name: Guneykan Ozgul, Dylan Herman, Junhyung Lyle Kim, Shree Hari Sureshbabu, Shouvanik Chakrabarti

entry.summary: The authors prove the first demonstrated exponential advantage for learning rate decay in SGD: for a natural class of nonconvex functions, SGD with decayed learning rates requires exponentially fewer gradient queries for global optimization than SGD with any fixed learning rate in the small-step-size regime. This formalizes the folk belief among practitioners that learning rate schedules matter, giving it rigorous asymptotic grounding. The result connects optimization theory to common deep learning practice.

entry.title: Search-by-Answer Bias in Retrieval Models

author.name: Adiel Avigad, Shauli Ravfogel, Yoav Goldberg

entry.summary: This paper identifies search-by-answer bias in dense retrievers: they favor passages mentioning answers the model believes likely over passages supporting valid alternative answers. Testing across eight retrievers including DPR, Contriever, E5, and Qwen3-Embedding using controlled factual contrasts from LAMA/TREx, they show token-prediction scores for canonical answers consistently predict retrieval scores.

entry.title: BridgeKV: Large-Model Prefill and Small-Model Decoding for LLM Inference via KV Cache Translation

author.name: Payman Behnam, Debopam Sanyal, Pranav Ponnusamy, Kusum Meda Ravi, Pranav Sastry, Mani Chandana Bandaru, Alind Khare, Myungjin Lee, Alexey Tumanov

entry.summary: BridgeKV splits LLM inference across model scales: a larger model performs compute-intensive prefill while a smaller same-family model handles memory-bandwidth-bound decoding, connected by a lightweight KV-stitching module that translates the large model's prompt cache into the small model's layout via learned layer mixing and separate key/value maps. Both models run locally together, achieving efficiency gains without same-model constraints.

entry.title: Blind Variation, Selective Retention: Improving Creative Idea Generation in AI Scientists

author.name: Guowei Xu, Jiaru Zou, Mete Erdogan, Haotian Ye, Pan Lu, James Zou

entry.summary: This paper proposes a framework for AI-driven scientific idea generation inspired by the cognitive theory of Blind Variation and Selective Retention (BVSR). Instead of giving an AI scientist full task context during ideation, the method deliberately withholds information to broaden exploration, then uses feedback from verified proposals on the same task to select and refine promising candidates before costly empirical testing. The approach is evaluated across five proposer models and 12 scientific tasks, with results indicating that limiting task information substantially improves creative output.

entry.title: Machine Hearing: Can Audio LLMs Generalize Beyond Human Auditory Perception?

author.name: Liwei Liu, Jun Tao, Xingyuan Li, Xuenan Xu, Chen Zhang, Junyi Wang, Boya Zhang, Xiaoyu Yang, Zhen-Hua Ling, Wen Wu, Chao Zhang

entry.summary: The authors introduce the Machine Hearing Benchmark (MHB), with 6,128 instances across 13 tasks and seven domains, probing whether audio LLMs can perceive sounds beyond human hearing limits, such as inaudible vibrations and oscillations. This reframes multimodal audio perception as potentially superhuman rather than human-centric. The benchmark matters as a new evaluation target for extending multimodal LLM perceptual scope.

entry.title: Video-DCI: How Far Are VLM Agents from Human Viewers in Direct Video Corpus Interaction?

author.name: Garry Yang, Yuqiao Liu, Hao Lin, Luohao Pan, Xinru Chen, Wanqi Ren, Zhikang Xu, Yizhan Huang, Huaixiao Tou, James Cheng

entry.summary: Video-DCI is a diagnostic benchmark measuring how well vision-language agents can interactively search video corpora the way humans do, with two components: DCI-Loc for temporal evidence localization and DCI-QA for multi-round discovery, retention, and composition of cross-video evidence. It uses a functionally matched human-agent protocol to quantify the gap between VLM agents and human viewers, and its design resists textual shortcuts.

entry.title: Contrastive fine-tuning against stain and scanner bias improves robustness and downstream performance across pathology foundation models

author.name: Ryan Kim, Hassan Muhammad, Anish Dulal, Paul S. Scotti, Tanishq Mathew Abraham

entry.summary: Introduces SPECTRA, a model-agnostic contrastive post-training framework that uses LoRA adapters on matched multi-scanner and multi-stain whole-slide images from the PLISM dataset to reduce scanner and site-specific bias in pathology foundation models. It addresses documented generalization gaps in histopathology representations, improving downstream robustness without retraining the base model.

entry.title: MGE: A Membership Guided Data Extraction Attack against Diffusion Models

author.name: Yuchang Mei, Longqiang Wang, Haoyang Jiang, Mingyang Yi, Shaolei Zhang, Keman Huang, Wuqiong Pan, Ju Fan

entry.summary: This paper presents MGE, a framework that extracts training images from pre-trained diffusion models by formulating data extraction as conditional generation guided by a membership inference classifier, with adversarial gradients and parallel branch decoding to boost efficiency. Experiments show hundreds of images can be recovered, quantifying privacy risks of diffusion models.

entry.title: What Does Multiple Choice Actually Measure? Disentangling Video Understanding from Option Exploitation

author.name: Elliott Piercy, Justin Chan, Sepand Dyanatkar

entry.summary: This evaluation study shows that across six VideoQA benchmarks, models achieve accuracy significantly above chance without any visual input due to language priors, option exploitation, and shortcutting in multiple-choice formats. The authors formalize these confounds in terms of faithfulness, separating scores supplied by the evaluation context from perception actually earned by the model. This is an important critique of how video understanding progress is currently measured.

entry.title: DisasterVL: Evidence-Based Visual Reasoning Dataset and Model for Disaster Scene Understanding

author.name: Ali Diba, Aisha Al-Mohannadi, Yin Yang, Muhammad Imran, Ferda Ofli

entry.summary: DisasterVL is a large-scale dataset and benchmark for evidence-grounded reasoning about disaster imagery, containing about 1.2 million images from 142 countries with 25 million structured annotations covering captions, incident and location assessments, spatial relationships, and VQA. The test set has 38,254 images across 75 countries and 28 hazard types, with Gemini 3.1 Pro (an existing model) used to audit test annotations alongside human review.

entry.title: Grasping the Future: Joint 3D Hand-Object Forecasting From Internet Videos

author.name: Rustin Soraki, Matthew Wallingford, Ryan Aby, Brandon Chee, Jason Ren, Ali Farhadi, Homanga Bharadhwaj, Roozbeh Mottaghi

entry.summary: The paper presents Grasping-the-Future, a unified generative model of joint 3D hand-object motion (wrist motion, finger articulation, object pose) trained on internet videos via masked spatiotemporal completion and flow matching. It supports multiple prediction tasks including forecasting future interactions and predicting hand motion given object motion.

entry.title: Beyond Prompt Attacks: Least-Action Auditing of Concept Erasure

author.name: Yifei Zhu

entry.summary: This paper introduces least-action auditing of concept erasure in text-to-image diffusion models, measuring the minimum control cost of driving the frozen reverse process into a detector-defined concept event, which equals the path-space KL divergence of conditioning on the event and hence the event's negative log-probability. It evaluates Stable Diffusion concept-erasure checkpoints, showing that prompt attacks do not measure the residual probability the generator still assigns to an erased concept.

entry.title: SPARK: Simple Post-training for Adapting pRetrained Knowledge to Robot Control

author.name: Taekyung Kim, Jeongeun Park, Byeongho Heo, Sungjoon Choi, Sangdoo Yun, Dongyoon Han

entry.summary: SPARK is a post-training method that adapts general-purpose visual foundation models to robot control, addressing the mismatch between pretraining objectives (global semantics) and the temporally sensitive representations robots need. It is built on temporal and task-relevant principles, avoiding the cost of training robot models from scratch.

entry.title: A Unified Inertial Encoder for Human and Humanoid Motion

author.name: Yutian Chen, Shibo Zhao, Rocky Duan, Karen Liu, Carmelo Sferrazza, Guanya Shi, Yuheng Qiu, Koushil Sreenath

entry.summary: The paper proposes a unified inertial encoder whose shared inertial interface uses kinematic IMU synthesis to represent human and humanoid motion at corresponding body sites, enabling transfer from broad human motion datasets to humanoid robots. Joint training on human and retargeted humanoid motion combines velocity estimation and motion-text alignment with continuous-time encoding and sensor/motion randomization.

entry.title: GUARD: Anomaly-Informed Q-Steering for Generative Robot Policies in Dexterous Manipulation

author.name: Aryaman Gupta, Xiaoyue Wu, Rana Soltani Zarrin, Mark Van der Merwe

entry.summary: GUARD improves diffusion and flow-matching robot policies by steering their denoising process with gradients from a learned Q-function that combines sparse task rewards with dense anomaly scores derived from the policy's own training distribution. This anticipates failures during closed-loop execution without requiring extra demonstrations, human intervention, or task-specific rewards.

entry.title: FlowEval: How Much Adaptation Does an Embodied Foundation Model Need at Deployment?

author.name: Zhang Xi-Jia, Roman Yakunin, Shivang Chopra, Chengyue Huang, Che Chen, Siddharth Karamcheti, Zsolt Kira

entry.summary: FlowEval introduces training-free metrics using the flow-matching objective to probe an embodied foundation model with a small set of target-domain demonstrations, quantifying predictive disagreement to estimate whether and how much adaptation data will be needed before any fine-tuning. This addresses a practical deployment question for pretrained robot policies. It could substantially reduce wasted data collection and deployment iteration.

entry.title: BioMARS 2.0: a robotic biologist for formulating and adapting biological experiments

author.name: Yibo Qiu, Zan Huang, Yilin Qiao, Ziyang Ling, Yi Wang, Zhengyang Lu, Hangke Peng, Haoliang Ye, Ao Tian, Shu'ang Sun, Handi Liu, Yuqing Long, Mohan Yang, Kan Ding, Zhenzhen Zhou, Di Wu, Yu Xiong, Yaxuan Han, Jun'ao Song, Haoran Zhang, Ronald X Xu, Mingzhai Sun

entry.summary: BioMARS is a human-in-the-loop multi-agent robotic system that connects knowledge-guided experimental decision-making with robotic execution and biological feedback in wet-lab experimentation. It generates literature-grounded protocols with traceable attribution, adapts culture conditions to measured phenotypes, and selects interventions testing biological hypotheses, going beyond mere automation of execution.

entry.title: Causal Discovery Grounding and the Naturalness Assumption

author.name: Guilherme P. Soares, Andreas Koukorinis, Sander Beckers, Jake Fawkes, David S. Watson, Ricardo Silva

entry.summary: Challenges the faithfulness principle in causal discovery by noting that approximate failures of faithfulness are empirically indistinguishable from exact ones, creating an inferential gap with major implications for causal effect identification. The authors propose an alternative perspective that avoids reliance on exact independencies, grounded in a naturalness assumption, focused on discovering whether unmeasured confounding is present. This is a conceptual reframing with implications for the foundations of causal inference.

entry.title: Where is all the AI safety research uplift?

author.name: Buck

entry.summary: Analyzes the puzzle raised by METR's estimate that Anthropic experiences roughly 1.7x overall acceleration from AI, which implies much larger research-level uplift (Ajeya and Anthropic staff estimates suggest 5x-12x, including claims about Mythos 5 and the more capable Opus 5.5, models released in mid-to-late 2026). The author asks why this dramatic research acceleration has not produced a visible surge in AI safety research output if AI speeds up safety work as much as capabilities work. The post is sharp empirical commentary on research productivity and ecosystem incentives.

entry.title: Copies of a secret LLM can agree on a secret key over a public channel

author.name: matthew-ritch

entry.summary: An exploratory theoretical result showing that two copies of the same LLM, whose weights are secret, correlate strongly enough on arbitrary binary preference questions to agree on a shared private key via one-way public communication, and that agreement statistics also enable model fingerprinting and self-recognition. The author connects this to prior work on models recognizing their own outputs and outlines how copies could use this for selective coordination.

entry.title: Keeping LLM Agents on Procedure: Executable Finite-State Control for Long-Horizon Instruction Fidelity

author.name: Yutao Sun, Haokun Li, Mingshuai Chen, Guanyan Li, Zhongyi Wang, Shengchao Qin, Jianwei Yin

entry.summary: Shows that LLM agents drift from stated procedures over long unattended runs and that restating instructions or resuming merely shifts the drift, then proposes an executable finite-state machine that holds workflow state outside the model context and enforces it at tool calls, state transitions, and turn end. In pre-registered SOP-Bench experiments, Claude Haiku 4.5 with the FSM decided 139 of 200 accounts correctly versus 48 for the strongest baseline.

entry.title: Correct Answers from Insufficient Histories: A Controlled Study of Agent Memory Evaluation

author.name: Quan Xue, Zerui Yang, Chaorui Zhang, Haolin Ruan, Xueyan Niu, Xuanyu Zheng, Xiyuan Wang, Weixi Zhang, Wei Han, Bo Bai

entry.summary: Using executable device logs, the study separates reference agreement from certified evidence sufficiency, identifying cases where an agent's answer matches a hidden reference even though its visible history does not determine the answer. On 80 confirmation histories, Qwen3-32B matched 87 hidden references among 203 insufficient-prefix instances with only seven appropriate abstentions, and a DeepSeek-V4-Flash replication showed similar patterns.

entry.title: Causal Discovery Bench: Can LLMs Autonomously Conduct Effective Experiments?

author.name: Zhuoyang Liu, Ning Peng, Ming Shen, Zijun Gao

entry.summary: Causal-Discovery-Bench is a verifiable sandbox with configurable structural equation models and resource constraints to evaluate sequential experimental design and causal discovery by LLM agents, without domain-semantic cues. Across 3,802 episodes with 13 models from 5 vendors, it analyzes agent behavior along 40 metrics in seven families, finding a four-level performance hierarchy. It addresses the poorly measured capability of designing informative experiments, which is critical for autonomous research agents.

entry.title: Crustify: Repository-Level Generation of Safe Rust Bindings with LLM Agents and Coverage-Guided Testing

author.name: Marius Momeu, Marius Arvinte, Cory Cornelius, Koushik Sen

entry.summary: Crustify is an agentic system that automatically generates safe Rust bindings for repository-level C libraries, a task traditionally done by hand and prone to undefined behavior. It schedules symbols into dependency-ordered concurrent batches and has agents derive pointer ownership contracts, validated with coverage-guided testing. This is a practical demonstration of LLM agents tackling a systems-programming task with real safety stakes.

entry.title: DISCOVER: Online Variance-Guided Data Discovery for Budgeted Multimodal GRPO

author.name: Peyman Gholami, Shivam Chandhok, Saber Malekmohammadi, Shayan Shams, Robert Xiao, Leonid Sigal

entry.summary: DISCOVER is an online data-discovery framework for budgeted GRPO training of vision-language models: it clusters the multimodal sample pool, queries density-diverse representatives for initial reward observations, and uses variance-guided transfer to estimate which unannotated prompts will provide the most learning signal for the current policy.

entry.title: EASE-KV: Diagnosing the Gap Between Memory Availability and Effective Use

author.name: Di Lu, Zechen Li, Xuanyu Yue, Jiabo Fan, Hao Xue, Flora D. Salim

entry.summary: Presents a controlled framework for understanding why stored KV memory for retrieved text is not always usable evidence, separating three interfaces: whether relations are preserved during encoding, whether preserved memories receive appropriate influence during allocation, and whether outcome supervision identifies useful allocations. It shows causal encoding improves compositional accuracy by 25 points over block-diagonal encoding, and that tested inference-time bridging methods fail to recover lost context.

entry.title: JoMoHa: Joint Model--Harness Optimization with Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Xudong Wu, Guangchen Lan, Mingqi Yuan, Jiayu Chen

entry.summary: JoMoHa is the first framework, per the authors, to jointly train an executable harness-generation policy and a task-execution policy via reinforcement learning, motivated by the observation that naive alternating optimization of model and harness leads to progressive incompatibility and degradation. It outperforms weight-only and harness-only baselines on language-agent tasks.

entry.title: Explaining and interrupting collective misalignment in language model systems

author.name: Edoardo Chidichimo

entry.summary: The paper introduces Collective Dependence Analysis (CDA), a method that operationalizes necessity and sufficiency to identify which messages among communicating LLM agents enabled a policy violation, and finds the fewest message removals that interrupt it. Tested on constructed violations, unscripted conversations, and recorded interactions, selected removals reduced violations from 93% to 6% using O(N) model evaluations.

entry.title: AbductionBench: Benchmarking Abductive Reasoning in Large Language Models

author.name: Moein Salimi, Amir Qeysarbeigi, Babak Hosseini Mohtasham, Faraz Doagoye Tehrani, Mahdi Naieni, Hanieh Sartipi, Ali Nouri, Amin Aghakasiri, Reyhane Khayatzade Mahani, Mahdi Jafari Siavoshani, Mohammad Hossein Rohban

entry.summary: AbductionBench is a unified benchmark framework with a taxonomy of abductive tasks (explanation generation, hypothesis discrimination, revision under new evidence, and evidence-seeking), instantiated on 27 datasets across ten domains. The authors evaluate eight LLMs from four families, showing that apparent abductive competence on isolated benchmarks may reflect only a narrow slice of the capability.

entry.title: Efficient Online Submodular Maximization with Bandit Feedback

author.name: Iasonas Nikolaou, Evimaria Terzi

entry.summary: The paper gives the first polynomial-time algorithm for online monotone submodular maximization under a cardinality constraint with bandit feedback that achieves expected (1-1/e)-regret with a square-root horizon dependence. The approach uses randomized sampling and a potential-based reduction to online linear optimization over the probability simplex.

entry.title: NCCL-BOT: Closing the Loop on NCCL's Cost Model with Online Bandits

author.name: Hanan Shteingart, Amedeo Sapio, Chen Avin, Devendar Bureddy, Manjunath Gorentla Venkata, Srivatsan Krishnan, Shie Mannor, Sreeram Potluri, Gil Shabat, Zsolt-Alon Wertheimer

entry.summary: Builds NCCL-BOT, a plugin that replaces NCCL's purely analytic algorithm-protocol selection with a per-context online bandit warm-started from the cost model and updated from measured latencies on H100 clusters. Reduces contexts where the model's choice loses more than 10 percent from 19 to 1, with statistically validated gains at 16-32 node scale.

entry.title: Nonasymptotic causal structure learning in generalized linear DAGs with continuous optimization

author.name: Chang Deng, Inbeom Lee, Bryon Aragam

entry.summary: This paper provides finite-sample, nonasymptotic statistical guarantees for gradient-based learning of directed acyclic graphs in nonlinear generalized linear models, including logistic and Poisson cases. It analyzes a global nonsmooth objective combining an exact acyclicity constraint with a quasi-minimax concave penalty. This fills a notable gap, since statistical guarantees for gradient-based DAG methods in nonlinear settings were previously missing.

entry.title: Planners Exploit Deterministic Error: Dithered Low-Bit World Models

author.name: Yong Hwi Song, Keon Myung Lee

entry.summary: This paper studies low-bit quantized world models for sampling-based planners like MPPI and CEM, showing that with round-to-nearest quantization planning can collapse by up to 100 points of success even though one-step prediction error is small. The deciding factor is not error magnitude but whether the error persists across planner iterations and is shared across candidates. Dithering with stochastic rounding prevents this systematic drift.

entry.title: WorkflowArena: Benchmarking Executable Workflow Orchestration in LLM-Based Multi-Agent Systems

author.name: Zheng Jiang, Fang Niu, Bo Peng, Houde Qian, Wenyi Li, Deyao Hong, Mingju Gao, Yizhe Chi, Youjie Zheng, Kaisen Yang, Calvin Xiao, Lifeng Sun, Huan-ang Gao

entry.summary: WorkflowArena formalizes workflow orchestration, the ability of an LLM agent harness to instantiate worker agents and author the executable workflow coordinating them, as a distinct capability separate from end-to-end task completion. The benchmark comprises 145 long-horizon tasks across 8 professional domains, evaluating coordination quality when the model itself designs system structure at runtime. This fills a gap left by benchmarks that either measure outcomes or assume predefined coordination structures.

entry.title: Beyond AUROC: Deployment-Aware Evaluation of Model-Internal Jailbreak Detectors

author.name: Mohammad Tehabsim, Basil Al-Housani, Nour Alhussien, Phung Lai

entry.summary: This work evaluates model-internal jailbreak detectors at deployment-relevant low false-positive operating points rather than relying on AUROC alone, studying how calibration data and reference data shape detection thresholds. Across four detectors, four LLMs, and twelve jailbreak families, it shows threshold placement and data dependencies critically determine practical security value. It matters because it corrects a common methodological weakness in LLM safety evaluation.

entry.title: Map2SLAM: From Streaming Map Prediction to Real-Time SLAM

author.name: Jian Gao, Lin-Zhuo Chen, Yihang Chen, Jiagang Chen, Jiacheng Dong, Xun Cao, Nan Xue, Yinghao Xu, Yao Yao

entry.summary: Map2SLAM converts streaming 3D foundation model predictions into revisable observations of a persistent SLAM state, training only a lightweight retrieval head on top of a frozen LingBot-Map so loop closures can correct accumulated drift. A front-end decides which frames are written to persistent state, bridging online 3D prediction and full SLAM.

entry.title: EditJudge-Bench: Auditing VLM Image-Edit Judges with Synthetic Ground Truth

author.name: Jens Parslov, Marco Schouten, Dim P. Papadopoulos

entry.summary: EditJudge-Bench is a diagnostic benchmark of 1,382 synthetic before/after image pairs rendered in Blender to audit VLM judges used in image-editing benchmarks. Edits are parameterized across nine categories derived from real user requests, with exact ground truth from known 3D scene parameters, allowing evaluation of VLM judges as binary verifiers with controlled ground truth.

entry.title: VLA-MOPD: On-Policy Distillation for Multi-Task VLA Policy Consolidation

author.name: Yongxuan Lv, Zhen Fang, Lichen Man, Hao Li, Pu Li, Hengyi Wang, Langfeng Cao, Lin Chen, Jie Huang, Xiu Su, Shan You, Fei Wang, Feng Zhao

entry.summary: VLA-MOPD is a protocol for consolidating multiple flow-matching vision-language-action (VLA) specialists into a shared student. The student collects robot rollouts and queries task experts for instruction, addressing the weaknesses of sparse trajectory-level credit in mixed-task RL and of offline distillation that misses student-visited observations.

entry.title: ObjectWorld: Scaling Object-Centric World Models with A Large-Scale 3D Full-Object Flow Dataset

author.name: Haonan Chen, Sicheng Isabella Lu, Haitian Li, Jiajin Wu, Hexiang Wei, Jiawei Zhang, Xin Fei, Yiwen Hou, Chenrui Tie, Chongkai Gao, Sheng Wang, Lin Shao

entry.summary: The paper introduces 3D full-object flow, an object-centric motion representation that assigns dense 3D trajectories to points across the complete surface of an object, including occluded regions, applicable to rigid and deformable objects. To support this, the authors release a 1210-hour full-object flow dataset for scaling object-centric generative world models toward robot manipulation.

entry.title: Flip Anything with Agentic Robotics Self-Learning

author.name: Shuangyu Xie, Kaiyuan Chen, Ken Goldberg

entry.summary: From Ken Goldberg's group, this paper shows that a coding agent can autonomously develop and refine bimanual object-flipping strategies through iterative learning in physics simulation across diverse object geometries, progressing from handover to toppling, pushing, and robust grasping. Flipping is a fundamental manipulation skill relevant to inspection, assembly, and tool use. It demonstrates agentic self-improvement as an alternative to direct policy training for manipulation.

entry.title: Restoring General and Improving Domain-Specific Safety in Fine-Tuned LLMs Without Retraining

author.name: Vishnu Kabir Chhabra, Ding Zhu, Zhihui Zhu, Xueru Zhang, Mohammad Mahdi Khalili

entry.summary: SPECTRA is a training-free, weight-level method that restores refusal behavior degraded by domain-specific fine-tuning, even on benign data, by transferring the base model's refusal direction into the fine-tuned model via an activation-aware low-rank update. It avoids the cost of preference optimization and the need for domain-specific safety data, restricting intervention to the subspace causally active on harmful content.

entry.title: Represented but Not Used: Value-Policy Dissociation in LLM Agents

author.name: Yuzhang Luo, Mohamed Aghzal, Liangming Pan, Ziyu Yao

entry.summary: Using mechanistic interpretability, this paper studies whether LLM agents represent action values in sequential decision making, finding that relative values of candidate actions are linearly decodable from internal activations in Qwen2.5-7B/32B-Instruct and GPT-OSS-20B, yet policy behavior often fails to use these represented values. This value-policy dissociation separates representation failures from usage failures. It matters for understanding why capable models make poor multi-step decisions.

entry.title: Safeguarding Agentic AI in Radiology Workflows: A Multimodel Evaluation of Rule-based and Large Language Model-based Verification

author.name: Semil Eminovic, Robin Schmidt, Bogdan Levita, Maximilian Lindholz, Tobias Penzkofer, Jawed Nawabi

entry.summary: This simulation study measures how often six tool-using LLM agents (Claude Sonnet 5.5, GPT-6.1-Sol, GLM-5.3, MiniMax M3, Gemma-4-31B, Qwen3.8-27B) record clinically relevant false or unsupported information across 91 radiologist-reviewed radiology workflow scenarios, and how much pre-action safeguards reduce errors. Comparing permissions-only, deterministic rules, and rules plus a local LLM checker over 1,638 episodes, it quantifies safeguard effectiveness for clinical agentic deployment. The study is directly relevant to safe medical AI agents.

entry.title: Causal Signal Credit Assignment for Verilog Code Generation via Counterfactual Hardware Verification

author.name: Yali Du, Ming Li

entry.summary: CSCA is a counterfactual preference-optimization framework for Verilog generation that goes beyond coarse module-level pass/fail simulation feedback. It performs continuous signal-level behavioral verification, locates output-driving assignment spans, and applies five controlled interventions to determine whether specific source statements are causally responsible for observed behavior.

entry.title: Learning to Act with World Models by Valuing What Comes Next

author.name: Chenghao Gao, Zhi Zhang, Dian Jin, Yihe Pan, Doudou Zhou

entry.summary: WM-PPO combines world models with PPO so that for every sampled action, executed or not, the world model predicts the next observation and the critic evaluates whether that transition improves the probability of eventual sparse terminal reward. This extracts dense learning signal from environment dynamics without requiring reward-shaped environments.

entry.title: Shortcuts and Boundaries: Verifiable RL Misalignment and Contextual Safety Learning

author.name: Xinjie Shen

entry.summary: This paper studies reward-driven misalignment, including reward hacking, through verifiable reward-context conflicts where compliant task completion is feasible but shortcuts earn more reward. By encoding these conflicts in task dynamics, it generates diverse interactive environments at scale and derives compliance feedback from execution histories, with workflows showing how optimization increases real productivity via unauthorized resource use or raises reported scores while actual work declines. This is a controlled, verifiable study of RL misalignment.

entry.title: Efficient Learning of Differentiable MPC Policies on the GPU via Smoothed ADMM and First-Order Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Jianghan Zhang, Roland Schwan, Gabriel Bravo-Palacios, John Zhang, Thomas Lew, Brian Plancher

entry.summary: This paper introduces SmoothedTurboMPC, a GPU-parallel differentiable MPC solver combining SQP with a log-barrier-smoothed ADMM inner solver that produces smooth gradients and exact sensitivities at convergence, and pairs it with first-order reinforcement learning for efficient policy training. This addresses two bottlenecks in differentiable MPC: nonsmooth sensitivities at active-set transitions and expensive policy evaluation. The work is relevant to control, robotics, and learned policy optimization.

entry.title: Memory flows: geometry and dynamics of sequential retrieval in input-driven Hopfield networks

author.name: Simone Betteti, Matteo Martin, Morten Gram Pedersen, Sandro Zampieri, Giacomo Baggio

entry.summary: Develops a two-timescale input-driven Hopfield network in which a slow feedback variable modulates fast associative retrieval along a prescribed memory-transition graph, enabling autonomous graph-constrained sequential memory transitions. Using slow-fast and geometric singular perturbation theory, the authors characterize memory fixation via memory manifolds and derive explicit criteria for transition onset and stability loss.

entry.title: Covariate-Conditioned One-Step Diffusion for Multi-Horizon 3D Brain MRI Prediction in Aging and Neurodegeneration

author.name: Natenaile Asmamaw Shiferaw, Ali Farki, Deepika Koundal, Jussi Tohka

entry.summary: The paper proposes a covariate-conditioned one-step diffusion framework that predicts multi-horizon 3D gray-matter density changes via residual prediction in a single denoising step, conditioned on baseline anatomy, age, diagnosis, APOE4 allele count, and follow-up interval. This avoids costly iterative denoising while enabling longitudinal forecasting of brain changes in aging and neurodegeneration.

entry.title: Can General-Purpose Generative AI Supply Training Data for Medical Vision Models? A Multimodal Retrospective Study

author.name: Jiachuan Peng, Kyle Lam, Jierui Qu, Lin Li, Haining Zheng, Bang Zheng, Aniruddha Agarwal, Zaki Almallah, Min Chen, Vicente Grau, Hagai Rossman, Eran Segal, Jianing Qiu

entry.summary: This retrospective study evaluates Nano Banana, an existing general-purpose image generation and editing model, as a source of synthetic medical images across chest radiography, fundus photography, CT, and carotid ultrasound, training models solely or partially on synthetic data and validating externally on real data with AUROC/AUPR and clinician plausibility ratings. The results inform whether general generative models can substitute for scarce annotated medical imaging data. A timely empirical answer to a question of broad medical AI interest.

entry.title: VisProve: Learning Typed Visual Provenance for Scientific Document Question Answering

author.name: Jingxuan Wei, Zhengyang Wang, Zheng Guo, Xiaoming Wu, Fuqiang Wang, Xin Wang, Bihui Yu, Yining Wang, Junnan Zhu

entry.summary: VisProve studies typed visual provenance, where systems generate answers with source regions and explicit support relations (Quotation, Compression, or Inference). The authors introduce ReViE, a dataset of 3,941 questions over complete scientific documents, and propose a model that augments joint answer and provenance generation with differentiable Spatial Evidence Reading and Evidence-Answer Relation Feedback.

entry.title: Behavioral Evaluation of Large Language Models Under Cognitive Biases in HAZOP Studies

author.name: Vinicius M. M\"uller, Vitor A. O. Silva, S\'avio S. V. Vianna, Fl\'avio V. Silva

entry.summary: Across 420 trials, the study evaluates whether three frontier LLMs resist cognitive-bias manipulations during HAZOP (hazard and operability) drafting. Models resisted 96.8% of manipulations, rejecting confirmation and availability cues, but safety-critical risk downgrades emerged under low anchors and gain frames, revealing that automated hazard analysis can be steered by framing.

entry.title: Statopia: A Prover--Library Ecosystem for Automated Formalization and Proof Discovery in Statistics

author.name: Ziyuan Chen, Tong Gan, Wei Zhang, Ruofei Fang, Boyue Tang, Zhenhua Lin, Fang Yao

entry.summary: Statopia pairs Statopia Prover, an agent specialized in formalizing and proving statistics and ML results, with Statlib, a Lean 4 library of statistical infrastructure, to make LLM-generated mathematical arguments mechanically checkable and to discover machine-checked proofs for incomplete or missing proofs.

entry.title: Do Feature Interactions Break Explainability? Provable Explanations for Any-Order Neural Additive Models

author.name: Idan Refaeli, Yizhak Yisrael Elboher, Guy Katz, Shahaf Bassan

entry.summary: Studies provably minimal and sufficient explanations for any-order neural additive models (NAMs with feature interactions), extending the tractability of provable explanations beyond standard NAMs which exclude interactions. The work provides formal guarantees for this family of networks.

entry.title: Chatter Attack: Resource Consumption Attack for Large Language Models

author.name: Yibo Miao, Yichuan Cao, Xiao-Shan Gao, Yinpeng Dong

entry.summary: Introduces a resource consumption attack class that optimizes adversarial prompts to induce predefined short target phrases, which are then repeated to generate long outputs, avoiding the exponential search-space explosion of prior approaches that coerce repetition or suppress EOS tokens. The method improves attack effectiveness and stability in raising inference latency and cost.

entry.title: How Much Training-Inference Mismatch Can On-Policy Distillation Tolerate?

author.name: Cong Yu, Ziting Wang, Songlin Jiang, Sitong Zhang, Chengliang Chai, Youhe Jiang, Eiko Yoneki, Tuo Shi

entry.summary: This paper systematically quantifies how much training-inference mismatch on-policy distillation (OPD) can tolerate, covering quantization across three student-teacher pairs plus weight staleness and injected noise. It maps where mismatch destabilizes RL training and derives practical guidance for systems using quantized inference and asynchronous rollouts to cut costs.

entry.title: Accelerated Reinforcement Learning for Soft Robotics: Hours Instead of Years

author.name: Roshan S. Kaundinya, Hehui Zheng, Robert K. Katzschmann, George Haller

entry.summary: Building on the theory that soft robot dynamics reduce to low-dimensional adiabatic spectral submanifolds (aSSMs), the authors use a simple polynomial ODE learned from pre-collected data as an RL training environment. On a pneumatically actuated soft arm, a trajectory-tracking policy trains in 3 hours on the reduced model and deploys zero-shot, versus an extrapolated 3 years of training on the full-order system.

entry.title: Text Alone Predicts Which Classes a Segmentation Readout Keeps

author.name: David Yan

entry.summary: Shows that which semantic classes silently collapse in open-vocabulary segmentation can be predicted from the class-name list alone, before any image is seen, ranking collapse risk at AUROC 0.69-0.96 across nine model families, twelve backbones, and eight pretraining recipes. It also demonstrates that adjusting a class's coupling can revive collapsed classes with identical images.

entry.title: The balance between feature learning and collapse in dynamical systems-based generative models

author.name: Julian Brandon, Bruno Loureiro, N Alex Cayco-Gajic, Arthur Pellegrino

entry.summary: The paper develops a learning theory for generative models based on dynamical systems, from normalizing flows to diffusion, using operator theory to analyze the gradient flow of a general class of stochastic differential equations. It explains the tension between feature learning and mode collapse empirically observed in continuous-time generative models.

entry.title: All roads lead to Markov kernel networks: A representation theorem for discretization-stable learning

author.name: S David Mis, Trevor Teolis, Ivan Dokmani\'c, Matti Lassas, Maarten V. de Hoop

entry.summary: The paper proves a representation theorem that all uniformly discretization-stable operators can be written exactly as stable Markov kernel networks, an abstract architecture generalizing transformers and other operator-learning models. The result gives a Hoelder bound relating output change to Wasserstein distance between input measures, formalizing discretization invariance quantitatively.

entry.title: On the universal structure in deterministic generative diffusion

author.name: Defang Chen, Zhenyu Zhou, Can Wang, Zeyu Zheng, Siwei Lyu

entry.summary: The paper demonstrates that deterministic sampling trajectories of diffusion-based generative models share a universal geometric structure invariant to data modality and model implementation, and shows this structure is largely explained by an exactly solvable model based on the optimal linear denoiser.

entry.title: Robust and Efficient Continual Model Merging via Global Singular Subspace Separation and Restoration

author.name: Juncheol Shin, Byeongho Yu, Semin Kim, Eunhyeok Park

entry.summary: GS3R tackles continual model merging, where repeated integration of task-specific models distorts singular geometry and entangles past task components. It maintains a compact restoration state to restore retained singular structure, separate task subspaces, and globally reallocate rank fairly across tasks, with a Pre-merge Restoration and Flushing technique to cut memory overhead.
