entry.summary: The paper recasts causal discovery as Bayesian symbolic regression: given candidate parents for each variable, the method samples closed-form expressions from a posterior and uses each variable's posterior inclusion probability as a causal score. This ensemble-based approach avoids pointwise model selection and works in bivariate and strongly autocorrelated regimes where constraint- and score-based methods fail. It connects mechanistic modeling with causal inference.

entry.title: Evaluating Physically Grounded Procedural Reasoning in VLMs through Real-World Execution: Crochet as a Testbed

author.name: Maximiliano Wardle

entry.summary: This paper proposes crochet as a testbed for physically grounded procedural reasoning in VLMs: patterns cannot be simulated reliably, yet physical verification is cheap and tangible. The author hand-crochets 40 patterns generated by four VLMs in the FoundationChain test, where models must infer from an image how an object was made and produce a matching pattern. Physical execution reveals failure modes invisible to paper-based evaluation, showing that convincing-looking procedures often do not work.

entry.title: Beyond the Transcript: Measuring and Improving the Use of Acoustic Information in Audio Language Models

author.name: Linkai Peng, Baorian Nuchged, Yuyang Yao

entry.summary: The authors show audio language model benchmarks confound acoustic understanding with language ability because many tasks can be answered from the transcript or question alone. They separate lexical from global-attribute and within-recording-structure tasks, evaluate 19 open models plus Gemini 3.1 Pro across 92 tasks from 6 benchmarks, and measure recording gain to isolate genuine acoustic competence.

entry.title: Unlearning at Speed: Rapid Activation Dampening for Efficient Machine Unlearning in Real-World Face Recognition

author.name: Rouqaiah Al-Refai, Leo Scheubel, Philipp Terh\"orst

entry.summary: RAD is a fast, targeted machine unlearning method for large-scale open-set face recognition that approximates activation differences between forget and retain identities and selectively suppresses neurons, addressing the gap between closed-set unlearning research and deployed recognition systems. It is motivated by GDPR-driven data-removal requirements.

entry.title: DASH-SLAM: Calibration-Free Metric Monocular SLAM via Depth Scale Propagation

author.name: Otavio Ribas, Jacopo Panerati, Pierre-Yves Lajoie

entry.summary: DASH-SLAM integrates metric depth predictions from the pretrained Depth Anything 3 model into a shared-keyframe pose graph without task-specific fine-tuning. It derives scale corrections from depth ratios at shared anchor images, accumulates them with damping, and uses these to rescale odometry translations, loop constraints, and map geometry, outperforming state-of-the-art monocular SLAM on TUM, Replica, and 7-Scenes.

entry.title: Explicitly capturing demonstrator multi-modality for distillation into diffusion policies

author.name: Shao Yuan Chew Chia, Rebecca H. Jiang, Abhinav Agarwal, Andreas Hofmann, Leslie Pack Kaelbling, Russ Tedrake

entry.summary: This paper examines how to distill multi-modal demonstrators into diffusion policies that reproduce conditional action distributions, noting that sliding-window BC data can be fit either by a multi-modal policy or by a unimodal policy with high Lipschitz constant. The authors argue that output diversity matters for downstream applications like test-time search and policy improvement, and propose methods to explicitly capture demonstrator multi-modality.

entry.title: D-REAL: Acceptance-Length Optimization with Unbiased Gradients for Speculative Decoding

author.name: Meng Wei, Yefei Chen, Antong Li, Yanan Gao, Xingliang Shi, Xin Gao, Zhiling Ye, Yun Yue, Chunxiao Guo, Peng Wei

entry.summary: D-REAL is a post-training method for speculative decoding drafters that directly optimizes expected acceptance length using a gradient estimator that accounts for prefix survival probabilities and stochastic verification, with an unbiasedness guarantee. It moves beyond token-level objectives that do not align with the actual efficiency metric. It matters because speculative decoding is widely deployed for fast LLM inference.

entry.title: RetinaGuard: Risk-Controlled Agentic Triage for Multi-Disease Retinal Screening

author.name: Sohaib Sulman, Muhammad Atif Saeed, Akhtar Jamil, Alaa Ali Hameed, Roland Aydin

entry.summary: Proposes RetinaGuard, an agentic triage framework for retinal screening where quality, diagnostic, uncertainty, verification, and explanation agents gather evidence, a learned failure predictor estimates decision risk, and acceptance thresholds are certified via conformal risk control. On RFMiD it outperforms confidence and calibrated-uncertainty referral at matched budgets and equal certified safety.

entry.title: Hallucination-Guided Unlearning: Using Hallucination Traces to Reveal Overfitted Memories

author.name: Jiayu Zhang, Ziqi Zhong, Yuliang Gai, Canran Xiao

entry.summary: Proposes HGU, which uses a model's own hallucinations as diagnostic signals for selective unlearning: it localizes unsupported spans via evidence and internal consensus, traces high-responsibility MLP neurons, and edits them with compact gates under a utility-preserving KL constraint. On TOFU it achieves the best MU-FE trade-off with reported Avg scores of 0.7221 and 0.7699 on forget05 and forget10 splits.

entry.title: Lightfoot: Graph Retrieval-Augmented Generation with Exact, Model-Free Document Deletion

author.name: Uday Allu

entry.summary: Lightfoot is a GraphRAG system where every entity, link, fact, and synonym edge is a deterministic function of per-passage extractions with chunk-level provenance, enabling exact document deletion as a pure database operation with no model calls. Retrieval requires no LLM calls, and indexing uses one call per passage. The authors verify on the MuSiQue corpus that after deleting 10% of documents the graph exactly matches a fresh index, and compare against HippoRAG 2.

entry.title: Self-Indexing Latent Memories for Access-Aware Continual Instruction Tuning of LLMs

author.name: Dhruv Dixit, Paritosh Pandey, Snehalkumar 'Neil' S. Gaikwad

entry.summary: TILA-CT is a replay-free continual instruction tuning method that attaches a latent memory and adapter bank per task to a frozen LLM, making each module self-indexing via a persistent routing prototype. On the 8-task CT-Pipeline stream it achieves strong acquisition and final scores with minimal forgetting (about 1.4 points average).

entry.title: ACROSSVAM3.0: Resource-Bounded 4D Scene Construction and Adaptive Surface Association

author.name: Nan Wu, Hong Yee Hung

entry.summary: AcrossVAM3.0 is an offline system combining frozen video generation, dynamic reconstruction, and monocular SLAM components into a versioned point representation, running sequentially on a single GPU with predictable memory use (max 17.14 GB observed). It coordinates map corrections jointly across cameras, points, and trajectories, achieving 4D reconstruction on all 16 test scenes with SLAM maps in 15.

entry.title: OGDA: Ontology-Grounded Data Agents for Reliable Analysis over Heterogeneous Data Lakes

author.name: Boyi Zhang, Hong Ting Tsang, Yisen Gao, Qiao Xiao, LI Yufei, Haoyu Huang, Zhongwei Xie, Jiaxin Bai, Yangqiu Song

entry.summary: OGDA tackles LLM data agents running out of context on large heterogeneous data lakes by constructing a compact ontology through agentic hypothesis testing to constrain exploration and data processing. A proposer-critic style loop induces schemas, concepts, and relations, reducing the exploration overhead and error propagation that plagues task-specific exploration.

entry.title: ECOS: Environment-Calibrated On-Policy Self-Distillation for Language Agents

author.name: Chenhao Zhang, Zhongan Wang, Mingxuan Li, Hehe Fan, Zheng Zhu, Ming Li

entry.summary: ECOS improves on-policy self-distillation for language agents by using environmental outcomes to decide how much to trust a self-teacher's guidance and which self-written skills to reinforce. Command-level advantages, estimated by comparing commands executed at similar observations, scale teacher preferences so that harmful self-written skills do not propagate through later updates.

entry.title: Detecting Shadow AI: Unsanctioned LLM Agents on Enterprise Endpoints: A Taxonomy, an Open Detector and a Controlled Evaluation

author.name: Jeremy Canale, Fabien Soulis

entry.summary: The paper addresses the growing problem of shadow IT amplified by autonomous AI agents, which can create unsanctioned tools, scripts, and MCP servers at near-zero cost and act with user privileges. It proposes a taxonomy of nine agent classes and six endpoint footprint layers, an open detector for Windows endpoints, and a controlled evaluation. This is a timely and practically important contribution to AI governance and security.

entry.title: GMD-Mamba: Lightweight 3D Medical Image Segmentation Using a Grouped Multi-Directional Mamba

author.name: Rahim Ullah, Hasan Abbas, Hazrat Ali, Syed Waqar Nabi

entry.summary: GMD-Mamba reduces the cost of Mamba-based 3D medical image segmentation by grouping input channels and scanning each group in different directions in a single pass, cutting directional-scan complexity from O(K*C^2) to O(C^2/G), and applying Mamba only at the deepest encoder stages. The result is a 19.2M-parameter model achieving best average Dice of 92.0% on BraTS2023.

entry.title: FAIR Universe Weak Lensing ML Uncertainty Challenge: Dataset and Cosmological Inference Competition

author.name: Biwei Dai, Po-Wen Chang, Erwan Allys, Wahid Bhimji, Boris Bolliet, Thomas Borrett, Paolo Calafiura, Ragansu Chakkappai, Yuan-Tang Chou, No\'e Dia, Sascha Diefenbacher, Ibrahim Elsharkawy, Steven Farrell, Sacha Guerrini, Isabelle Guyon, Chris Harris, Shih-Chieh Hsu, Wassim Kablan, Fran\c{c}ois Lanusse, Celia Lecat, Julia Linhart, Yuezhou Ma, Benjamin Nachman, Shubhojit Naskar, Andy Nilipour, Laurence Perreault-Levasseur, S\'ebastien Pierre, Benjamin Remy, David Rousseau, Uro\v{s} Seljak, Haonan Shangguan, Sammy Nasser Sharief, Yuanxu Sun, Andreas Tersenov, Ihsan Ullah, Huikun Weng, Licong Xu, Justine Zeghal, Yulei Zhang, Hang Zhou

entry.summary: This paper presents the FAIR Universe Weak Lensing ML Uncertainty Challenge, a NeurIPS 2025 competition providing a standardized benchmark dataset for machine-learning cosmological inference from weak gravitational lensing. It addresses the lack of benchmarks capturing dataset complexity, simulator imperfections, and systematic biases, with emphasis on uncertainty quantification. The resource aims to accelerate ML methods for precision cosmology.

entry.title: Track or Follow? A Jev-Compatible Multi-Agent Trading System When Web News Lags the Market

author.name: Yebo Feng, Guangyan Gan, Liangrui Pan, Ruichao Liang, Cong Wu, Jiahua Xu, Yang Liu

entry.summary: This paper asks whether LLM agents trading on web news actually predict market moves or merely echo reactions already priced in, since much financial news is published after the move it reports. The authors build a multi-agent trading system with point-in-time data stores and a typed decision model (Jev) with provable position bounds, showing judgments track announcement-window abnormal returns rather than anticipate them. It highlights a subtle look-ahead leakage problem in LLM-based finance applications.

entry.title: Learning a Unified Cross-Model Semantic Dictionary via Gated Bottleneck Sparse Autoencoders

author.name: Jinchi Zhu, Tie Luo

entry.summary: GB-SAE casts unified cross-model interpretability as representation factorization, learning a single shared semantic dictionary usable across multiple foundation models rather than aligning model-specific concept sets post hoc. This enables cross-model feature reuse and unified interpretability. It extends sparse autoencoder research, a central interpretability tool, toward model-agnostic explanations.

entry.title: RTLREX: LLM-Guided Framework for Exact High-Level RTL Recovery

author.name: Wuqian Tang, Fangzhou Liu, Ruijie Wang, TingTing Hwang, Bei Yu, Chun-Yao Wang

entry.summary: RTLREX is an LLM-guided framework that coordinates domain-specific tools to recover exact high-level RTL from gate-level netlists, including function recovery, RTL generation, and independent verification of full input-space equivalence. It addresses the problem of understanding and rewriting hardware designs when original RTL sources are unavailable.

entry.title: System Prompts Affect Response Bias More Than Discriminability in LLM Safety

author.name: Mohan W. Gupta, Sandy Tanwisuth

entry.summary: Using signal detection theory across HarmBench, XSTest, and IHEval with 13 models and eight safety-prompt families at three clarity levels, the authors separate whether system prompts improve discriminability (telling safe from unsafe requests) from whether they merely shift the response criterion (willingness to refuse). They find prompts affect response bias substantially more than discriminability.

entry.title: Viscot-steer: Disentangling and Transferring Visual Chain-of-Thought via Activation Steering

author.name: Ningning Wang (University of Science and Technology of China), Beier Zhu (University of Science and Technology of China), Xingyu Zhu (National University of Singapore), Kaiyun Yang (University of Science and Technology of China), Xun Yang (University of Science and Technology of China)

entry.summary: Viscot-steer is a training-free activation steering framework for transferring visual chain-of-thought capabilities across heterogeneous large vision-language models. It disentangles visual-CoT into grounding and reasoning components rather than treating it as a monolithic capability, avoiding stage-irrelevant interventions during transfer.

entry.title: scBIG++: Learning Across Genes and Cells to Predict Single-Cell Perturbation Responses

author.name: Jiafa Ruan, Zican Qiao, Zongxin Yang, Ruijie Quan, Yi Yang

entry.summary: Presents scBIG++, a full-gene framework for predicting single-cell transcriptional responses to genetic and chemical interventions, moving beyond the usual highly-variable-genes restriction. It models heterogeneous cellular responses by connecting expression-adaptive gene modules with population-conditioned generation, using Gene-Relation Clustering to organize genes into common windows.

entry.title: PROLA: Principal-Orthogonal Low-rank Adaptation for Predictive Spatiotemporal Weather Downscaling

author.name: Minseo Yoon, Minseong Bae, Sojin Lee, Hyunwoo J. Kim

entry.summary: Formulates Predictive Spatiotemporal Weather Downscaling (PSWD), jointly refining spatial and temporal resolution while predicting future high-resolution trajectories, using a shared pretrained backbone, fixed numerical scaffolds, and lightweight residual heads. For backbone adaptation, PROLA decomposes the parameter delta into principal and orthogonal components for targeted low-rank adaptation.

entry.title: Identifiable alignment of unpaired representations

author.name: Stas Syrota, Albert Lopez I Serrano, Johanne Franck, S{\o}ren Hauberg

entry.summary: The paper shows that under the manifold hypothesis, the pullback of the data metric provides a shared distance that makes alignment of unpaired representations identifiable for arbitrary encoders, decoders, architectures, and training setups. It characterizes identifiability via symmetry breaking of the data distribution and proves this holds generically.

entry.title: PRISM: Causal Counterfactual Minimization of Agent Tool Privileges via Information Bottleneck Role Induction

author.name: Yang Luo, Qingni Shen, Tairui Wang, Jiajun Li, Zhonghai Wu

entry.summary: PRISM addresses over-authorization when LLM agents receive full tool privileges through the Model Context Protocol by treating tool necessity as an intervenable causal proposition learned via sandboxed counterfactual interventions. It compresses trajectories into discrete latents via an information bottleneck, picks the number of roles from the rate-distortion knee, and formalizes privilege pruning as a bilevel Stackelberg game sampled by a generative flow network.

entry.title: Towards Trustworthy Mobile Speech Interaction: Ensuring Voice Authenticity and Transmission Integrity

author.name: Guodong Liu, Lei Wang, Dongxu Liu, Qianran Qiao, Haipeng Dai, He Huang, Guihai Chen

entry.summary: MoBiMark is a real-time mobile biometric speech watermarking system that binds ultrasonic articulatory signatures to speech content during capture, emitting a multi-frequency ultrasonic probe on commodity smartphones and extracting echo features to verify a live utterance originates from the genuine speaker. It counters the growing threat of cheap voice cloning to voiceprint authentication.

entry.title: Answer or Defer? Testing VLMs' Stated Confidence on Brain MRI

author.name: Amir Sabbaghziarani, Parsa Ghazvinian, Sepehr Salem, Sergey Plis

entry.summary: The paper tests whether thresholding vision-language models' stated confidence can support safe triage on brain MRI, evaluating eight open-weight VLMs (including two reasoning models) on 3,888 slices from post-treatment glioma patients and healthy volunteers. On BraTS, no confidence threshold yields a nonempty set with at most 5% empirical error for any model, even chosen retrospectively, indicating stated confidence is unreliable for medical deferral decisions.

entry.title: LO-World: Unified BEV Latent Modeling for Joint 4D Occupancy and LiDAR Forecasting

author.name: Zhimin Liao, Ping Wei, Kai Mao, Shuaijia Chen

entry.summary: Proposes LO-World, a unified 4D world model that forecasts LiDAR point clouds and 3D semantic occupancy in a shared BEV latent space, letting dense semantics and metric geometry mutually reinforce each other instead of running independent pipelines. It uses a hybrid range-voxel representation for efficiency.

entry.title: TS-GEAR: Taobao Shangou GEnerative Ad Retrieval

author.name: Guofeng Tong, Xu Zhang, Guangliang Yu, Haiqiang Wang, Guannan Cong, Xing Guo, Yang Zhou, Jingjing Duan, Shuang Li, Feng Shi, Hualei Liu

entry.summary: Taobao presents TS-GEAR, a generative retrieval system for instant-delivery advertising that encodes delivery-range reachability directly into semantic IDs rather than relying on post-generation truncation. It conditions user-interest aggregation on geography and the current query and addresses the retrieval-candidate validity constraint unique to on-demand delivery platforms.

entry.title: Selected-Risk Calibration for Feasibility at Returned Decisions

author.name: Raghav Thind, Youran Sun, Ling Liang, Haizhao Yang

entry.summary: The paper proposes Selected-Risk Calibration (SRC), a framework providing distribution-free guarantees that decisions returned by an optimizer satisfy a learned surrogate constraint, with certified upper bounds on infeasibility probability. It also proves that split conformal prediction coverage and likelihood-ratio reweighting do not bound this selected risk, motivating the new framework.

entry.title: Bias, Measurement Error, and Double-Dipping: When Can GNN Convolutions Help Brain Connectome Prediction?

author.name: Tommaso Castellani, Jiaqi Li, Muriah D. Wheelock, Rezwana Rosen Razzaque, Helmut Laufs, Hong Chen, Claire Donnat

entry.summary: The paper explains why GNNs often fail to outperform graph-agnostic baselines on fMRI connectome prediction by formulating the task as an errors-in-variables problem where the observed covariance is a noisy estimate of the latent connectome. It decomposes graph convolution effects into smoothing-induced bias and variance reduction, graph estimation error, and a double-dipping effect.

entry.title: A Geometric Theory for Nonequilibrium Transformer Dynamics

author.name: Aythami Bethencourt de Le\'{o}n, Darryl D. Holm

entry.summary: The authors develop a variational, statistical-physics-based geometric theory of transformer attention dynamics at fixed parameters, modeling attention weight evolution as Fisher-Rao gradient flow of a free energy. They prove the softmax matrix is the unique free-energy minimizer, show all positive attention trajectories converge to it, and derive convergence and tracking guarantees for time-varying token representations.

entry.title: AERO: Adaptive Ensemble-Disagreement Routing for Oracle Feedback in Sample-Efficient Online RLHF

author.name: Shrey Singhal, Nannan Huang, Haytham M. Fayek

entry.summary: AERO is a fully online RLHF algorithm built on a Dyna-style model-based RL architecture that uses ensemble disagreement to decide when synthetic reward labels are reliable enough and when to spend budget on real oracle (human) feedback. It targets the dominant bottleneck of preference-label acquisition cost in LLM alignment. The approach improves sample efficiency over uniform querying of the oracle.

entry.title: Elastic Representations via Hyperbolic Geometry

author.name: Arjun Ramesh Kaushik, Rudrasis Chakraborty, Nalini Ratha, Venu Govindaraju

entry.summary: The paper introduces HERL, a framework for dimension-adaptive embeddings using hyperbolic geometry that supports both compression and post hoc expansion, unlike Matryoshka Representation Learning which requires full retraining. It addresses limitations of prior elastic-representation approaches, offering flexible sizing under varying downstream resource constraints.

entry.title: How Efficient Is Your Agent? Online Predictive Bounds under Budget Constraints

author.name: Roy Maor Lotan, Shai Feldman, Yaniv Romano

entry.summary: PROBE is a method for constructing calibrated upper predictive bounds on an AI agent's time-to-success while tasks arrive online and a limited budget forces early stopping of some runs. Using inverse-propensity-weighted calibration and adaptive budget allocation, it maintains valid coverage despite right-censored outcomes. This addresses a practical and underexplored question of statistically rigorous agent evaluation under compute budgets.

entry.title: Are UFOs Real? Introducing Unified Factored Organizers

author.name: Thomas X. Sheppard, Alon Albalak, Joel Lehman, Kenneth O. Stanley

entry.summary: Building on recent claims that gradient-descent-trained networks learn fractured entangled representations while open-ended evolutionary processes can learn unified factored representations, this paper introduces Unified Factored Organizers. UFOs are a training-free or lightweight mechanism that reorganizes a trained network's representations into a unified factored form, addressing the critique of low loss not implying good representation.

entry.title: HyPLM Technical Report

author.name: Haowei Lin, Cai Zhou, Xiangxin Zhou

entry.summary: HyPLM-Flash is an open 650-million-parameter masked protein language model trained on 726 billion tokens with an efficient inference engine (fused kernels, INT8), embedding about 130,000 residues per second on a single NVIDIA H20 GPU, 1.9 to 2.7 times faster than other 600M-class encoders. It is trained on less data than ESM-2 650M and ESM C 600M and evaluated against 28 public checkpoints on 32 tasks.

entry.title: One-Shot Federated Graph Learning via High-Fidelity Proxies and Transferability-Guided Collaboration

author.name: Jia Jiang, Zihan Tan, Wenke Huang, Bin Yang, Mang Ye

entry.summary: This work targets one-shot federated graph learning (OFGL), where all collaboration must be compressed into a single transmission round, and identifies a fundamental Single-Transmission Bottleneck. The authors show that existing proxy distillation causes a fidelity crisis, distorting local graph topology and semantics so that externalized knowledge is underexpressed, and that server aggregation of proxies has further weaknesses. Their solution combines high-fidelity proxies with transferability-guided collaboration to improve knowledge quality under strict bandwidth constraints.

entry.title: Can the Confidence and Decisions of System 1 Models Be Trusted? An Explainability and Perturbation Audit of Jev-Style Decision Models

author.name: Julien Delaunay

entry.summary: This paper introduces an open, deterministic audit benchmark for System 1 decision models (single-pass models returning typed probability distributions over declared schemas), evaluating calibration under label-preserving perturbations, cross-question interference, and post-hoc attribution faithfulness. It audits five open-weight models (0.8B to 27B) against generative System 2 baselines across NLI and other tasks.

entry.title: Mitigating Agentic Deception via Evaluation-Side Partially Observable Games

author.name: Hanxiao Li, Shutong Liu, Yongjia Ma, Jiaming Ji, Juntao Dai, Shuning Zhang, Kejian Shi, Kai Chen, Pu Feng, Yuqing Ma, Qi Dou, Yaodong Yang, Xianglong Liu, Simin Li

entry.summary: The paper attributes LLM agent deception to evaluation-side partial observability, where evaluation checks only final outcomes and not the faithfulness of reasoning, tool use, and environmental effects. It formalizes deception mitigation as an Evaluation-Side Partially Observable Extensive Form Game (e-PoG), a max-min framework in which an evaluator queries the agent to elicit honest behavior. The approach aims to generalize beyond one-shot monitoring that stronger deceivers can evade.

entry.title: Statistical Geometry of Group Actions: Symmetry, Transport, Estimation

author.name: Quentin Berthet, Peter Bartlett, Romuald Elie, Yu-Han Wu

entry.summary: This theoretical work analyzes variational inference under distributional symmetry, examining how a symmetry action on a sample space interacts with a transport action generating a parametric variational family via pushforward. It proves that symmetry constrains the Riemannian gradient of the KL divergence to the trivial representation, forcing it to vanish along non-trivial directions at the true transport parameter.

entry.title: LEGIT: Live Eligibility Gating over Identifier Tries for Constrained Decoding of Heterogeneous Pages

author.name: Felix Fang, Zheng Liu, Robert Saliba

entry.summary: LEGIT is a constrained decoding method for generative recommenders that write whole results pages (stores with menu items) in one pass, enforcing per-request eligibility and repetition constraints via live gating over identifier tries. It addresses rules that change with every request and token, which grammar-constrained decoding could not enforce exactly, and is deployed in the Uber Eats search engine.

entry.title: On the Geometric Bottlenecks of Cross-Lingual Knowledge Editing

author.name: Aastha A K Verma, Anwoy Chatterjee, Sparsh Jain, Tanmoy Chakraborty

entry.summary: This work investigates why model editing applied in one language often fails to propagate to semantically equivalent facts in other languages, challenging the interlingua assumption in multilingual language models. The authors perform a geometric dissection of cross-lingual representations and show that representational anisotropy creates a structural bottleneck for source-only associative-memory editing. The analysis reframes cross-lingual editing degradation as structural rather than merely algorithmic.

entry.title: MoTo: Mixture of Tokenizers Towards Fair Multilingual Language Modeling

author.name: G\"ul Sena Alt{\i}nta\c{s}, Colin Raffel

entry.summary: MoTo is a modular tokenization framework that trains dedicated per-language BPE tokenizers and composes them into a unified superset vocabulary with deduplicated shared tokens. Each language keeps its own normalization policy, pre-tokenization rules, and vocabulary budget, addressing the under-service of morphologically rich and non-Latin-script languages by English-dominant tokenizers. Despite allocating smaller budgets per language, the approach reportedly improves representation quality for underserved languages.

entry.title: CVaR Deep Optimal Stopping

author.name: Yechan Jeong, Youngjoon Hong

entry.summary: Develops a theoretical framework and deep-learning algorithm for risk-sensitive optimal stopping using Conditional Value at Risk, addressing pathologies of naive risk-sensitive RL via three structural properties of optimal stopping problems. Targets applications like option exercise, sequential medical treatment, and safety-critical control.

entry.title: Semantically Aligned KV Cache Compression for Efficient Agentic Autoregressive Video Generation

author.name: Weizhong Huang, Huaijia Kou, Tianyu Xie, Xiawu Zheng, Liujuan Cao

entry.summary: Proposes SemanticKV, a training-free KV cache compression method for agentic autoregressive video generation that uses planner-extracted semantic constraints to decide which cached visual states to retain across rollouts. Claimed as the first such method to explicitly align cache retention with the planner's semantic requirements.

entry.title: ChemInsight: A Comprehensive Benchmark for Evaluating and Diagnosing Chemistry Understanding and Reasoning in Large Language Models

author.name: Changyu Hu, Yiming Zou, Xin Tang, Yiru Pan, Zicheng Huang, Deng Zhao, Qing Cui, Zhenduo Zhang, Wang Ren, Xiao Li

entry.summary: This paper introduces ChemInsight, a benchmark of 203 challenging chemistry questions in 50 bundles with a two-dimensional scope-and-depth scoring system for LLM evaluation. Ten representative LLMs perform poorly, with scope scores below 30 percent and depth below 11 percent, far below human experts. The paper then diagnoses what factors limit current LLMs on chemistry reasoning.

entry.title: Prune, Don't Merge: Expert Compression of Mixture-of-Experts LLMs on Multilingual Production Tasks

author.name: Tomas Rasymas, Povilas Kvedaras

entry.summary: This work compares the two leading one-shot expert compression methods, REAP (pruning) and REAM (merging), on five multilingual production tasks at a web-hosting company, using 30B-parameter MoE models including Qwen3-30B-A3B-Instruct-2507 and Nemotron-3.5-Lightning at 25% and 50% compression. Prior evaluations covered only academic benchmarks, and this real-world evaluation supports pruning over merging. It provides rare industrial validation of MoE compression.

entry.title: Hidden Tails: Certifying Tail-Risk Claims under Selective Labels

author.name: El Mustapha Mansouri

entry.summary: The paper addresses selective labels problems where historical decisions hide the worst outcomes of a predictor, deriving sharp bounds on conditional value-at-risk for binary outcomes with bounded losses. It provides statistical certificates that cover tail-risk ranges simultaneously across candidate predictors, given a stated limit on outcome-odds differences between observed and hidden cases. This enables defensible risk limits and model comparisons even when extreme errors are unobservable.

entry.title: I play of the cello: Evaluating Constructional Bleeding in Multilingual LLMs with CALQUE

author.name: Toshiki Nakai, Yu-Yin Hsu, Marie-Catherine de Marneffe, Joakim Nivre, Jakob Prange, Nathan Schneider, Wesley Scivetti, Tiago Timponi Torrent, Leonie Weissweiler

entry.summary: The paper introduces CALQUE, a dataset of 5583 sentence pairs across seven languages designed to detect constructional bleeding, where LLMs overgeneralize English morphosyntactic strategies into other languages. By comparing literal translations in both directions, the authors quantify how cross-lingual generalization introduces calques that native speakers would not produce. This provides a new lens on how English-dominant training data distorts multilingual model behavior.

entry.title: MNN-Pocket-0.3B Technical Report

author.name: MNN Team

entry.summary: MNN-Pocket-0.3B is a 300M-parameter dense language model designed for on-device deployment with 32K-token context, achieving a 173 MB INT4 footprint and up to 466 tokens/s decoding on iPad Pro M5 via Metal. The work emphasizes co-design across architecture, data, training pipeline, and inference, including hardware-aware architecture selection and dependency-aware vocabulary pruning, trained on roughly 4.1 trillion tokens across four stages. It demonstrates that capable sub-1B models can run efficiently on smartphones and smart glasses.

entry.title: How Well Does AI Peer Review Work? A Benchmark Built from 100 Planted Errors

author.name: Paul Litvak

entry.summary: The author planted 100 known errors into 10 open-access psychology papers and ran the modified papers through frontier LLMs and two commercial AI review tools. The best single system caught 71 of 100 errors and the worst caught 30, while pooling all systems caught 93; systems were only weakly correlated, making ensembles a key lever. Notably, all seven errors missed by every system were omissions, i.e., deleted information rather than inserted mistakes.

entry.title: STAIRS: Staging the Inverse Problem via Admissible-Support Scheduling for Unrolled MRI Reconstruction

author.name: Xiangjian Hou, Chang Ni, Chao Qin, Zhiwei Tan, Xin Wang, Xinrui Ye, Rong-Rong Chen, Chun Yuan, Xiaodong Ma

entry.summary: Proposes STAIRS, a method for accelerated MRI reconstruction that projects intermediate unrolled-network reconstructions onto nested Fourier supports that gradually expand to the full spectrum, conditioning each update on the support transition. It uses a normalized spectral coordinate derived from a regularized log-determinant score of training covariance to account for dependencies between newly and previously admitted frequencies.

entry.title: ESTRA: Enabling Extreme Attention Sparsity for Training-Free Video Diffusion Acceleration

author.name: Enhuai Liu, Yunke Wang, Yutong Wang, Changming Sun

entry.summary: ESTRA is a training-free method to accelerate video diffusion transformers by concentrating exact attention on a small set of important key-value tokens and approximating the rest with cluster representatives, preserving quality at sparsity levels where prior training-free methods degrade. This directly targets the high cost of attention over long spatiotemporal sequences.

entry.title: PLS-GS: Probabilistic Lidar Scaffolds for Compact, Surface-Aligned Gaussian Splatting

author.name: Krishnan Harikumar, Alejandro Fontan, Thierry Peynot, Emili Hern\'andez, Niko S\"underhauf

entry.summary: PLS-GS uses a probabilistic hierarchical Gaussian mixture model fit jointly over LiDAR position and color as an adaptive scaffold to guide compact, surface-aligned 3D Gaussian Splatting in robotics settings with both camera and LiDAR data. This avoids discrete voxel/octree partitioning and improves geometric alignment.

entry.title: Beyond Real or Fake: A Dual-Channel Authenticity and Reasoning Protocol for Photographic Assessment

author.name: Xiaoxiao Li, Ruinan Jin, Lili Meng, Miaosen Wang, Athula Balachandran, Pei Cao

entry.summary: The paper argues that binary real-vs-fake image forensics conflates distinct manipulation types, and proposes decomposing GenAI manipulations into a camera channel (sensor fingerprints) and a semantic channel (scene coherence). It instantiates this as 2CAP, pairing a contrastively-trained camera encoder with a frozen semantic encoder to support four-class authenticity classification via cross-attention fusion. This reframing matters as synthetic and AI-edited imagery proliferates.

entry.title: Not All Layers Are Equal in Image-to-Video Transfer

author.name: Thinesh Thiyakesan Ponbagavathi, Constantin Seibold, Alina Roitberg

entry.summary: A layer-wise sensitivity analysis across four video model families shows that temporal sensitivity grows with depth and that the growth profile depends on pretraining paradigm, contradicting the uniform adapter placement used in parameter-efficient image-to-video transfer. The authors derive STRAP, a training-free rule for placing adapters based on a spatial-to-temporal transition boundary.

entry.title: AgentCT: A Vision-Language Agent for Universal CT Imaging

author.name: Zhihao Chen, Qi Gao, Chuang Niu, Qiegen Liu, Yi Zhang, Hongming Shan

entry.summary: AgentCT is a vision-language agent using a LoRA-adapted Qwen3-VL-4B controller that identifies CT degradation type and severity, routes images to specialist restoration models (diffusion-based LDCT, projection-domain SVCT/MAR pipelines), and reassesses outputs. This unifies low-dose, sparse-view, and metal-artifact restoration under one routing framework.

entry.title: QCC-WM: Linking Macro-State Dynamics and Visual Generation via Quotient Causal Construction

author.name: Zhizhong Fu, Wei Zhou, Zhaoyang Jiang, Yudong Lin, Songlun Li, Zhi Li, Feifan Chen, Gaoming Li, Xiaorong Ding, Yifan Chen

entry.summary: QCC-WM is a visual world model that constructs macro-states from high-dimensional observations to support recursive action-conditioned prediction, with action responses guiding macro-variable construction. A shared reference quotient measurement constrains consistency between predicted macro-states and observed visual changes, allowing structured macro-level predictions to constrain future visual generation.

entry.title: Click3R: Interactive Stereo 3D Reconstruction with Sparse Correspondence Clicks

author.name: Hao Gu, Jin Yao, Zezhou Cheng

entry.summary: Click3R introduces interactive geometric correction of feed-forward 3D reconstruction models using sparse user-provided cross-view correspondence clicks, injected via a lightweight point correspondence adapter. This enables correction of failures from repetitive textures, symmetric structures, large viewpoint changes, and textureless regions.

entry.title: DPGS-SLAM: Diffusion-Prior and Provenance-Aware Monocular Gaussian Splatting SLAM for Dynamic Visual Sensing

author.name: Yifan Luo, Takafumi Matsumaru, Vibekananda Dutta, Xin He

entry.summary: DPGS-SLAM is a monocular RGB SLAM framework combining 3D Gaussian splatting with diffusion priors to handle dynamic environments. It maintains provisional representations of dynamic objects and uses provenance-aware tracking to avoid contamination of camera tracking and mapping, while filling occluded static background regions.

entry.title: ReSkill: Selective Self-Improvement for Robot Manipulation

author.name: Zheng Sun, Zhihao Li, Zhuo Li, Wenrui Liu, Xin Wang, Fei Chen

entry.summary: ReSkill uses a coding agent to build an object-centric task graph from an instruction and a skill library, then uses node-level execution records to locate failures and decide what to revise at the task and skill levels. Candidate revisions undergo full-task evaluation and paired comparison before adoption, enabling validated local changes to accumulate.

entry.title: BAT-WAM: Bridging Action and Touch in World-Action Models for Dexterous Hands

author.name: Dong Fang, Feixuan Huang, Yuanxin Zhong, Yuxiang Gao, Qi Song, Yunlong Wang, Xiaosong Jia, Yu-Gang Jiang

entry.summary: BAT-WAM bridges visual, joint-state, and tactile representations for world-action models in dexterous manipulation, using separate codebooks and decoders for tactile and action streams connected by an RGB-conditioned continuous latent bridge. This enables bidirectional learning and recovery of missing tactile and joint-state information from RGB.

entry.title: MOSU2: Long-range Navigation System with Multi-modal Scene Understanding

author.name: Jing Liang, Zhenyu Hou, Senthurbavan Kirubaharan, Md Safwan Mondal, Ashok Gudivada, Xuesu Xiao, Dinesh Manocha

entry.summary: MOSU2 is a long-range outdoor navigation system that addresses how robots should decide to proceed, yield, or detour around pedestrians, cyclists, and vehicles, decisions that depend on how scenes evolve. It uses VLM-based scene understanding but avoids the cost of querying heavy models at every step through a multi-modal, selective-reasoning design. This is relevant to deployable social navigation in real public spaces.

entry.title: GAP: Generalized Adaptation Prior for Dexterous Piano Playing

author.name: Jinyi Chen, Hongyi Li, Lei Jiang, Xianwei Liu, Yanhong Liang, Yulin Chen, Yucheng Tao, Yongbin Jin, Hongtao Wang

entry.summary: GAP is a sample-efficient sim-to-real adaptation framework for dexterous manipulation that learns how to adapt rather than how to act during simulation pretraining, then transfers this adaptation prior to hardware. A gradient guidance network learns from paired executions how action adjustments affect performance, using piano playing as a precise multifinger testbed.

entry.title: LoRazor: Trimming Adapter Execution for Efficient Multi-LoRA Serving

author.name: Xiang Li, Pengcheng Wang, Azam Ikram, Saurabh Bagchi

entry.summary: LoRazor addresses overhead in multi-LoRA serving by showing that adapters are unnecessary at every decoding step, so they can be released early with limited accuracy loss. Because translating that workload reduction into throughput gains requires tailored GPU kernels, the authors build a full system including custom kernels for efficient multi-adapter inference.

entry.title: Sampling Is Not Curiosity: Why LLM Agents Should Investigate

author.name: Alfonso Amayuelas, Piotr Pi\k{e}kos, Xin Eric Wang, William Yang Wang, J\"urgen Schmidhuber, Alex Pentland

entry.summary: This position-style paper argues that current LLM agents explore stochastically rather than curiously: sampling mechanisms like temperature, best-of-N, tree search, and RAG vary conditioning but never update the agent's predictive model of the environment, unlike curiosity in the RL literature. It calls for agents that genuinely investigate by building predictive structure. It matters as a conceptual critique guiding open-ended agent research.

entry.title: LiveAsset: Learning Intent Assets from Corrective Interactions for Agent Runtime Control

author.name: Guanming Liu, Weihang Wang, Peng Zhang, Meng Wu, Kainan Tu, Jiahao Liu, Yu Zhang, Liuxin Zhang, Qianying Wang, Ning Gu, Tun Lu

entry.summary: LiveAsset is an intent harness that learns reusable intent assets from users' corrective interactions with LLM agents, interpreting each correction against the agent's preceding and revised outcomes without requiring users to specify desired results. These context-bound intent assets are then used for runtime control of agent execution across web applications and services. The work addresses how multi-turn corrections can be accumulated into durable, enforceable user intent.

entry.title: When Should AI Overturn a Human Decision? Controversy at the 2026 World Cup and a $\sqrt{2/\pi}$ Solution

author.name: Amir Ali Ahmadi, Parsa Alavi, Radeen Alavi

entry.summary: The paper derives a maximum-likelihood rule for when a referee's binary call should be overturned by a conflicting AI measurement (VAR offside), assuming independent Gaussian errors for human perception and AI measurement. Under known standard deviations, the reversal threshold takes the closed form sqrt(2/pi) * sigma_AI^2 / sigma_H.

entry.title: Benchmarking language models and agents for scientific reasoning in evolving materials laboratories

author.name: Xuyu Dong, Yixuan Li, Jianguo Huang, Feng Chen, Yiyun Zhou, Bo An, Zheng Liu, Da Shu

entry.summary: MatScope benchmarks language models and multi-agent systems on materials-science reasoning, testing whether they can distinguish closely related material states and reason with quantitative evidence as experimental evidence accumulates. It evaluates three connected capabilities spanning unaided prediction and condition-sensitive reasoning in evolving laboratory contexts.

entry.title: SciMARS: Multi-Agent Recursive Self-Improvement for Closed-Loop Scientific Discovery

author.name: Weimin Wu, Han Liu

entry.summary: SciMARS proposes recursive task-local adaptation of multi-agent harnesses for closed-loop scientific discovery, addressing shared memory loss and fixed role procedures that perpetuate mistakes. It introduces a shared evidence graph and separate component editors, including an editor for memory policies, with candidate probes guiding composition and selection of the next harness. This contributes to the emerging area of self-improving AI agents for science.

entry.title: MotionGraphicsBench: Evaluating Motion Graphics Generation with Programmatic Verification

author.name: Jiaju Ma, Ashvini Kumar Jindal, Chuhua Wang, Sumithra Bhakthavatsalam

entry.summary: MotionGraphicsBench is an expert-curated benchmark of 100 instances for animating static SVG designs with motion edit prompts, derived from real-world Lottie motion designs. Each instance pairs the model input with a deterministic, human-readable verification program, enabling objective evaluation of spatial, appearance, and temporal requirements in motion graphics generation.

entry.title: Anatomy-Activated Mixture-of-Experts for 3D Medical Vision-Language Pre-training

author.name: Szymon P{\l}otka, Gizem Mert, Pedro R. A. S. Bassi, Wenxuan Li, Zongwei Zhou, Anna Marcinkiewicz, Wiktoria Roma\'nczyk, Jaros{\l}aw B. \'Cwik{\l}a, {\L}ukasz Struski, Ewa Szczurek, Jacek Tabor, Arkadiusz Sitek

entry.summary: A2MoE introduces anatomical inductive biases into medical vision-language pre-training via a Histogram Representation Router that conditions expert routing on the organ composition of the scan or crop, moving beyond anatomy-agnostic uniform encoders. The MoE design aims to bring organ-specific context into 3D volumetric representation learning from radiology reports.

entry.title: Do Benign-Trained Hidden-State Probes Detect Tool Errors Under Adversarial Conditions?

author.name: Bibek Bhandari, Kshitij Lingthep

entry.summary: The study tests whether hidden-state probes trained only on benign tool-use trajectories remain useful for detecting incorrect tool actions under adversarial conditions, using four AgentDojo suites, four conditions (benign, prompt injection, system override, tool poisoning), and three models including Qwen2.5 variants and GLM-4.6V-Flash, with task-grouped out-of-fold evaluation.

entry.title: MCSA: Multi-Cutoff Spectral Aggregation in SO(3) Equivariant GNNs for Interatomic Potentials

author.name: Junfu Tan, Mengfan Wu, Yu Zhu, Yu Shi, Yifang Qin, Chang Liu, Bonan Zhu, Ziheng Lu

entry.summary: Analyzes the radial spectral properties of SO(3)-equivariant message passing and shows that the cutoff radius controls the characteristic spatial-frequency scale of radial interactions. Based on this, it proposes Multi-Cutoff Spectral Aggregation (MCSA), a plug-and-play module that aggregates radial kernels with different cutoff radii for multi-scale geometric representations in machine learning interatomic potentials.

entry.title: Direct GPU Energy Measurements of Batch-Level Sharing in Mixture-of-Experts and Recurrent Models

author.name: Rafael Pina, Varuna De Silva

entry.summary: This paper reports direct GPU energy measurements rather than operation-count estimates for batch-level computation sharing in two settings: recurrent policies in GPU-vectorized MARL and MoE language models. For recurrent policies, sharing rarely persists and trained masks only help because they collapse to narrow GRUs at 11x the energy of a small dense policy; the MoE side is examined for analogous sharing savings.

entry.title: RecoGEM: A Serving System for Production-Scale Generative Recommendation

author.name: Xiangrui Yang, Yunfeng Zhao, Jiawei Yang, Fangyu Zhang, Enrui Zhao, Liang Zeng, Cheng Peng, Minhui Xie, Jiaqiang Liu, Xiao Liang, Yiming Qiu

entry.summary: RecoGEM is a production serving system for generative recommenders that autoregressively generate item identifiers, using a runtime-engine decoupling architecture to handle the dependent decoding steps and huge item spaces on the latency-critical path. It fills an architectural gap since neither classic RecSys pipelines nor LLM serving stacks fit GR workloads.

entry.title: WanderBench: Can World Models Explore Dynamic Worlds from Video?

author.name: Yuhang Chen, Jiheng Li, Jiale Wang, Zai Wang, Guangyue Liu

entry.summary: WanderBench is a benchmark of 745 single-shot source videos of real and synthetic dynamic scenes for evaluating video-conditioned world models on faithful exploration of recorded worlds. Unlike image- or text-conditioned benchmarks, it tests whether rollouts preserve subject identity, event progression, and scene consistency upon revisiting locations, capabilities needed for re-shooting footage and real-to-sim embodied environments. This fills a clear evaluation gap as video world models mature.

entry.title: HiVe-Mem: Interleaving Horizontal Memory Expansion and Vertical Evidence Composition for Multimodal Agents

author.name: Haozhen Zhang, Bohan Liu, Jianzhu Bao, Qingyuan Liu, Haodong Yue, Xiao Li, Zi Pong Lim, Wenya Wang

entry.summary: HiVe-Mem is a memory framework for multimodal agents that organizes interaction episodes into a relational graph anchored by text and visuals, expanding semantically retrieved seeds and composing heterogeneous evidence per query. It addresses the failure of flat semantic retrieval over compressed memories in long-horizon multimodal interaction.

entry.title: Projected Neural Additive Models as Universal Approximators

author.name: Nhon N. Phan, Qiang Du, John D. Clayton, WaiChing Sun

entry.summary: The paper establishes the first theoretical foundation for projected neural additive models (PNAMs), which add a learnable linear projection to NAMs to capture cross-variable interactions while retaining interpretability. It proves PNAMs are universal approximators, characterizes the minimum projections needed for exact polynomial representation, and derives approximation rates, overcoming NAMs' inability to model even simple interaction terms.

entry.title: Implicit Bias in State Space Models and Linear Autoregressive Training

author.name: Gal Katzhendler, Gilad Yehudai, Gal Vardi

entry.summary: The paper analyzes gradient descent on linear SSMs and autoregressive models, where shared parameters induce sample-dependent effective predictors, showing convergence in direction to a KKT point of an effective-degree max-margin problem. Only examples with minimal effective degree matter for the implicit bias, extending implicit-bias theory to weight-tied sequence models.

entry.title: How Much Is Left Matters: False Positives and False Negatives in Partial-Prompt Contamination Tests

author.name: Abhishek Anand

entry.summary: The paper audits partial-prompt completion tests for benchmark contamination across seven open-weight models on MATH-500 and AIME 2025/2026 problems, showing that memorization flags depend strongly on how many words remain after the prefix. Short leftovers drive most ROUGE-based flags, and common thresholds produce substantial false positives on true negatives.

entry.title: Discrete Diffusion Playground: A 2D Benchmark for Discrete Generative Models

author.name: Justin Shao, Sihyun Park, David Ryan Koes, Maria Chikina

entry.summary: The Discrete Diffusion Playground converts known 2D continuous distributions into binary token sequences via an exact discretized bijection, enabling direct comparison of generated samples against ground-truth distributions. The benchmark spans smooth mixtures and structures with sharp boundaries, disconnected support, and coordinate-dependent structure, exposing failures that standard discrete-diffusion evaluation protocols miss.

entry.title: A Hierarchical Tokenization Framework for Voxel-Level fMRI Representation Learning

author.name: Karanpartap Singh, Yue Zhao, Mohammad H. Abbasi, Ehsan Adeli

entry.summary: HBAR organizes voxel-level resting-state fMRI into a hierarchy spanning sub-parcel voxel groups, parcels, and large-scale functional networks, achieving up to 415x compression while preserving fine-grained spatial information. It supports fixed, learned, and prior-guided hierarchies, outperforming rate-matched flat tokenization on parcel and network correlations on HCP-YA.

entry.title: CRAFT-GBM: Selecting Best Features for Gradient-Boosted Machine Learning

author.name: Basil Kuok, Yi Zhou, Yao Xuan, Shuping Li, Ke-Wei Huang

entry.summary: CRAFT-GBM is a LightGBM extension that adaptively selects which features are searched at each boosting round by using split-gain evidence accumulated during training, rather than fixing feature counts in advance. It transforms root-split gains into bounded observations with time-uniform confidence bounds valid under adaptive, non-stationary training histories, letting the feature-set size emerge endogenously.

entry.title: Beyond Flat Walks: Compositional Abstraction for Autoregressive Graph Generation

author.name: Kaiwen Bian, Andrew H. Yang, Yusu Wang, Ali Parviz, Gal Mishne

entry.summary: The paper addresses a limitation of autoregressive graph generators that linearize graphs via flat node-edge walks, which obscure higher-order structure in large graphs. It introduces a hierarchical graph abstraction and coarse-to-fine generation pipeline that separates coarsening, tokenization, and decoding, exposing three design axes: community coarsening, hierarchical tokenization, and order randomization. The authors find that traversal-based hierarchy consistently improves distributional and structural fidelity, and that randomizing traversal order across communities substantially reduces the fidelity-V.U.N. cost trade-off.

entry.title: Odds-Structured Distributional Regression for Interpretable Time-to-Event Prediction

author.name: Jakob Versnjak, Manuel Welte, Titus Kuehne, Marcus Kelm, Gr\'egoire Montavon

entry.summary: The paper proposes a distributional regression paradigm for time-to-event prediction where output parameters are designed to align with domain concepts (odds structure), improving interpretability of distributional forecasts in clinical settings. It addresses the challenge that raw distribution parameters do not map naturally onto human-understandable quantities.

entry.title: MicroSim: Contrastive Graph Neural Networks for Binary Code Similarity Detection

author.name: Moussa Moussaoui, Tarik Houichime, Abdelghani Souhar, Abdelalim Sadiq

entry.summary: Presents MicroSim, representing binary functions as graphs over IDA Pro Hex-Rays microcode and comparing them with a contrastive Siamese GNN under a strict class-disjoint evaluation protocol. Achieves 0.9972 ROC-AUC and 0.9762 MCC on TREX, outperforming retrained Gemini, SAFE, and jTrans baselines.

entry.title: AudioCodex: Streaming Autoencoders for Live Audio

author.name: Marco Pasini, Javier Nistal, Cyran Aouameur, Stefan Lattner, George Fazekas

entry.summary: AudioCodex is a fully causal audio autoencoder for live generative audio, compressing stereo audio into ~10 Hz latent sequences using a mean-flow magnitude autoencoder, latent hypersphere projection, bounded-noise augmentation, and adversarial phase recovery. It achieves state-of-the-art generation-reconstruction trade-offs while remaining strictly causal in both directions. This enables real-time interactive and streaming generative audio systems.

entry.title: Improving Confidence Estimation in Language Models with Linear Representations of Ambiguity

author.name: Themistoklis Nikas, Nishant Subramani, Aaron Mueller

entry.summary: The authors derive linear representations of input ambiguity in LLM activations using difference-in-means on minimal pairs, showing steering with these representations selectively modulates ambiguity judgments. They connect aleatoric uncertainty detection to improved confidence estimation, addressing why LLM confidence estimates poorly predict success.

entry.title: SMO: Compiling Natural Language Skills into Graphs of Reusable State-Move-Outcome Bricks

author.name: Chao Chen, Jiashuo Zhang, Yunhang Shen, Liangyu Lian, Rongrong Ji

entry.summary: SMO argues that the reusable essence of an LLM agent skill lies in its procedural transitions rather than surface wording, and compiles skills into reusable State-Move-Outcome bricks organized as an externalized symbolic structure. New skills are composed by retrieving and connecting existing bricks, enabling comparison, deduplication, and composition of growing skill libraries for agents. This reframes skill management as a compilation problem.

entry.title: Improving the Diffusability of Motion Tokenizer

author.name: Guanhe Huang, Songqiao Han, Tangzheng Lian, Oya Celiktutan

entry.summary: Proposes the Diffusable Motion Tokenizer (DiMoT), which targets the spectral mismatch inside a motion VAE tokenizer (high-frequency-biased latents and temporal decoder artifacts) to resolve the generation-reconstruction trade-off in latent diffusion for human motion generation. Rather than scaling the diffusion backbone, it improves the tokenizer's latent space for better text-conditioned generation quality.

entry.title: Permute-then-Adapt: Weak-to-Strong Contrastive Image-Text Adaptation

author.name: Jinhao Li, Sarah Erfani, Lei Feng, Guangrui Li, James Bailey, Feng Liu

entry.summary: PTA improves CLIP-style contrastive learning by identifying missed positives among unpaired examples, using a conditional permutation reference distribution estimated from weak models to control Type-I error statistically instead of heuristic similarity thresholds. This reduces noise from penalizing semantically related image-text pairs.

entry.title: Differentiable Virtual-Slot Partitioning for Adaptive Tokenization in Vision Transformers

author.name: Gaoxiang He, Bin Zhu, Bo Xie, Xiaotong Yu, Yi Chen, Hongfei Yan

entry.summary: The paper proposes DVSP, a differentiable two-scale quadtree tokenization for vision transformers that lets a coarse token and its four fine children be endpoints of a single continuous interpolation, enabling end-to-end training without deleting tokens or using straight-through estimators. This addresses the noisy-gradient and frozen-scoring limitations of prior adaptive tokenization while staying on the pre-trained regular grid. It reduces compute on uninformative image regions while preserving accuracy.

entry.title: ForeAct: Geometry-Guided Action Learning from World Representations

author.name: Wei Lu, Jiaxi Zhang, Yunheng Wang, Taowen Wang, Yuetong Fang, Zhenhui Zhang, Shuning Zhang, Zizhao Yuan, Yixiao Feng, Zecui Zeng, Renjing Xu

entry.summary: ForeAct unifies scene geometry and its evolution during interaction for robotic manipulation, avoiding the high cost of diffusion/flow-based world action models and the lack of future-geometry supervision in geometry-centric policies. It learns actions guided by world representations with explicit spatial structure.

entry.title: Beyond Semantic Classes: Online Physical Parameter Estimation via Embedding-Conditioned Gaussian Mixtures

author.name: Alexander Borca-Tasciuc, Prayag Sharma, Franck Djeumou

entry.summary: The paper proposes a real-time estimator that replaces semantic class indexing with an interaction-grounded Gaussian-mixture posterior over latent physical parameters, conditioned directly on continuous visual embeddings. This enables robots to infer friction, stiffness, or sinkage from vision before contact, preserving distinct physical regimes that appearance alone cannot disambiguate.

entry.title: Detecting and Explaining Robot Policy Failures from Sparse Internal Features

author.name: Riad Ahmed, Sujosh Nag, Moniruzzaman Akash, Momotaz Begum

entry.summary: MIND applies mechanistic interpretability to visuomotor robot policies, using a sparse autoencoder to decompose internal activations into features linked to robot position, motion, and environment. It enables failure detection during execution and explanatory analysis of what went wrong inside the policy.

entry.title: RoboMoCap: A Large-Scale Whole-Body Motion Capture Dataset with Egocentric Vision for Robot Learning

author.name: Mayur Deshmukh, Aaron Tung, Junyi Li, Nikash Bhardwaj, Ademi Adeniji, Vincent Liu, Michael Cho, Jiafei Duan

entry.summary: RoboMoCap is a large-scale multimodal dataset combining egocentric vision with marker-based optical motion capture for locomotion-centric humanoid learning, addressing the gap of lower-body movements and foot placements invisible from first-person views. It comprises over 200 hours of loco-manipulation data designed for humanoid robot learning.

entry.title: HINT-VLM: Humanoid Interactive Navigation over Rough Terrain with Embodiment-Grounded Vision-Language Model

author.name: Ziwon Yoon, Seok Hwan Kim, Yiyu Chen, Quan Nguyen, Lu Gan, Ye Zhao

entry.summary: HINT-VLM extends Navigation Among Movable Obstacles (NAMO) to humanoid robots in cluttered outdoor rough terrain, jointly reasoning about terrain traversability and object movability with an embodiment-grounded VLM that predicts object interaction rather than only reacting. This addresses gaps where prior NAMO work assumed flat ground and reactive pushing. It is a step toward more autonomous humanoid operation in unstructured environments.

entry.title: Generalizable Output Feedback Optimal Control via Transformers Without Explicit State Estimation

author.name: Maitham F. AL-Sunni, Turki Bin Mohaya, John M. Dolan, Peter Seiler

entry.summary: The paper asks whether one learned policy can serve a whole family of partially observed, noisy linear systems, showing that a single transformer trained to imitate optimal LQG control across a heterogeneous MIMO LTI family can do so. With system-wise standardization, zero-padding, masking, and cost/noise covariance encoding, a short window of noisy measurements suffices to produce control actions without explicit state estimation.

entry.title: Causal Outcome Learning with Noisy Proxies

author.name: Eric V. Strobl

entry.summary: Introduces SCOUT, a framework for learning clinically interpretable, treatment-responsive outcomes from high-dimensional observational biomedical data while adjusting for confounding distributed across many noisy baseline variables. SCOUT builds low-dimensional adjustment representations to estimate average and conditional average treatment effects throughout the learning process. It addresses a practical bottleneck in estimating treatment effects from modern observational health datasets.

entry.title: AI-assisted learning platform helps robots reason beyond literal commands

author.name: Jennifer Chu | MIT News

entry.summary: MIT and NYU researchers present FLEX, a flexible feature-editing pipeline for robot motion planning that will be shown at CoRL 2026. Using natural-language commands, FLEX lets a robot infer broader intentions beyond literal instructions, for example reasoning from a warning like a no-spill comment to avoid the laptop entirely, integrating LLM-based reasoning with motion planning in simulated scenarios.

entry.title: BunshinRL: Splitting Live Agent Workspaces for Memory-Efficient Agentic RL

author.name: Yutong Huang, Vikranth Srivatsa, Alex Asch, Yiying Zhang

entry.summary: BunshinRL is an agentic RL rollout system that reduces memory and latency costs through cross-environment memory sharing, tool-prefix caching, and speculative tool execution, built on a BunshinFork mechanism that forks live whole-workspace containers with copy-on-write memory and preserved process, file, and GUI state. It matters because scaling agentic RL rollouts is a major systems bottleneck for training tool-using agents.

entry.title: In Search of Lost Time: Temporal Competence in Large Language Models

author.name: Ryan Liu, David Lee, Icey Siyi Ai, Marwa Abdulhai, Rachit Dubey, Thomas L. Griffiths

entry.summary: This paper evaluates LLM temporal competence across four evaluations from knowledge to action, finding models know time rules (92.0-97.5% accuracy on theorem-based questions) but drastically underestimate their own task completion times by up to 99.5%. It highlights the gap between secondhand temporal knowledge and lived temporal experience. It matters for time-aware AI agents that schedule, coordinate, and allocate thinking time.

entry.title: Audit Before You Merge: Provenance, Probing, and Continual LoRA Composition

author.name: Lenny Aharon, Neta Glazer, Lior Aharon

entry.summary: Treats post-hoc merging of public LoRA adapters as sequential continual learning on Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct and shows that adapter hubs contain modules failing basic provenance checks, including silent base-version mismatches and near-zero delta norms that inflate measured interference by about 10 percentage points. Proposes a two-check audit and a leakage-free probing protocol as preconditions for trustworthy forgetting measurements.

entry.title: GARP: Real-Time Generative Agents on Local Hardware in a Game Engine

author.name: Piero Molino, Patrick John Chia, Federico Bianchi, Jonathan P. Chen, Paul Szerlip

entry.summary: GARP is a platform for real-time generative agents inside the Godot game engine whose planning, memory, reflection, conversations, emotions, Big Five personality axes, needs, and relationships are driven by a 3B-parameter open-weight model running entirely on local hardware with no cloud service. It extends the original Generative Agents demonstration with richer agent psychology and a Character Behavior System (GARP 2). The work demonstrates that sophisticated generative agent loops are feasible on consumer-grade machines.

entry.title: AMSchem: Automated Schematic Visualization of AMS Circuits via Verifiable Agentic Generation

author.name: Yichen Shi, Zhiyuan Wang, Jianing Cui, Yao Lai, Jinting Zhang, Zhuofu Tao, Hongyang Wang, Zhiping Yu, Ting Jung Lin, Lei He

entry.summary: AMSchem is a training-free, verifier-guided agentic framework that converts analog/mixed-signal netlists into human-readable schematics, closing the long-standing netlist-to-schematic gap in design automation. It separates visual planning intent from executable schematic geometry and uses localized visual feedback, also enabling LLM design tools to see the circuits they iterate on.

entry.title: Seeing Like a Shopper: Validating Vision-Language Models as Synthetic Consumers

author.name: Woongki Kim, Seungkook Baek, Minhyeok Lee

entry.summary: Tests whether VLM-based synthetic shoppers can emulate real consumer behavior, having them plan trips from store directories and select products from shelf images. Synthetic baskets match held-out real purchases as often as households' own past trips, and synthetic group differences correlate with real ones twice as strongly as a text-only baseline.

entry.title: FADE: Fractional Anomalous Dynamics Extrapolation for Training-Free Diffusion Transformers Acceleration

author.name: Jinlong Yang, Lizilin, Jinke Wu, Yao Zhou

entry.summary: FADE accelerates diffusion transformer sampling training-free by modeling DiT feature evolution as anomalous diffusion with spatiotemporal heterogeneity, using fractional-order extrapolation instead of static integer-order feature caching operators. This reduces error accumulation on highly curved latent trajectories. A solid efficiency contribution for the dominant DiT generative paradigm.

entry.title: CoupledFlow: One-Step Neural Operators for Coupled Multi-Physics PDEs

author.name: Trong Khiem Tran, Minh Long Bui, Phi Le Nguyen, Mrinal Sen, Sanjay Srinivasan, Trong Nghia Hoang, Jana Doppa

entry.summary: CoupledFlow is a neural operator framework for multi-physics PDE systems that models cross-process interactions via a structure-constrained flow matching algorithm learning process-specific mean velocity fields conditioned on the full multi-physics state. This enables fast one-step prediction of coupled PDE systems that otherwise require expensive numerical simulation, with the key challenge being sampling of structure-constrained conditional flow interpolants.

entry.title: CrossLiDAR: Controllable Multi-Sensor LiDAR Sequence Generation

author.name: Khanh Nguyen, Thomas Walker, Hichem Telli, Carlos de la Torre-Ortiz, Stefano Fiorini, Salah Eddine Bekhouche, Mohammed-En-Nadhir Zighem, Wassim Swaileh, Tinghuai Wang

entry.summary: CrossLiDAR is a transformer-based generative framework producing controllable, spatio-temporally consistent multi-sensor LiDAR sequences using a rectified flow objective with an MM-DiT backbone over a compact range-image latent space, plus inter-sensor and conditioning modules. It targets scalable simulation for autonomous system validation.

entry.title: Agent Self-Improvement with Frozen Weights: The Added Value and Limits of Failure Traces

author.name: Arkid Mitra

entry.summary: Evaluates whether an agent's harness (notes around its model) can learn from failure traces beyond a matched search that never sees them, using a frozen 9-billion-parameter model with a larger teacher writing notes. Failure-trace-based notes improved accuracy by 4.0 percentage points over a matched process, but that process alone reached about 60% of the total improvement, and full customer-service conversations showed no demonstrated improvement.

entry.title: Data-informed Adaptation of Foundation Models for Causal Effect Estimation

author.name: Chunwei Ma, Russell D Wolfinger

entry.summary: The paper addresses the transparency gap in causal foundation models built on prior-data fitted networks, whose amortized inference obscures which assumptions they implicitly rely on for a given dataset. It proposes data-informed adaptation of CFMs to better align the training objective with causal estimands like CATE and ATE in the presence of diverse real-world data-generating processes.

entry.title: Kimodo-Policy: Learning Kinematic Action Models for Humanoid Loco-Manipulation

author.name: Yunheng Wang, Jiaxi Zhang, Wei Lu, Yuetong Fang, Taowen Wang, Yixiao Feng, Shuning Zhang, Junzhe Xu, Yichi Wang, Zizhao Yuan, Kailun Huang, Lusong Li, Mingqian Zhou, Zecui Zeng, Renjing Xu

entry.summary: The paper introduces Kinematic Action Models (KAMs), a paradigm that treats whole-body humanoid motion as a direct pretraining target and uses a pretrained text-to-motion generator as the action-generation backbone for loco-manipulation, grounding temporal and cross-body coordination priors via task conditioning, visual observations, and execution feedback. Kimodo-Policy is an initial instantiation combining a frozen motion generator with these grounding mechanisms.

entry.title: ShadowBench-MCP: Measuring Shadow Invocations in MCP-Style Tool Routing

author.name: Eyhab Al-Masri, Wenjun Yang

entry.summary: ShadowBench-MCP is a benchmark and metric suite for shadow invocations, where a task-preserving request variant causes an LLM tool router to select a riskier execution path that may skip validation or audit controls without asking for anything overtly malicious. It introduces decomposed metrics (task preservation, operational pressure, route-geometric drift) combined into a pre-execution SODS score, evaluated on a Groq-hosted Qwen3-32B router.

entry.title: MixRoute: Rethinking Single-Distribution Training for Generalizable Neural Routing

author.name: Hang Yi, Ziwei Huang, Yining Ma, Zhiguang Cao

entry.summary: Demonstrates that single-distribution training in neural combinatorial optimization generalizes far better than assumed, using a simple architectural inductive bias called Mix Normalization. It builds a benchmark spanning three routing problems and 179 fine-grained distributions, challenging the need for complex multi-distribution or meta-learning training.

entry.title: Bayesian Low-Rank Posteriors for Scalable Membership Inference

author.name: Khanh Nguyen, Antonio Emanuele Cin\`a, Andrey Barsky, Alejandra Reinares, Fabio Roli, Dimosthenis Karatzas

entry.summary: The paper proposes a scalable membership inference attack that replaces explicit shadow-model training with a Bayesian approximation over LoRA parameters, constructing a posterior from a single training run and sampling diverse virtual reference models. It instantiates this using Stochastic Weight Averaging Gaussians to address the cost of reference-model ensembles for large VLMs.

entry.title: Actions Should EARN Their Credit: Test-Time Adaptation and Route Consolidation for Frozen LLM Agents

author.name: Bian Sun, Kevin Zhai, Mubarak Shah, Song Wang

entry.summary: EARN is a parameter-free test-time adaptation method for frozen LLM agents that re-weights action proposals using past experience: it reduces credit for actions that repeatedly reach previously attained scores, boosts credit for action segments achieving higher scores, and conditionally reuses effective action sequences to preserve earlier performance. It also consolidates successful routes while respecting a fixed interaction budget. This improves LLM agent search without any weight updates.

entry.title: When Answer Decodability Is Not a Decision: Separating Final-Answer and Imminent-Emission Signals in Chain-of-Thought

author.name: Hyojung Han, Jongmin Kim, Seung-Hun Jeon

entry.summary: The paper shows that answer probes on chain-of-thought hidden states conflate two signals: whether the model has decided its final answer and what it is about to mention next. It introduces emission-controlled dual-target probing, which fits separate low-rank readers for imminent mention and final answer with target-specific nulls, finding large emission gaps, for example roughly 0.7 on Qwen3.5-4B rollouts where a distractor precedes the answer.

entry.title: Firepool: Brokering Warm GPU Capacity for Agentic and RL Workloads at LinkedIn

author.name: Ankit Goyal, Santosh Jha, Zhuo Zhi, Youmin Han, Cong Gu, Chen Xie, Animesh Singh

entry.summary: Firepool is LinkedIn's production sandbox and execution broker for agentic and RL workloads, which launch thousands of short GPU jobs where pod startup takes 20-35 seconds or minutes. It makes pods interchangeable via shared base images per hardware profile, binds job-specific code and dependencies at job start, and keeps pods warm without wasting GPUs or leaking state between callers. The paper reports practical lessons from operating this infrastructure at scale.

entry.title: What Travels Across Languages? Reading, Transfer and Erasure of Cross-Lingual Concept Subspaces in Bangla Idioms

author.name: Syed Rifat Raiyan, Yousuf Ibne Kamal Niloy

entry.summary: Studies cross-lingual concept subspaces in six frozen encoders using 10,359 Bangla idiom senses, examining which information transfers through subspace directions versus what classifiers and erasers can move through them. Finds class-mean directions give the most consistent evidence of shared coarse meaning across models and label types.

entry.title: Data-Driven Precision Control of Soft Helicoid Robots

author.name: Roshan S. Kaundinya, Mark Leone, Roberto Sabella, Hugo Buurmeijer, Luis Pabon, John Irvin Alora, Marco Pavone, George Haller

entry.summary: This paper extends adiabatic spectral submanifold (aSSM) reduced-order modeling from simulators to real hardware, learning a 5D reduced nonlinear ODE for a soft-helicoid trunk robot from collected data. The learned model is used in a model predictive control scheme achieving real-time precision trajectory tracking across 2D and 3D tasks with static and dynamic constraints. Reported results improve accuracy over alternative methods.

entry.title: Evaluating Cross-Signal Coherence in Mammography Vision-Language Models

author.name: Rebeca Nam, Chase M. Fensore, Christian A. Fauria-Robinson, Judy Gichoya, Joyce C. Ho

entry.summary: The study evaluates coherence among answer, confidence, and explanation for four vision-language models on breast density and BI-RADS categorization across two mammography datasets. Controlled perturbations show confidence often does not decrease when the image changes, shuffled options change most models' answers, and stated justifications can contradict predictions. The findings expose reliability gaps beyond accuracy-centric evaluation of medical VLMs.

entry.title: Prove What You Can: Hybrid Neurosymbolic Reasoning for Logical Natural Language Inference

author.name: Ada Cano\u{g}lu, Sadiq Qara

entry.summary: The paper presents Hybrid Reasoning, a three-stage neurosymbolic pipeline for logical natural language inference that decouples proof proposal, step validation, and label decision. An LLM proposes a structured proof tree with a raw verdict, a theorem prover validates derivations locally keeping only the provable subset, and uncertain verdicts are handled explicitly, avoiding the brittleness of whole-problem logic translation. This improves robustness over fully symbolic translation approaches.

entry.title: The Average Patient: Do Simulated Psychiatric Patients Answer Like Real People?

author.name: Weixiang Sun, Zehong Wang, Kaiwen Shi, Hong Huang, Colby Nelson, Yiyang Li, Yanfang Ye

entry.summary: The paper provides a framework for evaluating LLM-simulated psychiatric patients, proposing an information budget and average-patient hypothesis, and tests these against item-level data from eight human samples including clinical and feigning samples. Across 17 models, simulated patients vary 1.5 to 11 times less than real people, revealing that simulations flatten real response heterogeneity.

entry.title: Fairness in Explainable AI Narratives: Decomposing Social Disparities in LLM-Generated Explanations

author.name: Wannes Van den Bulck, Sofie Goethals, David Martens

entry.summary: The paper defines fairness in XAI narratives (XAINs), where LLMs translate technical explainability artifacts like SHAP values into lay-readable explanations that people may rely on to contest adverse decisions. Because narratives are bound to a ground-truth artifact, fairness must consider not only tone but equal faithfulness across social groups; the authors propose a framework generating narratives under three conditions, including protected-attribute variations, to decompose disparities. This opens a new fairness research area at the intersection of XAI and LLM generation.

entry.title: What Changed in Engineering Writing After Generative AI Chat Assistants: Evidence from 1.8 Million Articles

author.name: Taner Cokyasar

entry.summary: Analyzing 1.84 million engineering articles from 2015 to 2025, the study measures how wording, style, and structure shifted after ChatGPT's November 2022 release, comparing twelve measures against their pre-2023 trends. It finds 31 words associated with language model output appearing 82% more often than projected by 2025, while control words stayed stable. The paper matters both for its findings on AI's impact on scientific writing and for methodological care (e.g., correcting false January peaks from year-only dating).

entry.title: ClearForm: Shared-Surface Gaussian Splatting for Transparent and Opaque Scenes

author.name: Hajeong Lee, Jong-Il Park

entry.summary: Presents ClearForm, a shared-planar-Gaussian method for jointly reconstructing transparent interfaces and the appearance seen through them, and identifies the Geometry-Appearance Compositing Dilemma (GACD) where the same transparency-dependent alpha controls both color and geometry. The paper derives the effect on plane-based depth estimation and develops geometry-preserving machinery to resolve the conflict.

entry.title: WordEval: Evaluating Word-Native Operation Fidelity in Document Editing

author.name: Jinyoung Park, Yupan Huang, Shimin Zhang, Jiayu Ding, Yilin Jia, Yuzhong Zhao, Tengchao Lv, Wenshan Wu, Shaohan Huang, Nan Yang, Xiangyang Zhou, Dongdong Zhang, Li Dong, Lei Cui, Sun Mao, Xun Wang, Tao Ge, Huitian Jiao, Si-Qing Chen, Changick Kim, Furu Wei

entry.summary: WordEval is a benchmark centered on whether document agents faithfully execute Microsoft Word editing operations as intended changes to Word's structured object model, unlike prior benchmarks that rely on keyword matching or screenshot comparison.
