entry.summary: JoVox introduces a discrete flow matching framework that learns the joint distribution across all levels of a voxel hierarchy rather than independent per-level distributions, allowing fine cells to inform coarse-level decisions. This targets the long-standing trade-off between high fidelity and lightweight voxel generation.

entry.title: Beyond Bit Matching: Orthogonal Watermarks for Collusion-Resistant Image Fingerprinting

author.name: Zhakshylyk Nurlanov, Tobias Wei\ss{}berg, Florian Bernard

entry.summary: This paper introduces VectorMark, an image fingerprinting scheme that maps user keys to near-orthogonal high-dimensional unit vectors rather than discrete bit strings, making averaging collusion attacks ineffective. It provides a geometric analysis showing colluder signals of order 1/sqrt(K) survive averaging while unrelated keys concentrate near zero, enabling collusion detection via cosine similarity. This matters for provenance and leak-tracing of AI-generated and distributed media.

entry.title: What You Show Is Not What You Get: Rethinking Demonstration Following in Visual In-Context Segmentation

author.name: Xiao Hu, Ilia Sucholutsky

entry.summary: This paper identifies systematic failure modes in visual in-context segmentation with SegGPT, namely background color mapping deviations and part-to-parent expansion, where predictions diverge from the demonstration even when internal features remain discriminative. The authors analyze how demonstrations guide role and color assignment over learned semantic regions and propose Semantic Contrast Prompt Selection to mitigate the issues.

entry.title: NuJEV: Structured Visual Judgments for Consistent Nuclei Quantification

author.name: Yonghuang Wu, Pengfei Wang, Zhenyang Liang, Yize Ma, Pengfei Song, Guoqing Wu, Jinhua Yu

entry.summary: This paper introduces NuJEV, an adaptation of the Qwen3-VL-2B vision-language model for nuclear perception in pathology images, replacing free-form generation with structured judgments that predict nuclear presence, centers, and types via a jointly trained visual LoRA and parallel head. Counts are computed from predicted nuclei rather than generated directly, achieving a five-query MAE of 1.844 on the 2,732-image PanNuke test set, with localization and typed F1 scores of 0.816 and 0.682 respectively. It matters because it shows structured prediction heads on compact VLMs can deliver reliable, consistent cell quantification for computational pathology.

entry.title: NightSteps: A Night-Time Dataset and Benchmark for Pedestrian Crossing Intention Prediction

author.name: Sjoerd Takken, Shaodi You

entry.summary: NightSteps is a new benchmark of night-time dashcam footage from six cities with pedestrian locations, track IDs, and annotations for crossing intention prediction, addressing the absence of low-light data that limits robustness evaluation of pedestrian safety models. It provides construction methodology and baseline evaluation.

entry.title: Color wave: A systematic evaluation of active screen illumination for injection attack detection in remote face authentication

author.name: Daniyar Kurmankhojayev, Elmurat Nigmatov, Dmitrii Gordin, Andrei Shadrikov, Mikhail Shkorin, Danijar Gabdullin, Vyacheslav Shen

entry.summary: This paper systematically evaluates active screen illumination methods for detecting injection attacks in remote face authentication, complementing the better-studied presentation attack detection (PAD) use case. It classifies injected content into static images, prerecorded videos, and real-time deepfakes, and adapts a screen-illumination challenge-response approach into an implementation evaluated for injection attack detection.

entry.title: What Breaks Scribble-Supervised Segmentation? An Audit-Informed Benchmark for Scribble Annotation Robustness

author.name: Minheng Wu, Di Wen, Ruiping Liu, Junwei Zheng, Yufan Chen, Kailun Yang, Kunyu Peng

entry.summary: This paper introduces a benchmark for scribble-supervised segmentation robustness, built on an audit of 12,031 manual PASCAL VOC 2012 scribbles and six controlled perturbation operators (class corruption, spatial offset, directional perturbation, stroke-length reduction, dropout, fragmentation). It evaluates manual and automatic scribbles across two image domains, two backbone settings, and multiple training pipelines, with each operator reporting requested versus achieved changes.

entry.title: HSGNav: Hypothesis Scene Graphs for Multi-Scale Lifelong Navigation under Object Relocation

author.name: Kaiyao Liao, Qingfeng Li, Chen Chen, Qing Sun, Ningbo Gu, Xiaoze Wu, Haochen Zhao, Ying Li, Jianwei Niu

entry.summary: HSGNav proposes a Hypothesis Scene Graph (HSG) that separates persistent 3D furniture entities from revisable surface-object hypotheses, preserving small-object evidence and supporting local revision without rebuilding the stable entity topology. This enables lifelong navigation under object relocation in real homes, with explicit object-state validation to avoid stale entries.

entry.title: Budget-aware Correspondence-driven View Selection for Real-time 3D Perception of Mobile Robots

author.name: Vaishnav Ramesh, Jacob Carter, Shivali J. Patel, Sanjeev J. Koppal, Md Jahidul Islam

entry.summary: BCVS is a pose-free view selection algorithm that filters redundant image sequences online for 3D perception, achieving 22+ FPS on a CPU without full structure-from-motion pipelines. It uses a purely correspondence-based scoring strategy that prioritizes view novelty while maintaining overlap for geometric stability, under a user-specified budget.

entry.title: Who Taught the Robot That? Removing One User's Corrections from a Robot Policy That Learns Online

author.name: Eshika Pathak, Leela Krishna

entry.summary: This paper addresses machine unlearning for online robot learning: a robot corrected by multiple users must be able to remove one person's contributions. It shows that when corrections occur via take-over control, ordered retraining on the remaining sessions approximates the counterfactual robot, while simple data deletion and one-pass retraining does not, because update ordering matters.

entry.title: Large-Scale Hierarchical Decision-Making in Robot Control via ADMM

author.name: Kai Pfeiffer, Jia Wang, Gordon Owusu Boateng, Yuquan Wang, Vincent Bonnet, Abderrahmane Kheddar

entry.summary: The authors reformulate sparse hierarchical quadratic programming subproblems arising in robot kinematic control using ADMM, enabling effective warm-starting across sequential control steps where prior interior-point solvers fell short. This allows efficient integrated hierarchical decision-making over large sets of end-effector candidates. It contributes a numerical tool that could make hierarchical robot control more real-time capable.

entry.title: OASIS: Optimization-Aware Subgoal Inference with Safety Constraints for Autonomous Mobile Robot Navigation

author.name: Arian Hajizadeha, Javad Pourrafia, Negar Shenavara, Sana Bashiria, Seyed Majid Esmailzadeh

entry.summary: OASIS is a hierarchical navigation framework that feeds recent MPC optimization outcomes back into an RL-based subgoal policy, so that subgoal generation is aware of whether the low-level controller can actually solve the resulting problem. A Soft Actor-Critic high-level policy proposes local subgoals tracked by a nonlinear MPC with motion limits and collision-avoidance constraints. This closes the loop between planning and control, addressing a common failure mode in hierarchical navigation.

entry.title: Certified Zonotopic Reachability Analysis for Trajectory Tracking on Lie Groups

author.name: Yanliang Huang, Peng Xie, Zhen Zhang, Zhuoqi Zeng, Amr Alanwar

entry.summary: Develops certified zonotopic reachability analysis for bounding trajectory-tracking error of aerial and space vehicles whose error dynamics evolve on matrix Lie groups. Exploiting group-affine structure, the error dynamics become linear in Lie algebra coordinates, yielding less conservative safety certificates than single invariant ellipsoids or interval methods. This enables pre-execution safety certification of planned trajectories near obstacles under bounded disturbances.

entry.title: A Topological Encoder Decoder Framework for Temporal Graph Learning

author.name: Ronan Buck, Kiarash Shamsi, Tran Gia Bao Ngo, Astrit Tola, Baris Coskunuzer, Cuneyt Gurcan Akcora

entry.summary: This paper reframes temporal graph prediction as an inverse topology problem: instead of predicting edges directly, the model first predicts a multiscale topological descriptor of the future graph and then reconstructs a plausible future snapshot under inductive constraints. This makes global structure and node churn explicit targets, addressing breakdowns when new nodes and edges appear. It matters for forecasting dynamic graphs with changing size and composition.

entry.title: DFT-Agent Bench: Scaffold Effects and Execution Provenance in Autonomous DFT

author.name: Shijie Liu, Jin Yang, Weilin Wan, Jingtao Han, Jia LI, Tianqi Deng

entry.summary: Introduces DFT-Agent Bench, a benchmark of 200+ Quantum ESPRESSO tasks for LLM agents doing first-principles materials simulation, with execution-provenance auditing of whether agents actually ran the required simulations. Compares a bare ReAct baseline with a bundled scaffold across two models, showing scaffold improvements on some task families but not uniformly.

entry.title: BiVerify: Closing the Loop Between Backward and Forward Verification for Mathematical Self-Correction

author.name: Rui Zou, Xin Zhao, Mengqi Wei, Ji-Rong Wen

entry.summary: BiVerify combines backward verification (checking candidate answers against original constraints) and forward verification (following problem conditions through the solution) in a closed loop for LLM mathematical self-correction, exploiting their complementary failure modes. The paper analyzes when each direction catches different error types and shows that looping between them improves correction reliability. It targets more dependable self-correction on complex math problems.

entry.title: Reproducible quantum clustering for single-cell transcriptome atlases

author.name: Henry Han

entry.summary: KQE-2 is a training-free hybrid quantum-classical framework for reproducible whole-transcriptome clustering that maps cells into entanglement-free quantum states, enabling exact classical evaluation and direct quantum-processor checks. It proves removing entanglement is necessary and sufficient to bound single-qubit feature variance, and shows more stable biological results than retrained scVI baselines.

entry.title: PARIS: A multi-agent LLM framework for end-to-end, PRISMA-guided systematic literature reviews with pre-synthesis corpus quality assessment

author.name: Christophe Cruz (ICB, UBE), Hussam Ghanem (ICB, UBE), Samir Jabbar (ICB, UBE), Ait Kbir (ICB, UBE), Hocine Cherifi (ICB, UBE)

entry.summary: PARIS is an open-source multi-agent framework in which a conductor agent running in Claude Code orchestrates 15 specialized LLM agents to conduct end-to-end PRISMA-guided systematic literature reviews, from scoping to manuscript draft export. Agents coordinate through validated persisted artifacts with deterministic Python utilities for retrieval and scoring, plus three human checkpoints including a QualityScore-based corpus adequacy gate.

entry.title: SurvAD: How Anomalies Survive Diffusion Reconstruction

author.name: Lexing Zhang

entry.summary: Characterizes anomaly leakage in diffusion-based anomaly detectors, deriving an exact recursion for deterministic samplers whose continuous limit is a survival law: anomaly signal decays exponentially at a rate set by a retention parameter dependent on noise level, not step count. One measured path therefore predicts leakage across samplers and schedules, and the law identifies leak growth as exposure bias.

entry.title: Update Slope Is Bounded by Prior Calibration: A Structural Bound and Its Contingent Empirical Signature

author.name: Ben Jenkins, Mihaela Cardei

entry.summary: The paper identifies two confounds in the update-slope metric used to evaluate LLM forecasters: outcome-aware evidence construction inflates measured responsiveness roughly fourfold versus resolution-blinded ladders, and update slope has a prior-dependent structural ceiling that can reflect starting calibration rather than genuine updating. Empirical coupling varies across Manifold, ForecastBench, and ACLED pools. This is a cautionary methodological contribution for LLM forecasting evaluations.

entry.title: Split and Bridge: Multimodal Generation via Diffusion Bridging

author.name: Ahmad Arrabi, Xiaohan Zhang, Xingyu Li, Safwan Wshah

entry.summary: Split and Bridge (SnB) is a bottom-up multimodal generation framework that couples pretrained unimodal diffusion models at sampling time: samples follow a shared diffusion trajectory to a split point, then branch into modality-specific trajectories guided by a bridge module. This avoids training a unified latent space from scratch and enables plug-and-play composition. It offers a scalable alternative to joint multimodal diffusion training.

entry.title: Imperfectly Imperfect: Evaluating Graded Cognitive Diversity in LLM Persona Simulations

author.name: Sion Weatherhead, Ben Newell, Aaron Belbasis, Flora Salim

entry.summary: The paper evaluates whether LLM agents conditioned on profiles of cognitive reflection, Need for Cognition, and Big Five traits reproduce human variation when answering a cognition suite compared to 473 human adults, including two newly assembled tests (CRT and BRT). It assesses whether synthetic participants in behavioral research can express graded cognitive diversity as assigned. Useful caution and methodology for the growing use of LLMs as synthetic research subjects.

entry.title: Learning Biological Hierarchies in Single-Cell Foundation Models

author.name: Xiangyu Guo, Ricardo Henao

entry.summary: The paper introduces scOntoFM, a biologically informed single-cell foundation model that embeds the hierarchical cell ontology into representation learning using lowest-common-ancestor distances. It pairs efficient offline triplet sampling with ontology-guided learning to shape both local neighborhoods and global embedding geometry, improving performance across cell- and gene-level benchmarks.

entry.title: HydroTuring: A physics probe benchmark testing mass, energy, and momentum conservation in hydrologic models

author.name: Zhi Li, Changming Li, Siavash Shams, Han Wang, Qingyi Yang, Yuanhang Liu, Taiqi Lian, Xin Lan, Shunan Zhou, Binlan Zhang, Siddik Barbhuiya, Songkun Yan, Bing Li, Jinlong Hu, Yaji Wang, Zhenjiang Wu, Mofan Zhang, Kaihao Long, Jingzhi Chen, Yuan-Heng Wang

entry.summary: HydroTuring is a black-box benchmark of 37 physics probes testing mass, energy, and momentum conservation in hydrologic models, including deep learning systems now used for operational flood forecasting. The motivating experiment shows a conceptual model leaking 15% of water input to an unreported sink can still achieve a Nash-Sutcliffe efficiency of 0.93, illustrating that hydrograph skill does not imply physical consistency.

entry.title: An Evaluation of Tabular Foundation Models as Training-Free World Models

author.name: Xian Yeow Lee, Ryoichi Takase, Ahmed Farahat

entry.summary: Investigates whether pretrained tabular foundation models can serve as training-free dynamics models by framing next-state prediction as in-context regression over transition pairs. Across synthetic systems and robot locomotion benchmarks, TabFMs beat LSTM and MLP models trained from scratch on limited data in almost all settings, while also mapping where they break.

entry.title: HumanSightBench: A Benchmark for Human Visual Perception in MLLMs

author.name: Zixin Su, Yangguang Lin, Zegang Peng, Yuntong Sun, Xuanyi Wang, Jiahao Wang, Qiankai Xu, Bing Yuan, Jinze Bai, Youbin Wu, Jingjia Huang, Ruyang Liu, Yanxu Hu

entry.summary: HumanSightBench contains ~2,870 items constructed to be human-easy but model-hard, isolating visual perception failures of multimodal LLMs from language priors, background knowledge, and ambiguous questions. Its guidelines address the confounds of end-to-end multimodal evaluation.

entry.title: BiMuon: A Geometry-Aware Stochastic Bilevel Optimization Approach

author.name: Zhen Qin, Zhiyao Zhang, Yingbin Liang, Jia Liu

entry.summary: BiMuon extends Muon-style geometry-aware optimization to stochastic bilevel problems, integrating implicit hypergradient estimation while respecting matrix structure in gradients and correcting spectral imbalance induced by lower-level curvature. Applications include hyperparameter learning, data reweighting, language model alignment, and actor-critic RL.

entry.title: Pruning DNA Sequence

author.name: Faias Satter, Shaker Islam, Aminul Islam

entry.summary: The paper introduces Sequence Pruning, a dynamic data-pruning framework for DNA language-model pretraining that removes genomic sequences as they become easy to predict, using per-sequence accuracy computed directly from the forward pass without a separate scoring model. Across five pretraining settings and two corpora it reduces pretraining data processing by up to 96% while largely preserving downstream genomic benchmark performance.

entry.title: Universal Approximation by Equivariant Message-Passing Graph Neural Networks with a Bilinear Readout

author.name: Pingbing Ming, Han Wang

entry.summary: The authors prove universal approximation for BREMP networks, a reference architecture for equivariant GNN interatomic potentials, where readout forms invariants from products of equivariant features. They construct explicit spherical-harmonic filters that determine local atomic environments up to permutations, with degree bounds tied to neighbor counts and layer cutoffs.

entry.title: Data Manipulation Attacks Against Machine Learning Integrated Cyber-Physical Systems

author.name: Soyon Choi, Scott Alfeld, Meiyi Ma

entry.summary: This paper develops methods for constructing attack policies against composed ML systems in cyber-physical settings, where an attacker who can trick individual learners (vision, planning) seeks to manipulate the system-level behavior and resulting physical actions. It formalizes how vulnerabilities of individual models compose into system-level attack surfaces. This extends ML security beyond single-model threat models to integrated autonomous systems.

entry.title: When Does Physics Beat Data? Data-Efficient Traffic State Estimation with Amortized PINNs

author.name: Anna Lazareva, Alexander Tarakanov

entry.summary: The paper shows that imposing the Lighthill-Whitham-Richards conservation law as a physics-informed prior makes traffic state estimation far more data-efficient than pure data-driven models including deep kriging. On four real corridors, physics-informed estimators generalize to held-out sensors where data-driven models overfit, with a clear crossover benefit on shock-rich corridors.

entry.title: Vendi Anomaly Scores for Efficient and Accurate Anomaly Detection

author.name: Amey Pasarkar, Adji Bousso Dieng

entry.summary: The paper introduces the Vendi Anomaly Score, which flags anomalies by measuring how much removing a sample changes the dataset's diversity as quantified by the Vendi score. This diversity-based formulation captures both local redundancy and global structure without density estimation, partitioning heuristics, or restrictive distributional assumptions. The approach offers a new conceptual paradigm for anomaly detection relevant to trustworthy ML and scientific discovery.

entry.title: Group-Conditional Conformal Risk Control: Exact Guarantees, Limits, and Overlapping Extensions

author.name: Tareq Aldirawi, Wenge Guo

entry.summary: This paper establishes exact finite-sample group-conditional conformal risk control for disjoint groups under bounded monotone losses, with two-sided bounds and fundamental limitations from local support and calibration-rank granularity. For overlapping groups it develops two exactly valid approaches, characterizes reconciliation gaps, and demonstrates a strict size-versus-coverage trade-off.

entry.title: Flex-DDCM: Zero-Shot Task-Oriented Image Compression via Diffusion Trajectory Guidance

author.name: Yixin Gao, Runsen Feng, Xin Li, Zhibo Chen

entry.summary: Proposes Flex-DDCM, a zero-shot image compression framework that guides diffusion trajectories with task-specific noise selection so compressed representations serve downstream machine-analysis tasks as well as human viewing. Builds on Turbo-DDCM and supports individually applicable guidance terms for flexible reconstruction targets.

entry.title: Music Inpainting With Similarity-Guided Latent Diffusion

author.name: Sean Turland, Eloi Moliner, Vesa V\"alim\"aki

entry.summary: Proposes SimDPS, a model-agnostic music inpainting method that retrieves contextually similar segments from the surrounding signal and uses them to guide diffusion posterior sampling toward coherent reconstructions. Outperforms RePaint and DPS on objective metrics across waveform and latent diffusion backbones, with positive subjective results.

entry.title: Query- and Candidate-Aware Long User Sequence Modeling for Sponsored Product Ranking in Search

author.name: Dongyue Xie, Sergey Kolbin, Manavender Malgireddy, Iurii Shcherbak, Weixing Tang, Arushi Jain, Wanchen Shao, Kurt Zimmer, Raja Hafiz Affandi, Matt Lindsay

entry.summary: This paper presents a production sequence modeling framework for sponsored-product search ranking that augments recent behavior with dual retrieval channels over long-term history: candidate-nearest-neighbor and query-nearest-neighbor retrieval. It combines dedicated query and candidate context tokens with candidate-aware early fusion. Offline ablations show improved ranking metrics over baselines.

entry.title: How Far Does Second-Order Linear Response Predict Quantization Mismatch? Pre-Registered Measurements on Five Language Models

author.name: Dezhen Lu, Zixiang Ni

entry.summary: The paper tests whether a second-order screening tool based on Fisher information (the quadratic term underlying Hessian-aware quantizers) reliably predicts post-quantization KL divergence across int8, fp8, and int4 formats on five language models including Qwen3 and OLMo-2 variants. Relative predictions are robust across perturbation scales and configurations, absolute predictions are heavy-tailed, and the MoE model exhibits non-quadratic behavior. Pre-registered measurement design adds credibility.

entry.title: From Granger causality to causal structure in dynamical systems

author.name: V\'ictor Elvira

entry.summary: This survey-style article reviews the gap between Granger causality, which detects predictive relations among measured signals, and true causal structure among the mechanisms generating them. It traces recent advances in observation-space Granger analysis and follows a path toward directed structure in latent dynamical models, asking when such structure can be interpreted causally. The clarification is important given widespread misuse of Granger causality across neuroscience and economics.

entry.title: Distinguishing Extraction Failures and Clinical Discordance with LLM Uncertainty on Radiology Reports

author.name: Jerjes Aguirre-Chavez, Shant Malkasian, Roshun Sankaran, Brendan Crabb, Albert Hsiao

entry.summary: Using a real-world cohort of 1,045 patients undergoing coronary CT angiography, this study evaluates whether LLM uncertainty during vessel-level stenosis extraction can separate extraction failures from genuine clinical discordance, validated against expert annotations and invasive angiography. Quantifying uncertainty signals like stenosis margins helps clinicians know when structured LLM outputs should not be trusted. This supports safer use of LLMs for structuring clinical datasets.

entry.title: Large Language Models as a Universal Searcher for Open-World Automated Machine Learning

author.name: Yuxuan Hu, Jihao Liu, Weikang Shi, Xijie Huang, Linda Wei, Mingjie Zhan, Aojun Zhou, Rui Liu, Hongsheng Li

entry.summary: The paper proposes an LLM-based AutoML framework that jointly optimizes architecture, training hyperparameters, and data ratios without task-specific fine-tuning, bridging siloed domain-specific AutoML pipelines. NCode, a unified numerical encoding scheme, converts diverse AutoML design choices into universal discrete sequences, recasting optimization as a unified ranking task learned from limited single-domain optimization trajectories. This enables open-world, cross-domain AutoML via LLMs.

entry.title: Adapting Frozen Promptable Segmenters to User-Defined Taxonomies via Few-Shot Proposal Learning

author.name: Khayrul Islam (Computational Engineering Division, Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory, Livermore, CA, USA), Christopher Frederic Miller (Computational Engineering Division, Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory, Livermore, CA, USA)

entry.summary: SNAP is an annotation pipeline that learns a project's own class boundaries from the labels an annotator draws anyway, fitting a per-project SnapHead on top of a single frozen SAM2.1 pass per image, with the head refitting in seconds after each labeled image. Where SAM 3 is available, the same labels decide per class whether to keep the general model's boundary or the learned one. It matters because promptable segmenters fix class boundaries by their training vocabulary, while real annotation projects need project-specific taxonomies.

entry.title: LIFT: Local Metric Alignment and Foundation-guided Propagation for Few-shot Depth Completion

author.name: Xiang Li, Xiaojin Gong

entry.summary: LIFT leverages a frozen monocular depth estimation foundation model for few-shot depth completion, estimating local scale/shift fields for metric initialization and refining via multi-scale foundation-feature-guided propagation plus a lightweight residual head. It balances annotation cost against adaptation quality.

entry.title: Remembering to Reason: Structured Memory for Scene and Workflow Understanding in Robot-Assisted Surgery

author.name: Zhiran Zhang, Hu Wang, Yichen Wu, Yutong Xie

entry.summary: MemSurg introduces a structured memory graph for surgical video understanding that stores timestamped entity categories, locations, motion cues, and interaction summaries, with chronological and entity-associated links. Task-adaptive retrieval supplies evidence-grounded prompts for scene and workflow reasoning, addressing the limitation that frame-centric prompting lacks procedural history. This is significant for intelligent assistance in robot-assisted surgery.

entry.title: Source-Anchored Visual Autoregression for Extreme Image Compression

author.name: Bingxin Wang, Yuan Lan, Yang Xiang, Yiqing Huang

entry.summary: SAVAR reframes extreme-low-bitrate image compression (below 0.01 bpp) as constrained generation using Visual Autoregressive modeling, transmitting early-scale tokens plus a compact caption so reconstruction stays faithful to the source. The token anchoring plus semantic caption reduces source-inconsistent reconstructions of object identity and texture.

entry.title: Dropping Tokens Without Dropping Them: Causal Attribution for Diabetic Retinopathy

author.name: Pramath Girish Haritz, Chandra Sekhar Seelamantula

entry.summary: This work decomposes ViT attention into contribution and pull maps, where the pull quantifies causal explanations and an identity characterizes when contribution fails to capture causality. On the MAPLES-DR diabetic retinopathy dataset, token dropping/insertion tests show the pull map achieves the highest causal faithfulness.

entry.title: HIST3R: Decomposing and Rectifying State Updates with History for Streaming 3D Reconstruction

author.name: Kenneth Yang, Yu-Chiang Frank Wang

entry.summary: HIST3R analyzes CUT3R-style recurrent state updates for streaming 3D reconstruction via a direction-magnitude decomposition, where magnitude sets update gain and direction encodes geometric intent. This unified view of CUT3R and its variants reveals shortcomings of existing training frameworks and motivates history-aware rectification of state updates to prevent long-horizon geometric drift under bounded memory.

entry.title: V3DSAM: Semantic-Geometric Loop Verification and Geometry-Anchored Persistent Instance Mapping for Feed-Forward Dense SLAM

author.name: Maolin Ye, Dongqing Zhao, Linyang Li, Shuai Xue, Yuan Liu, Yiyuan Wang, Wen Li

entry.summary: V3DSAM is an open-vocabulary semantic dense SLAM system combining feed-forward geometric estimates from VGGT-SLAM 2.0 with open-vocabulary semantics from SAM3. It introduces semantic-geometric dual-scale loop verification to reject false loop closures and geometry-anchored persistent instance mapping for long-sequence robustness.

entry.title: MoE-DAgger: Transition-Aware Router-Entropy Gating for Selective Human Correction in Phase-Structured Manipulation

author.name: Sungjun Heo, Sungjun Yang, Heedon Jeong, Junhyoung Ha, Jeong hwan Jeon

entry.summary: MoE-DAgger improves selective data acquisition in DAgger for phase-structured manipulation by using causal router history from a phase-supervised soft mixture-of-experts to distinguish genuine phase transitions from anomalous routing. The acquisition rule requests human correction only when high entropy persists outside settling transitions, times out, or routing persists anomalously, without giving the policy any phase labels at execution.

entry.title: ColNav: Uncertainty-Aware Spacetime Collision Checking with Bounding Volume Hierarchies

author.name: Sanjeev Ramkumar Sudha, Lars Ivar Hatledal, Erlend M. Coates

entry.summary: ColNav proposes robust collision checking for mobile robots in dynamic environments by encoding positional and velocity uncertainty of the robot and moving targets into spacetime tubes, organized in bounding volume hierarchies. Unlike point-sampling forward propagation, the geometric formulation guarantees collision checks between sampled points and is robust to state-estimate uncertainty. Two variants support bounded-set and Gaussian uncertainty descriptions.

entry.title: CSG-Nav: Confidence-Aware Semantic-Geometric Fusion for Robust Exploration and Accurate Zero-Shot Object-Goal Navigation

author.name: Shoubin Chen, Rui Xu, Zehao Wu, Kai Zhang, Tao Huang, Zhou Liu, Qingquan Li

entry.summary: CSG-Nav is a zero-shot object-goal navigation framework built on confidence-aware fusion of semantic and geometric information, integrating semantic-source fusion and other mechanisms to counter hallucination-induced directional bias and geometrically incorrect stopping from foundation-model perception. It targets reliable exploration and goal termination in unseen environments. This addresses known failure modes of foundation-model-based navigation.

entry.title: SAM-VTP: Video Memory and Measured Geometry for Continuous Traversability Segmentation

author.name: Lucas Hoefs, Hui Xie, Senjian An, Fangyi Zhang

entry.summary: SAM-VTP fine-tunes SAM2's video memory pathway for dense, prompt-free traversability segmentation, producing temporally consistent predictions rather than frame-wise ones. It measures terrain geometry (slope, roughness, height) from depth and fuses it with image features, and introduces an offline pipeline generating dense per-pixel supervision without robot deployment.

entry.title: DeepResearch RewardBench: Evaluating Reward Models for Deep Research Report

author.name: Shudong Liu, Yuting Zhong, Guanhua Chen, Xinyi Yang, Junnan Liu, Lidia S. Chao, Jiaheng Liu, Derek F. Wong

entry.summary: DeepResearch RewardBench is the first benchmark dedicated to evaluating reward models and LLM judges for long-form, multi-step deep research reports, which are hard to assess due to long context, high information density, and domain specificity. It collects diverse report candidates from multiple agent systems to test how well existing reward models understand research-report quality.

entry.title: CoRA-Bench: Evaluating Evidence Preservation by Context Selectors Under Token Budgets

author.name: Huzaifa Pardawala, Siddhant Sukhani, Sudheer Chava, Agam Shah

entry.summary: CoRA-Bench evaluates evidence preservation under shared token budgets across context selection methods including truncation, BM25, dense retrieval, reranking, LLMLingua-2, and Provence on BABILong, LOONG, a NoLiMa diagnostic, and LongMemEval. It reveals task-dependent tradeoffs, with supporting-fact and needle recall numbers showing no single method preserves evidence best across tasks.

entry.title: PatternBloom: Empowering Agentic RAG with Externalized RL-Distilled Graph Patterns

author.name: Yi Ge, Heng Huang

entry.summary: PatternBloom shifts agentic RAG retrieval from content to logic: an RL stage scores the agent's constructed evidence graphs by an oracle's information gain, and distilled reasoning patterns are externalized so procedural knowledge recurs across queries of the same logical type instead of remaining in hidden states. This addresses plateauing of content-only methods as reasoning depth grows. It matters as a structural change to how agentic RAG systems accumulate expertise.

entry.title: Factor Rank: A Canonical Algebraic Generalization of Tree Decision Diagrams

author.name: Alexis de Colnet, Stefan Szeider

entry.summary: Introduces algebraic tree decision diagrams (ATDDs), which replace the subfunction-count width of tree decision diagrams with the rank of the cut matrix, showing every TDD converts to an equal-or-smaller-width ATDD and that ATDDs are exponentially more succinct than TDDs and quasi-polynomially more succinct than structured deterministic DNNF, corresponding to canonical-form tree tensor networks.

entry.title: When Are Nearby Experts Composable? Cross-Task Model Merging in Neural Thickets

author.name: Suxin Ji, Hungtao Wan, Mingjun Liu, An Zhang

entry.summary: The paper formulates expert-pair selection for cross-task model merging in neural thickets (task experts from random perturbations of a shared checkpoint), showing via exact finite-difference decomposition and counterexamples that proximity and orthogonality alone do not guarantee composability. It proposes quality-constrained spectral selection with cross-task screening, layerwise geometry, and abstention-aware metrics. Experiments span six checkpoints, 21 task pairs, and multiple perturbation patterns.

entry.title: FinCutBench: A Continually Updated Benchmark for Measuring the Temporal Boundaries of LLM Financial Knowledge

author.name: Siyuan Li, Ke Wan, Boyong Hou, Yujie Deng, Zixuan Yuan

entry.summary: FinCutBench is a continually updated monthly benchmark of 9,000 Chinese and English multiple-choice questions spanning January 2023 to September 2026 that measures how far a fixed model's parametric financial knowledge extends over calendar time, detecting parametric look-ahead bias in point-in-time tasks like backtesting. It builds monthly knowledge profiles using approximate disclosure months and applies decline tests and knot checks to validate profiles. This addresses contamination in time-sensitive financial evaluation.

entry.title: Layer Roles Matter: Mitigating Modality Imbalance in Multimodal Emotion Reasoning via Adaptive Layer Profiling

author.name: Pengyu Huang, Peipei Song, Beier Zhu, Zhiyuan Han, Jinpeng Hu, Xun Yang

entry.summary: The paper analyzes modality imbalance in multimodal emotion reasoning with MLLMs, identifying two failure modes—unimodal over-reliance and insufficient cross-modal utilization—that require different interventions. It shows MLLM layers have implicit functional hierarchies in multimodal processing and proposes adaptive layer profiling to mitigate imbalance.

entry.title: COMPASS: Composable Policy-Amortized Structured Search for LLM-Based Optimization Modeling

author.name: Nguyen Le Minh Hoang, Van Duc Cuong, Bui Trong Duc, Huynh Thi Thanh Binh

entry.summary: COMPASS treats template retrieval for LLM-based optimization modeling as a learnable policy rather than a fixed inference-time rule, amortizing hierarchical taxonomy search across past modeling experience. The framework builds a composable policy over a template library so retrieval improves from prior successes and failures when translating natural-language problems into solver code.

entry.title: AuDiR: Diagnosing Audio Reasoning with Rule and Percept Interventions

author.name: Chengwei Wei, Yi Ma, Nancy F. Chen

entry.summary: AuDiR is a diagnostic benchmark for audio reasoning that disentangles failures in acoustic perception, rule knowledge, and rule application through controlled input interventions, including a condition that removes the audio entirely. The benchmark contains 201 items in 18 families from 9 sources, with answer references documented separately. It matters because answer accuracy alone cannot distinguish these failure modes in multimodal audio models.

entry.title: Med-DualLoRA: Local Adaptation of Foundation Models for 3D Cardiac MRI

author.name: Joan Perramon-Lluss\`a, Amelia Jim\'enez-S\'anchez, Grzegorz Skorupko, Fotis Avgoustidis, Carlos Mart\'in-Isla, Karim Lekadir, Polyxeni Gkontra

entry.summary: Med-DualLoRA is a client-aware parameter-efficient fine-tuning method for federated adaptation of foundation models for 3D cardiac MRI disease detection, addressing heterogeneous non-IID multi-center data and communication overhead under privacy constraints. It targets the practical challenge of adapting large medical foundation models without centralized fine-tuning. This is a solid contribution to medical imaging and federated learning.

entry.title: Fairness Explanations Improve Fairness In Human-AI Decision Making: an empirical evaluation of parole decision-making

author.name: Peter Daish, Alan Dix, Muneeb Ahmad, Matt Roach

entry.summary: This paper extracts fair data samples from biased datasets and adapts fairness-explanation techniques to highlight potential AI bias during parole decisions, conducting a within-subjects study (n=48) across three conditions: human judgment, unexplained AI assistance, and AI assistance with visual ethnic-bias explanations (Fair-XAI). Fairness explanations significantly reduced both sex and ethnic bias compared to human-only and unexplained AI conditions. This is a useful empirical contribution to human-AI decision-making.

entry.title: SPRING-5: Measuring Tool Documentation Repair for LLM Agents by Efficiency

author.name: Guan Zheng Huang

entry.summary: SPRING-5 is a benchmark scoring automatic tool-documentation repair by cost rather than accuracy alone: 20 tool families and 344 tasks with degraded specifications, deterministic backends, and answer keys, charged calls against an ideal call path. Across 2,644 baseline sessions, 54% of wrong answers came with no rejected call, refusal, or retry, and the benchmark includes validity instruments such as a build-time ceiling assertion.

entry.title: Learning of Tree Automata applied to Neural Language Acceptors

author.name: Juan Pedro da Silva, Sergio Yovine

entry.summary: The authors extract visibly pushdown grammars from neural language models in a fully black-box setting, extending the VPL* framework by replacing its white-box equivalence oracle with PAC sampling over trees. This makes the method applicable to transformers and any acceptor exposing binary decisions. They also identify a blindness of the original framework to behavior outside the most permissive VPG and propose fixes, contributing to formal verification of neural language models.

entry.title: From Weapons to Events: Evaluating Evidential Support in Multimodal AI for Policing

author.name: Armin Mustafa, Syed Sameed Husain

entry.summary: The paper presents KnifeHunter, a dataset of over 25,000 images across 543 knife classes developed with UK law enforcement, plus KHNet, a retrieval architecture achieving 85.7% and 63.4% mAP on medium and hard protocols with about 125,000 distractors. At the event level, it introduces an evaluation protocol for multimodal video-understanding pipelines that describe evidential support in body-worn video review. The work aims to make BWV review faster and more accountable.

entry.title: CPNav: Calibrated Vision-Language Navigation for Object-Goal Search in Unseen Environments

author.name: Qizhao Chen, Yuanhong Zeng, Shoh Nishino, Anushri Dixit

entry.summary: CPNav combines collision-aware planning with statistically calibrated VLM action scoring for map-free object-goal navigation in unseen environments. It builds a navigability map from RGB-D input, generates collision-free motion primitives, and calibrates VLM scores offline via conformal prediction using oracle actions from tree-structured exploration with backtracking. The approach addresses overconfident VLM decisions in embodied navigation.

entry.title: Think or Remember: The Exchange Rate of Agentic Inference

author.name: Juan Wisznia, Santiago Luis Groba Alonso, Mat\'ias G\'omez Taddeo, Gonzalo Zabaleta, Joaqu\'in Cullen, Luciano Del Corro

entry.summary: The paper builds an exact cost model for agentic inference where the client decides which messages to retain and the server decides whether earlier reasoning returns in the prompt, defining a ratio P* = c/beta per processed token versus attended pair as an exchange rate between a thinking regime and a memory regime. It distinguishes mechanical cost of a policy change from behavioral cost and validates the model against an instrumented engine.

entry.title: Slim Foundation Models for Latency-Critical Recommendation Serving

author.name: Danyal Aftab, Anas Zafar, Assadig Abakr, Steven Davy

entry.summary: SlimFM makes online LLM-based semantic modeling feasible for CTR prediction by pruning LLaMA3-8B by 44% via dependency-aware structured pruning into a 4.5B backbone, followed by LoRA-based field-aware fine-tuning to output discriminative features. This avoids the prohibitive inference cost that has pushed prior LLM-enhanced CTR methods to offline caching.

entry.title: TLRS-DPO: Token-Level Risk Scoring for Better Direct Preference Optimization

author.name: Suxin Ji, Hungtao Wan

entry.summary: Augments DPO with token-level control by converting the policy-reference log-ratio on rejected responses into localized risk scores, adding a curriculum-style schedule that gradually increases compensation strength, and a risk-aware mechanism. The method remains fully offline and reference-based, aiming to suppress local unsafe patterns in otherwise acceptable responses.

entry.title: MOMENT-DP: Momentum Aware Evaluation of Correlated Noise for Differentially Private Training

author.name: Sunny Gupta, Raja Viswanadha

entry.summary: MOMENT-DP is an optimizer-state-aware framework modeling how temporally correlated privacy noise propagates through momentum-based optimization, expressing privacy-induced final loss via an optimizer transfer operator for locally quadratic objectives. It shows that persistent optimizer state changes the relative utility ranking of correlated-noise mechanisms in differentially private training.

entry.title: A Physical Testbed for Self-Driving Laboratories: Comparing Bayesian and Agentic Optimization in a Minimal Closed-Loop Color Formulation Task

author.name: Tony Qin, Ziheng Wu, Maximilian Schommer, Roya Amini-Naieni, Aldair Gongora

entry.summary: The authors build a physical testbed for self-driving laboratories that integrates commercially available lab automation into a closed-loop design-build-test-learn workflow, demonstrated with 24 cumulative hours of unattended operation. They validate it on a color formulation task, comparing Bayesian optimization against agentic LLM-driven optimization.

entry.title: EmoHarness: Boosting Multimodal Emotion Understanding with Meta-Harness Evolving

author.name: Fenghai Li, Bingxuan Li, Jiawen Zhang, Yifan Shen, Jiateng Liu, Yutong Zhang, Yue Guo

entry.summary: EmoHarness wraps a frozen small multimodal model in an evolving harness where a stronger Builder LLM reads the student's errors and execution traces offline and edits prompts, settings, and verification code, with static checks and validation gates filtering edits without ever seeing evaluation items. It improves task-macro performance on 5,507 MME-Emotion items.

entry.title: Controlling Temporal Pseudo-Label Marginals for Stable Online Test-Time Adaptation

author.name: Rani Amar, Ofir Lindenbaum

entry.summary: The paper identifies shrinking pseudo-label class usage as a measurable indicator of continual test-time adaptation instability and proposes Sinkhorn Class-Marginal Regularization to explicitly enforce a target class marginal over temporal windows. This differs from prior sample-selection or loss-reweighting approaches and improves stability against drift and collapse.

entry.title: Safe Reinforcement Learning for Multi-Turn Clinical Agents: When Dense Rewards Beat Outcome Rewards

author.name: Brendan P. Murphy, Agustina Saenz

entry.summary: This paper studies RL with verifiable rewards in clinical multi-turn agents across three controlled environments with hidden clinical states, query costs, and deterministic outcome verifiers. It shows that outcome-only GRPO often improves aggregate reward while producing undesirable procedures such as premature commitment and one-question diagnosis, and that denser rewards mitigate these failure modes. The findings warn that outcome-reward training can degrade sequential decision procedures in safety-critical settings.

entry.title: 2D Gum-Net: Unsupervised Dense Elastic Image Registration via Symmetric Correlation and Spectral Pooling

author.name: Aarya Bhave, Anushka Ajay Bhave

entry.summary: The authors adapt Gum-Net, originally designed for 3D subtomogram alignment in cryo-electron tomography, to 2D dense elastic image registration in a fully unsupervised setting. The redesign uses symmetric correlation and spectral pooling to predict deformation fields without ground-truth annotations, addressing a key bottleneck in medical imaging and structural biology.

entry.title: MAGE: Towards Generalizable Multi-timescale EEG Representations

author.name: Tuan-Kiet Doan, Van-Chien Nguyen, Trung-Hieu Tran, Quang-Hung Pham, Ngoc-Son Vu, Huy Phan, Phi Le Nguyen, Duc-Han Le, Nikola Simidjievski, Van-Tam Nguyen

entry.summary: MAGE is an EEG foundation model that dynamically adapts to integrate information across multiple temporal timescales, unlike prior models fixed to a single scale. It combines mechanisms to capture neural dynamics spanning different timescales, aiming for stronger cross-dataset and cross-task generalization in brain-activity decoding.

entry.title: DisMUSE: An Efficient Distributed Singular-Spectrum-Based Optimization Approach with Theoretical Convergence Guarantee

author.name: Zhen Qin, Zhiyao Zhang, Yingbin Liang, Jia Liu

entry.summary: DisMUSE extends singular-spectrum-based (Muon-style) optimizers to distributed and federated settings, using exactly orthogonalized momentum with a distributed spectral estimator. The paper provides convergence guarantees and analyzes communication efficiency, addressing the open problem of scaling geometry-aware optimizers beyond centralized training.

entry.title: Match the Geometry Before the Surrogate: Extreme Low-Budget Optimization in High Dimensions

author.name: Michal Pr\r{u}\v{s}ek, Adam Novoz\'amsk\'y, Filip \v{S}roubek

entry.summary: The paper revisits low-budget molecular optimization with only 30 evaluations using a SELFIES VAE and GuacaMol objectives, finding that encoder means of reference molecules concentrate on a narrow spherical shell while common optimizers propose from box-shaped regions. A simple on-sphere constraint on candidate generation improves performance without a new surrogate model.

entry.title: Two-Sided Conformal Evidence Sets for Retrieval-Augmented Generation

author.name: Ben Jenkins, Mihaela Cardei

entry.summary: Conformal Evidence Sets (CES) extend calibrated grounding for RAG by returning separate support and refutation sets with finite-sample coverage guarantees on each side, using a Bonferroni union for joint coverage. Experiments on the contrastive VitaminC benchmark show close tracking of nominal coverage across multiple alpha levels.

entry.title: Dynamic State Estimation from Sparse PMUs via Physics-Informed Graph Neural Operators

author.name: Huy Hoang Le, Haoguang Wang, Christian Moya, Marcos Netto, Guang Lin

entry.summary: The paper proposes a physics-informed graph neural operator for power system dynamic state estimation that estimates rotor-angle and speed trajectories of all machines from sparse, intermittent measurements in one forward pass. Swing equations are imposed as hard or soft constraints, training uses simulated measurements without state labels, and the operator is the most accurate estimator on four transmission systems.

entry.title: JUBILEE: A Benchmark Environment for Off-Policy Evaluation in Debt Collections

author.name: Diego Silva Prado, Tiago Amaral Penteado de Jesus, Bruno Caldas de Souza, Cristiano Bevitori Maffia De Oliveira

entry.summary: JUBILEE is a benchmark environment for off-policy evaluation built on a debt-collections simulator producing million-loan panels with competing risks, rare recovery events, and hidden confounders. It includes an extensive evaluation of tabular and gradient-boosted OPE estimators with Monte Carlo reference values, filling a gap in realistic OPE benchmarking.

entry.title: ProtLink: Sequence and Multispecies Graph Context for Protein Interaction Prediction

author.name: Xingyuan Zhang

entry.summary: ProtLink combines frozen ESM-2 sequence representations with protein interaction topology and cross-species orthogroup connections for protein-protein interaction prediction. It compares several graph architectures and finds a multispecies heterogeneous graph transformer with ESM-2 650M features achieves an average precision of 0.980 under random negative sampling, dropping to 0.878 under a harder evaluation.

entry.title: EbbFlow: PINN-Inspired Progressive Curriculum for MeanFlow Training

author.name: Mengfan Yuan, Xunheng Kuang, Jianbin Chen, Lei He

entry.summary: EbbFlow improves MeanFlow training for few-step generative models by reinterpreting temporal coordinates as collocation points, distinguishing diagonal supervision from interval-based differential-consistency targets. It introduces Temporal Supervision Allocation, a curriculum that starts with diagonal supervision and progressively admits interior samples with expanding intervals, borrowing ideas from physics-informed machine learning. The result is a principled training schedule for flow-based few-step generation.

entry.title: CHANNELS4WORLD: An Environment-Scale Dataset for Wireless Foundation Models

author.name: Joonkyu Jang, Hyung-Joo Moon, Kwang Soon Kim, Seong-Lyun Kim, Jakob Hoydis, Robert W. Heath, Jr., Chan-Byoung Chae

entry.summary: Channels4World is a scene-centered dataset of 100,000 distinct outdoor RF scenes generated procedurally, linking environments and material assignments to 32 base-station and 16,384 user positions with aligned multipath records at 3.5 and 7 GHz. The corpus comprises over 52 billion physical BS-UE pairs and a 29-TB payload, designed to provide the environmental breadth that wireless foundation model pretraining needs. It is the first environment-scale resource of its kind for wireless ML.

entry.title: Payoff-Aware Prediction of Population Game Dynamics

author.name: Kang Wang, Xiao Wang, Bo Li, Renzhe Xu

entry.summary: The paper studies predicting how aggregate population behavior evolves under a new payoff function before any trajectory data under that payoff is available. Building on Riemannian game dynamics, the proposed PA-RmD method explicitly separates payoff-dependent incentives from payoff-independent response structure, enabling out-of-distribution prediction of game trajectories.

entry.title: FocusBranch: Combinatorial Branch-and-Bound for $\ell_0$ Neural Network Robustness Verification

author.name: Renwei Deng, Yang He, Linyi Li, Yuepeng Wang

entry.summary: FocusBranch is a branch-and-bound framework for verifying neural network robustness under l0-norm perturbations, built on a node abstraction that decomposes the l0-ball using a focus pixel set and a level. It unifies concrete branching through upper shadows and super-node branching through covering designs to cover many perturbation cases efficiently.

entry.title: UCB-min: Combining Bandits Under Variance Heterogeneity (Extended Version)

author.name: Lilia Izri, Benoit Groz, Silviu Maniu

entry.summary: The paper proposes UCB-min, a bandit algorithm that combines variance-independent and variance-aware exploration strategies to handle unknown and heterogeneous reward variances across arms. It addresses the case where no single rule is uniformly best, offering robustness when variances are small while retaining tightness when variance estimates are reliable.

entry.title: TACTUS: A Robotic Palpation System for Spatially Heterogeneous Hardness Mapping of Woody Breast Myopathy

author.name: Chaitanya Pallerla, Yihong Feng, Avisekh Tripathy, Yang Tian, Pouya Sohrabipour, Amirreza Davar, Casey M. Owens, Cengiz Koparan, Dongyi Wang

entry.summary: TACTUS is an automated tactile array with 20 independently motorized tactuators, force-sensing resistors, and a LiDAR depth camera that generates thickness-normalized 3D hardness maps of poultry meat in about 30 seconds. It addresses spatially heterogeneous hardness characterization in woody breast myopathy, a quality problem for the poultry industry.

entry.title: Where Does Alignment Emerge and What Does It Mean? A Closer Look at the Platonic Representation Hypothesis

author.name: Julia Herbst, Simon Roschmann, Quentin Bouniot, Zeynep Akata

entry.summary: This work investigates where cross-modal representation alignment emerges across layers and dimensions, revisiting the Platonic Representation Hypothesis with controls for depth and width confounds in similarity metrics. The authors find the capability-alignment trend persists for newer language models provided captions are sufficiently compositional/rich. The paper clarifies when and why unimodal models converge toward shared representations.

entry.title: Counting Events, Not Seeing Them: Diagnosing and Repairing the Readout Failure in Video LLMs

author.name: Dongwu Qian

entry.summary: Using synthetic testbeds with validated labels, the paper shows that video LLMs' failure at counting object crossings is not purely missing object permanence: linear probes decode per-window presence at 93%, but global count decoding collapses to a duration confound, indicating a representation-output dissociation. Two readout-directed repairs raise same-object counting from 46.7% toward the 66.7% oracle on a benchmark. The work reframes a perceived perception failure as a partially repairable readout failure.

entry.title: Adaptive Budgeted Data Acquisition for Robust Off-Policy Evaluation from Multiple Loggers

author.name: Amitakshar Biswas, Ruoqing Zhu

entry.summary: The paper studies off-policy evaluation when data must be purchased from multiple logging policies with heterogeneous costs, proposing an Adaptive Greedy algorithm that sequentially buys the observation with the best cost-normalized variance reduction. The authors prove each purchase approximates a conditional-gradient step and establish convergence guarantees for the empirical allocation.

entry.title: PhysDNet: Physics-Driven Gradient Amplification for Real-Time Image Dehazing

author.name: Rayen Dhahri, Lei Sun, Victor Javier Kartsch Morinigo, Alice Pagnoux, Luca Benini, Danda Pani Paudel, Luc Van Gool

entry.summary: PhysDNet is a lightweight multimodal dehazing network fusing near-infrared imagery with sparse LiDAR depth, trained with a physics-constrained dual-head objective. Differentiating through a fixed Koschmieder inversion induces density-adaptive gradient amplification that concentrates learning on heavily degraded regions without increasing inference cost, enabling real-time edge deployment.

entry.title: Matchability-Aware Conformal Prediction for Open-Ended Language Model Generation

author.name: Ilia Azizi

entry.summary: CAELUM is a framework for calibrated uncertainty in open-ended LLM generation that builds semantic prediction sets while separating aleatoric from epistemic uncertainty. It samples answers via an ensemble of clarification prompts, clusters them by semantic equivalence, estimates uncertainty components with kernel-based von Neumann entropy, and calibrates nonconformity scores using split conformal prediction with an instance-dependent weighting. A fitted coefficient minimizes prediction set size.

entry.title: Optimal Polynomial-Query Approximation for Consistent Submodular Maximization with Short Lookahead

author.name: Vaneet Aggarwal

entry.summary: Establishes tight approximation bounds for consistent submodular maximization under streaming arrivals with bounded recourse and polynomial query budgets. Shows lookahead raises the best achievable ratio from 2-sqrt(2) to 1-1/e for both deterministic and randomized algorithms.

entry.title: Learning calibrated probabilistic forecasts using Koopman mode decomposition and the continuous ranked probability score

author.name: Benjamin M. Kent, Richard E. Turner

entry.summary: Combines Koopman mode decomposition with probabilistic ML architectures to forecast nonlinear dynamical systems, training directly on the continuous ranked probability score to produce calibrated predictive distributions. Validated on nonlinear ODE benchmarks relevant to fluid dynamics and weather prediction.

entry.title: How Far Must a Test Explore? Certifying Composable Read-Write Interfaces from Their Own Random Edits

author.name: Jiaxuan Guo, Xingyu Ren, Jingxin Yang, Youran Sun, Haizhao Yang

entry.summary: This paper studies random testing of stateful code interfaces where random writes generate the query distribution, a setting where existing self-testing and stability theorems do not apply. It asks how far a test must explore before passing laws, such as reading back a written value, actually certifies that the code behaves like a record. The paper derives exploration bounds for interfaces of m binary variables with read and write operations.

entry.title: GPU-Accelerated Non-Interactive Encrypted Neural Network Training with Batched Diagonal Packing

author.name: Kentaro Mihara

entry.summary: This paper trains neural networks under homomorphic encryption entirely non-interactively, combining rectangular diagonal packing, feature-major SIMD batching, baby-step giant-step evaluation, and a CUDA-accelerated CKKS implementation in Rust. Device-resident bootstrapping cuts a 100-update MNIST training run from about 14,268 to 293 seconds, a 48.68x speedup with bit-exact decoded parameters. The MIT-licensed implementation lowers the barrier for privacy-preserving training research.

entry.title: Learning inexact alternating minimization for convex problems with quadratic coupling

author.name: Paul H\"ausner, Jevgenija Rudzusika, Jens Sj\"olund, Ozan \"Oktem

entry.summary: This paper proposes learning inexact alternating minimization schemes where neural networks approximate the inner subproblem solutions at each iteration. For convex problems with quadratically coupled blocks, the authors derive worst-case bounds on the optimality gap identifying the per-iteration errors each network should greedily minimize, and combine these with PAC-Bayes analysis for high-probability fixed-horizon guarantees. It provides theory for learned optimizers with convergence assurances.

entry.title: LongCapHarness: Capability-Guided Auto-Harnessing for Long-Context Reasoning

author.name: Tao Zhang, Yuhang He

entry.summary: LongCapHarness improves long-context reasoning in LLMs without data synthesis or post-training by recursively revising capability primitives, capability state, and control logic through self-improvement on a development set. Applied to Llama3-8B and transferred to Qwen2.5-3B, it substantially outperforms recent data-centric and post-training approaches. The framework reframes long-context enhancement as capability harnessing rather than model modification.

entry.title: WarBias: A Bilingual LLM Benchmark of Stereotypes About Internally Displaced People and Veterans

author.name: Viktoriia Makovska, Tetiana Zakharchenko, Oleksandra Ostafiichuk

entry.summary: WarBias is a Ukrainian-English benchmark of 1,007 stereotype-counter-stereotype items about veterans and internally displaced people, two groups absent from legally protected characteristic lists used in social bias evaluation. Built from a taxonomy of 120 stereotype claims grounded in research reports, it extends bias evaluation to war-affected populations.

entry.title: CaseLaw: A Policy-Decoupled Framework for Training-Free Content Moderation

author.name: Qi Lu, Sen Li, Likun Shi, Xiaolong Jiang

entry.summary: CaseLaw reformulates content moderation as precedent-based retrieval and voting, converting multimodal content into evidence-preserved structured semantics embedded in a stable space and classified via thresholded voting over retrieved precedents. It is policy-decoupled and training-free, avoiding costly rule rewriting or retraining, supported by a NoteCap corpus of structurally annotated notes.

entry.title: Can Frontier Auto Researchers Reconstruct Human Research Decisions in AI?

author.name: Shengyun Si, Junjie Chu, Ye Leng, Yang Zhang

entry.summary: This study evaluates auto-research agent systems by asking whether, given comparable research context, their research decisions and outputs match those of human experts, framed as research reconstruction. It investigates how closely end-to-end autonomous research workflows in AI align with human decision-making, an underexplored evaluation axis beyond raw task completion. The work offers a new lens for assessing agentic research capabilities.

entry.title: CHO-Bench: How Do Context Hints Affect Ad Rankings in LLM Advertising?

author.name: Shiqi Zhang, Yang Fei, Xiaokui Xiao

entry.summary: The paper formalizes Context Hint Optimization (CHO) as the problem of constructing natural-language context hints to improve an advertisement's ranking in LLM-based advertising systems like ChatGPT Ads under a budget constraint. Drawing on marketing frameworks, it develops seven hint-generation strategies covering What, Who, and When, plus a unified strategy, evaluated on the CHO-Bench benchmark. It matters as one of the first systematic studies of an emerging, economically significant LLM application surface.

entry.title: Representation Learning for 3D Brain Imaging: A Benchmark

author.name: Pierre Falconnier (MYRIAD), Robin Trombetta (MYRIAD), Nicolas Duchateau (MYRIAD), Carole Lartizien (MYRIAD)

entry.summary: This benchmark paper from MYRIAD presents an extensive comparison of vision encoders and self-supervised pre-training strategies for 3D brain imaging, addressing the domain gap between natural 2D image pre-training and volumetric medical data. It evaluates feature-extraction performance across 3D volumes with an emphasis on standardized evaluation of self-supervised and foundation-model approaches. It matters because medical imaging lacks the standardized pre-training benchmarks that drove progress in natural-image vision.

entry.title: Domain Generalization for Style-Debiased Object Detection via Label-Consistent Training across Multiple Styles

author.name: Chaoran Zhang, Shirshak Bhusal, Zhilin Gao, Qiang Xue, Haoting Shen

entry.summary: Introduces OAMSC, a source-only domain generalization framework for object detection that combines multi-style data synthesis using diffusion models with cross-style consistency learning to suppress style-sensitive shortcut learning. The approach is motivated by human perception, which ignores irrelevant style cues, and trains models that remain consistent across multiple styles.

entry.title: SRA: Spatial Reasoning Adapter via Evolving Social Interaction Graphs for Trajectory Prediction

author.name: Jaewoo Jeong, Seonkyu Song, Hyeonwoo Park, Jegyeong Cho, Yujin Bae, Giwon Lee, Daehee Park, Kuk-Jin Yoon

entry.summary: SRA is a modular graph denoiser adapter for multi-agent trajectory prediction that re-evaluates inter-agent interaction graphs at every reverse diffusion or flow-matching step, rather than reading interactions once from the observed past. It plugs into existing predictors without redesigning their generative cores.

entry.title: Latent-WAM++: Shaping World and Action Representations for End-to-End Autonomous Driving

author.name: Yichen Zhang, Yupeng Zheng, Linbo Wang, Pengxuan Yang, Zebin Xing, Junli Wang, Shiwei Li, Kangwei Liu, Fan Ren, Qichao Zhang, Yifeng Pan, Ji Tao, Dongbin Zhao

entry.summary: Latent-WAM++ is a representation-centered World Action Model for end-to-end autonomous driving that aligns supervision of intermediate world and action representations with their planning roles. It combines scene-ego future prediction with SIGReg-based distribution stabilization and frozen geometric priors, plus a MeanFlow-based trajectory planner predicting multimodal proposals.

entry.title: DynOLAT: OLAT Video Prediction for Controllable Dynamic Full-Body Relighting

author.name: Taoming Liu, Yinji ShenTu, Guangzhao He, Yudong Jin, Yukang Ye, Siyu Zhang, Fan Jia, Wei Hua, Hujun Bao, Xiaowei Zhou

entry.summary: DynOLAT predicts one-light-at-a-time video sequences for dynamic full-body human relighting, improving physical accuracy of shadow direction and relative light intensity over methods that merely harmonize appearance. It targets generalizable, controllable relighting rather than single-image synthesis.

entry.title: Martine: Benchmarking Multi-View 3D Surface Reconstruction Across Viewpoint Coverage, Resolution, and Lighting

author.name: Robin Bruneau, Baptiste Brument, Frederic Giraud, Bastian Sigrist, Sascha Jecklin, Philipp F\"urnstahl, Bjoern Menze, Lilian Calvet

entry.summary: Martine is a controlled benchmark for multi-view 3D surface reconstruction that jointly varies viewpoint coverage, image resolution, and illumination with accurate 3D ground truth and quantified image-to-geometry alignment, addressing biases in existing benchmarks that restrict acquisition regimes. It enables fairer comparisons across reconstruction paradigms.

entry.title: Benchmarking CNNs, Vision Transformers, and Foundation Models for Explainable Brain Tumor MRI Classification: Calibration, Decision Analysis, and External Validation

author.name: Akwasi Asare

entry.summary: A careful benchmark of six architectures (CNNs, vision transformers, and foundation models including DINOv2-L and MedSigLIP-448) for four-class brain tumor MRI classification, evaluating accuracy, calibration, explainability, ensembles, and decision curves with validation-only estimation. Pixel-verified duplicate screening revealed that 36% of test images had near-duplicates in training data, and test accuracy differences across architectures were not significant after correction.

entry.title: EgoLabel: Zero-Shot Egocentric Auto-Labeling with Cross-Modal Consistency

author.name: Xiaozhi Zhang, Changjia Xu, Yaoyuan Yan, Haoxiang Jie, Bingjie Fu

entry.summary: EgoLabel is a zero-shot pipeline for egocentric auto-labeling that composes off-the-shelf models (MonST3R, LocateAnything, SAM 2, V-HPOT) without target-domain training, adding explicit cross-modal registration and consistency diagnostics to resolve unit, coordinate, and scale mismatches between independently developed models. It provides a demonstration with fisheye ViT and evaluates hand-related labels using H2O sensor depth.

entry.title: Plant Orbiter: 3D Plant Reconstruction and Generation with Video Diffusion Orbit Cameras and 3D Gaussian Splatting

author.name: Zane K. J. Hartley, Yong En Kok, Lewis A. G. Stuart, Andrew P. French, Michael P. Pound

entry.summary: Plant Orbiter generates 3D Gaussian Splats of plants from a single image by leveraging video diffusion models with orbit camera conditioning, targeting high-throughput digital phenotyping of 3D morphological traits. The approach addresses the difficulty of reconstructing thin structures and occlusions in plant morphology.

entry.title: Noise-Regularized Training for Learned Image Compression

author.name: Renjie Zou, Zhiwei Huang, Dong Jiang

entry.summary: This paper introduces noise-regularized training for learned image compression, adding Gaussian noise to the encoder input at every training step while keeping the distortion target clean, drawing on the line of work from Tikhonov regularization to denoising score matching. The noise acts as a structured probe of the data manifold rather than data augmentation.

entry.title: Single-Radar Bilateral 3D Near-Field Imaging for Mobile Robots

author.name: Yingqi Wang, Tingwei Chen, Zhongqin Wang, Min Xu

entry.summary: This paper presents a motion-assisted framework for reconstructing 3D structures on both sides of a robot's path using a single forward-mounted millimeter-wave radar. A near-field model relates scene reflectivity to stepped-frequency MIMO observations across frequencies and robot positions, overcoming near-field wavefront curvature and limited elevation diversity.

entry.title: AutoVLA-D: Learn a Trajectory-Geometric Condition from Reasoning for Autonomous Driving VLA

author.name: Yuguang Yang, Zhewen Tan, Canyu Chen, Linlin Yang, Cheng Chi, Chunyang Liu, Kehua Sheng, Jinyu Yang, Baochang Zhan, Bo Zhang, Yan Wang, Xianbin Cao

entry.summary: AutoVLA-D introduces TrajCond, a discrete trajectory-geometric condition learned via a two-stage framework before final continuous trajectory prediction in autoregressive VLA driving planners. It uses a 1D-Brohan differential action trajectory representation with simultaneous autoregressive generation of discrete and numeric trajectories, evaluated on NAVSIM, nuScenes, and NeuroNCAP.

entry.title: The forces at hand: social learning is permissive, not instructive, for the evolution of phenotypic plasticity

author.name: Nam H. Le

entry.summary: This theoretical paper analyzes whether social learning plays an instructive or permissive role in the evolution of phenotypic plasticity and the Baldwin effect. Using a minimal model of learning and evolution, it shows analytically and computationally that environmental change is the only source of benefit from plasticity, and that social learning enters only permissively.

entry.title: Burden, Bounty, or Bliss? Muscle-Aware Retargeting and Null-Space Exploration for Whole-Body Musculoskeletal Control

author.name: Ruiyang Kong, Takeshi Oishi

entry.summary: The paper proposes a motion-to-policy pipeline for learning whole-body musculoskeletal control from human motion, tackling two challenges: kinematically plausible but dynamically hard reference trajectories, and a highly redundant 700-dimensional muscle action space. It uses muscle-aware retargeting with bounded adaptation under hard semantic, anatomical, and contact constraints, combined with null-space exploration.

entry.title: PA-SaR: Perception-Aware Learning, Control, and Coordination for Multi-Robot Search and Rescue

author.name: Jocubas Dimsa, Maria Grouev, Filip Keerberg, Nicolas Laplagne, Tigo Schutgens, Sven Schoonebeek, Anahita Jamshidnejad

entry.summary: PA-SaR is a framework coordinating heterogeneous components — local control, learning-based exploration, supervisory task allocation, and adaptive victim guidance — around mission-level objectives for multi-robot search and rescue. Notably, it analyzes how improving individual robot capabilities can worsen mission outcomes, such as safer motion restricting exploration. The framework distinguishes environmental ground truth, robot perception, and simulated victim models.

entry.title: Causal Machine Learning for Multilevel Studies with Unmeasured Cluster-Level Covariates via Variational Autoencoders

author.name: Youmi Suk, Yuxuan Li

entry.summary: Proposes VAE-R, a variational autoencoder-augmented R-learner that infers unmeasured cluster-level confounders from within-cluster dependence of outcome and treatment residuals, then uses the learned adjustments to estimate conditional and average treatment effects. The decoder uses an offset likelihood so latents capture only between-cluster variation. This targets unmeasured confounding in multilevel observational studies, a common setting in education and health research.

entry.title: How I'm thinking about extreme power concentration

author.name: NotFromConcentrate

entry.summary: A structured overview of extreme power concentration (EPC) risk from an AI safety practitioner, defining the concern as an individual or small group seizing power at a high-stakes moment and locking in bad values permanently. The post enumerates key dynamics: AI dissolving the loyalty-competence tradeoff in staffing, executive overhang, an asymmetric frontier where leaders get privileged AI access, instability inviting strongmen, and epistemic degradation. It aims to consolidate threat models and candidate interventions in one place.

entry.title: GOPR-CAD: Graph-of-Operations Progressive Reasoning for CAD Generation

author.name: Yitian Pang, Yifan Li, Xiaowei Yue, Li Zheng

entry.summary: GOPR-CAD is an agentic text-to-CAD pipeline where an LLM acts as a decision agent over a graph of encapsulated CAD operations rather than generating long CAD programs directly, addressing the unreliability of LLMs in coordinating coupled geometric, topological, and dimensional constraints. Progressive reasoning over the operation graph reduces structurally incorrect models that execution-rate and appearance metrics fail to catch. It targets more accurate and constraint-respecting CAD generation.

entry.title: Zero-Search Reinforcement Learning for Slay the Spire 2 with Failure-Driven Restarts

author.name: Xiangqin Chen, Zhengxuan Xie

entry.summary: Trains a 6.6M-parameter entity transformer to pick every action in Slay the Spire 2 with one forward pass and no lookahead, running the game's own compiled assembly headlessly with exact seed-based replay. A failure-driven curriculum allocates restarts to states where complete runs are lost, yielding 8.05 percent average wins at Ascension 10 over 12,800 held-out games.

entry.title: How Many Candidates Does a One-Step World Model Need? A Random-Codebook Account of Nearest-of-m Training on Frozen DINO Tokens

author.name: Yong Hwi Song, Keon Myung Lee

entry.summary: The paper tests recent conjectures about nearest-of-m matching, the simplest one-step stochastic world model objective based on conditional IMLE, using frozen DINOv2/v3 patch tokens and benchmarks with enumerable futures. Under mode-like uncertainty, m of 16 covers enumerated futures better than expected, challenging claims that small m suffices and that a proper energy score should replace the hard minimum.

entry.title: Simple Test-Time Refinement for Plot-to-Code Generation via Visual-Code Diagnostics

author.name: Peiming Guo, Jinpeng Huang, Yangbin Sun, Gaoxiong Cao, Ensheng Shi, Yuchi Ma, Yu Zhang, Meishan Zhang, Baotian Hu, Min Zhang

entry.summary: The authors present the first study of iterative test-time refinement for plot-to-code generation, proposing a Visual-Code Diagnostics framework that mimics the human generate-then-debug workflow. They categorize generation errors into four coarse types, train lightweight diagnostics components, and use visual feedback from rendered code to locate and fix errors at test time. This improves on one-pass generation and verifier-based sampling for multimodal LLMs.

entry.title: VLM as an Editing Pilot: VLM-Steered Velocity Control for Flow-Based Image Editing

author.name: Kuan-Shen Chiu, Jia-Wei Liao, Yu-Chieh Chao, Li-Xuan Peng, Wei-Yun Ma, Cheng-Fu Chou

entry.summary: V2C-Edit is a training-free framework for text-guided image editing that diagnoses the zero-edit failure mode of FlowEdit, where source-anchored velocity coupling keeps the output near the input and the requested change never emerges. The method constructs complementary coupling-controlled velocities and uses a VLM with instruction-level analysis to dynamically select among them per timestep. It matters because it turns a VLM into an active editor that adapts the preservation-editing trade-off instead of applying a fixed coupling schedule.

entry.title: CompositionEvidence: Controlling Geometric Evidence for Cinematic Composition Reasoning with Frozen Vision-Language Models

author.name: Yichen He, Xin Huang, Yuxi Liu

entry.summary: The paper shows that naively injecting geometric evidence can hurt frozen VLMs on cinematic composition questions (dropping Qwen2.5-VL-7B accuracy), and proposes CompositionEvidence, which derives nine reproducible geometric features from frozen detection, depth, and line experts. A training-free gated channel improves ShotBench accuracy to 56.2 percent with statistical significance and robustness under corrupted evidence.

entry.title: UltraVoxelGS: Voxel-First Feed-Forward Gaussian Splatting for 3D Ultrasound Reconstruction

author.name: Yue Wang, Haoxin Chen, Xiaoqing Guo

entry.summary: UltraVoxelGS is a feed-forward Gaussian splatting method for 3D ultrasound reconstruction that predicts a complete Gaussian scene representation from posed ultrasound images directly, bypassing per-scene optimization and enabling live spatial feedback during 2D scanning. It overcomes ultrasound-specific violations of dense-overlap and photometric assumptions, since slices share at most one-dimensional intersections and exhibit view-dependent acoustic appearance.

entry.title: ReVMap: Vectorized Global Mapping via Connectivity-Aware Local Map Fusion

author.name: Hongjae Shin, Jungho Kim, Donghyuk Kwak, Myeongjun Kim, Seunghoon Yu, Jiyong Oh, Jun Won Choi

entry.summary: ReVMap is a local-to-global framework for auto-labeling vectorized HD maps that iteratively refines local map predictions and global map construction using uncertainty-guided prior utilization and connectivity-guided global map revision. It addresses the problem that existing methods ignore prediction uncertainty and use heuristic integration, which propagates errors and creates topological inconsistencies.

entry.title: Graph-Sparse Distributed Predictive Control for Multi-Robot Motion Planning vianEdge-Consensus ADMM

author.name: Josep Borras-Borras, Pablo Segovia, Carlos Ocampo-Martinez

entry.summary: This paper presents a distributed MPC architecture for collision-avoiding motion planning of planar robots, using a time-varying predicted conflict graph to select relevant pairwise interactions, convexified constraints producing a fixed QP, and edge-consensus ADMM for parallel robot-local optimization. Closed-form projections onto separating half-spaces enable efficient computation, with selective centralized supervision. It reduces coordination demands in multi-robot motion planning.

entry.title: AYO: A Safe and Privacy-Preserving Platform for Studying Children's Interaction with LLMs

author.name: Huiwen Alex Yang, Rachel Skwersky, Bill D. Thompson, Celeste Kidd

entry.summary: AYO (AI Youth Open Science) is an open-source platform enabling safe, systematic research on children's interactions with conversational AI, with age-based safety guardrails, researcher monitoring, and privacy-preserving data practices.
