It addresses a real gap, since most prior work relies on surveys rather than direct observation of child-LLM interactions.

entry.title: AVCORP: Identifying and Resisting Deception via Communication Theory and Theory of Mind

author.name: Fardin Saad, Zhe Zhang, Sanjana Cheerla, Amanul Haque, Munindar P. Singh

entry.summary: AVCORP is a corpus of 5,000 annotated utterances from 250 games of Avalon, mapping 37 deception tactics to a behavior matrix and capturing reasoning traces with abductive hypotheses, suspicion levels, and nested Theory of Mind beliefs. Training Qwen3-8B on the corpus yields deception detectors that outperform untrained baselines on held-out and human-played games.

entry.title: Ensemble Routing for Prompt-Adaptive Cost-Aware LLM Inference

author.name: Saul Urso, Emanuele Carlini, Patrizio Dazzi, Matteo Mordacchini

entry.summary: The paper introduces PISA, a prompt-adaptive cost-aware single-model router, and PISA-E, which extends routing to adaptive ensembles whose composition and cardinality are jointly selected under an explicit cost-quality preference adjustable at inference time without retraining. It improves on one-model-per-prompt routing and fixed ensembles that cannot adapt to individual requests.

entry.title: SituRecBench: Evaluating Frontier Models as Situated Recommendation Assistants in 3D Environments

author.name: Jingtong Yang, Dongding Lin, Jian Wang, Wenjie Li

entry.summary: SituRecBench is an interactive benchmark evaluating frontier vision-language models as situated recommendation assistants in high-fidelity 3D shopping environments, requiring spatial navigation, visual grounding, and multi-turn social interaction from an egocentric shared view. It reframes recommendation as an embodied assistance process rather than static retrieval. It matters because it tests a combination of capabilities largely ignored by prior recommendation benchmarks.

entry.title: MMGraph-Agent: Agentic Multimodal RAG via Cache-Inspired Multimodal Knowledge HyperGraphs

author.name: Haoran Luo, Ziyue Zhu, Shangyang Wu, Linhao Luo, Yikai Guo, Qika Lin, Fangzhi Xu, Jiapu Wang, Xiaobao Wu, Yifan Zhu, Luu Anh Tuan

entry.summary: Presents MMGraph-Agent, a unified multimodal RAG framework using cache-inspired multimodal knowledge hypergraphs that support lightweight zero-API-cost construction and dynamic memory-based retrieval to mitigate long-context limitations. Reports experiments across multiple benchmarks.

entry.title: R-BED: A Consequence-Aware Framework for System-Level AI Evaluation and Continuous Assurance

author.name: Vishal Srivastava

entry.summary: Presents R-BED (Risk-Based Evaluability Design), a specification-level methodology with a fixed 6+4+3 architecture of thirteen diagnostic dimensions covering technical failure, deployment controls, and consequence, connecting evidence about failures and controls to defensible deployment authorization decisions across a system's lifecycle. It separates failure-mediated expected-loss from intended-behavior and misuse pathways.

entry.title: Inference for Reasoning Models: Practical Lessons from Evaluation and Serving

author.name: Luv Verma

entry.summary: A book-style practical treatment of how inference settings shape reported and deployed behavior of reasoning models, covering evaluation (generation limits, answer extraction, scoring, quantization) and serving (batching, memory, backends, caching), including a striking experiment where changing only maximum response length moved a math benchmark accuracy from 0.08% to 93.18%.

entry.title: How Short Is Too Short? Length-Conditional Calibration and Abstention for Detecting AI-Generated Text

author.name: Ritesh Janga, Justin Zhan

entry.summary: This work analyzes AI-generated text detection as a function of passage length, giving closed-form results for how false-positive rates change as text shortens and how many tokens are needed for a target true-positive rate. It proposes length-binned threshold calibration using conformal p-values plus an abstention rule for lengths where detection is uninformative, validated on zero-shot detectors. This addresses a practical gap since most detectors are tuned on long passages.

entry.title: Can the Remaining Answers Change the Prediction? Worst-Case Stability Checks for Personalized Rating Models

author.name: Priyanka Siddappa, Muntaqim Ahmed Raju, Shifat Haider Al Amin, Ruizhe Ma

entry.summary: For personalized models with additive response scores, the paper derives exact worst-case bounds over all missing rating assignments, auditing whether unseen answers could overturn the current prediction. It evaluates the audit retrospectively in clinician triage and counseling-annotation cohorts, showing Fisher adaptation reduces log loss relative to frequency-based baselines.

entry.title: Enhancing Multi-Step Chemical Mechanism Prediction with Graph-Guided Preference Data

author.name: Yu Zhang, Ruijie Yu, Xuelin Zhao, Jinming Yang, Feng Zhu, Xiaokang Yang, Yaohui Jin, Yanyan Xu

entry.summary: This work builds a graph-guided framework for predicting multi-step chemical reaction mechanisms using a new chemical mechanism knowledge graph (ChemMechKG) to steer LLMs, plus a graph neural network predictor generating candidate pathways. A relation retrieval module supports inference, addressing the limitation of prior single-step reaction prediction methods.

entry.title: Toward Sustainable Agentic AI: Carbon Tradeoffs Across Iterative Self-Refinement and Tool-Augmented Coding

author.name: Boris Ruf, Adrien de Mailly Nesle, Marcin Detyniecki

entry.summary: Two empirical studies quantify the energy and carbon footprint of agentic strategies: iterative verbal self-refinement with GPT-4.1-mini on MATH splits, and tool-augmented coding with GPT-4.1-mini, Claude Opus 4.6, and GPT-5.3-codex on SWE-bench Lite inside grounded environments. The work maps when accuracy gains from self-refinement and tool use are worth their environmental cost.

entry.title: TANSAR: Editable and Attributable Correlation Matrix Memories under Correlated Keys, with Rule-Constrained Multi-Hop Knowledge Editing

author.name: Abdulhady Abas Abdulla, Jiyan Salim Mahmud, Fatemeh Daneshfar, Hussein Mohammed Ali, Mourad Oussalah, Muhammad Bilal

entry.summary: This work analyzes correlation matrix memories (CMMs) when keys are correlated, as produced by real semantic encoders, deriving capacity bounds, an exact characterization of deletion collateral effects, and geometric transparency bounds for attribution. It then builds a rule-constrained multi-hop knowledge editing system on top of this theory. The work matters because classical associative memory analyses assume orthogonal keys, which real encoders violate.

entry.title: LogCDM: Interpretable Log Anomaly Detection via Behavioral Graph Drift and Adaptive Signal Fusion

author.name: Suryansh Talukdar, Taha Sarwat, Jin Soung Yoo

entry.summary: LogCDM is a compact log anomaly detector designed to run on monitoring nodes without GPUs, contrasting with BERT-scale or 8B-parameter models. It scores each session using three complementary signals: next-event surprise from a small causal Transformer, graph-attention embedding distance, and a transition-drift statistic shown to be exactly a frequency-weighted chi-squared divergence with an asymptotic null distribution. This efficiency and statistical grounding is valuable for practical monitoring.

entry.title: EarthJev: Efficient Visual Evidence Acquisition and Decision for UHR Remote Sensing Understanding

author.name: Pengyu Dai, Yao Zhang, Jian Song, Junjue Wang, Yafei Ou, Yuzeng Chen, Junshi Xia, Hongruixuan Chen, Naoto Yokoya

entry.summary: Proposes EarthJev, a framework for ultra-high-resolution remote sensing visual question answering that separates region scoring from answer generation and applies target-specific decision signals (spatial pointer validity, evidence presence, reasoning correctness) while keeping the answering model frozen. A spatial pointer verifier guides selective exploration to reduce the cost of repeated generative judgments during evidence search.

entry.title: GSynPEF: A Privacy Evaluation Framework for Synthetic Graphs

author.name: Yu Duan, Luca Baldesi, Carter T. Butts, Athina Markopoulou

entry.summary: GSynPEF is a practical framework for empirically evaluating privacy and utility of synthetic graphs generated from real-world inputs. It links a broad class of graph synthesizers, both statistical and deep-learning based, with privacy metrics, expanding evaluation to practical utility and risk dimensions while accounting for output variation. It addresses a gap between synthesizer design and rigorous privacy assessment for network data release.

entry.title: Longtail-SWE: High-Quality SWE Tasks for Underrepresented Languages

author.name: Vladimir Dobrovolskii, Ibragim Badertdinov, Alexander Golubev

entry.summary: Longtail-SWE is a benchmark of 202 repository-level issue-resolution tasks across 13 underrepresented programming languages including Clojure, Haskell, Erlang, and OCaml. Construction uses a solver-judge-repairer pipeline where a judge reviews solver trajectories and test results to fix defective tests and ambiguous descriptions, avoiding the data loss typical of filtered scarce candidates. It extends software-engineering evaluation beyond Python-centric ecosystems.

entry.title: AFVE-Bench: Measuring Abandoned-Frame Verbalization Errors in Multi-Turn LLM Revision

author.name: Jiaming Chu

entry.summary: AFVE-Bench evaluates abandoned-frame verbalization errors, where a model adopts a new organizing frame in multi-turn revision but still exposes the superseded one, a failure existing instruction-following benchmarks miss. It uses 192 matched four-turn dialogues across eight writing domains in English and Chinese with controlled request histories. This fills a real gap in evaluating long-horizon instruction following and revision consistency.

entry.title: Tiny Evidence Region Localization with Selective Contrastive On-Policy Self-Distillation

author.name: Yujuan Pang, Wenhao Xu, Yinglei Teng

entry.summary: The paper proposes SPN-OPSD, a selective positive-negative on-policy self-distillation method for multimodal LLMs that supervises both evidence regions and background regions. Selective token-level distillation improves resistance to interference from irrelevant regions and strengthens fine-grained localization of tiny image evidence.

entry.title: Unified Framework with Convex-Concave Decomposition and Sparse Topological Learning for Skeleton-Based Clinical Assessment

author.name: Quang-Anh N. D., Duc Pham Minh, Minh-Anh Nguyen, Hien Quang Kha, Manh Hung Ha, Minhhuy Le, Oscal Tzyh-Chiang Chen

entry.summary: CC2-STG is a multi-stream graph convolutional framework for skeleton-based rehabilitation assessment that decomposes joint relationships into convex and concave distance functions, uses sparse regularization with proximal optimization to select clinically relevant geometric features, and performs multi-scale adaptive topology analysis.

entry.title: Selective Cooperative Perception via Blind Spot Reasoning and Agentic Dialogue with Vision-Language Models

author.name: Chengyuan Ma, Shixiao Liang, Hangyu Li, Zheng Li, Hang Zhou, Keke Long, Bofeng Cao, Zhaohui Liang, Xiaopeng Li

entry.summary: The paper proposes a VLM-driven agentic framework for selective cooperative perception in multi-agent traffic, triggering communication only for safety-critical blind-spot scenarios involving impactful occlusions. A mixed-model architecture combines conventional object detection, vision-language reasoning about occlusions, and physical plausibility checks to reduce the resource burden of real-time cooperative perception.

entry.title: Hybrid Source Code Change Impact Analysis

author.name: Katharina Stengg, Christian Macho, Martin Pinzger

entry.summary: The authors address dataset limitations in change impact analysis by manually labeling 1,931 changed code entities from 263 commits across 22 open-source Java projects, then introduce two variants of katIA, which combines static impact analysis with LLM reasoning. The hybrid approach aims to improve on prior CIA methods that suffer from either low precision or low recall.

entry.title: PIA: Agentic Physics-Informed Runtime Anomaly Detection

author.name: Ali Mohammadi Ruzbahani, Abbas Yazdinejad, Hadis Karimipour

entry.summary: PIA uses an LLM agent to write anomaly detectors as interpretable physical residuals (e.g., pump characteristics, tank mass balances, controller logic) for cyber-physical systems, refining candidates against normal operating data before deployment. The resulting detectors run in milliseconds, are human-readable, and attribute each alarm to a component, evaluated on the BATADAL water benchmark.

entry.title: Phase-Conditioned Reward Shaping for Token-Efficient LLM Reasoning

author.name: Zhe Chen, Xiaolin Zhou, Xiyang Hu

entry.summary: PCRS improves token efficiency in LLM reasoning by classifying response chunks into phases (reasoning, execution, revision) and modulating token-level length penalties by phase rather than penalizing length uniformly. Two classifier routes are explored: a hidden-state classifier (PCRS-H) and a frozen text classifier (PCRS-T).

entry.title: Disentangling Where and When:Factored Spatio-Temporal Explanations for Video Action Recognition

author.name: Bhavan Vasu, Giuseppe Raffa, Prasad Tadepalli

entry.summary: Introduces a perturbation-based post-hoc explanation framework for video action recognition that separates spatial appearance and temporal dynamics into two jointly optimized masks (appearance and motion), using nearest frame replacement, a separation penalty, and a ReLU-based area constraint. It also proposes evaluation methods for these disentangled explanations.

entry.title: MoT3DVG: A Benchmark for Outdoor 3D Visual Grounding with Motion-Aware Descriptions and Temporal Cues

author.name: Shijia Zhao, Xusheng Guo, Qiming Xia, Xun Huang, Kezheng Xiong, Zhihong Liu, Chenglu Wen

entry.summary: Introduces MoT3DVG, a large-scale dataset for dynamic outdoor 3D visual grounding with temporally evolving motion descriptions, built from 850 nuScenes scenarios with 31,128 frames and 144,568 language prompts. It also proposes DynaVG, a framework that uses temporal cues for grounding dynamic objects.

entry.title: Learning to Rank Propagators in Constraint Programming

author.name: Matija Lojovi\'c, Mladen Nikoli\'c

entry.summary: This work learns instance-dependent propagator priorities for constraint programming solvers by formulating the problem as learning-to-rank, where preferences are derived from solver runtimes under randomized propagation orders rather than directly observable labels. A self-attention model jointly scores propagators from static instance features.

entry.title: Weight-Space Programming of Variational Quantum Circuits: Large Language Models Write Quantum Circuit Parameters Without an Optimizer

author.name: Debarshi Kundu, Swaroop Ghosh, Vasant G Honavar

entry.summary: Extending weight-space programming from classical networks to variational quantum algorithms, the authors prompt a frontier LLM to directly write quantum circuit angles that are executed exactly as written, with no loss, gradient, or accuracy feedback. Across 139 requests spanning digit classification, VQE for spin chains and H2, and MaxCut QAOA, they compare against random weights, classical optimization, and LLM-warm-started optimization.

entry.title: Scalable Counterfactual Explanations for Time Series via Policy Learning

author.name: Peiyu Li, Pouya Hosseinzadeh, Soukaina Filali Boubrahimi, Shah Muhammad Hamdi

entry.summary: The authors train an actor-critic agent in the latent space of a pre-trained autoencoder to generate counterfactual explanations for time-series classifiers in a single forward pass, framing it as a one-step contextual-bandit problem. This replaces per-instance iterative optimization with a transferable learned policy that captures global structural regularities.

entry.title: HolidayFactory 1.0: Simulating, Generating, and Evaluating Industrial Robot Tasks

author.name: Holiday Robotics, :, Jeongmin Lee, Taehyeon Kim, Dohyun Jang, Minji Lee, Seonghun Oh, Dongwoo Park, Geonhyup Lee, Jaehyung Kim, Jaemin Yoon, Jinseop Bok, Jungwoo Kim, Minseok Yang, Philsik Chang, Soomin Lee

entry.summary: HolidayFactory 1.0 is a framework for simulating, generating, and evaluating industrial robot work that models repeated jobs with persistent scene state rather than reset-based episodes. It comprises HOLIDAY-SIM (extending Newton's hydroelastic contact simulation), a generation component, and an evaluation scheme defining jobs, metrics, and rubrics for a human-specified workplace and task.

entry.title: How Path Integral Diffusion Decides a Finite Spin Glass

author.name: Michael Chertkov

entry.summary: This theoretical paper shows that isotropic Path Integral Diffusion bridge models are time-changed Gaussian stochastic localization and that every signal-to-noise schedule is realizable by a PID protocol, meaning what the generator decides is protocol-independent while the protocol sets timing and cost. It describes the generator's evolving partial commitments to nested configuration classes as martingales, offering a rigorous account of how diffusion samplers settle macroscopic alternatives in frustrated systems.

entry.title: A Large-Scale Dataset for Cross-Lingual Multi-Jurisdiction Patent Drafting from Patent Cooperation Treaty Applications

author.name: Trung Phuong Le, Hirofumi Nonaka, Koji Marusaki, Katsuhito Sudoh, Seiya Kawano

entry.summary: Formulates cross-lingual patent drafting as generating jurisdiction- and prosecution-stage-specific claim sets, beyond simple translation, and releases a large-scale Japanese-English dataset built by linking Japan Patent Office and international PCT applications. This enables models that understand legal and stylistic conventions across patent offices.

entry.title: Thermo-VLA: A Thermal-Aware Vision-Language-Action Model with Gated Residual Modulation for Robotic Manipulation

author.name: Jingxuan Chen, Junshi Luo, Chencheng Dong, Xiaojian Nie, Tongge Huang, Qiang Huang

entry.summary: Proposes Thermo-VLA with a ThermoRes Encoder that decomposes thermal images into cold and hot attribute representations injected into RGB tokens via language-conditioned residual modulation, enabling temperature-aware relational reasoning in manipulation. It validates on six real-world tasks on a dual-arm Unitree G1 platform.

entry.title: GeoMind: A Benchmark for Spatial Understanding in Robotic Manipulation

author.name: Jinghe Wang, Xinrui Cao, Duo Wu, Chenghao Gu, Yong Zhong, Linjia Kang, Tianyi Xiong, Zhi Wang

entry.summary: GeoMind is a tabletop-manipulation benchmark testing spatial reasoning (identifying targets in complex layouts) and spatial memory (adapting to scenes evolving through interaction). It is designed to avoid strong visual cues that let agents bypass genuine spatial reasoning and covers dynamic rather than static scenes.

entry.title: Be My Eye: Learning to See Beyond a Robot's Own Perspective

author.name: Baifu Huang, Shilin Fang, Jianan Wang

entry.summary: The paper proposes a task-oriented active context sharing framework for multi-robot collaboration, where robots compress observations into compact representations that preserve task-relevant information given objectives and execution progress. This moves beyond raw-observation sharing to support collaborative decision-making under partial observability.

entry.title: dNaViT: Discrete Codes are General-Purpose Visual Representations

author.name: Xiaotong Li, Zhengrong Yue, Xu Huang, Jialv Zou, Minhao Jing, Wenhao Yan, Haodong Li, Hai Huang, Bo Zhao, Yan Feng, Peng Pei, Xunliang Cai

entry.summary: This paper introduces dNaViT, a Discrete Native-resolution Vision Transformer that converts visual content into discrete tokens analogous to language tokens, enabling autoregressive next-token prediction for vision. It builds on a frozen pretrained encoder with lightweight residual modulation and a dual-branch objective that injects reconstruction-aware cues into semantic features. The work matters because it advances the convergence of vision and language models on a unified discrete-token framework.

entry.title: AgentOPSD: Turn-Level Credit Assignment via Recursive Belief Revision

author.name: Yizhuo Li

entry.summary: AgentOPSD is a critic-free scheme that assigns credit at each interaction turn for multi-turn agent RL, addressing the coarseness of trajectory-level advantages in RL with verifiable rewards. Within a turn, token-level log-probability gaps between a skill-conditioned self-teacher and the student are summed and used as evidence in a recursive Bayesian log-odds update. This densifies supervision for long-horizon agent training without a learned critic.

entry.title: Library of Hands: Fix the Hands, Not the World Model

author.name: Hasaan Ahmad, Qizhen Ying, Yuxuan Sun, Tianjin Huang, Guangming Wang

entry.summary: This paper proposes Library of Hands, a training-free method that keeps a learned world model frozen and corrects only the map from commands to applied actions, called the hand, when the camera or controller changes. It reads the hand through the frozen model without extra sensors by finding the action that best explains observed scene changes, recovering performance when a frozen LeWM planner drops from 77.5 percent to 7.8 percent success under rotated commands. This addresses a practical failure mode of world-model planners without retraining.

entry.title: Learning Across Heterogeneous Feature Spaces with Group Robustness

author.name: Xenia Konti, Arjun Tschand, Chuan Hong, Nicoleta J. Economou-Zavlanos, Michael M. Zavlanos

entry.summary: The paper proposes a group robust learning framework for clinical data where groups are patients sharing a feature space, optimizing for worst-case group performance while accounting for uninformative features that cap achievable loss reduction. Unlike prior approaches, it enables knowledge transfer even when feature spaces are fully disjoint.

entry.title: Rethinking How to Leverage Cheap Physics for Data-Efficient Neural Operators

author.name: Shuo Zhang, Senwei Liang

entry.summary: The paper shows that using cheap physical information to actively select PDE inputs for labeling offers no consistent advantage over random sampling, contradicting a natural assumption in data-efficient neural operator training. It instead explores using physics to initialize or shape the neural operator itself as a more effective route to reduce labeled-solution requirements.

entry.title: FedLoVA: Value-Only Aggregation for Federated LoRA Fine-Tuning of Large Language Models

author.name: Ensieh Khazaei, Baturalp Buyukates, Dimitrios Hatzinakos

entry.summary: The authors analyze the roles of query and value projections in federated LoRA fine-tuning and find the value projection converges much faster. Building on this, FedLoVA trains LoRA adapters on both projections locally but shares only the value projections during aggregation, reducing communication cost.

entry.title: CHARM: Certified Homology-Aware Reverse-scale Mapping via Diffusion-Guided Quotient Towers

author.name: Zhe Li

entry.summary: CHARM combines two-dimensional coordinates with certified homology records and sample-level localization, using diffusion coordinates to guide cover proposals and Cover Quotient Towers to reduce the domain of structural computation. Exact algebra certifies and tracks homology representatives and places their supports via reverse-scale layout.

entry.title: Safe Offline Reinforcement Learning using Behavior Regularisation and Latent Feasibility Guidance

author.name: Mahesh Keswani, Parth Bhardwaj, Ankur Kumar, Raunak P. Bhattacharyya

entry.summary: FOCAL is a method for safe offline RL that combines behavior-regularized policy gradients with reachability-based feasibility guidance, learning policies that maximize return while provably respecting safety constraints from static data. It argues behavior regularization makes more effective use of learned critics than advantage-weighted regression, which amplifies value estimation errors.

entry.title: Hydro-Dataset: A Multi-Modal Open-Source Pipeline for Nordic Hydrological Research and Foundation Model Benchmarking

author.name: Getnet Demil, Md Moinul Islam, Mourad Oussalah

entry.summary: Hydro-Dataset v1.1 harmonizes 582 Swedish and Finnish meteorological stations over nine hydrological winters into a CF-1.9 NetCDF product with 1.8 million annotated station-days and six derived snow parameters. It provides benchmark-ready labels for training and evaluating hydrological foundation models, with ERA5-Land cross-validation.

entry.title: TEAM: Topology-Aware, Semantic-Sensitive, General Transformer for Multimodal-Attributed Graphs

author.name: Yushuo Li, Xunkai Li, Zhengyu Wu, Ronghua Li, Guoren Wang

entry.summary: TEAM is a modality-centric transformer for multimodal-attributed graphs that treats node-modality tokens, rather than whole nodes, as interaction units, addressing the problem that topology-defined neighborhoods can contain semantically weak evidence. It unfolds local topology into modality encoding sequences to capture fine-grained modality contributions. This generalizes graph learning toward heterogeneous text/image-attributed graphs.

entry.title: MG-Cache: Multi-Granularity Caching for Accelerating Diffusion Transformer Inference

author.name: Zesen Chen, Youxuan Xu, Shigang Li

entry.summary: MG-Cache is a training-free acceleration method for diffusion transformers that exploits computational redundancy at both the timestep and Transformer-layer granularities, coordinating cache reuse across levels to control error accumulation. It addresses the high inference cost of DiT image generation and the limitations of single-granularity caching strategies. The core innovation is jointly identifying which modules can be reused with bounded error.

entry.title: GenISys: Integrated Ship Systems Design Using Subsystem-Conditional Tabular Diffussion

author.name: Noah J. Bagazinski, Faez Ahmed

entry.summary: GenISys is a generative framework for early-stage bulk-carrier design that uses a simultaneous conditional denoising diffusion model to generate coupled ship subsystems together, so hull, structure, propulsion, and operations respond to each other. It is trained on a dataset of nearly 218,000 proposed designs, of which about 16,000 satisfy engineering constraints.

entry.title: Severity-Controlled Prediction Sets for Medication Recommendation

author.name: Yu Gu, Zijun Yu, Chi-Kuang Yeh, Xinyu Wang, Ziyang Song

entry.summary: The paper introduces Conformal Severity Control, a post-hoc calibration framework for medication prediction sets that uses the ATC hierarchy to quantify how severe a mismatch is rather than treating all missed medications equally. It controls patient-level average and upper-quantile severity without retraining the underlying predictor.

entry.title: Can Hindsight Critics Guide Delayed Actors?

author.name: Francisco M. L\'{o}pez, Francisco Cruz

entry.summary: The paper tackles reinforcement learning under sensory delays, which breaks Markovian assumptions, by training asymmetric critic networks on hindsight-aligned state-action transitions while the actor learns from privileged value estimates despite delayed observations. Experiments on the DelayBench suite show Hindsight Critics outperform delay-aware and unaware baselines.

entry.title: Pairwise distortion distribution for compression and quantization

author.name: Carl Nuzman, Jeongmin Chae, Kursat Rasim Mestav, Urbashi Mitra

entry.summary: The paper introduces the pairwise distortion distribution (PDD) and its asymptotic limit, the pairwise dimension (PD), generalizing the correlation integral to general distortion measures. It shows PD bounds Renyi information dimension and that PDD provides a lower bound for random codebook quantization performance, offering a practical way to choose latent dimensions in compression.

entry.title: Exact Natarajan Dimension of Homogeneous Multiclass Linear Predictors

author.name: Jiahua Liu, Benchong Li

entry.summary: The paper proves the exact Natarajan dimension of homogeneous multiclass linear predictors with pairwise distinct class weights is n(k-1)-1 for n,k >= 3, establishing matching lower and upper bounds. This resolves a fundamental capacity question in multiclass learning theory.

entry.title: Calibrating Document-Local Boundaries for Contextual Chunk Retrieval

author.name: Yuanxiang Wang, Hui Jiang, Da Zhu, Zhihua Chang

entry.summary: This paper improves retrieval-augmented chunking by analyzing the decision boundary between a gold chunk and its hardest sibling within the same document, building on late chunking and the InSeNT approach. It shows that entropy of the conditional negative allocation decreases monotonically with the scaling factor at fixed logits, and proposes a two-part framework that calibrates document-local chunk boundaries by adapting the discriminative scale from within-document margins. The work addresses a genuine weakness in contextual retrieval: semantically similar same-document negatives are hard to distinguish when shared context is pooled.

entry.title: Learning to Select Sparse Linear Solvers with Convolutional Neural Networks

author.name: Artemis Pados, Alan Edelman, Emmanuel Lujan, Daniel Pickard, Felipe Tome, Christopher Rackauckas

entry.summary: The paper trains a CNN to regress log timing ratios between candidate sparse linear solvers using spy plot images of matrix sparsity structure, achieving strong prediction accuracy on held-out SuiteSparse matrices and real-world matrices from high-performance simulation codes. This enables automatic, structure-aware solver selection.

entry.title: Anchor Behavior, Not Parameters: Rehearsal-Free Continual Learning with a Single Shared Prompt

author.name: Duy-Cuong Bui, Trung-Anh Dang, Vincent Nguyen, Duc V. Le, Ngoc-Son Vu

entry.summary: TEA-Prompt is a continual learning method for frozen vision Transformers that preserves a shared prompt's behavior on old classes rather than protecting its parameters, using a single shared prompt across all tasks for maximal parameter efficiency. The key insight is that parameter-space protection is the wrong invariant: drift in shared tokens corrupts prompt function on past classes even when weights are frozen. The approach claims better plasticity-stability balance than prior one-prompt methods.

entry.title: Rethinking Supervision Targets for Multimodal LLM Unlearning: Less Private Information, Reduced Distribution Shift

author.name: Leijiang Gu, Zhen Zeng, Feng Li, Le Zhang, Zenglin Shi

entry.summary: The paper studies machine unlearning for multimodal LLMs that memorize sensitive information across text and vision, identifying the choice of supervision target as the key driver of the forgetting-utility trade-off. The authors show targets containing more private information cause insufficient forgetting while also inducing distribution shift, and propose targets that minimize both. This improves selective removal of private content without degrading model utility.

entry.title: Reliability-Aware Benchmarking of Self-Supervised Learning in Histopathology Under 1-10% Label Regimes

author.name: Alicem Koyun, Pranjali Changadeo Pingale, Sachin Mote, Gianluca Pizzuti

entry.summary: This work benchmarks SimCLR, BYOL, and a masked-reconstruction baseline on histopathology datasets under extremely low-label regimes (1-10%), evaluating not just accuracy but confidence reliability under domain shift. Notably, it repeats experiments across multiple splits and seeds to address single-run reproducibility concerns common in SSL evaluations.

entry.title: Spiking Sensory Networks

author.name: Lleyton Ariton

entry.summary: This paper presents a model of how peripheral sensory neurons transduce external signals into spiking representations, grounding Bayesian processing in empirical biology and validating on non-stationary temporal data. It aims to bridge machine-learning Bayesian spiking approaches, which are often phenomenological, with neuroscience models that rely on strong experimental biases or post-hoc kinetic fits.

entry.title: Zeroth-Order Langevin Dynamics for Stochastic Nonconvex Optimization: Curvature Regularization and Non-Asymptotic Guarantees

author.name: Stefano Bruno, Dong-Young Lim

entry.summary: The paper develops non-asymptotic theory for stochastic zeroth-order Langevin dynamics, which optimize using only noisy function evaluations. It shows Gaussian smoothing induces implicit Hessian-trace regularization to leading order, and analyzes the curvature-regularized objective with convergence guarantees in the nonconvex setting.

entry.title: NeuroHorizon: Long-Horizon Forecasting of Neural Population Activity with Hierarchical Memory

author.name: Peng Jiang, Xiaoxuan Jia

entry.summary: NeuroHorizon addresses long-horizon forecasting of neural population activity, showing that short-horizon accuracy and teacher-forced evaluation fail to measure how well models sustain predictions from initial history alone. The method pairs event-based spike encoding with a causal decoder and uses a hierarchical prediction memory that keeps recent predictions at full resolution while compressing earlier ones. It compares direct multi-step prediction versus autoregressive rollout on spiking recordings.

entry.title: Risk-Sensitive Reinforcement Learning for an Options Market Maker: An Empirical Study with Real S&P 500 Options

author.name: Jacky Chen, Ing-Haw Cheng, John Hull, Landis Li, Zissis Poulos, Justin Shi, Andreas Veneris, Zeyu Wang

entry.summary: This paper evaluates whether an RL agent for hedging options market-making inventory risk, trained on historical S&P 500 options data (1996-2017), outperforms traditional delta hedging, simple hedge-ratio rules, and simulation-trained agents in tail-risk protection. The authors introduce an empirical replay environment using real market data and compare it against matched geometric Brownian motion, SABR stochastic-volatility, and hybrid simulators, addressing the common problem that RL agents trained in synthetic markets miss real crashes and volatility regimes.

entry.title: Fast Approximate $\ell_p$ Chamfer Distance via Lopsided Embeddings and Structured JL

author.name: Ying Feng, David P. Woodruff

entry.summary: Gives efficient near-linear-time algorithms for approximating Chamfer distance under l_p norms (1 < p <= 2) using lopsided embeddings combined with structured Johnson-Lindenstrauss transforms and fast matrix multiplication. Achieves strong runtime guarantees for high-dimensional point-set similarity.

entry.title: Off-Policy RL with Online Inference Tuning: My Solution to the CoRL 2026 RoboEval Challenge

author.name: Ilia Larchenko

entry.summary: Describes a competition solution combining off-policy RL on a pi0.5-based policy that serves as its own value function, trained with AWR and RECAP on exact official score advantages, plus Thompson-sampling over roughly 20 inference parameters during rollouts. Achieved 0.85 RDS on held-out seeds for eight bimanual manipulation tasks within two days of training.

entry.title: FastGRT: Accelerating Training of 3D Gaussian Ray Tracing

author.name: Meet Banthia, Xiaoteng Liu, Hexu Zhao, Aurojit Panda, Jinyang Li

entry.summary: FastGRT speeds up training of Gaussian-based ray tracing, whose cost far exceeds rasterization-based 3D Gaussian Splatting, by analyzing how ray tracing executes on GPUs. It decouples ray traversal from blending, reuses forward-pass work in the backward pass, and adds fast gradient accumulation and a hybrid BVH update strategy, implemented in Vulkan.

entry.title: A Sequential Monte Carlo Method for Data Assimilation in Subsurface Flow Systems with Hierarchical Uncertainty

author.name: Wenchao Teng, Guido Di Federico, Louis J. Durlofsky

entry.summary: This work develops an adaptive-tempered sequential Monte Carlo method for joint Bayesian estimation of both metaparameters and cell-by-cell geological properties in subsurface flow systems. It uses noncentered parameterizations with adaptive likelihood tempering, importance weighting, resampling, and blockwise MCMC mutation, aided by flow surrogates. The method targets hierarchical geological uncertainty that complicates data assimilation.

entry.title: RBA: A Read-out Basis Adapter for Parameter-Efficient Interactive OCTA Vessel Segmentation with SEEM

author.name: Jaafar M. Al-Ghabban, Mohammad Reza Mohammadi

entry.summary: This paper adapts the promptable SEEM segmentation model to optical coherence tomography angiography (OCTA) vessel segmentation, where thin vessels are poorly captured by its coarse quarter-resolution readout. The Read-out Basis Adapter (RBA) adapts the read-out branch rather than only the encoder, avoiding full fine-tuning of 342 million parameters on small datasets. This improves vessel and foveal avascular zone segmentation with click-based refinement.

entry.title: FALC: An Artifact-Centric Life Cycle Model and Research Agenda for AI Forensics

author.name: Adrian Johannes Staeves, Mayur Rattan Jaisinghani, Rebekah Overdorf, Frank Breitinger

entry.summary: FALC proposes a life cycle model for AI forensics that catalogs the artifacts AI systems leave behind when they are tools, targets, or evidence sources in criminal investigations. The authors derive a reference list of forensic artifacts, map crimes with AI involvement to investigative questions, and outline a research agenda for artifact analysis techniques. This establishes groundwork for a new subfield.

entry.title: CADMA: Capacity-Aware Coverage Decomposition for Generative Model Assessment

author.name: Debin Meng, Zheng Gao, Ziquan Liu, Yanran Li, Ioannis Patras, Georgios Tzimiropoulos

entry.summary: CADMA improves recall-oriented evaluation of generative models by decomposing distributional coverage beyond simple geometric measures. It distinguishes failure modes such as mode dropping and mode collapse, which single aggregate recall scores cannot separate, and corrects unreliable geometry-based estimates that assign high scores to poorly covered distributions. This strengthens the diagnostic toolkit for generative model assessment.

entry.title: A four-step validation protocol for radiomic survival analysis in small cohorts: a body composition case study

author.name: Mariela Talavera-Mu\~noz, Cecilia Diana-Albelda, Miguel Antonio Sampedro-Nu\~nez, Victor Rodriguez-Laval, Jesus Bescos, \'Alvaro Garc\'ia-Mart\'in

entry.summary: The authors propose a four-step validation protocol for radiomic survival modeling in small clinical cohorts, combining FDR-corrected feature selection, comparison of selection versus embedded regularization, repeated nested cross-validation, and a negative-control test with Gaussian noise features. Applied to 78 GEP-NET patients with CT-derived body composition features, the protocol addresses overfitting and optimistic single-split evaluation. It offers a reusable template for credible biomarker studies in low-data medical settings.

entry.title: MultiTurnRoute: A Platform for Building and Evaluating Multi-Turn LLM Routers

author.name: Jiaqi Xue, Mengxin Zheng, Heng Huang, Qian Lou

entry.summary: MultiTurnRoute is a platform for building and evaluating LLM routers in multi-turn conversations, where the model chosen at one turn shapes both the next query context and reusable prompt-prefix costs. Its Chain-of-Route algorithm uses a learned gate over recent and recurrent dialogue history to predict response quality while estimating cost from reusable prefix lengths, and a MultiTurnRoute Arena ranks routers on recorded conversations. This extends model routing beyond the single-turn setting.

entry.title: Gendered Misclassification from Surname-Based Race Imputation

author.name: Noah Dasanaike

entry.summary: This paper shows that race imputation from voter-file surnames is systematically biased against women who adopt a spouse's surname, especially in interracial marriages, degrading accuracy for Asian and Hispanic women. The bias interacts with political behavior, violating downstream inference assumptions in social-science applications of imputed race data.

entry.title: Out of Parameters, Saved by Syntax: UD-PrMPT for Parser Augmented Low Resource Machine Translation

author.name: Emma Thronson, Abhishek Purushothama, Amir Zeldes

entry.summary: UD-PrMPT augments LLM-based machine translation prompts with Universal Dependencies syntactic analyses for five very low-resource languages: Beja, Chintang, Chukchi, Coptic, and Xibe. Syntactic prompt components yield additive gains on top of lexicon-based prompting, stronger for manual analyses but consistent even with predicted parses.

entry.title: When Audio and Video Mislead: Evaluating Multimodal AI for Conversational Emotion Recognition

author.name: Youngseok Kim, Minjae Kim, Eunsoo Lee, Jihie Kim

entry.summary: This work audits off-the-shelf multimodal omni models for conversational emotion recognition by holding transcript and context fixed while adding, removing, or replacing target audio and video. Across Qwen2.5-Omni-7B, Baichuan-Omni-1.5, and MiniCPM-o 2.6 on MELD and IEMOCAP, text plus audio improves accuracy in most pairs, while unrelated audio/video consistently lowers accuracy, indicating fragile reliance on non-textual signals.

entry.title: BDBBQ: A Human-AI Collaborative Benchmark for Bengali Social Bias in LLMs

author.name: Provat Saha, Ashika Habib Khan, Tahseen Tanha, Hasin Ishrak, Muhammad Iqbal Hossain

entry.summary: BDBBQ extends the BanglaBBQ benchmark into a bilingual (English and Bengali) social-bias benchmark grounded in Bangladesh's sociocultural context, with 61,312 question-answer instances across 12 social categories. It includes balanced answer permutations, contrasting question framings, and both ambiguous and disambiguated contexts, validated through structural checks, 220 statistical tests, and expert annotation. The benchmark enables culturally grounded bias evaluation that existing Western-centric benchmarks miss.

entry.title: Language processing in the autistic brain: A meta-analysis of neuroimaging studies across modalities and age

author.name: Hanlin Wu, Bei Xiao, Qingxi He

entry.summary: This meta-analysis synthesizes 45 fMRI and PET studies (753 autistic and 777 non-autistic participants) using SDM-PSI with meta-regressions adjusted for language modality and age. It finds similar left-lateralized language network activation in both groups while clarifying where findings diverge. It matters for resolving inconsistent neuroimaging results about autism and language, informing both neuroscience and computational work on neurodiverse language processing.

entry.title: SceneShifter: Training-free Multi-Scene Temporal Control for Audio-driven Human Animation

author.name: Jianzhi Long, Rong-Cheng Tu, Hao Guan, Siyuan Liang, Shunyu Liu, Xiao Luo, Dacheng Tao

entry.summary: SceneShifter is a training-free framework for audio-driven human animation that orchestrates background scene transitions at precise timestamps while keeping the foreground subject coherent. It attributes the challenge to diffusion transformer self-attention and introduces semantic-aware temporal decoupling plus foreground motion localization across latent frames. It matters as an inference-time technique for controllable video generation without retraining costs.

entry.title: QCVS: Question-Contrastive Visual Steering for Multimodal Reasoning

author.name: Tong Fu

entry.summary: QCVS is an inference-time steering method for vision-language models that isolates query-relevant reasoning directions using double-differential activation probing, contrasting spatial perturbations under the target query against a generic description reference. A dual-threshold gating mechanism applies a single bounded hidden-state update only when needed, avoiding collateral damage to correct predictions. This matters because it offers a training-free, supervision-free way to steer multimodal reasoning without degrading low-level perception.

entry.title: REFORM-3D: A Representation-Centric Evaluation Framework for 3D Medical Vision Foundation Models

author.name: Maregu Assefa, Muzammal Naseer, Divya Velayudhan, Gedamu Alemu Kumie, Naoufel Werghi

entry.summary: REFORM-3D is a representation-centric evaluation framework that benchmarks frozen 3D medical vision foundation models on representation quality rather than downstream task scores, which entangle features with adaptation choices. It probes three questions: acquisition robustness (feature stability under varying voxel spacing with fixed anatomy), cross-modal anatomical alignment, and more. It matters because volumetric imaging evaluation has been dominated by task metrics that obscure representation properties.

entry.title: DAPointRWKV: Domain Adaptive Vision RWKV for Point Cloud Completion

author.name: Yinghui Li, Qianyu Zhou, Hao Yang, Richard Dazeley, Ye Zhu, Xuequan Lu

entry.summary: Applies RWKV (linear-complexity recurrent sequence modeling) to domain adaptive point cloud completion, addressing challenges of missing geometric priors, the mismatch between recurrent modeling and coarse-to-fine generation, and unstable target-domain adaptation. It aims to overcome limitations of CNNs, Transformers, and Mamba-like models in terms of receptive fields, computational complexity, and serialization sensitivity.

entry.title: They Can See It but Not Say It: Iterative Self Knowledge Re-expression in Visual Reasoning Relative Pose Identification

author.name: Mengyu Wang, Ken Deng, Yftah Ziser, Shay B. Cohen, Tiejun Ma

entry.summary: This paper analyzes vision-language models on visual reasoning relative pose identification (VRRPI), exposing stable output biases where VLMs predict specific motion patterns regardless of visual evidence. It proposes SKR-ID, an annotation-free debiasing pipeline using randomly extracted unannotated image pairs that shifts VLMs from next-token prediction to task-optimized classification heads.

entry.title: Scaling Optimization-Oriented Hypernetworks for Implicit Neural Representations

author.name: Lulu Cai, Hanxiang Ren, Siyan Dong, Li Sun, Jiefeng Wu, Youyi Zheng, Yi Ma, Yanchao Yang

entry.summary: The authors present a hypernetwork that generates implicit neural representation (INR) parameters in a single forward pass without test-time optimization, showing that quartic parameter growth in prior MLP instantiations is structural to MLPs rather than to the optimization-oriented principle. They resolve this by replacing the MLP body with attention.

entry.title: STAR-VF: Spatio-Temporal Aware Representation Condensation for Data-Efficient Video Fusion

author.name: Yuchen Xian, Yunqiu Xu, Guosheng Lin, Yang He

entry.summary: STAR-VF is presented as the first dataset-condensation framework for video fusion, condensing training sets into compact learnable spatio-temporal representations to reduce storage and optimization costs while preserving cross-modal complementarity and temporal coherence.

entry.title: REDiff-AD: No Training and No Target Masks for Industrial Anomaly Image Generation via Diversity-Driven In-Context MMDiT

author.name: Chih-Yu Tsai, Chih-Heng Chang, Jian-Jiun Ding

entry.summary: REDiff-AD generates realistic industrial defect images without model fine-tuning or target mask annotation by using in-context learning with Rectified Flow MMDiT to transfer defect appearance from a single masked reference onto a normal product image. This addresses data scarcity for training industrial anomaly detectors. The training-free, mask-free design lowers the barrier to deploying anomaly generation pipelines in manufacturing settings.

entry.title: BiRefNet-V2: Rethinking Bilateral Reference for High-Resolution Dichotomous Image Segmentation

author.name: Peng Zheng, Deng-Ping Fan, Binglu Wang, Nicu Sebe

entry.summary: BiRefNet-V2 recasts bilateral-reference dichotomous image segmentation as controlled information recovery, adding locality-preserving semantic references, improved semantic selectivity, and focused boundary supervision to fix weaknesses in the original BiRefNet design. It targets pixel-accurate foreground-background separation with fine structures.

entry.title: Let the Gallery Learn Itself: Training-Free Iterative Side-View Face Recognition

author.name: Zijun Huang, Suncheng Xiang

entry.summary: Gallery Self-Evolution is a training-free test-time adaptation framework for face recognition that archives novel appearance samples into a bounded dedup-FIFO gallery after successful recognition while locking enrollment templates. It closes the side-view gap by +23 points at 45-degree yaw and improves TAR@FAR=0.001 by +9.4 points on CFP-FP and IJB-C at CPU-level cost.

entry.title: SurfScaff3D: Bridging Geometric and Semantic Representations for LLM-based 3D Object Generation

author.name: Anay Loya, Rishi Gupta, Arnav Samal, Anirban Chakraborty

entry.summary: This paper addresses the mismatch between LLM-native reasoning and conventional 3D parameterizations for text-driven 3D object generation. It proposes a representation designed to bridge geometric and semantic worlds without expensive fine-tuning or restrictive structural priors that exclude organic shapes.

entry.title: RAPA: Ray-Aware Physics Augmentation for Robust Camera-LiDAR Calibration

author.name: Kyung-Rin Oh, Ji-Hoon Kim, TaeJoon Ha, Jae-Sang Hyun

entry.summary: RAPA formulates checkerboard localization for camera-LiDAR calibration as a 2D detection problem on cylindrical LiDAR reflectivity images, and proposes ray-aware physics augmentation to generate training data that simulates the sparsity and measurement physics of LiDAR. This addresses the unreliability of checkerboard corner extraction when features are insufficiently observed.

entry.title: Towards Reconstructing and Recognizing Objects behind Fragmented Occlusion using Video

author.name: Roman Pflugfelder, Michael Lindenbaum, Daniel Cremers

entry.summary: This paper proposes a de-occlusion framework that reconstructs objects behind high-density fragmented occlusions such as foliage from grayscale video sequences. It jointly registers images and optimizes alignment parameters to maximize contrast of the average (integrated) image, which serves as the reconstructed representation, then supports recognition.

entry.title: AI-based characterization of lymphoid structures and the tumor microenvironment reveals lower mature tertiary lymphoid structures, lymph-node follicles, and plasma cells after neoadjuvant therapy in lung squamous cell carcinoma

author.name: Arne Schmidt, Justin Nieder, Cornelius Boehm, Julika Ribbat-Idel, Marius Teodorescu, Marie-Lisa Eich, Simon Schallenberg, Gabriel Dernbach, Katja Lingelbach, Miriam Haegele, Timo Milbich, Adam Narai, Maria Stoelben, Hans Pinckaers, Lukas Ruff, Kai Standvoss, Christian Watermann, Christiane Kuempers, Sven Perner, Verena Sailer, Jasmin Tiebach, Torsten Goldmann, Sebastian Marwitz, Johannes Braegelmann, Frederick Klauschen, Marija Pezer, Rosemarie Krupar

entry.summary: Using AI models (Aignostics Atlas HETA) on H&E whole-slide images from matched neoadjuvant-treated and therapy-naive lung squamous cell carcinoma patients (n=20 each), the study quantifies cell densities and co-localization of tertiary lymphoid structures, lymph-node follicles, and plasma cells. It finds lower mature TLS, follicles, and plasma cells after neoadjuvant therapy.

entry.title: Benchmarking Neural Image Compression with DCT-Based Spectral Diagnostics

author.name: Nikolay I. Kalmykov, Razan Dibo, Yujun Du, Yipeng Liu, Ivan Oseledets, Anh-Huy Phan

entry.summary: This paper proposes a diagnostic benchmark probing neural image compression codecs with the DCT basis matrix and single-frequency test images, measuring relative off-target energy leakage and target-frequency gain. It finds that several models (BMSHJ, MBT, Cheng2020) leave 80-97% of reconstructed high-band energy outside the target bin near 1 bpp, while TCM and FTIC perform better.

entry.title: OfficeTwin: Realizing 3D Reconstruction of Redundant Scenes through Partial Viewpoint Perception

author.name: Quanyun Wu, Kyle Gao, Daisy Li, Kshitij Goyal, Dayou Mao, David A. Clausi, Jonathan Li, Yuhao Chen

entry.summary: OfficeTwin addresses 3D reconstruction of redundant office scenes from robot-native partial viewpoints, combining feed-forward 3D reconstruction with partial-view perception to produce watertight, object-identifying volumes needed for robot learning. It targets the problem that office workstations are nearly indistinguishable under weakly textured, repetitive structure.

entry.title: Task-Critical Part Alignment Improves Imitation of Object Interactions

author.name: Denis Hadjivelichkov, Sebastian {\AE}gidius, Valerio Modugno, Dimitrios Kanoulas

entry.summary: This paper extends the DINOBot imitation-learning framework for object-object interactions with two contributions: RANSAC-based outlier rejection to handle noisy depth data and spurious feature matches, and refinement of semantic correspondence to focus on task-relevant interaction regions. The improvements aim to make demonstration transfer to real-world robotic manipulation more robust and accurate.

entry.title: Capturability-Aware Footstep Planning in Cluttered Environments: A Recursively Feasible Sequential MPC on Axis-Aligned Safe Corridors

author.name: Athanasios Kyriakopoulos, Shubham S. Kumbhar, Kunal S. Narkhede, Abhijeet M. Kulkarni, Ioannis Poulakakis

entry.summary: The paper presents a capturability-aware sequential MPC framework for LIP-based humanoid footstep planning with obstacles, combining obstacle avoidance with capturability constraints through safe corridors of intersecting rectangles. It provides recursive feasibility guarantees and adapts to constrained scenarios, such as switching to in-place walking when doors close unexpectedly.

entry.title: Mobility Information Capacity of Multi-Robot Systems: Safety-Aware Maneuver Design

author.name: Weijie Yuan

entry.summary: The paper introduces a mobility information capacity (MIC) framework that quantifies both the maneuver freedom of a multi-robot fleet and how reliably those maneuvers can be observed, via mutual information between joint maneuver sequences and noisy trajectories. This provides a principled metric for safety-aware coordination design beyond simple fleet-size or throughput measures.

entry.title: Passivity-Guaranteed Variable Impedance and Compliance Control via Online Parameter Optimization

author.name: Huseyin Tugcan Dinc, Ersin Da\c{s}, Nikolas Thelenberg, Christian Ott

entry.summary: The paper proposes a quadratic programming-based framework for variable impedance control that guarantees passivity by modulating desired inertia to compensate for energy injected by stiffness variations, while preserving a critically damped response. This avoids the common trade-off of adding damping or limiting stiffness profiles that degrades dynamics.

entry.title: From Festival Video to the Stage: A Sim-to-Real Ladder for Long-Horizon Expressive Whole-Body Dance on a Commercial Humanoid

author.name: Hesham Shehata (Research, Development Division, Arithmer Inc., Tokyo, Japan)

entry.summary: This work presents a sim-to-real pipeline transferring a traditional Japanese festival dance (Awa Odori) from monocular video to a Unitree G1 humanoid, combining human mesh recovery, retargeting, RL motion tracking, and ONNX deployment trained on a single consumer GPU. An eleven-version deployment ladder documents real hardware debugging, including artifact corruption and state-estimator drift, culminating in repeated rope-free completions of a 43-second routine. It is a valuable practical playbook for long-horizon expressive humanoid behaviors.

entry.title: Action Representation for Spatial Generalization in Robot World Models

author.name: Yuhang Sun

entry.summary: This study evaluates matched action representations defined in world, object, and surface coordinate frames for spatial generalization in robot world models, using a controlled robotic peeling benchmark with global pose and contact relocation experiments. It reveals a cost of limited training data when equivalent interactions receive different spatial descriptions and analyzes how representation choice affects learned prediction. It offers useful empirical guidance for designing world-model action spaces.

entry.title: Learning Contextual Motion Constraints for Object Rearrangement Exploration

author.name: Lexing Zhang, Zeyu Zhang, Gang Zeng, Hangxin Liu

entry.summary: MoCo-Net is a two-stream network that jointly predicts continuous motion ranges of articulated parts and obstacle heatmaps for potential collisions from partial point-cloud observations. By capturing both intrinsic joint limits and extrinsic clutter constraints, it improves feasible-motion prediction and generalization to novel objects, supporting robot rearrangement exploration.

entry.title: DreamLander: A 6-DOF World Model based Reinforcement Learning Planetary Lander

author.name: George Nehma, Patrick Quinn, Madhur Tiwari, Camilo Riano-Rios

entry.summary: DreamLander applies model-based reinforcement learning based on DreamerV3 to generate optimal guidance and control for a realistic 6-DOF planetary lander, addressing fuel-optimal powered descent. The work leverages world-model learning to simplify the complex process of generating optimal guidance trajectories for planetary landings.

entry.title: Graph-Guided Bayesian Factor Analysis: A Fast Integrated EFA-CFA Approach for High-Dimensional Data

author.name: Shitao Fan, Lizhen Lin, Zhenyao Ye, Shuo Chen

entry.summary: Introduces graph-guided Bayesian factor analysis (gg-BFA), which learns latent graph structure to identify which variables can and cannot be represented by low-dimensional factors, how many factors are needed, and factor covariances. It integrates exploratory and confirmatory factor analysis in one Bayesian framework using dense-subgraph selection, and remains feasible when variables outnumber subjects. This addresses interpretability and breakdown failures of maximum-likelihood factor analysis in high-dimensional biomedical data.

entry.title: TurnFlow: Benchmarking User-State Reasoning in Multi-Turn LLM Agents via Scene-Guided User Simulation

author.name: Zhixun Chen, Ming Li, Anjie Liu, Xiaoyuan Zhang, Quanyu Dai, Huangxun Chen

entry.summary: TurnFlow is an interactive benchmark testing whether LLM agents maintain and reason over evolving user states across multi-turn conversations, using scene-guided user simulation to expose subtle failures like unrecognized changed constraints or unenforced conflicts. It targets open-domain requirement reconciliation, which existing benchmarks undermeasure. It matters because single-turn accuracy does not predict multi-turn reliability.

entry.title: Agentic discrete-event simulation for manufacturing system design: an open 3D simulator, a benchmark and an industrial case

author.name: Javier Pernas-\'Alvarez, Diego Crespo-Pereira

entry.summary: SimuLean is an open-source Unity-based 3D discrete-event simulation platform designed for AI-agent programming, where modeling semantics are verified once in the platform and agents operate via domain-level commands, evaluated on 18 manufacturing tasks with a frontier agent building valid models in 93 of 108 attempts plus an industrial case. It addresses the problem that agent-written simulation code is unverified software. It matters for trustworthy AI-assisted engineering design.

entry.title: The Lagrangian Brain: A Constraint Mechanics of Mind and Machine

author.name: Yuhang He, Si Wu

entry.summary: Proposes a theoretical framework in which brain circuits and machine systems handle constraints via Lagrange-multiplier-like quantities carried by neurons and synapses with distinct time constants, where each constraint (memory, goal, statistics) acts through its own multiplier that accumulates violation and pushes the state. The paper aims to unify aspects of neuroscience and AI under a constraint mechanics view.

entry.title: RealEmbedBench: Benchmarking LLMs on Real-World Application-Layer Embedded Software Tasks

author.name: Yujun Huang, Yuwei Zhang, Yi Zhou, Shanshan Wu, Xiang Chen, Lina Gong

entry.summary: RealEmbedBench is a 5,142-sample benchmark covering application-layer embedded software tasks: code generation and completion, state machine modeling, and cross-OS code translation, filling a gap left by hardware-in-the-loop simulation benchmarks. Evaluations of six LLMs reveal substantial task-dependent performance differences and show that project context, especially the local code window, strongly affects code generation. Models handle state machine modeling reasonably but struggle with other embedded tasks.

entry.title: Reconfigurable Action Theories: A Formal Foundation for Dynamically Composable Agent Harnesses

author.name: Jianmin Ji

entry.summary: This paper introduces Reconfigurable Action Theories (RAT), a formal framework in which agent actions can load and unload modules of vocabulary, causal laws, and initializers, so that an agent's own theory of action changes at runtime. It provides sufficient conditions for unique next configurations, behavior preservation when modules are added, and equivalence results.

entry.title: Beyond Sunny Skies: Using Large Language Models to Predict Urban Traffic in Adverse Weather

author.name: Zhu Xiao, Kuan Feng, Tong Li, Chenxi Liu, Gang Wang, Zhuo Tang, Kenli Li

entry.summary: Multi-STG integrates LLM-derived semantic priors into spatio-temporal graph models for urban traffic prediction under adverse weather, where rare meteorological events create sparse data and non-linear shifts that existing models handle poorly. The key insight is that weather conditions should be treated as rich semantic context requiring reasoning about how they alter mobility behavior, not just shallow numerical features. This is a practical contribution to intelligent transportation.

entry.title: Reproducible LoRA Inference Through Deterministic Split-K Reduction

author.name: Dhayaneshwar Balusamy, Ankur Mohan

entry.summary: The authors show that Split-K kernels with floating-point atomic additions introduce numerical nondeterminism in LoRA inference in vLLM, producing different FP32 outputs in 97.61% of identical-input replays across GSM8K, MBPP, and toxicity tasks. They implement a deterministic Triton Split-K that eliminates observed variation, supporting reproducible evaluation and auditing of LoRA-adapted models. This matters for systems where repeated inference must be bit-consistent.

entry.title: Self-contained Data Cleaning for Unsupervised Anomaly Detection

author.name: Jordan F. Masakuna, Ahmed Yacine, Djeff K. Nkashama, Arian Soltani, Marc Frappier, Pierre M. Tardif, Froduald Kabanza

entry.summary: The authors propose a self-contained preprocessing framework that identifies and removes contamination in training sets for unsupervised anomaly detection without requiring prior knowledge of the contamination ratio. Existing robust methods typically assume a known contamination fraction or fail to generalize across architectures, which this approach addresses for more dependable downstream detection in security settings.

entry.title: Agents Propose, Code Verifies, Humans Decide: Verified Agentic Ingestion of Heterogeneous Scientific Tables into Relational Databases

author.name: Bharatha Rankothge, Suzanne Hodgkins, Virginia Rich, Michael Kirby

entry.summary: The paper describes an AI-assisted pipeline for ingesting messy scientific datasets into relational databases under the rule that LLM agents propose, deterministic code verifies, and humans decide. Agents see compact citable evidence rather than raw data and return typed proposals, which a verifier with 39 check types tests in schema and content loops.

entry.title: Robust and Private Swarm Learning via Zero-Knowledge Validator Admission and Consensus Aggregation

author.name: Marco Arazzi, Mert Cihangiroglu, Antonino Nocera

entry.summary: This paper proposes a Swarm Learning framework in which validators must prove via zero-knowledge attestation, without revealing raw data, that a reference model ran correctly on their private data before joining. This makes verifiable data quality a condition for admission and closes the decentralized-validation attack surface.

entry.title: Bridging Task Planning and Execution for Language-Conditioned Bimanual Manipulation

author.name: Emanuele Cuzzocrea, Giuseppina Iannotti, Luca Rossini, Arturo Laurenzi, Nikos Tsagarakis

entry.summary: The paper presents a zero-shot vision-language framework for bimanual humanoid manipulation that jointly reasons about task objectives and physical feasibility, grounding planning in a structured scene representation combining semantic relations with execution constraints. Targets household and logistics tasks in cluttered environments.

entry.title: From Task Affinities to Optimal Allocations: Probabilistic Graphical Modelling for Supervised Finetuning

author.name: Prateek Chanda, Saral Sureka, Krishnateja Killamsetty, Ganesh Ramakrishnan

entry.summary: TASKMIXPGM learns continuous task mixtures for supervised fine-tuning under a fixed budget by modeling task interactions through energy-based modeling over SFT tasks, replacing heuristic uniform or size-proportional sampling. The goal is to select an effective subset of tasks and avoid wasting budget on redundant task sources.

entry.title: Breaking Precision Walls in First-, Second-, and Zeroth-Order Optimizers: One Constant, Set in Advance

author.name: Lngel Kyo (A2O Labs)

entry.summary: The paper defines a precision wall: the steepest power-law signal decay for which the weakest direction can still be recovered within 5% under a fixed optimization budget. It shows that across Adam, grafted Shampoo, and zeroth-order Adam, a single constant set in advance governs where the wall occurs, and provides rules for choosing it from curvature or spectrum estimates.

entry.title: UTOPI: Efficient Egocentric Long-Video Understanding in AR via User-Guided Token Pre-Compression

author.name: Ziqi Wang, Su Chen, Qiance Tang, Jieyu Lin, Ziyun Li, Barbara De Salvo, Sai Qian Zhang

entry.summary: UTOPI is a plug-and-play token pre-compression module for egocentric long-video understanding on resource-constrained AR devices. It uses user motion signals to estimate inter-frame overlap for viewpoint-shift-invariant pruning and eye-tracking fixations to separate attended foreground content for preferential retention. This addresses the severe temporal redundancy and compute limits of on-device long-video models.

entry.title: KKT-Perturbation-Aware Communication for Fully Distributed Online Convex Optimization with Nonseparable Coupling

author.name: Zhaoye Pan, Tao Li, Yunjie Guo, Guanpu Chen

entry.summary: This work addresses distributed online convex optimization where costs and constraints couple all agents and cannot be decomposed per agent. It reduces the communication overhead of prior belief-consensus methods by exchanging KKT-perturbation-aware, compressed information instead of full primal-dual belief states each round, while retaining no-regret guarantees.

entry.title: EmbodiedIntentBench: Benchmarking Intent-Driven Runtime Adaptation for Mobile Robotic Missions

author.name: Rajat Bhattacharjya, Changwoon Lee, Hyeonjong Ju, Sing-Yao Wu, Hamidreza Alikhani, Zhuoyi Yang, Ian Harris, Nalini Venkatasubramanian, Nikil Dutt

entry.summary: EmbodiedIntentBench is a benchmark for intent-driven runtime adaptation in mobile robotic missions, representing mission intent through structured contracts for coverage, temporal evidence, reporting, urgency, and resources. It couples simulated UAV workloads with causal, resource-accounted execution so that computation decisions can be evaluated against mission objectives rather than isolated perception accuracy.

entry.title: Sensitivity-Gated Accumulator Caching for On-Device Learning of Low-Bit Hand Networks

author.name: Soroor Ghandali, Kanika Mamgain, Manjot Kaur, Akanksha Shukla, Shashira Guntuka

entry.summary: SGAC enables on-device continual learning for 4- and 8-bit hand-tracking networks within memory roughly the size of the model itself. Unlike quantization-aware training that keeps 32-bit master weights and optimizer state (about 96 bits per weight), or stochastic rounding that injects noise, SGAC keeps residual state only for a small, dynamically changing set of sensitive weight groups using a set-associative cache of 8-bit accumulators. This allows models to keep adapting to a user's camera after deployment.

entry.title: DeFSM: Robust and Efficient Decentralization of Federated Submodular Maximization

author.name: Duc A. Tran, Dung Truong, Duy Le

entry.summary: This paper proposes DeFSM, a Byzantine-robust, communication-efficient architecture that removes the central server from federated submodular maximization by replacing it with a smart contract and a consensus-free pool of independent agents. Its aggregation rule SafeGM uses Tukey depth and safe points evaluated on 2D Gaussian random projections that the contract can verify cheaply. This addresses the trilemma of decentralization, efficiency, and security.

entry.title: Mitigating SM-Level Load Imbalance in 3D Gaussian Splatting on GPUs

author.name: Junha Ryu, Hoi-Jun Yoo

entry.summary: The paper identifies severe SM-level load imbalance in GPU-based 3D Gaussian Splatting rendering, caused by uneven tile workloads that leave most streaming multiprocessors idle, especially in large urban scenes. It proposes a software-defined GPU scheduling approach requiring no retraining and no specialized accelerators. This improves throughput for a technique increasingly used in world models and driving simulators.

entry.title: BIBIMBAP: A Benchmark for Instructional BIM-Based Automated Programming

author.name: Clemens Kujat, Bharathi Kannan Nithyanantham, Stefan Telgmann, Tobias Sesterhenn, Joern Ploennigs, Stefan L\"udtke, Christian Bartelt

entry.summary: BIBIMBAP is a Text-to-BIM benchmark of 100 curated tasks evaluating whether LLMs can edit Industry Foundation Classes (IFC) models, covering CRUD operations across spatial, geometric, topological, numeric, and conceptual categories. Each task includes prompts, IFC models, expected outputs, and automated test scripts. Baseline results show best performance of only 50.2% with frequent failures in constraint preservation and spatial reasoning, revealing a significant capability gap in a domain-relevant LLM application.

entry.title: ShopMind: A Mental World Model for Personalized and Realistic E-commerce User Simulation

author.name: Peixuan Hou, Bin Chen, Li He, Jian Xu, Xiuli Ma, Guojie Song

entry.summary: ShopMind introduces a mental world model for e-commerce user simulation grounded in Theory of Mind, explicitly tracking evolving beliefs, uncertainties, and intentions that drive user behavior rather than predicting actions directly from interaction histories. This enables both personalization and behavioral realism in simulated users.

entry.title: Improving Large Audio-Language Model Embedding Baselines for Instruction-Aware Speech Retrieval

author.name: Chen-An Li, Cheng-Han Chiang, Hung-yi Lee

entry.summary: The authors introduce IRIS-Embed, adapting large audio-language models into embedding models for instruction-aware speech retrieval, where a text instruction expresses the retrieval goal for a spoken query. Analysis shows different retrieval requirements favor hidden states from different audio-encoder layers, motivating instruction-aware layer weighting combined with contrastive training on about 900K samples built from real and synthetic data. This establishes stronger baselines for a nascent retrieval setting.

entry.title: Clinically Informed Colour Encoding Improves the Localisation and Stability of Explanations in Deep Learning ECG Models: External Validation in a UK Biobank Epilepsy Cohort

author.name: Lauren Hutchinson, Moses Nkgari, Alaa Alahmadi

entry.summary: The study tests whether input representation governs explanation quality in deep learning ECG models by comparing two identical residual networks differing only in a clinically informed pseudo-colour encoding of the QT interval and T-wave. The encoding is designed from electrophysiology knowledge and mapped to the validated QT-nomogram risk model, with external validation in a UK Biobank epilepsy cohort. Clinically informed encoding improves localization and stability of explanations.

entry.title: Retrieval-Grounded Multi-View Reasoning for Clinically Reliable Radiology Report Generation

author.name: Wanshu Fan, Zeyu Wang, Zheng Tong, Qi Ai, Wencai Weng, Haifan Gong, Congyu Liao, Guoliang You, Xiaofeng Liu, Dongsheng Zhou, Cong Wang

entry.summary: RG-MVR is a retrieval-grounded framework for chest radiograph report generation that combines dense memory summaries with visually gated sparse retrieved evidence, adaptive per-case weighting of image, memory, and evidence views, and a clinical prompt learner that models finding mentions separately from their positive, negative, or uncertain status. On MIMIC-CXR it reports clinical-label F1 of 0.483 with a small exploratory external cohort. It matters because it targets clinically reliable generation rather than just text-overlap metrics.

entry.title: ROLECUE: Diagnosing Cross-Lingual Role-Binding Failures in Vision-Language Models

author.name: Niaz Mohaiman Abtahi, Evan Maksud

entry.summary: ROLECUE is a controlled diagnostic pairing 192 validated two-person action images with sentences in six languages (German, Turkish, Japanese, English, Korean, Bangla) in canonical and patient-first orders, separating image-only role recognition, text-only parsing, and image-sentence matching. Across eight open-weight VLMs it reveals structured cross-lingual failures in binding visual Agent-Patient structure to semantic roles.

entry.title: Dynamics-Informed Action Learning for Goal-Conditioned Latent Planning

author.name: Yinuo Jiang, Guangzhi Wang, Yiran Wang, Junfu Pu, Cheng Cheng, Honghao Chen, Cheng Cheng, Ying Shan

entry.summary: DIAL bridges gaps between latent world model training and planning: rollout alignment exposes the forward model to its own autoregressive latent predictions during training, and multi-step inverse supervision trains a lightweight goal-conditioned proposal mechanism. This improves sampling-based planning by exploiting action-conditioned dynamics rather than goal-agnostic initialization.

entry.title: Beyond Similarity Entropy: A Rank-Guided Data-Free Quantization Framework for Vision Transformers

author.name: Runqing Jiang, Ye Zhang, Pengpeng Yu, Zhuo Song, Changjun Li, Longguang Wang, Yulan Guo

entry.summary: RankQ-ViT improves data-free quantization for Vision Transformers by showing that similarity-entropy-based synthetic calibration samples lack feature-direction diversity, and instead uses rank information from patch similarity matrices to guide sample synthesis. This targets efficient ViT deployment on mobile devices without training data access.

entry.title: Dense Flow from Adaptive Correspondence

author.name: Cheng-Lin Hsieh, Stella X. Yu

entry.summary: The paper proposes FATE (Flow from Adaptive Token Estimation), which decouples the scale of correspondence matching from the resolution of dense flow reconstruction in optical flow estimation. Token supports adapt their size and shape to image structure, expanding in coherent regions and contracting near boundaries, and are reused for precise dense flow reconstruction.

entry.title: Perturb, Aggregate then Reconstruct: Consensus Aggregation and Fourier-Attended Multi-Decoders for Reconstruction-based Multi-View Anomaly Detection

author.name: Yongho Son, Junyeong Yun, Je Hyeong Hong

entry.summary: The paper presents PAR, a reconstruction-based framework for multi-view anomaly detection in industrial inspection. It introduces a feature perturbation strategy with a consensus aggregation module that integrates perturbed features across viewpoints to construct view-consistent pseudo-anomalies, and uses Fourier-attended multi-decoders for reconstruction.

entry.title: Reliability-Adaptive Multimodal Relative Pose Tracking for Underwater Leader-Follower Robots

author.name: Mingyang Yang, Zeyu Sha, Xiaorui Wang, Jun Wang, David Chen Wang, Feitian Zhang

entry.summary: This work presents a reliability-adaptive multimodal perception framework for six-DOF relative-pose tracking between two underwater robots, fusing visual, acoustic-ranging, and hydrodynamic measurements with time-varying reliability weighting and linear-complexity temporal modeling for embedded hardware. Extensive experiments on a custom AUV platform validate the approach. It addresses a genuinely harsh sensing environment where no single modality suffices.

entry.title: Motion Belief Action: From a Visual Scene Map to Physical Decisions

author.name: Dibyendu Ghosh

entry.summary: Motion Belief Action (MBA) is a decision layer that augments scene maps with hidden physics estimates: how often objects move, required forces, loads, and blockage. It chooses actions under a force limit (look again, nudge, open, brace, decline) with risk set by task costs, validated on real activity in 9 kitchens for predicting object motion and door/drawer pull risk.

entry.title: TimeHF 2.0: Multimodal, Multivariate, and Multi-Region Collaborative Forecasting for Large-Scale Retail Supply Chains

author.name: Zhongxuan Han, Zhengxin Shi, Kunxiu Chen, Xiaolin Huang, Yulin Huang, Anni Zhang, Xiaoming Lin, Zhengyu Chen, Xue Yu, Yang Liu, Yuanyuan Yang, Yangyang Zhang, Junheng Huang, Dongyang Geng, Ben Zhang, Xin Wang, Jiaxin Wang, Haowei Zhou, Qiqi Yan, Jiaheng Yin, Jintao Xu, Zijiang Liu, Changfei Zhan, Zhe Chen, Yutong Pan, Jinqiu Deng, Shaomin Li, Ningxuan Kang, Jianshen Zhang, Yongzhi Qi, Wei Qi, Dazhou Lei, Zuo-Jun Max Shen

entry.summary: TimeHF 2.0 is a forecasting framework for large-scale retail supply chains that integrates regional sales, covariates, and natural-language business plans via a coverage-aware directed encoder and semantic alignment of language-model representations. It handles regional sparsity, nonstationarity, and volatile sales across products, dates, and regions. Its large author team suggests real industrial deployment, making it valuable evidence of LLM-augmented forecasting in production settings.

entry.title: Interpretable Cyber-Physical Attack Detection in Smart Grids: A Leakage-Controlled Multi-Testbed Evaluation of Fusion, Robustness, and Observability Limits

author.name: Muhammad Ridwanul Hoquea, Sarah Sharif, Reza Saeed Kandezy, Yaser Banad

entry.summary: The paper evaluates interpretable, time-windowed fusion Random Forest detectors for smart-grid cyber-physical attacks across multiple testbeds, adopting the pessimistic result when protocols disagree. It shows shuffled cross-validation is optimistic (macro-F1 falling from 0.96 to about 0.88 under rolling-origin temporal evaluation), characterizes adaptive feature-space attacks, and probes observability limits of the detection task.

entry.title: Neural Activity Synchronization-Based Fast Local Learnable Spiking Neural Network Architecture
