author.name: Pranith Dutta, Sk Wasim Rajjak, Siddhanta Ray, Santlal Prajapati, Manobendra Nath Mondal

entry.summary: The paper proposes a local learning framework for multi-layer spiking neural networks inspired by neural activity synchronization, where each layer updates weights with locally computed gradients and no backpropagation is needed. This reduces computation and training latency for battery-powered edge devices.

entry.title: BECON: Belief-Conditioned Constrained Multi-Objective Reinforcement Learning under Drifting Preferences and Budgets

author.name: Bui Trong Duc, Huynh Thi Thanh Binh

entry.summary: Formulates constrained preference-conditioned multi-objective RL as a partially observed task-specification problem where preferences drift, safety budgets shift, and exposed descriptors are noisy or delayed. BECON infers latent task context from received signals to navigate the conflict between unreliable external specifications and latent interaction dynamics.

entry.title: Clinical predictions using artificial intelligence in neurosurgery and its subspecialties: a systematic review and meta-analysis

author.name: Prajwal Ghimire, Aswin Chari, Jonathan Shapey, Keyoumars Ashkan

entry.summary: A PRISMA systematic review and meta-analysis of AI clinical-prediction studies in neurosurgery, pooling discriminative metrics with random-effects modeling, stratifying by diagnostic/prognostic/forecasting task type, and appraising risk of bias with PROBAST-style tools. It maps evidence levels and methodological quality across the neurosurgical care pathway.

entry.title: Fresh Enough to Decide: Age of Intelligence for Cost-Aware Model Synchronization in Dynamic IoT Systems

author.name: Hui Wang, Seyyedali Hosseinalipour, Jacob Chakareski, Ming Shi

entry.summary: The paper defines Age of Intelligence (AoInt), a model-version-relative and client-specific measure of decision utility distortion, to formulate when cached models on IoT devices should be refreshed. It develops KL-aware and parameter-aware synchronization algorithms with theoretical regret/cost tradeoff analysis for bandwidth- and energy-constrained settings.

entry.title: Dual-Granularity Learning for Regression with Continuous Noisy Labels

author.name: Hui Guo, Boyu Wang, Grace Y. Yi

entry.summary: The paper addresses learning with noisy labels in regression, where label noise has heterogeneous magnitudes, by proposing a dual-granularity method that balances instance-level sensitivity to small-to-moderate deviations with ordinal structure leveraging for large deviations. This captures both global structure and sample-specific deviations.

entry.title: Learning When to Think: Adaptive Internal Computation for Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Rohit Kumar Salla, Simon Stepputtis

entry.summary: Adaptive Internal Computation (AIC) is an iterative RL policy that jointly learns action selection and when to stop refining its latent representation, using an expected-depth penalty to value computation and auxiliary value predictions for supervision. Across twelve benchmark tasks it uses only 3.3 refinement steps on average out of a possible eight, demonstrating that state-dependent compute allocation outperforms fixed stopping schedules.

entry.title: Autonomous Continual Learning and Knowledge Transfer via Cortex-Inspired Neural Assemblies

author.name: Kevin L. McKee

entry.summary: The paper introduces Functional Task Networks, a continual learning method inspired by mammalian neocortical assemblies, formulated as a distributed stochastic mixture of experts with sparse binary routing computed at inference from a small support sample. The goal is to avoid catastrophic forgetting under concept and domain shifts without requiring each data batch to cover the full distribution.

entry.title: Operation-aware Multimodal Clinical Decision Support System for ICU Discharge Risk Assessment

author.name: Guoqing Zhang, Rafik Hadfi, Takayuki Ito

entry.summary: This system predicts unplanned 30-day ICU readmission by combining multi-agent collaborative extraction and self-evolving retrieval-augmented generation to clean noisy progress notes, while incorporating hospital operational context such as departmental workload and bed turnover pressures. It argues that discharge risk is a dynamic trade-off between patient stability and resource capacity.

entry.title: Guiding Data Allocation for Robust Subpopulation Generalization

author.name: Zhaoying Pan, Yipei Wang, Shenyu Lu, Xiaoqian Wang

entry.summary: The paper extends a Gaussian feature-model framework to characterize when balanced subgroup training proportions are, and are not, necessary for robust subpopulation generalization. The authors show multiple configurations, including substantially imbalanced ones, can match balanced data, and derive gradient-based directions for adjusting data collection. This offers practical guidance for cost-efficient dataset curation under subpopulation shift.

entry.title: Fade to... Red? Scheduling Coloured Noise Exploration Supports Efficient Robot Learning with Reduced Movement Jerk

author.name: Francisco M. L\'{o}pez, Francisco Cruz

entry.summary: This paper systematically studies 49 linear schedules between white and red noise, alongside generalized state-dependent exploration, on four sparse-reward manipulation tasks with a Fetch arm and a Shadow Dexterous hand. It asks whether scheduling noise color over training can outperform standard white-noise exploration for continuous control. Coloured noise schedules support more efficient robot learning while reducing movement jerk.

entry.title: YRC-Bench: Benchmarking Culturally Aware Machine Translation for Historical Heritage via Tri-Level Semantic Bridging

author.name: Huang Yan, Aobo Li, Jiayi Wang, Huidong Zhu

entry.summary: YRC-Bench is the first human-curated, multi-parallel benchmark for translating historical cultural heritage texts, spanning Classical Chinese, Modern Chinese, and nine foreign languages. It establishes a tri-level semantic bridging evaluation to probe how models handle culturally-specific items and diachronic shifts in terse classical syntax, where current LLMs struggle despite strong generic translation results. The benchmark targets Yellow River cultural records as a rich domain.

entry.title: Dhara: Evidence-Oriented Retrieval for Indian Knowledge Systems

author.name: Avinash Holenarasipur Nagendra, Anand Kaniyaar Sriranga Prasad, Rahul Vishwakarma, Trupti Gavit, Anish Amol Tipnis, Yashaswini Mandayam Rangayyan, Vinod Appajanna, Kousik Sarathy Sridharan, Mohan Raghavan

entry.summary: Dhara is a retrieval engine for Indian Knowledge Systems collections that combines hybrid search, entity notes, fuzzy verse retrieval (matching partially remembered Sanskrit verses), and neural reranking. Evaluated on Dhara Bench with 325 questions, BGE-M3 single-vector retrieval beats BM25 across all categories. It matters as a domain-specific retrieval system for culturally significant but technically challenging multilingual commentary/translation corpora.

entry.title: Disentangled Stylized Image Generation via IP-Cross-Attention Rearrangement

author.name: Beibei Dong, Yueming Lyu, Yue Jiang, Jing Dong

entry.summary: This work tackles stylized image generation in diffusion models by decoupling style representations directly in attention space via IP-Cross-Attention rearrangement, avoiding costly cycle-consistency training and the coupled-latent problem of diffusion latent spaces. It enables controllable style extraction and transfer.

entry.title: Towards Rotation-Only Imaging Geometry: Multi-View Pose Estimation

author.name: Xinrui Li, Qi Cai, Yuanxin Wu

entry.summary: The paper introduces GRAM, which estimates global rotations directly from relative rotations and inlier matches by minimizing edge-wise rotation-only algebraic residuals, replacing the standard two-stage pipeline of pairwise refinement plus rotation averaging. It further extends rotation-only imaging geometry to multi-view nonlinear optimization (MORE) with rotation-only reprojection error.

entry.title: 3R-Adapter: Retrieval, Rewiring, and Refinement for Efficient Adaptation of 3D Reconstruction Model

author.name: Zixiang Ai, Zhenyu Cui, Xu Zou, Jiahuan Zhou

entry.summary: The paper identifies relational attention structure collapse (failure of cross-view correspondences) as a cause of poor generalization in feed-forward 3D reconstruction models under long-tail conditions like low light or human-scene joint reconstruction. It proposes 3R-Adapter, a parameter-efficient fine-tuning approach that adapts relational structure via retrieval, rewiring, and refinement rather than channel-wise feature adjustment.

entry.title: Occupancy Modelling of Biased Landslide Inventories: When Does Separating Occurrence from Recording Improve on Neutralisation?

author.name: Abdirashid Omar, Abdikadir Ugaas

entry.summary: This paper adapts occupancy-detection modelling from ecology to landslide susceptibility mapping, treating multiple inventories as imperfect observers of one event and separating occurrence from recording. Using near-complete inventories from the 2018 Hokkaido, 2015 Gorkha, and 2010 Haiti earthquakes with simulated bias, the occupancy model reduces road bias in 24 of 25 paired draws and raises AUC by 0.08-0.14 on Gorkha and 0.03 on Haiti, but offers no advantage on Hokkaido.

entry.title: Frequency-consistent synthesis and selective transfer for medical image analysis

author.name: Zhuhui Wang, Jianwei Zuo, Xin Peng, Kai Zhong, Xuliang Deng, Jiajia Luo

entry.summary: The paper introduces a training framework linking medical image synthesis to downstream task learning via adaptive frequency consistency and selective feature transfer, where features are transferred only when a teacher on synthetic images achieves lower task-error than the student by a task-specific margin. Evaluations across five datasets show improved translation fidelity and brain-tumor segmentation gains.

entry.title: Understanding Spike Encoding across IoT Sensing Modalities: An Empirical Study

author.name: Yuxuan Hou, Di Yu, Linshan Jiang, Jin Zhang

entry.summary: This empirical study examines input encoding choices for spiking neural networks across wireless, inertial, surface EMG, and tactile sensing modalities, measuring energy, latency, and accuracy trade-offs. It finds that interleaving reduces energy and latency for wireless activity recognition, while repeating compact inputs can yield higher accuracy with the same input size per time step.

entry.title: Floquet-Parameterized Koopman-MPC for Tracking Periodic Orbits

author.name: Kartik A. Pant, Vishnu Vijay, Yufei Zhu, Xintong Deng, Taewoo Nam, Inseok Hwang

entry.summary: The paper proposes a physics-informed Koopman learning approach that incorporates periodic-orbit stability directly into the learned linear predictor, using Floquet theory to obtain stability information via monodromy matrices. This enables real-time MPC for tracking periodic orbits in complex coupled systems such as tethered kites.

entry.title: Correctness Boundaries of Typed Plans for Natural-Language Robot Fleet Control

author.name: Artem Tuzov, Dmitrii Vizitei, Evgenii Shlomov, Senya Belykh, Anastasia Malakhova, Alexander Maloletov

entry.summary: The paper examines what plan validation and execution reports establish in natural-language robot fleet control, tracing commands through typed plans, deterministic corrections, fleet coordination, and outcome checks in a three-level ROS 2 implementation with twenty simulated robots. An offline benchmark of 44 cases shows 70.0-87.3% of responses pass without a response schema, and the work documents failure modes like duplicate pickup assignments.

entry.title: Veterans' Mental Health Crisis Severity Annotation: Do LLMs Agree More Than Human Experts?

author.name: K M Sajjadul Islam, Pranav Yaramalla, Nadiyah Johnson, Mark Flower, Praveen Madiraju, Zeno Franco

entry.summary: The study evaluates LLM-based annotation of crisis severity in veteran-related social media posts against eight veteran subject matter experts, testing 25 LLMs across eight prompt variants on 149 tweets in five severity categories. It finds humans show higher ordinal than nominal agreement, indicating disagreements often occur between neighboring severity levels, and compares this against inter-model LLM agreement.

entry.title: Generative Active Learning for Label-Efficient Pan-Organ Ultrasound Diagnosis

author.name: Yaofei Duan, Yuhao Huang, Yuan Gao, Ruixiang Qi, Tianyu Zhang, Yanlin Geng, Yue Sun, Sio-Kei Im, Dong Ni, Dong Xu, Ritse Mann, Tao Tan

entry.summary: EvoDiff integrates diffusion modeling with information-theoretic objectives, evolutionary search, and curriculum-based sampling to select informative samples across heterogeneous ultrasound datasets for pan-organ diagnosis. It frames sample selection as a generate-to-retrieve process to address data scarcity, costly annotation, privacy constraints, and cross-center generalizability in medical AI.

entry.title: ProofDiff: Auditable Argument-Level Comparison of AI-Generated Mathematical Proofs

author.name: Matan Tsafrir, Esdras Medeiros, Jorge Poco, Kevin Gomez, Eduardo V. Teixeira, Claudio Silva

entry.summary: ProofDiff is a system for comparing informal mathematical documents at the argument level, reconstructing which claims, dependencies, and reasoning steps are preserved, reorganized, or replaced when proofs are generated or revised by generative models. Unlike formal verification, it checks whether a rewrite follows the same mathematical route, not just whether it proves the same theorem.

entry.title: Do large language models rank moral values? A transitivity test of moral competence

author.name: Katelyn A. Wasson, Kiwon Song, James M. Jennings III, Brittney Currie, Konstantina Sokratous, Clintin P. Stober

entry.summary: This paper distinguishes moral performance on benchmarks from moral competence, testing a necessary condition for weighing competing values: whether LLM moral choices can be represented by an ordinal ranking, which requires transitivity. Using pairwise trade-off vignettes and first-token probability extraction, choices are tested against three stochastic transitive choice models, with most choices showing mixed results.

entry.title: Too Big to Inspect? Ethically Auditing Large Datasets Through Small Samples

author.name: Giovana Marchetti, Jhessica Silva, Tiago Torrent, Carlos Caetano, Sandra Avila

entry.summary: This paper challenges the claim that web-scraped training datasets are too large to audit, proposing a practical method to identify structural biases using small samples combined with AI ethics guidelines. It addresses how biases absorbed from uncurated sources propagate into trained models. The work matters for dataset governance and responsible AI at scale.

entry.title: Beyond Query Similarity: Safety-Conditioned Cache Routing for LLM Response Reuse

author.name: Shilong Pan, Zhiliang Tian, Weiguo Chen, Zihan Chen, DongSheng Li

entry.summary: SafeCache is a semantic caching framework that makes the safety conditions of a cached response explicit and uses them to route reuse decisions, avoiding unsafe reuse when safety contexts change between similar queries. It balances safety and utility without the overhead of strict verification on every request. It matters as LLM serving systems increasingly adopt response caching for efficiency.

entry.title: SLA-Aware Task Offloading in the IoT Edge-Cloud Continuum: Class-Weighted Deep Reinforcement Learning Against an Exact Optimum

author.name: Shilpa Golla, Tharun Kumar Korine Palli, Urmila Bandaru

entry.summary: Builds four IoT task-offloading systems small enough to solve exactly by dynamic programming and measures DRL agents against the optimal policy. Shows class-blind penalties stay 65-118% above optimal cost even with perfect learners, while corrected per-class penalties come within 0.13% of optimum, highlighting a reward-design failure mode in edge offloading.

entry.title: Look Ahead: Search-Driven Reasoning in Embodied AI

author.name: Ahmed Zeer, Osama Shbib, Muzaffer Kaan Yuce, Himmet Toprak Kesgin, Mehmet Fatih Amasyali

entry.summary: The paper studies test-time search for vision-language action (VLA) models, applying beam search over perturbed action chunks around a frozen ACT policy's predictions in the PushT manipulation task, with candidates scored via rollouts from cloned simulator states. Selective search lifts task success from 0% to 18% and raises average cumulative reward substantially, and the proposed One Step Ahead (OSA) gate invokes full search only when the simulated nominal chunk predicts a coverage drop beyond a threshold. It demonstrates that search-time reasoning can meaningfully improve a weak frozen policy.

entry.title: What Broke & Why: Practical Lessons from Reinforcement Learning Post-Training

author.name: Luv Verma

entry.summary: A practical book-style guide to RL post-training of language models with verifiable rewards, covering GRPO and the training loop step by step, then five training programs spanning math reasoning, search agents, training stability, and mixed objectives, emphasizing failure modes such as reward hacking, lost exploration, and misleading evaluations.

entry.title: But It Was True When I Checked: Compiling SHOP-Style Method Preconditions into Partially-Ordered HTN Planning

author.name: Harrison Oates

entry.summary: This paper resolves an open question in hierarchical task network (HTN) planning by compiling SHOP-style first-action method precondition semantics into HDDL's partially-ordered setting, where unrelated actions can otherwise invalidate preconditions before a method starts. The work closes a long-standing semantic gap between the SHOP planners and the International Planning Competition's HTN input language. This is a technical contribution to classical automated planning.

entry.title: Inside the Trading Loop: Markets, Models, and Moves with LLM Agents

author.name: Renee Jia, Di Mu, Yao Yu, Tianrui Liu

entry.summary: The authors build a hybrid multi-agent trading system combining LLM analyst agents (company-news and macroeconomic) with momentum-based portfolio construction and rule-based execution. Over roughly six months of 2026, a broker-recorded paper account returned 34.5% versus 14.4% for SPY, though with larger drawdowns; retrospective replays of reconstructed policies also beat matched benchmarks.

entry.title: From Fluent Text to Ontology-Compatible Definitions: A Quality-Control Agentic Workflow

author.name: Kun Feng, Chenchen Chu, Yan Liu, Haojie Sun, Jijun Tang, Chen Tian, Shuolin Xiao, Jianping He, Zhao Li

entry.summary: This paper presents a quality-control agentic workflow for generating biomedical ontology definitions that are both readable and compatible with controlled entities, relations, and logical constraints. It tackles the problem that fluent LLM-generated definitions may still violate ontology-level constraints or fail to ground implied entities, making them unsafe for direct insertion.

entry.title: Reconstructing hourly traffic on every street of a capital from a sparse counting network: a graph neural network applied to Paris

author.name: Xavier Jurado (ICube), C{\'e}dric Wemmert (ICube, ICube-SDC), Nicolas Reiminger (ENGEES, ICube)

entry.summary: A graph neural network reconstructs hourly traffic flows on all 32,163 road segments of Paris from only 1,573 counter-equipped segments (4.9%), using edge-decoded flows on a junction graph, a traffic climatology offset, and zero-inflated negative-binomial likelihood with masked-counter training. Such full-network traffic data is essential for micro-scale air quality modeling. This is a solid applied ML contribution for urban analytics.

entry.title: Pixie: A Context-Aware Multi-Agent Multi-Modal Large Language Models (LLM) Architecture for Digital Marketing

author.name: Vivek Vishwas Vichare, Akshat Singhal, Kirill Dubovikov, Vivek Kumar, Sreyas Chaithanya, Saurabh Verma, Humeil Makhija, Mrunal Nasery

entry.summary: Pixie is a multi-agent LLM architecture for digital marketing operations, combining an orchestration agent with task-specific and reviewer agents that blend zero-shot/few-shot prompting with proprietary marketing data and expert strategy guidelines. The authors compare single-agent versus multi-agent workflows, evaluating accuracy, consistency, and domain-specific performance using trained marketing experts and output-variance measurements.

entry.title: Topological Deep Learning Challenge 2026: Bridging the Gap

author.name: Guillermo Bern\'ardez, Lev Telyatnikov, Mathilde Papillon, Marco Montagna, Louisa Cornelis, Louis Van Langendonck, Antonio Purificato, Bruno Neri, David Leko, Donatella Genovese, Eleonora Grassucci, Jan-Willem Van Looy, Johan Mathe, Lucia Testa, Luka Beni\'c, Melanie Weber, Olga Zaghen, Pavlo Vasylenko, Raffael Theiler, Scott Mahan, Gaurav Khanal, Valentina S\'anchez, Dario Loi, Gabriele Onorato, Prasanna Devadiga, Taejin Paik, Anier Velasco Sotomayor, Jonas M\"uller, Aarav Gupta, Riyan Patel, Grold Otieno Mboya, Pushparaj Devadiga, Adam Gohain, Dominik Filipiak, Michael Banf, Alireza Mohammadian, Amirreza Akbari, Gabriel Chaviano D\'iaz, Marcos Ch\'avez Mesa, Ankit Grover, R\'emi Bourgerie, Alessio Comparini, Ankit Kumar, Mohammad Yusuf, Devesh Kaushal, Francesco Orsi, Ghazal Mostofi, Kolya Lettl, Salwa Khattami, Gabriel Franco, Yelizaveta Falkouskaya, Jorge Luiz Franco, Kajal Singla, Fernando David Espinosa I\~niguez, Raj Patil, Eric Dolores-Cuenca, Luigi Petti, Chenguang Xu, Stefano Blando, Christine Zeh, Lennart Bastian, Kaden Zheng, Vihan Tiwari, Sud Athreya, Hisataka Kajita, Hugo Micheron, R\'emi Devaux, Antoine Jardin, Tegan Emerson, Olga Fink, Nina Miolane

entry.summary: This paper documents the 2026 Topological Deep Learning Challenge at the TAG-DS conference, which for the first time evaluated graph neural networks and topological neural networks side by side in a shared TopoBench pipeline. Participants implemented recent state-of-the-art architectures and tested them on synthetic benchmarks from GraphUniverse with controlled homophily and degree distributions. It serves as a community resource standardizing comparisons across the GNN/TNN divide.

entry.title: Enmo Safety: External, Non-invasive, Model-agnostic Oversight for Off-the-Shelf Language Models

author.name: Mohammed Nayeem Khan, Sarun Kumar K. S., Allan Kevin T., Chirag Vaidya, Vrishank Tiwari

entry.summary: Enmo Safety is a safety harness that wraps chat models without touching weights, combining deterministic input assessment, trigger-matched guidance, spotlighting of untrusted content, and output guarding, with a reflector that makes bounded, ledgered harness updates. It is evaluated on six open safety benchmarks including HarmBench, JailbreakBench, and AgentHarm. Notably, the abstract reports that before/after differences on two models were not statistically significant, suggesting limited demonstrated effectiveness.

entry.title: PoseBench: Probing Pose Awareness in Visual Foundation Models

author.name: Most Nilufa Yeasmin, Draix Wyatt, Ruyi Lian

entry.summary: PoseBench is a systematic benchmark probing whether 2D-pretrained visual foundation models encode pose awareness, i.e., whether their feature spaces align with object-pose manifolds. The evaluation progresses from held-out rendered views to progressively harder probes. The question matters for downstream 3D vision tasks that implicitly rely on pose-sensitive structure in foundation features.

entry.title: Beyond the Mean Gap: What Transferred-Angle QAOA Retains on a Superconducting Processor

author.name: Sanim Yousuf Fahim, Mohammad Arif Hossain

entry.summary: The authors test depth-2 transferred-angle QAOA circuits on the IBM Heron processor ibm_marrakesh, showing under global depolarization that bitstring probabilities retain the same fraction of noiseless improvement as the mean gap, validated with and without dynamical decoupling and twirling. At 12 qubits, main-family circuits retained 29-46% of mean-gap improvement. A careful hardware study of what noise preserves in quantum optimization.

entry.title: Understanding the Effect of Visual Attention in CNNs: A Decision-Space Alignment Perspective

author.name: Niladri B. Puhan, K. Kamala Priya

entry.summary: The paper models multiplicative attention in CNNs as a feature perturbation and derives a first-order prediction of its effect on classification margins. It introduces a Decision Alignment Score (DAS) and evaluates it on CIFAR-100 with SimAM and CBAM across five CNN backbones to explain when attention helps or hurts decisions.

entry.title: The RenAIssance: Caption-Guided Diffusion Models for Historical-Art Visual Media

author.name: Zhanyu Tuo

entry.summary: This work builds a pipeline that converts a collection of historical European artworks into roughly 15,000 image-text pairs using BLIP captions, then trains a compact LoRA adapter for Stable Diffusion v1.5 to shift generations toward the historical-art distribution while preserving novel-concept rendering. It improves FID on historical and contemporary prompts.

entry.title: Trained, Frozen, or Absent: Identifying What a Quantum Layer Contributes to Cross-Sectional Equity Ranking

author.name: Chi-Sheng Chen, Xinyu Zhang, En-Jui Kuo, Rong Fu, Qiuzhe Xie, Fan Zhang

entry.summary: This study isolates the actual contribution of a quantum layer in a hybrid quantum-classical temporal convolutional network for ranking 2000 Tokyo Stock Exchange equities, using six conditions (trained, frozen, absent, classical surrogate, circuit alone) through one code path. Rigorous evaluation with walk-forward folds, bootstrap intervals, deflated Sharpe ratios, and a locked holdout aims to separate quantum gains from classical components.

entry.title: Robust Satisficing Ensemble: Scalable Model Aggregation Under Distribution Shifts

author.name: Ahmet Faruk Cetinkaya, Enes Agirman, Cem Tekin

entry.summary: RSE is a probabilistic ensemble aggregation framework that minimizes fragility against distributional changes by bridging a robust satisficing objective with a quadratic risk surrogate, yielding an analytical inner adversary. This reformulation enables efficient weight updates without the computational bottleneck of standard minimax optimization, decoupling optimization complexity from sample size.

entry.title: GradReason: LLMs as Meta-Learners that Replace Training Epochs with Training-Data-Free Weight Updates

author.name: Ali Mohammadi Ruzbahani, Abbas Yazdinejad, Hadis Karimipour

entry.summary: GradReason uses an LLM agent, invoked every ten epochs, to analyze weight snapshots, gradient statistics, and validation metrics, then generate a program producing new weights and designating upcoming epochs as data epochs or virtual (no-data) epochs. Virtual epochs are kept only if they pass a forward-only check on held-out validation images, with results reported on CIFAR-10 across 120 runs.

entry.title: Finite-Sample and Communication-Efficient Networked Information Aggregation

author.name: Mohammadhossein Bateni, Zahra Hadizadeh, MohammadTaghi Hajiaghayi, Mahdi JafariRaviz, Shayan Taherijam

entry.summary: Building on SODA 2026 work by Kearns et al., the paper studies learning in directed acyclic graphs where each agent sees only a subset of coordinates and can use parent predictions. The authors identify and fix a gap in the prior finite-sample proof and develop communication-efficient variants of the message-passing protocol.

entry.title: Agentic Attribution of Cloud Resource Ownership

author.name: Tiltan Gilat, Gal Engelberg, Ariel Zadok, Leon Goldberg

entry.summary: Addresses the problem that AI agents investigating cloud security findings need to reach the people responsible for and accountable for each resource, but ownership data is scattered across work records, code history, audit logs, and identity directories with no authoritative source. The paper proposes an agentic approach to recovering ownership from these heterogeneous sources.

entry.title: LLM-based Multi-Criteria Deep Reinforcement Learning for Dynamic Efficient 5G UPF Selection

author.name: Abdelrahman Soliman, Ahmed Refaey Hussein, Lei Lei

entry.summary: This paper proposes a deep reinforcement learning method for selecting user plane functions (UPFs) in 5G networks, using a dynamic multi-objective reward and LLM-based translation of operator intents plus NWDAF anomaly alerts. It is validated on a real-world 5G emulation platform rather than only simulation.

entry.title: Boundary Mass in Feature Space as a Label-Budget Diagnostic for Representations

author.name: Siming Zhang, Zhehui Shen, Shijie Chen, Yansen Yu, Hang Yu

entry.summary: The paper proposes effective boundary complexity, a label-budget diagnostic for frozen representations and linear probes that measures class-balanced mass in a thin strip around the learned decision boundary, complementing existing transferability and probe-quality scores. The authors prove that under smooth representation maps, density changes near the boundary characterize how many labels the downstream task will need.

entry.title: Continuous modeling of manipulative participation for stance analysis: Online discourse on the 2024 Street Animal Law in T\"urkiye

author.name: Ulya Bayram, Ebru Belk{\i}s G\"uzelo\u{g}lu, Emel Ku\c{s}ku \"Ozdemir, Elif \"Ust\"unda\u{g}l{\i} Erten, \"Oyk\"um Esra Yi\u{g}it

entry.summary: The paper proposes modeling manipulative (coordinated/inauthentic) participation as a continuous rather than binary quantity and integrates this with stance analysis, using discourse around Turkiye's 2024 Street Animal Law as a case study. It builds on a large dataset of over 7.3 million tweets from roughly 538,000 users with high-information sampling for labeling.

entry.title: Late but Valuable: Why Deadlines Change the Measured Value of LLM Reasoning

author.name: Sina Barazandeh, Benjamin E. Lundell, Jose Lugo-Martinez

entry.summary: Argues that in automated laboratories with hard deadlines, standard metrics that report answer quality and latency separately overstate reasoning value, because a late correct answer triggers the same safe fallback as no answer at all. The paper proposes deadline-aware evaluation on synthetic sample decisions where the optimal choice is known exactly.

entry.title: Transactional Data Change for Real-Time Analytics in Lakehouses

author.name: Dongyang Geng, Haoqiong Bian, Zinuo Li, Haoyue Li

entry.summary: Retina is a novel data synchronization framework enabling real-time, cost-efficient propagation of data changes into lakehouses with ACID guarantees. It tackles the RUM-conjecture tradeoff created by read-optimized immutable file storage that current git-style catalog versioning handles poorly.

entry.title: TrajLift: Lifting Memory Recall Trajectories with Latency-Modulated Heat Diffusion

author.name: Jiawen Kang, Jinchao Li, Mingyu Cui, Junan Li, Xixin Wu, Helen Meng

entry.summary: TrajLift models verbal memory recall in Alzheimer's assessment as timed trajectories over a hierarchical semantic graph, using latency-modulated heat diffusion to jointly represent multi-scale structure and retrieval timing. This disentangles the diagnostically entangled timing and hierarchy signals in word-recall data.

entry.title: Certify, Report, or Refuse: Harm-Constrained Conformal Prediction for Clinical Actions

author.name: Zhiyuan Li, Lequan Yu

entry.summary: HC-ROCP is a training-free framework that adds harm penalties to conformal prediction over frozen classifier probabilities, producing policies that certify supported claims, report descriptive fallbacks, and refuse unsupported subgroup claims. Evaluated across COVID-19 radiographs, ISIC 2019 dermoscopy, and EyePACS-to-APTOS retinopathy transfer with multiplicity-adjusted calibration, it reduces severe-action errors such as routing melanoma cases to routine follow-up. This connects uncertainty quantification directly to harm-aware clinical decision policies.

entry.title: Multi-Agent Screening: What Agreement and Acceptance Cannot Tell You

author.name: Benjamin Chang, Dell Zhang

entry.summary: This paper analyzes what evidence about AI agents used for screening (as in agentic search, e-discovery, and AI peer review) can establish about their errors when only passed items get human judgment. It shows agreement among agents demonstrates concurrence rather than correctness, assessor acceptance yields precision but only a lower bound on recall, and recall can be identified only by judging a random sample of items the agents did not pass. The results are a sharp methodological caution for evaluating multi-agent screening pipelines.

entry.title: PORT: Preference Optimization via Robust Token-Level Reweighting

author.name: Ding Zhu, Xiukun Wei, Tian Xie, Zhihui Zhu, Xueru Zhang, Mohammad Mahdi Khalili

entry.summary: PORT is a fine-grained framework for robust preference optimization under noisy annotations that reweights at the token level rather than treating entire responses as uniformly correct or incorrect. It exploits the observation that rejected responses may still contain informative reasoning steps while preferred responses can include subtle errors. This refines alignment methods such as DPO-style training for the realistic setting of imperfect preference data.

entry.title: Programming Prescience: Issues in Human Construction of Forecasting Bots

author.name: Priya Dhawka, Benjamin Wilson, Andrew Head

entry.summary: A qualitative interview study of 15 builders of AI forecasting bots from a recent competition, surfacing challenges in tuning bots to gather factual research, implementing coherent reasoning, and evaluating bot performance. The study finds builders often introduce complexity that harms calibration and accuracy.

entry.title: TripletAD: Weakly Supervised Anomaly Detection in Embedding Space with Rare Anomalies and Scarce Labels

author.name: Sumit Wadhwa, Souvik Nath

entry.summary: TripletAD is a weakly supervised anomaly detector for settings with only a handful of confirmed anomalies, using a curated-label protocol where unconfirmed anomalies are removed from training. It learns a triplet-margin embedding with a linear scoring head calibrated via partial cross-entropy on labeled anomalies and a relative-contrast hinge, reusing the few labels across all mined triplets.

entry.title: Applied bifidelity material response model construction and uncertainty quantification with a sampling hypernetwork

author.name: Reese E. Jones, Cosmin Safta, Dan Bolintineau, Craig M. Hamel, Gianluca Geraci, Sharlotte LB Kramer

entry.summary: The work develops a bifidelity Langevin sampling hypernetwork that constructs probabilistic neural response models for material response by learning a posterior distribution over parameters rather than a single deterministic fit, with shared-latent representation for transfer between low- and high-fidelity data. It includes robustness enhancements such as stability-promoting drift models.

entry.title: Confronting Uncertainty in Mechanism-AI Coupled Dynamical Systems via Optimal Transport and Information Geometry: Part I. Distribution Learning

author.name: Pengfei Song, Yanni Xiao, Shuangshuang Yin

entry.summary: The paper formulates uncertainty quantification for mechanism-AI coupled dynamical systems, common in biological modeling, using optimal transport and information geometry. It casts distribution learning as minimization of an energy functional on probability density space and unifies gradient flows under Wasserstein and Fisher-Rao metrics.

entry.title: Spectral Bias Reduction in Local Gated ReLU Architectures

author.name: Victorita Dolean

entry.summary: The paper provides a theoretical analysis of spectral bias — the tendency of gradient-trained networks to learn low-frequency content first — for shallow ReLU models linear in their trainable parameters, using a general symmetric bilinear form that unifies least-squares and physics-informed (variational) losses. It proposes gated local ReLU dictionaries as an architectural mitigation. This is primarily a theory paper on which architectural choices can and cannot reduce spectral bias.

entry.title: Constrained Look-ahead Guidance for Interference-Aware Flow Editing

author.name: Doudou Zhang, Qi Chen

entry.summary: The paper proposes an inversion-free framework for flow-based image editing that uses a one-step look-ahead mechanism to evaluate candidate updates against both edit-compliance and fidelity rewards, applying reward-driven corrections under an explicit fidelity constraint. This yields more stable and coherent editing trajectories than heuristic guidance or inversion-based pipelines.

entry.title: An Analysis of Reinforcement Learning with Function Approximation

author.name: Francisco S. Melo, Sean P. Meyn, M. Isabel Ribeiro

entry.summary: The paper analyzes convergence of Q-learning variants with function approximation in Markov decision problems with infinite state spaces, extending Tsitsiklis and Van Roy's TD-learning analysis to stochastic control settings. It identifies conditions for almost-sure convergence of approximate Q-learning methods.

entry.title: Hybrid Product Search Without the Copy: Lexical, Semantic and Filtered Retrieval Served Directly from a Data Lake

author.name: Raghvendra Yadav, Xiang Fu, Chinmay Soman

entry.summary: This systems paper extends Apache Pinot to serve hybrid product search - BM25 lexical scoring, semantic retrieval, and filtered queries - directly over lakehouse tables in object storage, eliminating separate lexical and vector database copies. It adds corpus-wide term statistics and reciprocal rank fusion in SQL, with a real-time table for freshness.

entry.title: ZarrFM: A Canonical Tensor Storage Architecture for EEG Foundation-Model Pretraining

author.name: Dheeraj Chintapalli, Sunkalp Chandra

entry.summary: ZarrFM proposes storing heterogeneous EEG corpora as a single Zarr v3 hierarchy with indexed metadata, canonical channel spaces, explicit masks, and hash-stable subject splits to reduce preprocessing and I/O overhead for BCI foundation-model pretraining. On PhysioNet recordings it reduces metadata queries from 601 requests to 14 and outperforms EDF, FIF, NPY, HDF5, and Parquet baselines.

entry.title: ALETHEIA: A Multi-Frequency Eddy Current Pulsed Thermography Dataset for Neural Operator Learning in Nondestructive Testing

author.name: Changbin Sun, Jie Xiao, Xiaotian Chen, Yuankai Wu

entry.summary: Aletheia is the first 3D benchmark dataset for learning neural PDE solvers in nondestructive testing, simulating eddy-current heating and transient heat propagation in conductive solids. It contains over 4,700 high-resolution volumetric samples across 10 excitation frequencies, supporting both forward temperature prediction and inverse defect identification under sparse, noisy boundary observations. It fills a real gap in scientific ML benchmarks for industrial inspection.

entry.title: ConvLUT: Rethinking Convolutional Architectures for Ultra-Low-Latency LUT-Based Inference

author.name: Marta Andronic, Olivia Weng, Danial Zuberi, Ryan Kastner, George A. Constantinides

entry.summary: ConvLUT extends lookup-table-based neural networks beyond MLP-style topologies to fully unrolled LUT-mappable convolutional architectures, including depthwise separable variants following MobileNet design principles, targeting MLPerf Tiny benchmarks on FPGAs. It is enabled by a unified LUT-based convolutional framework with explicit fan-in constraints plus supporting compiler/runtime contributions. This opens ultra-low-latency FPGA inference to vision and audio workloads.

entry.title: Resolvent Ellipsoid for Minty Set Inclusions

author.name: Ashkan Soleymani, Gabriele Farina, Patrick Jaillet

entry.summary: The paper studies Minty set inclusion with set-valued operators on compact convex sets and develops a geometric approach in a fixed-scale constrained-resolvent oracle model. It proves a sharp dichotomy: each oracle response either yields an epsilon-SVI certificate or a strict separating normal, forming the basis of a resolvent ellipsoid method.

entry.title: Constrained Variational Policy Optimization for Hybrid Action Spaces

author.name: Shuchang Yan

entry.summary: This paper extends Constrained Variational Policy Optimization (CVPO) to hybrid action spaces (discrete modes plus mode-conditioned continuous controls), introducing H-CVPO. It shows the constrained E-step has zero duality gap under boundedness and strict feasibility, and yields closed-form updates when the dual optimum is attained at positive temperature.

entry.title: MambaPD: Bidirectional Selective State Space Model for Parkinson's Disease Detection from Resting-State EEG

author.name: Ayesha Zulfiqar

entry.summary: MambaPD is a bidirectional selective state space model (Mamba) for detecting Parkinson's disease from resting-state EEG, combining channel mixing, patch tokenization, and a bidirectional Mamba encoder. It is evaluated against four baselines on two public datasets with subject-independent 5-fold cross-validation, and notes that many published EEG-PD detectors claiming >95% accuracy suffer from subject-identity leakage through epoch-level splits.

entry.title: Forecast Value Add: Reward-Based Action Selection over Probabilistic Demand Forecasts

author.name: Ankur Verma

entry.summary: The paper reframes demand forecast refinement as a reward-driven decision problem: an agent selects among values already produced by an ensemble (base forecast, distribution-free bounds, quantiles, bias-corrected estimates) for each forecast period, evaluated against context-matched historical periods accounting for calendar position, events, trend, price, and promotions. A structural seasonal guard constrains adjustments to avoid overcorrection. This is notable because it treats forecasting as action selection with measurable value-add rather than pure prediction, bridging forecasting and decision-making in supply chains.

entry.title: An Empirical Evaluation of Quantum Kernel Stability in Network Intrusion Detection

author.name: Sreejonty Chakraborty, Adrita Rahman Tory, Muhammad Aminur Rahaman, Khondokar Fida Hasan

entry.summary: This study tests whether quantum kernel methods' poor performance in network intrusion detection is due to hardware noise, using controlled Pegasos-QSVC experiments on NSL-KDD and ToN-IoT across noiseless and noise-simulated backends. XGBoost strongly outperforms the quantum model (98.94% vs 91.80% on NSL-KDD), and the quantum model shows high seed-dependent variability even without noise.

entry.title: Trade Promotion Optimisation for Consumer Goods

author.name: Ankur Verma, Namrata Gupta

entry.summary: The paper presents an end-to-end trade promotion optimization system built as a chain from analogue SKUs and point elasticity through to price recommendation and net lift, using causal estimators with Tobit likelihood for stock-out censoring. It addresses the problem that planners typically use a single, unreliable price elasticity per item.

entry.title: Controlled Binary Assignment Flows

author.name: Paul Fr\"ohling, Christoph Schn\"orr

entry.summary: The paper introduces a geometric approach to deep assignment flows for binary data labelings on graphs, where each edge carries an optimally controlled parameter flow in a 2-dimensional totally geodesic submanifold and flows are aggregated in higher-dimensional submanifolds. Numerical results demonstrate the expressivity and limitations of this highly parallel geometric construction.

entry.title: Fisher-Glass Learning: Classification Bounds and Subpopulation Audits

author.name: El Mustapha Mansouri

entry.summary: The paper extends the Fisher-glass framework to link nuisance-adjusted task information with local classification difficulty, deriving lower bounds on local minimax excess risk under explicit distinguishability conditions. It also proposes statistical audits for subpopulations, demonstrated on the Waterbirds benchmark with a feature-based diagnostic validated on held-out data. The work addresses why accurate classifiers fail when background cues shift without label changes.

entry.title: Adaptive Quantization Preserves Fast Rates for TD Learning over Rate-Limited Channels

author.name: Sreejeet Maity, Aritra Mitra

entry.summary: The paper studies policy evaluation with linear function approximation when an RL agent must transmit quantized temporal-difference update directions to a server over a finite-capacity channel. The proposed BAQ-TD algorithm combines batching to reduce transmitted-information variance with adaptive quantization, and the authors prove it preserves the statistical convergence rates achievable with infinite-capacity communication. This gives tight theory for distributed RL under communication constraints.

entry.title: Continual Instruction Tuning for LLM-ased Management of Continuum Resources

author.name: Lanpei Li, Antonino Vaccarella, Vincenzo Lomonaco, Massimo Coppola

entry.summary: The paper argues LLMs should not sit inside latency-sensitive cloud-edge control loops; instead, a continually instruction-tuned intent compiler runs once per management intent above a fast deterministic tactical controller. Intent compilation is formulated as a continual instruction tuning problem since intents arrive sequentially while infrastructure and workload contexts drift.

entry.title: Action Transfer Across Character Body Plans in Latent-Action World Models: An Empirical Study of Animated Characters

author.name: Amarnath R

entry.summary: This paper studies whether latent actions learned from video of one animated character can transfer to characters with different body structures, such as a cat, blob, or human performing a jump. The authors identify a flaw in standard transfer metrics that conflates body motion with screen movement, and introduce a corrected transfer score that compares correct actions against wrong actions from the same source. They evaluate five training objectives on a new synthetic benchmark of 2D characters.

entry.title: Network Contention State Aware Dynamic Optimizer for Accelerator Collective Communication Libraries

author.name: Rajat Bisht (Tennessee Technological University), Tevfik Kosar (University at Buffalo), Anthony Skjellum (Tennessee Technological University), Gene Cooperman (Northeastern University), MD S Q Zulkar Nine (Arkansas Tech University)

entry.summary: The paper presents a cooperative multi-agent runtime optimizer for collective communication libraries used in large-scale distributed AI training, whose static heuristics degrade under background network traffic. A two-agent architecture uses an LSTM-based detector with a sequential probability ratio test to distinguish sustained contention from transient spikes, plus a selector agent for configuration decisions. The empirical study shows near-optimal static performance in contention-free settings but substantial degradation under real traffic.

entry.title: Multi-Node Transformers for Object Detection and Captioning Across Distributed Edge Networks

author.name: Saurabh Kumar, Dewant Katare, Prakriti Jain

entry.summary: Presents a unified transformer framework for object detection and dense region captioning that shares a single visual encoder across both tasks, removing the second encoding path of decoupled pipelines. Includes a workload-allocation formulation distributing model stages across resource-constrained edge nodes under memory, power, and communication constraints.

entry.title: The Relative Value of Demonstration Data: Execution Time Limits and Operator Mixtures in Behavior Cloning

author.name: Jiaxuan Guo, Xingyu Ren, Youran Sun, Jingxin Yang, Kejia Zhang, Haizhao Yang

entry.summary: This paper quantifies how much data from lower-skill teleoperators is needed to match data from higher-skill ones in robot behavior cloning, introducing a data multiple metric on robomimic Square and Can tasks. It finds that an all-Worse training set needs about 1.55 times as many demonstrations as an all-Better set on Square, and shows that most of this difference is driven by how execution time limits interact with operator skill.

entry.title: Low-rank Low Precision Training of Gaussian Processes

author.name: Moritz Poguntke, Eda Oktay, Yuanzhe Xi, Erin Carson, Martin Stoll

entry.summary: This work develops a scalable Gaussian process training method combining AnchorNet landmark selection with FITC corrections, avoiding formation of dense kernel matrices and their derivatives. The entire procedure runs in single precision and matches reference predictive accuracy on nine large-scale regression datasets. It offers practical efficiency gains for large-scale GP inference.

entry.title: Cascading Circle Loss: Order-Preserving Contrastive Learning for Graded Legal Retrieval

author.name: Rayane Kimouche, Ahmed Touila

entry.summary: The paper introduces Cascading Circle Loss (CasCL), a contrastive learning framework for legal retrieval with graded relevance, combining InfoNCE with a cascade of ranking boundaries that encode ordered relevance levels. It adds negative-aware self-paced optimization and relevance gain weighting to improve ranking quality. Experiments on legal passage retrieval benchmarks show consistent gains over InfoNCE, Circle Loss, MNRL, and Margin MSE across binary and graded metrics.

entry.title: SCorPion: A Strategic, Controllable and Personified Conversational Companion

author.name: Luo Ji, Xiyuan Chen, Dan Wang, Qingqing Gu, Teng Chen, Feixiang Guo, Yetao Wu, Jinxian Qu, Yue Zhao, Kun Fan, Ningyuan Xi, Hange Zhou, Zhonglin Jiang, Yong Chen, Hongyan Li

entry.summary: This paper presents SCorPion, a conversational companion system that extracts chatting strategies from text corpora and uses GraphRAG to build knowledge-graph-derived community summaries and query-focused optimal strategies. The system steers a language model toward different conversational styles based on human principles, enabling controllable, personified responses in open-domain dialogue.

entry.title: Beyond Hard Labels: LLM Probabilities Improve Human-Assisted Regression

author.name: Xinyue Wang (Department of Statistics, The Pennsylvania State University), Qunhua Li (Department of Statistics, The Pennsylvania State University)

entry.summary: The paper studies whether retaining full LLM probability vectors, rather than collapsing them to hard categorical labels, improves downstream regression when LLM annotations are combined with limited human annotation. Using three LLMs and three social-science datasets, the authors find soft inputs are not uniformly better directly, but after human correction they consistently improve downstream regression.

entry.title: The Deception Archive as a repository of standardized datasets for large-scale verbal deception detection research

author.name: Caterina Borgese, Riccardo Loconte, Lucca Pfr\"under, Bennett Kleinberg

entry.summary: The Deception Archive is a curated, standardized repository of publicly available verbal deception datasets built from a large-scale systematic review, addressing fragmentation across disciplines that has limited cross-study comparison. It currently aggregates 41 datasets containing roughly 38 (truncated, likely tens of thousands of) samples, with manual inspection and a structured curation workflow. This infrastructure should accelerate robust computational deception-detection research.

entry.title: Collaboration Signatures: Tracking Long-Horizon Dynamics of Cross-Meeting Collaboration Networks

author.name: Shengqi Zhu, Sheshera Mysore, Bahareh Sarrafzadeh

entry.summary: The authors build a cross-meeting collaboration network from 45,426 meeting transcripts and 1.6 million agenda items at a multinational technology company, moving beyond fragmented email/chat logs. The network recovers natural shapes of workplace collaboration and enables tracking of long-horizon collaboration dynamics. This matters because it grounds organizational network analysis in actual meeting content rather than just contact counts.

entry.title: Agent4Crypto: A Dual-Reflective and Market-Feedback-Aligned LLM-Based Multi-Agent System for Cryptocurrency Trading

author.name: Guangyan Gan, Jiahao Li, Jiashun Wang, Lin William Cong

entry.summary: Agent4Crypto coordinates specialized LLM agents for data collection, analysis, risk assessment, reflection, and trading in cryptocurrency markets, synthesizing prices, indicators, news, and charts in an interpretable pipeline. Its core design uses three style-specific trader agents (Aggressive, Neutral, Conservative) under a trader-centric decision mechanism with market feedback alignment. It targets known weaknesses of autonomous trading agents: non-stationary regimes, opaque decisions, and fixed aggregation rules.

entry.title: Stochastic Deep Supervision for Gallery-Consistent Early-Exit Face Recognition

author.name: Guray Ozgur, Tahar Chettaoui, Eduarda Caldeira, Naser Damer, Fadi Boutros

entry.summary: SD-ViT is a training framework for face-recognition Vision Transformers that gives every intermediate block depth a usable exit by stochastically passing a random intermediate block through the embedding head with a weighted margin-penalty softmax loss each iteration. This enables budget-selected fixed-depth early exits in resource-constrained deployments. It matters because standard ViT intermediate representations are not directly optimized to form identity embeddings, limiting early-exit inference.

entry.title: Same Pixels, Different Documents: Measuring Part-Level Editability in Image Vectorization

author.name: Boheng Zhu, Zehua Wang, Wei Chen, Ming-Hao Lin

entry.summary: This paper argues that image vectorization should be evaluated by editability, not just rendering fidelity, and introduces Pass@k, which tests whether a prescribed edit can succeed using objects selectable within k clicks under a specified interaction model. The evaluation also includes eight document diagnostics, controlled perturbations for structural sensitivity, and designer operations for practical relevance, applied to twelve open and commercial methods over 211 references. It matters because it exposes a blind spot in how vectorization methods are currently judged.

entry.title: S2HAND: Accuracy-Preservation Trade-Offs for Hand Specialization in Whole-Body Pose Models

author.name: Singyu Muk, Xuanren Song, Kalin Stefanov

entry.summary: S2HAND specializes the Sapiens2-5B whole-body pose model for hands while preserving its 308-keypoint interface, offering a lightweight 0.87M-parameter routing branch (S2HAND-MT) and a stronger variant fine-tuning Fisher-selected Transformer blocks. It avoids the detection overhead and wrist-stitching artifacts of attaching standalone hand specialists.

entry.title: Decoupling Direction and Magnitude: Language-Steered Flow Matching for Super-Resolution in the Dark

author.name: Jiaxin Gao, Ziyu Yue, Yaohua Liu, Danchen Cui, Zhihui Zhao, Zhixun Su

entry.summary: DeLang-SR is a one-step flow-matching framework for super-resolution in low-light images that decouples restoration direction and magnitude, using language steering to treat degradation heterogeneity spatially. It targets the problem that uniform diffusion trajectories mishandle severely underexposed regions versus well-exposed areas.

entry.title: SHIN: Scalable Hierarchy for INcremental 3D Gaussian Splatting

author.name: Reagan Koo, Yeong-Gyu Kim, Eun-Seok Ryu

entry.summary: SHIN provides a scalable 3DGS hierarchy with a reusable base and additive enhancement layers, so each quality operating point extends rather than replaces the decoded representation. It derives a shared Gaussian ordering from multi-scale position-scale sensitivity and allocates each stage budget between geometry and spherical-harmonic appearance.

entry.title: Same Measurements, Different Velocity Risk: Complementary Rolling-Shutter Readouts under Clock Uncertainty

author.name: Lunshuo Tian, Dongheng Liu, Mingwei Ma

entry.summary: This theory paper proves that rolling-shutter camera rigs with identical measurement budgets can have different worst-case velocity estimation risk depending on readout complementarity under clock uncertainty, establishing minimax risk order separations (sigma*rho_eff versus sigma^2) with a finite compensation path lower bound.

entry.title: MySign: A High-Fidelity Motion-Capture Dataset for 3D Sign Generation in Bahasa Isyarat Malaysia

author.name: Jiayu Shen, Kalin Stefanov, Lay-Ki Soon, Vee Yee Chong, Alpha Agape Gopalai, KokSheik Wong

entry.summary: MySign is the first motion-capture dataset for isolated signs in Bahasa Isyarat Malaysia, containing 5,000 samples across 1,000 glosses produced by five Deaf native signers. Unlike prior datasets relying on SMPL-X parameters regressed from video (with depth ambiguity and temporal jitter), it provides ground-truth SMPL-X sequences retargeted from a sign-language-tailored mocap setup. This supports higher-fidelity 3D sign generation, particularly for under-resourced sign languages.

entry.title: Graphene: A Lightweight Transformer with Ising Mean-Field Refinement for Image Super-Resolution

author.name: Seungki Hong, Taekwang Jang

entry.summary: Graphene is a lightweight super-resolution transformer combining an Ising-model-inspired refinement block that reuses attention logits for signed pairwise token couplings with a History Attention module over stage outputs. The design targets efficient feature refinement for image restoration.

entry.title: Conditional Diffusion-Based Proxy Representation Recovery for BCVA Prediction with Missing SLO Modality

author.name: Chuyi He, Hua Zou, Fei Luo, Zixian Yang

entry.summary: For predicting postoperative visual acuity after cataract surgery, this work handles missing SLO images by using conditional diffusion to recover proxy representations rather than raw images, then fusing them with OCT and clinical text for multimodal prediction. This targets a common real-world problem of incomplete clinical multimodal data.

entry.title: Where Does Proposal Selection Fail? Diagnosing Frozen Vision-Language Queries over Detector Proposals

author.name: Bo Ma, Weiqi Yan, Jinsong Wu

entry.summary: This controlled study diagnoses failure modes in modular visual grounding, where a frozen detector proposes regions and a vision-language model selects one, holding perception fixed so selectors choose among identical proposals containing the referent for at least 99.8% of RefCOCO/+/g queries. Using Qwen2.5-VL-7B and Qwen3-VL-8B, it finds that what the selector reads matters more than architecture: image-conditioned query encoding of referent location beats text-only queries by 0.15-0.18 with every head tested.

entry.title: Attention-Guided Sequence Feature Fusion and Mixed-Space Metric Learning for Cross-View Image Sequence Geo-Localization

author.name: Nan Wu, Chunfang Yang, Jiangshan Li, Xiangyang Luo

entry.summary: The paper introduces ASML, a method for localizing ground-level image sequences against geo-tagged satellite imagery. It uses a Sequential Content Fusion module to suppress redundant overlapping features and preserve geographically informative non-overlapping content, paired with mixed-space metric learning to improve cross-view matching.

entry.title: GHiML: VLM-Guided Hierarchical Multi-Label Learning with Applications to Benthic Imagery

author.name: Isaac Xu, Devi Ayyagari, Martin Gillis, Benjamin Misiuk, Craig J. Brown, Thomas Trappenberg

entry.summary: GHiML extracts conceptual latent variables from a VLM conditioned on training data, generates sample-relevant captions grounded in those variables, and fuses textual embeddings with image embeddings via cross-attention and a per-node gated router for hierarchical multi-label classification. It is applied to benthic (seabed) imagery classification.

entry.title: National-Scale Crop Type Mapping in Morocco Using Google AlphaEarth Foundations Embeddings and the Fields of the World Field Boundary Map

author.name: Walid Elbarz, Mohamed Bourriz, Vincent Simonneaux, Hamd Ait Abdelali, Fran\c{c}ois Bourzeix

entry.summary: The authors demonstrate national-scale crop type mapping in Morocco using pretrained 64-dimensional embeddings from Google's AlphaEarth Foundations (an existing geospatial foundation model), paired with the Fields of the World field boundary map. Lightweight downstream classifiers on frozen embeddings avoid processing raw satellite imagery, targeting winter cereals, tree crops, and other crops.

entry.title: Confidence-driven adaptive semantic transmission for task-oriented communication

author.name: Suman Das, Prajnyajit Mohanty, Siddhartha S. Borkotoky

entry.summary: The paper proposes Confidence-Driven Adaptation (CDA) for image-based remote monitoring over wireless networks: an edge device runs a lightweight classifier and, based on confidence, selects among three transmission modes (text label, compressed ROI, or full image). This balances communication cost against classification reliability.

entry.title: Leveraging High-Activity Post-Therapeutic I-131 Scans for Deep Learning Reconstruction of Extremely Sparse Planar Images in Differentiated Thyroid Cancer

author.name: Boyang Pan, Hang Yang, Jianchen Pan, Cui Gan, Lanxi Zhang, Hongmin Li, Nan-Jie Gong

entry.summary: This prospective clinical study (111 patients) tests whether high-quality post-therapeutic I-131 scans can serve as training references for enhancing sparse diagnostic planar images in differentiated thyroid cancer, using Restormer-based models with transfer learning and input-image addition across five configurations.

entry.title: Grip, Trace, Write: Force-Aware Imitation and Reinforcement Learning for High-DoF Robotic Handwriting

author.name: Rongqian Chen, Yiding Chen, Jijie Zhou, Tom Z. Jiahao

entry.summary: The paper presents a force-aware simulation environment and learning framework for robotic handwriting with a freely held pen, coupling grasp stability, tip motion, and contact force. A two-branch actor separates pen retention from arm-wrist writing, trained with behavior cloning from IK demonstrations and refined with RL rewards on ink, force, time, and retention, outperforming pure BC and IK baselines.

entry.title: Online Geometric Consistency Assessment of LiDAR Measurements via Recursive Bayesian Comparison

author.name: Mingqiao Han, Qigeng Duan, Xuchen Liu, Jinqiang Cui, Xi Chen, Ben M. Chen

entry.summary: The paper formulates a recursive Bayesian comparison that couples geometric assessment of LiDAR point clouds with history maintenance, using a Normal-Inverse-Wishart model for historical voxel geometry and uncertainty. This enables online detection of registration errors such as duplicated surfaces and deformation without an independent reference.

entry.title: Kinora: A Versioned Workflow for Text-to-Motion Generation, Robot Retargeting, and Interactive Validation

author.name: Fangcheng Jin (University of Chinese Academy of Sciences)

entry.summary: Kinora is a system connecting text-to-motion generation, a motion library, agent tools, robot retargeting, and trajectory refinement through versioned, immutable artifacts with explicit geometry and model-specific validation reports. It separates a 52-joint authoring rig from external generation models and robot assets, supporting traceable edits and recoverable execution. It targets the engineering gap between generative motion models and reliable robot deployment.

entry.title: A Game-Theoretic MPC Planner for Cooperative and Adversarial Drone Coordination

author.name: Zden\v{e}k Bou\v{c}ek, Miroslav Fl\'idr

entry.summary: A game-theoretic model predictive control planner handles cooperative goal reaching and adversarial pursuit-evasion with drones, combining 3D prediction, individual objectives, shared separation constraints, and trajectory-tracking interfaces. The study compares cooperative game solvers and quantifies how drone count, prediction horizon, and move blocking affect computation time and feasibility.

entry.title: Simulating Vein Compressibility for Ultrasound-Guided Femoral Access: Speed, Accuracy, and Phantom Validation

author.name: Amit Manicka, Laurent Coulon, Darwin Ang, Michael Loushin, Timothy M. Kowalewski

entry.summary: The paper tests a physics-based tissue simulation in NVIDIA Isaac Sim for Healthcare for ultrasound-guided femoral access, where probe pressure deforms tissue and changes vascular anatomy during robot interaction. Using Stable Neo-Hookean tissue solved by Vertex Block Descent on one GPU, a phantom simulation predicted artery within 5 percentage points and vein within 3 points through 11 mm of a 25.4 mm press at real-time speeds.

entry.title: Building Rapport with Self-Disclosure in Human-Robot Interaction

author.name: Haritha Anupindi, Chayan Sarkar, Tapas Nayak, Marynel Vazquez

entry.summary: This article investigates the role of robot self-disclosure in fostering rapport during face-to-face human-robot interaction, motivated by the fact that LLM-driven conversational robots are typically reactive information providers with limited social reciprocity. The study bridges human-human communication research on self-disclosure to HRI, examining how robots can build sustained relational depth.

entry.title: Deep-Learning-Assisted Bayesian Inference for Extreme-Mass-Ratio Inspirals

author.name: Jian-Jun Song, Zhong-Wu Xia, Wen-Hong Ruan, Zu-Cheng Chen, Hongwei Yu, Puxun Wu

entry.summary: Develops a deep-learning-assisted Bayesian inference pipeline for extreme-mass-ratio inspiral (EMRI) parameter estimation, combining neural-network-guided localization of the parameter space, particle swarm optimization, and MCMC sampling. On simulated six-month EMRI signals, the framework recovers posteriors matching reference MCMC runs initialized near the truth, without requiring knowledge of true parameters. This addresses the multimodal likelihood challenge that makes EMRI inference difficult for LISA-era observations.

entry.title: We have AI 2027. Where's Cyberpocalypse 2027?

author.name: Jenna_Parr

entry.summary: Argues that AI scenario forecasting, exemplified by AI 2027, has a blind spot: it considers direct cyberattacks on AI labs, such as model weight theft, but not second-order societal effects of AI-supercapable hacking, such as mass takedowns of water utilities, banking systems, knowledge stores, and communications. The author sketches cascading failure dynamics, including overloaded replacement services, workforce disruption, and preemptive organizational network isolation. It is a foresight piece on cyber-AI interaction risks.

entry.title: How Scientists Can Work on AI Safety

author.name: Mikewins

entry.summary: A practical guide aimed at scientists outside the AI safety field who want to transition in, describing the unusual dynamics of the safety job market: rapidly growing organizations, many openings and applicants, and immature hiring processes at young organizations. It offers advice on how researchers can position themselves and contribute despite lacking a field track record.

entry.title: The Mathocalypse as a Dataset

author.name: rba

entry.summary: The author surveys the 2026 wave of AI-assisted mathematics breakthroughs, including OpenAI's disproof of the unit distance conjecture and an Anthropic researcher's disproof of the Jacobian conjecture, and proposes treating these events as a dataset for assessing AI research capabilities. The post blends personal narrative with commentary on the mathematics community's reaction to AI systems resolving long-open problems.

entry.title: Conformal Fair Decoding for Large Language Model Recommenders

author.name: Ziwei Wu, Jingrui He

entry.summary: Fair-Rec is an item-level decoding framework that controls fairness in LLM-based recommendation without access to model weights or full-vocabulary logits, using an offline-calibrated semantic-disparity threshold. A hard variant filters candidates and a soft variant trades off likelihood and disparity, with a pathwise enforceability guarantee established under an explicit assumption.

entry.title: InfoOrgBench: Can Agents Turn Scattered Information into Coherent Hierarchies?

author.name: Justice Ou, Lanming Ma, Zijian Zhang, Yilun Zhao

entry.summary: InfoOrgBench is a benchmark of 150 tasks where agents organize scattered records (meeting recaps, issue threads, design proposals) into hierarchies, evaluated with integrity checks and a Structure Score measuring agreement with source hierarchies independent of naming. Evaluating 45 systems pairing nine models with five agent harnesses, the best scores 83.2 with no system exceeding 78 on meeting recaps or issue threads. It matters for measuring higher-level organizational errors agent benchmarks overlook.

entry.title: Wireless AI Networks: Co-Adapting Communication Resources and Distributed Intelligence

author.name: Ziqiang Ye, Yue Xiao, Qiyan Zhan, Yulan Gao, Xianfu Lei, Vladimir Poulkov

entry.summary: The article proposes Wireless AI Networks as a unified design perspective for bidirectional adaptation between wireless communication and distributed AI, introducing an AI-executable resource budget and task-level information value to guide configuration and transmission strategies. It argues resource availability alone does not determine AI task performance under constraint.

entry.title: SCALE: Small-Model-First Concept Abstraction with LLM-Guided Experience Internalization

author.name: Hong Su

entry.summary: SCALE proposes a small-model-first agent architecture in which a lightweight model handles routine predictions and LLM reflection is selectively triggered by prediction errors and accumulated cross-episode evidence, distilling experience into compact concepts the small model can apply autonomously. This reduces reliance on costly LLM calls for every decision.

entry.title: KeyASRBench: Measuring Whole-Phrase Keyword Preservation in Real-World ASR

author.name: Guanzheng Wei, Ziyi Zhao

entry.summary: KeyASRBench operationalizes occurrence-based Keyword Error Rate over frozen whole-phrase annotations, using a 10-hour bilingual challenge set of 1,501 Chinese and English clips with 4,723 keyword occurrences. Despite sequence error rates of 5-13 percent, KER reveals substantially worse preservation of names, products, and technical phrases, explaining why production ASR still needs hotword lists and post-correction.

entry.title: Physics-informed neural networks in the small-data regime: A controlled comparison with classical PDE surrogates

author.name: Kirill Katsuba, Oleg Rudenko, Egor Bugaev, Alexander Tarakanov

entry.summary: The paper introduces hierarchical loss weighting (H-PINN) and gradient-direction-aware weighting (HO-PINN) and compares them against vanilla PINNs, gradient boosting, SVR, and Gaussian processes on a heat equation and three two-phase-flow benchmarks using only 20-1000 labeled points. It probes whether physics constraints truly rescue PINNs in the scarce-data regime.

entry.title: SAMBoost: Spatially Aware Mesh Boosting

author.name: Mulah Moriah, Franck Vermet, Pierre Ailliot, Juliette Legrand

entry.summary: SAMBoost is a gradient boosting method that jointly models tree-based covariate effects and an SPDE latent spatial field through a single penalised objective, decomposing the predictor into covariate and spatial components at each iteration. It targets applications like insurance where the geographic risk surface itself must be recovered alongside flexible covariate effects.

entry.title: Variance-Reduced Stochastic Hessian-Driven Nesterov Acceleration with Adam-Style Preconditioning

author.name: Yaxin Yu, Long Chen, Minfu Feng

entry.summary: Proposes scalar and diagonal variants of VR-Adam-SHANG for smooth stochastic convex optimization, combining STORM-type variance reduction, Adam-style preconditioning, and accelerated interpolation/correction with at most two gradient evaluations per iteration. Proves O(1/K) mean-square gradient-error rates under standard assumptions.

entry.title: More Than Just Style: Benchmarking Personality Influence in Large Language Models

author.name: Yuhao Liu, Mengyu Wang, Xiao Chen, Lu Liu

entry.summary: The paper introduces SPACE, a benchmark framework for measuring how personality-like behavioral tendencies in LLMs influence outputs, separate from explicit instructions and measured capability. It combines a controlled evaluation protocol with datasets for personality verification, capability assessment, and hierarchical situational tasks, using guided comparisons to disentangle personality effects from instruction and capability effects. This clarifies a poorly understood factor in LLM behavior.

entry.title: Quadratic Bezier Splatting with Structural Initialization for Efficient Painting Rendering

author.name: Jinfan Liu, Xuhan Zhan, Mengqin Zhao, Guangyi Deng, Wuze Zhang, Bingbing Ni

entry.summary: The paper proposes a stroke-audited rendering framework using Quadratic Bezier Splatting for differentiable curved-stroke modeling, combined with a feedforward multi-scale stroke decoder for structural initialization and test-time stroke optimization. It addresses fragmentation and hidden defects in stroke-based rendering.

entry.title: Beyond Head Importance: Collective Computation in Video Transformers

author.name: Yi Yang, Siyuan Liu, Bingbing Nie

entry.summary: The paper studies how attention heads in video transformers participate in collective computation, examining downstream use of head outputs and cross-layer composition of interactions. Ablation analyses across four video transformers show that high-importance heads on one task also support other video understanding tasks and preserve representational structure distinguishing videos, with ablation responses correlating more strongly with importance at certain network depths.

entry.title: A forensic evaluation framework for egocentric foundation models: an EFM3D case study for crime scene reconstruction

author.name: Davidson Chisom Onwubiko, Shahana Bano, Carlos Francisco Moreno-Garc\'ia

entry.summary: This paper proposes a structured forensic evaluation framework for egocentric foundation models, demonstrated on EFM3D using four simulated indoor crime scenes recorded with Meta Project Aria Gen 1 at a forensic training facility. It evaluates room-scale reconstruction, semantic scene understanding, computational performance, and forensic suitability, with meshes averaging around 12,668 vertices.

entry.title: Polarization Aware Deep Learning Framework for SAR Despeckling

author.name: Gianpaolo Passarello, Sergio Vitale, Hossein Aghababei, Giampaolo Ferraioli, Vito Pascazio

entry.summary: The paper presents a unified deep-learning framework for despeckling single-, dual-, and full-polarization SAR data using a single trained CNN with a common nine-channel polarimetric covariance matrix representation and a polarization-aware masking strategy. This removes the need for specialized architectures or separate training procedures per polarimetric configuration.

entry.title: Safety-Constrained Intelligent Control of a 2-DOF Robotic Manipulator Using Control Barrier Functions

author.name: Gabriel da Silva Lima, Made Widhi Surya Atman, Wallace Moreira Bessa

entry.summary: The paper studies a control barrier function filter whose dynamic model is uncertain, adding an RBF neural network compensator shared by a Cartesian tracking controller and a joint-space CBF filter. An auxiliary state driven by the difference between requested and applied torques corrects the learning signal, reducing the influence of filter intervention on adaptation, validated on a two-link manipulator with ablations and disturbance trials.

entry.title: LSRP*: Scalable and Anytime Planning for Multi-Agent Path Finding with Asynchronous Actions

author.name: Dachuan Liu, Shuai Zhou, Shizhe Zhao, Zhongqiang Ren

entry.summary: LSRP* extends the Loosely Synchronized Rule-based Planner for multi-agent path finding with asynchronous actions, converting a sub-optimal planner into an anytime algorithm with improved solution quality. It relaxes the common synchronized-action assumption that limits practical MAPF deployment. The result is scalable planning for many agents with bounded improvement over time.

entry.title: Leveraging Complementary Event Frame and Voxel Representations for RGB-Guided Multimodal Pre-training

author.name: Wentao Wu, Xiao Wang, Yi Wang, Chenglong Li, Yonghong Tian, Bin Luo

entry.summary: Presents CM3AE 2.0, a unified pre-training framework over RGB frames, event voxels, and event frames, with an Event-aware Spatiotemporal Masked Reconstruction strategy that uses event responses to guide masking toward dynamically salient regions. It learns multimodal spatiotemporal representations through cross-modal generation.

entry.title: FMA-Net: Flexible Modality Adaptation for Robust Multimodal Face Presentation Attack Detection

author.name: Yuhao Gao, Yichen Shi, Zitong Yu, Hongyang Wang, Hongrui Li, Ruixin Zhang, Shouhong Ding, Jun Feng

entry.summary: FMA-Net is a unified framework for multimodal face presentation attack detection (RGB, depth, IR) that handles missing modalities via instruction-guided latent-space translation rather than zero-filling or modality omission. A Face Modality Instruct Translator estimates target modality observations from RGB inputs, and learnable text prompts provide modality-invariant semantic context.

entry.title: Sliding into Balance: Benefits of a Sliding Payload for Load Distribution and Disturbance Rejection in Dual-UAV Transportation

author.name: Jorge Vicente-Martinez (Universidad de Zaragoza), Francisco Jos\'e Ma\~nas-\'Alvarez (Universidad Nacional de Educaci\'on a Distancia), Edgar Ramirez-Laboreo (Universidad de Zaragoza)

entry.summary: The paper analyzes cooperative dual-UAV transportation where the payload slides along a single connecting rope instead of hanging from two independent ropes. Analytical results show the sliding payload equalizes rope tension for any drone position, doubles the reachable payload region, and improves disturbance rejection except at low friction.

entry.title: ScreenProof: Where Is This Screen Wrong? Finding UI Faults Without a Reference

author.name: Huiming Sun, Yue Li, Kangning Yang, Ruineng Li, Jie Cai, Lan Fu, Yunwan Fu, Jinlong Li, Jinglin Shen

entry.summary: ScreenProof poses target-free UI critique: can a model box faults on a screenshot (overflowing labels, style inconsistencies, text layout errors) with no reference design or target image, while staying silent on clean pages? A data engine synthesizes each fault in page code with annotations, and the task spans general, local style, and text layout fault families.

entry.title: MambaLoc: Lightweight Indoor Localization Using Cross-Modal Knowledge Distillation

author.name: Mohab Bahnassy, Omar Saqr, Hamada Rizk, Moustafa Youssef

entry.summary: MambaLoc uses cross-modal knowledge distillation to train a linear-time Mamba-based student model on Wi-Fi CSI data, transferring geometric precision from UWB teacher signals to achieve accurate indoor localization on resource-constrained edge devices. It sidesteps the quadratic cost of transformer approaches and the infrastructure burden of UWB. The work matters for practical edge deployment of localization.

entry.title: Multimodal Models Can See, But Can They Think? A Study of Turkish Visual Reasoning
