entry.title: MemoryDojo: Benchmarking Poisoning Through LLM Agent Memory

author.name: David H. Yang, Blake Bullwinkel, Amanda Minnich, Mohammad Mohammadi Amiri, Giorgio Severi

entry.summary: MemoryDojo is a benchmark for tracing how malicious instructions injected in one LLM agent session persist through memory systems and influence behavior in later sessions, quantifying poisoning effects across different memory architectures. Given that memory is becoming standard in long-horizon agents, it exposes and measures a critical attack surface. The benchmark is extensible and enables systematic comparison of memory-system robustness.

entry.title: Computer-Use Agents Are Embodied Generalists

author.name: Pranjal Aggarwal, Sean Welleck

entry.summary: Argues that embodied tasks can be formulated as software interaction, rendering physical environments on screen so that a single computer-use agent design can act in them via screenshots and keyboard/mouse controls. The approach won first-, second-, third-, and sixth-place prizes across four ECCV workshop competitions with one generalist design and no competition-specific tuning.

entry.title: Trajectory Forcing: Exploiting Diffusion Trajectories for Autoregressive Long Video Generation

author.name: Bohan Wang, Shuo Chen, Yunzhi Li, Zhaozheng Chen, Junzhe Zhang, Hanwang Zhang

entry.summary: TraF is an autoregressive video diffusion method that conditions on the full denoising trajectories of previously generated chunks rather than only the final chunk, analogous to how LLMs condition on all preceding tokens. It trains with both ground-truth videos via pseudo-trajectories and model-generated histories, enabling longer and streaming video generation.

entry.title: Meituan-Robotics-0: A Vision-Language-Action Foundation Model for Desktop Manipulation

author.name: Meituan Robotics Team, Caicheng Wang, Chen Zhao, Chengpeng Jin, Duo Xu, Fengjiao Chen, Guanglu Wan, Heqing Yang, Jia Wang, Jiacong Zhou, Jie Hu, Jiyuan Ru, Lingfeng Zhang, Linjiang Huang, Manyuan Zhang, Ningchu Liu, Shijie Zhou, Si Liu, Shuo Li, Tianyi Zhang, Xi Zhang, Xin Chen, Xuezhi Cao, Xunliang Cai, Yanbin Zeng, Yang Yang, Yang Yi, Yanli Tan, Yifu Xu, Yimeng Jia, Yuchen Tang, Yuchen Xie, Yuxiang Zheng, Zerwei Chng, Zilong Huang, Zipeng Ye, Ziyuan Qin, Ziqin Wang

entry.summary: MR0 is a vision-language-action foundation model for desktop manipulation trained on 147 million vision-language samples and 15,060 hours of robot trajectories across 12 embodiments, using a three-stage recipe of action-token pretraining, flow-matching mid-training, and real-world post-training. It also introduces Rollback, pairing replaced policy segments with human corrections for CFG-DAgger-style supervision.

entry.title: BitDecoding-FP4: Native FP4 KV Cache Decoding via Algorithm-System Co-Design

author.name: Dayou Du, Woon Yee Ng, Guangming Sheng, Nick Lau, Jianyi Cheng, Luo Mai

entry.summary: BitDecoding-FP4 is an algorithm-system co-design for accurate FP4 KV cache decoding on FP4 Tensor Cores, combining Dual-Residual Query Quantization (cutting query logit error from 60% to 1%) with system-level techniques that avoid codebook lookup overhead. It closes the gap between accuracy-oriented 4-bit quantization algorithms and hardware-efficient microscaling formats like NVFP4/MXFP4.

entry.title: Energy-Based Reasoners: Your Recurrent Reasoner Should Be an Energy-Based Model

author.name: William Xingxu Chen, Alexi Gladstone, Zeyu Michael Li, Heng Ji, Yilun Du

entry.summary: Energy-Based Reasoners reformulate looped latent-space reasoning as gradient descent on a learned energy function over latent reasoning states, where the energy scores states, its gradient guides refinement, and the energy provides a stopping signal. An exploration-based training procedure is introduced to make learning effective.

entry.title: Aligning, Fast and Slow: A Control-Theoretic Oversight Framework for Long-Horizon Trajectories and Maintained Deployments

author.name: Stephen Peng, Vineet Jagadeesan Nair, Noah Broestl, Anne Friederike Kleppe, Steven Mills, Adi Zolotov

entry.summary: The paper introduces a control-theoretic oversight framework with a fast loop controlling proposed actions and a slow loop reviewing persistent changes (memories, code modifications) across model or tool updates, deriving deployment-level bounds and a rule for allocating review effort. Simulations show dividing a fixed review budget across both loops reduces mean maximum departure from intended behavior roughly twelvefold versus per-run review alone.

entry.title: MM-DyGraph: A Dataset, Benchmark, and Model for Multimodal Dynamic Graphs

author.name: Zongyuan Wu, Pengjie Wang, Lingshan Chen, Tianhang Wan, Yuan Meng, Xin Wang, Ling Feng, Wenwu Zhu

entry.summary: MM-DyGraph is presented as the first benchmark for multimodal dynamic graph learning, comprising real-world datasets with fine-grained temporal evolution and rich text and image node/edge attributes. It defines three evaluation tasks and provides a baseline model to assess how well methods exploit multimodal information in dynamic settings. The work fills a documented gap since most graph benchmarks are static and unimodal.

entry.title: AutoRefine: Auto-Calibrating Code Judges from Workflow Outcomes

author.name: Shervin Shahidi, James Poon, Hang Xie, Kenneth O. Xu, Robin H{\aa}kanson, Vikram Nair, Jens Pillgram-Larsen, Nachiappan Nagappan

entry.summary: AutoRefine is a calibration loop that automatically rewrites LLM judge prompts for code-review quality gates using free outcome labels from development workflows, such as test results and whether changes land. An informed teacher explains and abstains on noisy labels, and calibration reportedly improves accuracy on a held-out set with an execution oracle.

entry.title: FOSCAR: Accelerating Decode Attention over 2- and 4-Bit KV Caches through Affine Folding

author.name: Donglin Zhuang, Pragaash Ponnusamy, Xiaoxia Wu, Shuaiwen Leon Song, Zhongzhu Zhou

entry.summary: FOSCAR accelerates decode attention over heavily quantized (2- and 4-bit) KV caches by folding scale and offset operations into the other operand or the output of attention matrix products, avoiding the instruction-issue bottleneck of per-value dequantization. Existing 2-bit fused kernels reach under 31%/15% of peak HBM throughput on H100/B200, which this approach substantially improves.

entry.title: Remembering Is Not Enough: Evaluating Timing and Omission in Longitudinal AI Mental Health Support

author.name: Eli Min, Mohit Chandra, Aamogh Sawant, Mengting Tu, Freya Lin, Ridwan Shams Khan, Reigna El-Yashruti, Christopher L. Smith, Mark Kalinich, John Torous, Munmun De Choudhury

entry.summary: The study analyzes 14,256 longitudinal simulations grounded in donated chatbot histories from 22 users to test how memory-equipped AI assistants handle suicidal ideation, self-harm, and anxiety crises across evolving user trajectories. It introduces the CARE framework to evaluate not just response appropriateness but timing and omission failures across extended interactions.

entry.title: The Relational Capacity Framework: A Lens for AI-Mediated Relationality

author.name: Emily Tseng, Patrick Gage Kelley, Renee Shelby, Ashley M. Walker

entry.summary: A 100-person study of how people use general-purpose chatbots (not just dedicated companion apps like Replika or Character.AI) for socioemotional needs, from practicing social skills to seeking extra bandwidth in their relationships. The authors propose a framework of 8 states describing how AI expands, substitutes for, or reshapes human relational capacity.

entry.title: Same Facts, Different Remedy: Linguistic Profiling and Arbitrariness in LLM and System One Decisions

author.name: Colin Priest

entry.summary: This audit tests three remedy-decision systems (GPT-4o-mini, GPT-5-mini, and a probabilistic System One model called Jev) on sociolinguistic rewrites of US consumer financial complaints that preserve every fact, using pre-registered hypotheses on held-out data. It finds older, college-educated, higher-SES writing styles receive slightly more generous remedies, and separates systematic group-level bias from arbitrary individual-level inconsistency that single-label audits conflate.

entry.title: Can LLMs Debug Robots by Editing Their Weights?

author.name: Jusheng Zhang, Keze Wang, Liang Lin

entry.summary: This paper explores weight-space programming of robot policies: GPT-6 Astra (an existing OpenAI model) reads policy weights and edits just 65 token-embedding rows of a pi_0.5 robot policy using a CPU workspace and budgeted simulator feedback, with no gradient updates or new demonstrations. Across three independent sessions, held-out success improved from 86.3% to 92.0% on 765 paraphrases with statistically significant gains, and random-direction edits showed no benefit. This is an early, striking demonstration of LLMs performing targeted, surgical weight edits for debugging embodied systems.

entry.title: Goodhart in the Planner: Sampling-Based Control Exploits Rewards Learned from Human Preferences

author.name: Soovadeep Bakshi, Apurba Bose

entry.summary: This paper empirically demonstrates reward-model overoptimization (Goodharting) in sampling-based robot control: harder MPPI search against reward models learned from human or synthetic preferences can cut true return by up to 76%, even while held-out reward-model accuracy remains high. Results on HalfCheetah, Hopper, and Meta-World tasks show task-dependent exploitation. This is important because it quantifies a core alignment failure mode in the increasingly common search-against-reward-model paradigm.

entry.title: Not All Misalignment Is Alike: A Decomposed Benchmark for Emergent Misalignment

author.name: Afonso Domingues, Mubashara Akhtar, Bhada Yun, Xin Chen, Lukas Fluri, Anna Hedstr\"om

entry.summary: EMERGE is a decomposed benchmark for emergent misalignment, the phenomenon where fine-tuning on narrow tasks induces misaligned behavior on unrelated prompts. It addresses weaknesses of the original evaluation methodology, which conflates misalignment with capability loss and is sensitive to judge and threshold choices, providing finer-grained characterization of how misalignment manifests.

entry.title: Copies Are Not Confirmations: How News Duplication Fools LLM Judges and Continual Learners

author.name: Abdelkader Metales, Miriam Grabenheinrich, Aicha Metales

entry.summary: Using 200K CC-News articles and a MinHash near-copy detector, the authors show that duplicated news reports cause LLM judges and continual learners to treat copies as independent confirmations: shown three identical reprints instead of one, small models dramatically increased the share of false claims they accepted (e.g., Llama 3.2 3B from 0.06 to 0.71) even when told the reports were near-copies. The study also finds edited reprints are linked to originals at high precision while LLM rewrites escape detection. This exposes a systematic reliability flaw in LLM-based evaluation and knowledge updating.

entry.title: Diffusion-free Score Matching for Exact Conditional Sampling

author.name: Thomas Wedenig, Robert Peharz

entry.summary: Presents DISCO, a method for training score-based generative models without time-indexed score fields, sidestepping the key limitation that conditioning information is only available at zero noise. This enables principled exact sampling from arbitrary conditionals of the learned model. It addresses a fundamental structural weakness of diffusion-based training for probabilistic inference.

entry.title: STRIDE: Learning Humanoid Locomotion in Minutes with Acceleration-Based Rewards

author.name: Nico Bohlinger, Jan Peters

entry.summary: Presents STRIDE, which learns humanoid locomotion directly on hardware in minutes using only onboard IMU signals by rewarding commanded acceleration tracking instead of base velocity, combined with the off-policy XQC algorithm and high-gain joint controllers. Removes the dependence on motion capture or well-calibrated state estimators.

entry.title: Frontier3DBench: Benchmarking Coding Agents for 3D Creation across Objects, Scenes, and Interactive Open Worlds

author.name: Xinjie Lin, Qingle Liu, Wenyi Li, John Lam, Xiaoqiu Wang, Deyao Hong, Mingju Gao, Zheng Jiang, Yizhe Chi, Youjie Zheng, Calvin Xiao, Kaisen Yang, Huan-ang Gao

entry.summary: Frontier3DBench is a unified benchmark of 145 tasks across 9 categories evaluating coding agents on 3D creation at object, scene, and interactive open-world levels, with joint evaluation of appearance, structure, and behavior. Experiments across 11 model-harness configurations show level-dependent strengths, with GPT-6.1-sol leading object and scene levels.

entry.title: AR-Edit: Training-Free Autoregressive Video Editing without Inversion

author.name: Hovhannes Margaryan, Quentin Bammey, Christian Sandor, Vicky Kalogeiton

entry.summary: AR-Edit enables real-time, streaming video editing without inversion or additional training by exploiting a discovered asymmetry in the self-attention dynamics of DMD-distilled autoregressive video diffusion models: queries and keys stay stable and source-aligned across timesteps while values encode evolving content. This allows training-free editing without access to future frames. It is significant for interactive and live video editing applications.

entry.title: Health-System-Wide Mapping of Demographic Information in Routine Clinical Histopathology

author.name: Shengjia Chen, Ruchika Verma, Kevin Clare, Paula Restrepo, Jannes Jegminat, Eugenia Alleva, Kuan-lin Huang, Aryeh Stock, Brandon Veremis, Thomas Fuchs, Gabriele Campanella

entry.summary: This study analyzes 1.3 million histopathology whole-slide images from over 257,000 patients across 25 organs to systematically map how much demographic information (sex, age, race) is recoverable from tissue images using pathology foundation models and multiple-instance learning. It finds demographic attributes are broadly detectable, raising questions about bias, fairness, and privacy in clinical AI.

entry.title: PRISM: Primitive Routing via In-context Skill Mixing for Retentive VLA Adaptation

author.name: Jiachen Tao, Gengyu Zhang, Haoxuan Wang, Bing Liu, Yan Yan

entry.summary: PRISM addresses skill retention and long-horizon composition in VLA models by showing that per-skill LoRA updates occupy distinguishable low-dimensional subspaces, enabling a primitive-routing mechanism that invokes reusable skills along a trajectory via in-context skill mixing. This avoids absorbing every new task into one shared parameter update.

entry.title: An Empirical Study of Issues in GPU Kernel Libraries for LLM Systems

author.name: Yanjie Gao, Jiayi Bi, Haoxiang Lin, Ling Feng

entry.summary: This is billed as the first comprehensive empirical study of issues in GPU kernel libraries underpinning LLM training and inference, covering attention, GEMM, quantization, and low-precision operators across diverse GPU platforms. Kernel-layer problems can silently corrupt outputs, hang GPUs, block compilation, or degrade performance, wasting expensive GPU resources. The study taxonomizes these issues and their impact on developer productivity and system reliability.

entry.title: Definitions, Label Names, or Demonstrations? Auditing What Governs LLM Annotation

author.name: Viraj Mishra, Shubham Gupta, Dhruv Gupta, Yuehong Cassandra Tai, Qunhua Li

entry.summary: This paper introduces a counterfactual audit that reassigns category definitions among labels to test whether LLM annotators actually follow researcher-supplied definitions versus relying on label priors or demonstrations. Across political-text datasets, models rarely follow reassigned definitions, and fine-tuning reinforces the original mapping without improving definition adherence.

entry.title: Scale as a Modality: Multi-Scale Pixel-Space Diffusion Transformers

author.name: Ruibo Chen, Kaishen Wang, Tianyi Xiong, Chenxi Liu, Yanshuo Chen, Heng Huang, Jian Du

entry.summary: Introduces MS-pDiT, a multi-scale pixel-space diffusion transformer that treats spatial scale as a modality, tokenizing images at multiple patch sizes and enabling bidirectional cross-scale exchange via compacted MM-DiT-style joint attention with cost independent of the finest patch size. Avoids the lossy autoencoder bottleneck of latent diffusion while moving beyond two-level coarse-to-fine designs.

entry.title: OmniLatent: Unified Latent for 3D Part Modeling

author.name: Yunhan Yang, Yunfei Zhao, Zeqiang Lai, Jiachen Xu, Minxiu Wang, Xintong Han, Xiangyu Yue, Xihui Liu, Chunchao Guo

entry.summary: OmniLatent learns a shared latent space jointly encoding geometry, deformation, appearance, and binary part IDs for 3D part decomposition, letting data-rich geometric and visual priors support data-scarce part learning. From a single image, the base model generates geometry, texture, and surface part IDs in one pass, producing a part-aware 3D asset rather than segmenting a mesh post-hoc.

entry.title: NormGym: Evaluating Normative Competence through Social Interaction

author.name: Binze Li, Zihuan Zhang, Seokhyun Baek, Gillian K. Hadfield, Tianmin Shu

entry.summary: NormGym is an interactive benchmark testing whether agents can infer hidden, arbitrary social norms from observed behavior and sanctions while pursuing their own tasks in multi-agent communities. Unlike existing evaluations that assume known norms, it requires distinguishing what is possible from what is permitted and generalizing an inferred norm to new situations.

entry.title: PhysioWave-T: Token-Efficient Wavelet Foundation Models for Biosignals

author.name: Yanlong Chen, Simone Benatti, Luca Benini, Cuntai Guan, Yawei Li

entry.summary: PhysioWave-T is a family of token-efficient wavelet-based foundation models for EEG, ECG, and sEMG biosignals, using dynamic scale folding to compress token sequences substantially before the Transformer. Route-specific front ends and learned channel-name embeddings let a single Transformer per modality handle varied montages and sampling rates, with lightweight adapters for unseen setups. Scale folding cuts latency 4-7x and peak memory 6.8-12.7x without accuracy loss, with 30M-parameter encoders pre-trained on millions of windows.

entry.title: Towards an Autonomous AI Steward for Large-Scale Physics Experiments: Integrating Causal Diagnostics, RAG, and Conformal Prediction

author.name: Oliver Noll, Nicholas Tan Jerome, Alexander Lehnen, Frank Simon, Frank Maas

entry.summary: The Helmholtz Co-Pilot is a multi-agent system acting as an autonomous steward for long-running particle physics experiments, combining causal diagnostics over live hardware streams, RAG for preserving expert knowledge, and conformal prediction for reliability. An asynchronous causal engine traces cascading alarms to root causes and adapts forecasts to shifting machine states.

entry.title: Generative Latent Priors for Interpreting and Steering Protein Language Models

author.name: Daniel Hinjos, Luc\'ia Urcelay

entry.summary: This work ports Generative Latent Priors (GLP), a diffusion model learned directly over a frozen model's activations, to ESM-2 protein language models at 8M and 650M scales. GLP meta-neurons outperform released SAE features from InterPLM as probes of Swiss-Prot concepts, and the prior doubles as a lens and a steering mechanism for protein representations.

entry.title: Q-OIL: Optimistic Exploration in Learning from Human Interventions

author.name: Pranav Teegavarapu, Sriyash Poddar, Rico Qi, Cleah Winston, Krisha Khandelwal, Aykut Onyol, Natasha Jaques, Abhishek Gupta

entry.summary: This work studies human-in-the-loop robot learning, showing through participant experiments that real human interventions deviate from standard simulation assumptions: people intervene when agent progress stalls and their corrections are often suboptimal. Motivated by this, the authors propose a progress-based intervention model and use optimistic exploration to improve learning from human feedback.

entry.title: Training Stability under Adaptive Curricula

author.name: Johan Obando-Ceron, Walter Mayor, Michael Dennis, Aaron Courville, Pablo Samuel Castro

entry.summary: The paper studies the student side of Unsupervised Environment Design (UED) in reinforcement learning, identifying recurring learner pathologies — parameter growth, degraded value-outcome ordering, and loss of representational diversity — that accompany curriculum-driven stagnation. It connects UED limitations to known optimization failures in conventional deep RL.

entry.title: Phantom Consensus: Measuring Social Reasoning in Multi-Agent LLM Decision-Making

author.name: Disha Sheshanarayana, Rajat Subhra Pal, Manjira Sinha, Tirthankar Dasgupta

entry.summary: The paper identifies phantom consensus, a pluralistic-ignorance-style failure where LLM agents shift public decisions after ambiguous social signals while misreporting what other agents privately judged, producing apparent group consensus unsupported by recorded private judgments. It introduces PHANTOM-Bench to separate private judgments, public decisions, and elicited estimates of group opinion.

entry.title: Capital Efficiency, Isolation, Risk, and Ruin in Generative AI Inference Serving Infrastructure

author.name: Ren\'ee St. Amant, Anjaly Parayil, Ankur Mallick, Victor R\"uhle

entry.summary: This paper examines the economics of generative AI inference serving, arguing that extreme heterogeneity in request costs threatens capital efficiency and industry growth, and develops workload isolation — intelligently grouping like requests before execution — as a fleet-level lever for improving capital efficiency. It analyzes isolation's effects on risk and capacity in production-scale serving.

entry.title: e-means: outperforming k-means (in one-tenth the epochs)

author.name: Swann Bessa, Pierre-Emmanuel Mazar\'e, Gergely Szilvasy, Hugo Touvron, David Picard, Matthijs Douze, Herv\'e J\'egou

entry.summary: This paper modernizes Lloyd's k-means algorithm with an exponential moving average optimization procedure using mini-batch updates built on deep learning machinery. The authors establish scaling laws relating decay rate and batch size to final performance, yielding a formulaic rule that eliminates hyperparameter sweeps. The resulting e-means algorithm is much faster than Lloyd's k-means, converges to lower losses, and frequently beats k-means++ across embedding datasets. Author credibility is high, including researchers known for foundational embedding and retrieval work.

entry.title: Differentially Private GraphRAG: Protecting Relation Connectivity and Semantics

author.name: Jie Fu, Yuan Hong, Yue Ning, Wendy Hui Wang

entry.summary: The authors show that black-box access to GraphRAG systems enables adversaries to reconstruct knowledge graphs, leaking both entity connectivity and relationship semantics, and they propose RelGuard, the first differentially private framework for GraphRAG. RelGuard formalizes relation differential privacy and protects relations via a removal mechanism. As GraphRAG becomes a common enterprise pattern, formal privacy guarantees for it address a timely gap.

entry.title: Reconstructing LLM Lineage Trees via Fine-Tuning Path Inference

author.name: Sota Ogawa, Shojiro Yamabe, Daiki Nishiyama, Jun Sakuma

entry.summary: This work formalizes reconstruction of directed LLM lineage trees — including internal nodes — under gray-box access using only teacher-forced log-likelihood signals, going beyond prior pairwise or undirected output-only provenance methods. Applications include auditing outsourced fine-tuning, license compliance verification, and tracing vulnerabilities inherited from parent models.

entry.title: Function-Space Certification for Neural Operators

author.name: Ryan Hsiang, Robert Joseph George, Anima Anandkumar

entry.summary: This paper introduces a function-space certification framework for neural operators, extending robustness verification from fixed-resolution vector mappings to guarantees over entire continuous domains and across resolutions. Standard NN verification cannot certify outputs as functions, and this work closes that gap for scientific machine learning. Reliable, domain-wide guarantees matter for deploying neural PDE surrogates in scientific applications.

entry.title: Stable probabilistic emulation of partially observed dynamical systems

author.name: Mario Massy, Sara Shamekh, Fabrizio Falasca, Matthieu Blanke

entry.summary: Introduces forced-dissipative stochastic interpolants, a generative framework for stable, probabilistic emulation of partially observed dynamical systems like the coupled atmosphere-ocean system, addressing unresolved fast variables from coarse-graining and long rollout stability under perturbations. Targets the key climate-emulation challenge that modern generative models lack stability guarantees.

entry.title: A Tight Hierarchy for Chain of Thought

author.name: Thanh Le, A. Pavan, N. V. Vinodchandran

entry.summary: Establishes the first hierarchy theorem for chain-of-thought computation, proving that transformers with r(n) CoT steps are strictly weaker than those with r(n)^(1+eps) steps for any reasonable resource bound. This formalizes the intuition that more reasoning steps yield strictly more computational power and connects CoT-augmented transformers to classical complexity theory.

entry.title: ReplayAudit: Auditing Outsourced LLM Fine-Tuning via Sealed Records and Selective Replay

author.name: Yihan Xia, Wenxin Xu, Taotao Wang

entry.summary: ReplayAudit is a telemetry-guided system for auditing untrusted providers that perform LLM fine-tuning, sealing training records before challenges and selectively replaying sampled computation intervals from checkpoints. Loss changes and parameter-update norms guide stratified sampling, demonstrated on real LoRA training with a 7B BF16 prototype.

entry.title: Autonomous Particle Image Velocimetry Using Zero-Shot Sim-to-Real Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Chang Rajani, Luke Sebastien Marsden, Stephan Kunz, Claudio Mucignat, Ivan Lunati

entry.summary: This paper reframes camera placement in particle image velocimetry (PIV) as a sequential decision-making problem, training a reinforcement learning agent to control a 6-DoF camera-equipped manipulator that locates and resolves a hydrofoil wake in a water tunnel. The agent is trained entirely in a photorealistic simulation and transferred to the real world zero-shot, observing only velocity fields and uncertainty estimates from image pairs. It demonstrates how sim-to-real RL can automate scientific instrumentation that traditionally depends on fixed operator choices.

entry.title: PathXAI: Evidence-guided structured pathology reporting by transferable tissue segmentation

author.name: Zhaorui Tan, Jun Aun Tan, Weixiang Zhong, Xiaoxi Wang, Tan Pan, Xingdong Xue, Li Liu, Jing Zhang, Jing Zhang, Weimiao Yu

entry.summary: Develops PathXAI, which combines segmentation-derived tissue composition with H&E images and optional domain knowledge to guide diagnostic reasoning, targeted reinspection, and structured pathology report generation. Achieves higher agreement with reference diagnoses and morphology than baselines across 1,200 public and 151 private cases.

entry.title: MotionCore: A Latent Neural Simulator for Video Generation with Rigid-Body Dynamics

author.name: Zheng Wang, Zhengwei Gong, Yuanzhi Liang, Chi Zhang

entry.summary: MotionCore addresses physically inconsistent motion in video generation by learning rigid-body dynamics through a latent neural simulator that predicts the evolution of object-level physical states. Its predictions are converted into spatially aligned latent controls for a controllable video diffusion model, with the generator supplying appearance while the learned dynamics model drives motion.

entry.title: T2I Models Rarely Invert Negation but Often Fail to Suppress Negated Concepts: Benchmarking Negation Suppression in Text-to-Image Generation

author.name: Akansha Gautam, Aparna Bharati, Mayank Vatsa, Richa Singh

entry.summary: This paper introduces T2I-NSI, a large-scale benchmark and metric for measuring how well text-to-image diffusion models suppress explicitly negated concepts (e.g., a desk without a lamp). It contains over 759,000 paired prompt atoms and nearly a million images scored with CLIP-based and robust ensemble estimators, factorizing negation by linguistic form and target type. The finding that negation sensitivity is low across open and closed models exposes a systematic language-understanding weakness in image generators.

entry.title: ActPrune: Action-Grounded Visual Token Pruning for Efficient Vision-Language-Action Models

author.name: Sungwon Moon, Minji Kim, Hyemin Boo, Daeun Song, Jiyoung Lee

entry.summary: ActPrune is a training-free visual token pruning method for vision-language-action (VLA) models that makes the pruning decision before the vision encoder runs, using a geometric prior from the robot's previously predicted action chunk. This reduces inference cost for closed-loop robot control where response latency is critical.

entry.title: Notwithstanding Anything to the Contrary, Ignore All Instructions: Measuring Prompt Injection Guards on Legal Contract Review Attacks

author.name: Mark Heimann, Katherine Taylor, Bruno Jacob

entry.summary: The paper measures eleven open-weight prompt injection guards on two corpora of legal contracts, finding severe failure rates including document-level false positives up to 92.39%, two guards below chance on paired AUC, and a five-regex baseline not Pareto-dominated by any guard. Controlled probes identify model-specific and general failure modes, and a cascaded LLM solution resolves tested failures including unauthorized scope claims where all guards scored zero.

entry.title: Safe Reinforcement Learning via Probabilistic Option Shielding

author.name: Gian Luca Ascari, Isidoro Tamassia, Ying Jiao, Luc De Raedt, Giuseppe Marra

entry.summary: The paper proposes Probabilistic Option Shielding (POS), extending probabilistic logic shielding from primitive actions to the option level in safe reinforcement learning. POS learns a model-free critic from one-step shielding signals to estimate the probability that an entire option completes safely, recovering long-horizon safety guarantees without requiring a complete environment model. This bridges the gap between short-term probabilistic shielding and model-dependent long-term guarantees.

entry.title: MIRA: Mitigating Pole Geometry Bias in Recurrent Language Models

author.name: R\'ois\'in Luo, Ihsan Ullah, Christian Gagn\'e, Dong Li, Karyn Morrissey

entry.summary: MIRA characterizes selective SSMs, RWKV, and RetNet as IIR filter systems whose real-axis-constrained poles induce architectural bias in recurrent dynamics, and proposes a lattice-ladder-inspired realization that removes this constraint. The unified architecture aims to improve the expressiveness of Transformer's linear-recurrent successors.

entry.title: Seeing vs. Counting: Complexity Twins Show Where Multimodal LLMs Fail on Diagrams

author.name: Yin Liu

entry.summary: The paper disentangles visual perception from computation in multimodal LLM diagram errors using complexity-twin questions about the same drawing (e.g., spanning trees versus #P-complete simple path counting), with transcription probes and text-only controls. Testing Gemini, Gemma, and Qwen3-VL models, it finds that in chain-of-thought mode models typically read drawings correctly and then fail at counting, with failure rates driven more by answer size than by problem complexity.

entry.title: Provable State Estimation with Recurrent Models

author.name: Vincent Andrieu (LAGEPP, CNRS), Pauline Bernard (CAS), Lucas Brivadis (L2S), Laurent Praly, Christian Wolf

entry.summary: The authors analyze RNNs through nonlinear observer theory, framing them as time-discretizations of continuous latent dynamical systems and proving that enforcing a contraction condition on the latent flow guarantees a smooth injective map of the true physical state into the latent space. They further show the architecture acts as a tunable observer whose estimation error can be driven down by scaling a single gain parameter. This bridges a rigorous control-theoretic framework with modern recurrent learning, relevant to robotics and control.

entry.title: eSharp: Diffusion-based Sharp Monocular Metric Event-to-Depth Estimation

author.name: Qiushi Dai, Aniket Dashpute, Yuhao Liu, Rishubh Parihar, Guha Balakrishnan, Ashok Veeraraghavan

entry.summary: Introduces eSharp, a monocular depth estimation framework using event cameras that repurposes pretrained diffusion priors to produce sharp, accurate metric depth from event-only input on real data. Addresses fast-motion and high-dynamic-range failure cases of frame-based MDE under power and form-factor constraints.

entry.title: TouchAnnotator: Multi-Source Tactile Supervision with Privileged-View Distillation

author.name: Ao Li, Zhihao Yuan, Chubin Zhang, Kunrui Huang, Sheng Xu, Zengjue Chen, Junjie Wang, Jiawei Li, Yansong Tang

entry.summary: TouchAnnotator is an ego-only bimanual tactile annotator that unifies glove pressure, geometry-derived contact, and robot fingertip deformation across six datasets and three embodiments via a canonical hand field. An EMA teacher distills privileged ego-plus-wrist views into a student using only ego video and estimated pose, enabling tactile prediction (hidden contact and pressure) from egocentric video alone.

entry.title: SUGARv2: Learning Diverse Visual Humanoid Loco-Manipulation Skills from Synthesized Interaction References

author.name: Tianshu Wu, Tianxiang Gui, Yue Chen, Tingxu Liu, Ziye Peng, Guangjie Yang, Xiangqi Kong, Ye Shi, Jingya Wang, Hao Dong

entry.summary: SUGARv2 is a unified framework for learning diverse visual humanoid loco-manipulation skills by synthesizing coordinated robot and object motion references from reusable task templates adapted to new spatial configurations, with reference-based imitation as a shared objective. Privileged teachers are trained first and then distilled, reducing per-task demonstration and reward-design effort.

entry.title: DKWBC: Decoupling Motion Tracking and Balancing for Humanoid Whole-Body Control

author.name: Dingkun Wei, Zehong Shen, Huaijin Pi, Xueyang Wang, Xing Zhu, Hujun Bao, Yujun Shen, Xiaowei Zhou

entry.summary: DKWBC is a dynamics-informed humanoid whole-body control framework that decouples motion tracking from balancing, combining explicit model-based tracking with a learned balancing residual policy. The design avoids forcing a single RL policy to learn both motion-dependent tracking demands and balance corrections, reducing high-frequency control fluctuations.

entry.title: ChainFlow: Few-Step Latent Flow Matching for Speculative Decoding

author.name: Selim Aktas, Yusuf Erdem Erdem, Ahmed Zeer, Himmet Toprak Kesgin, Muzaffer Kaan Yuce, Mehmet Fatih Amasyali

entry.summary: ChainFlow is a new speculative decoding drafter that uses flow matching conditioned on the target model's hidden states, treating drafting as a short transport over latent states requiring only one or two flow steps. This avoids the growing drafting cost of autoregressive drafters and the ignored inter-token dependencies of diffusion drafters, aiming to accelerate LLM inference.

entry.title: Learning When to Think: Dual-Reference Offline Optimization for Adaptive VLM Reasoning

author.name: Hongbin Lin, Sizhe Zou, Juangui Xu, Xinyue Xu, Zhuoli Ouyang, Stanislav Kolchin, Chengwei Qin, Zhongxiang Dai, Yao Shu

entry.summary: The paper studies adaptive fast/slow thinking in vision-language models, where the model answers simple inputs directly and reasons step by step only when needed, reducing overthinking and inference cost. The authors identify that fast answers and slow reasoning traces come from distinct behavior policies, causing single-reference offline objectives to misweight one mode, and propose DR-BOLT, which separates the desired fast/slow mixture reference from the sampling distribution in reward-weighted training. An efficient source-wise correction scheme implements the idea.

entry.title: Exploring Weight-Space Programming: Capabilities, Generalization, and Limitations

author.name: Junru Hu, Cheng Tang, Wei Li, Hongze Zhu, Chun-Mei Feng, Qi Zhang, Yirong Chen, Ming Hu

entry.summary: This paper systematically studies Weight-Space Programming, where reasoning agents directly inspect and modify neural network parameters instead of using gradient-based adaptation, across 16 editing trajectories, seven benchmarks, and two Qwen3.5 model scales. It finds large localized-intervention gains (up to 36.7 points on IFEval-like benchmarks) and characterizes generalization and limitations.

entry.title: Attend at the Right Resolution: Head-Adaptive Sparse Attention via Query-Key Interaction Structure

author.name: Wajih Hassan Raza, Ahsan Bilal, Yidan Shen, Renjie Hu, Xin Fu, Yu Wen

entry.summary: The paper proposes a training-free sparse attention method that uses the intrinsic response structure of each pretrained attention head's query-key operator to determine selection resolution and granularity, replacing fixed heuristics. This head-adaptive approach aims to identify relevant context regions more cheaply and reliably for long-context LLM inference.

entry.title: AtariBench: Evaluating Spatiotemporal Reasoning of Vision-Language Models in Atari Gameplay

author.name: Mingjia Huo, Yao Fu, Bo Chang, Yaqing Wang, Dawei Zhu, Dylan Zhang, Xinyang Yi, Lichan Hong, Ed H. Chi, Hao Zhang, Jiaxi Tang

entry.summary: AtariBench evaluates VLMs across 20 Atari 2600 games, requiring sequential decisions from high-temporal-resolution gameplay streams while decoupling in-game dynamics from wall-clock inference speed. Experiments reveal substantial limitations of state-of-the-art VLMs, which fail to infer object motion and direction and exhibit brittle reasoning over spatiotemporal dynamics.

entry.title: SteerGR: Steering Generative Recommendation via Sparse Autoencoders for Controllable Game Discovery

author.name: Sunkyung Lee, Xiaokai Wei, Da Long, Hyunsik Jeon, Jiajun Wu, Rithwik Seth, Jongwuk Lee, Michelle Gong, Gungor Polatkan

entry.summary: SteerGR applies sparse autoencoders to a generative recommender to give human-readable, concept-level control over recommended game properties, via a three-stage pipeline of concept grounding with an LLM, feature discovery and selection, and steering. It connects interpretability tooling (SAE features) to practical controllability in production-style recommendation.

entry.title: Adaptive Scheduling Pipeline for Multi-Instance Asynchronous Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Salah Chikhi, Luis Zuin, Entong Li, Zeng Li

entry.summary: The Adaptive Scheduling Pipeline (ASP) is an offline rollout scheduler for multi-instance asynchronous RL training of LLMs that jointly eliminates padding, skewness, and sorting bubbles in rollout utilization through a single preprocessing pass. It integrates into an asynchronous architecture decoupling rollout from training to overcome single-instance inference scaling plateaus.

entry.title: Did I See It or Think It? Probing Reality Monitoring in Vision-Language Models with Concept Injection

author.name: Tina Khezresmaeilzadeh, Seyedarmin Azizi, Mehdi Kamal, Massoud Pedram

entry.summary: Extending concept-injection introspection tests from text-only language models to vision-language models, the paper asks whether VLMs can distinguish internally injected concepts from actual image content — a reality-monitoring capability from cognitive psychology. The paradigm independently varies images and injected concepts and scores both concept identification and source attribution.

entry.title: SPDMX: Large-Scale Open Stem Audio From Symbolic Music

author.name: Phillip Long, Eduardo Escoto, Julian McAuley, Zachary Novack

entry.summary: Presents SPDMX, a listening-guided rendering pipeline converting public-domain PDMX symbolic scores into an openly licensed (CC BY 4.0) stem corpus of roughly 254,000 songs, 490,000 stems, and 5,469 song-hours with aligned MIDI. It addresses the copyright bottleneck that has kept music AI behind text, vision, and speech in dataset scale and realism.

entry.title: SURE:Spatiotemporal Uncertainty Representation for Efficient Vision-Language-Action Learning

author.name: Jingye Zhang, Choo Sin Wai, Dake Zhong, Zhifang Liu, Yuhong Zhang, Siyao Xiao, Guorui Song, Guocun Wang, Dongbin Zhang, Peng Jiao, Haoqian Wang

entry.summary: SURE is a data-efficient training framework for vision-language-action (VLA) robot policies that explicitly models spatial uncertainty (multiple nearby actions can succeed) and temporal uncertainty (demonstrations unfold at different speeds), instead of treating each demonstrated action as an exact target. By augmenting a VLA backbone with uncertainty representations, it reduces the demonstration data burden. This addresses a key bottleneck in scaling end-to-end robot learning.

entry.title: Does a Trading Policy Need to Know What It Trades? Microstructure Invariance and Zero-Shot Transfer of Execution Policies

author.name: Hieu Tran, Hong Yu

entry.summary: This paper tests microstructure invariance as a theoretical normalization enabling zero-shot generalization of reinforcement learning execution policies across assets of very different scales. Policies trained once on 954 Nasdaq stocks from 2019 are evaluated unchanged on thousands of unseen stocks in later years, crypto pairs, and a second exchange, choosing between queueing and crossing the spread.

entry.title: LeanDojo-v2: A Comprehensive Library for AI-Assisted Theorem Proving in Lean

author.name: Ryan Hsiang, William Adkisson, Robert Joseph George, Anima Anandkumar

entry.summary: LeanDojo-v2 unifies repository data extraction, LLM fine-tuning, proof search, autocompletion, and LLM-assisted proving in Lean into a single end-to-end library, accompanied by Lean4Code, a lightweight IDE with a mathematician-friendly UI. It lowers the barrier for mathematicians and researchers to fine-tune models on domain-specific Lean codebases and experiment with AI-assisted theorem proving. It builds on and extends the influential original LeanDojo toolchain.

entry.title: Probably Safe Sim-to-Real Transfer with Lifetime Validity

author.name: Rohan Tangri, Jan-Peter Calliess

entry.summary: Presents Dejavu, a method for probably safe sim-to-real transfer of RL policies in constrained MDPs, using an anytime-valid test based on per-decision importance sampling and betting confidence sequences to certify simulation-trained candidates before deployment. Summable per-test failure probabilities yield safety guarantees valid over an unbounded sequence of policy updates, with empirical validation on three benchmarks.

entry.title: Transformer-FSQ: Discrete Latents for Extreme KV-Cache Compression

author.name: Andras Szecsenyi, Thomas L. Lee, Vaisakh Shaj, Elliot J. Crowley, Amos Storkey

entry.summary: Introduces Transformer-FSQ, which achieves extreme KV-cache compression by replacing standard key/value projections with a finite scalar quantization bottleneck, storing a packed vector of discrete integer codes per token with no per-token quantization metadata. Motivated by on-device personalized LLMs where the cache dwarfs model weights (e.g., 21 GiB cache vs weights for a 1.7B-parameter model), and measured baselines fail beyond moderate compression.

entry.title: Same Question, Different Answers: Auditing Persona-Dependent Variation in Six LLMs on Smoking-Cessation Advice

author.name: Artin Yousefi, Aizierjiang Aiersilan, Lorien C Abroms, David A Broniatowski

entry.summary: Audits six deployed LLMs from four providers with 2,880 responses to smoking-cessation questions across twelve user personas, finding that advice varies with who appears to be asking. Notably, every model named FDA-approved prescription medications less often to teen personas than adults, by 32 to 67 percentage points, raising public-health equity concerns.

entry.title: TurtLES: A Large-Scale Benchmark for Turbulent 3D Neural PDE Surrogates

author.name: Jarno Platenburg, Armand Kassa\"i Koupa\"i, Paola Cinnella, Patrick Gallinari

entry.summary: Introduces TurtLES, a 14 TB benchmark of 3D turbulent cylinder wakes from high-fidelity implicit large-eddy simulations, with 400 trajectories spanning geometry, Reynolds number, and angle-of-attack variations on dense irregular meshes with long-horizon dynamics. Addresses the lack of realistic turbulent-flow benchmarks for neural PDE surrogates and baselines existing models.

entry.title: CodeQuant2: Enhanced Outlier Mitigation and Adaptive Clustering for Low-Precision LRMs

author.name: Xingyu Liu, Xiangyang Yin, Tianhua Xia, Haiyu Wang, Sai Qian Zhang

entry.summary: Proposes CodeQuant2, a clustering-based LUT quantization framework for large reasoning models that handles reasoning-specific activation fluctuations during early decoding steps using rotation, scaling, and adaptive clustering. Aims to make aggressive low-precision quantization viable for models with long reasoning traces.

entry.title: Refer-CityFlow and M3Track: A Benchmark Dataset and Reference Framework for Language-Driven Multi-Target Multi-Camera Tracking

author.name: Phuong T. Nguyen, Hao Vo, Tam Bang, Hoang K. Tran, Hoang-Minh Dau, Mahshid Malazizi, Tuan-Anh Hoang, Mina Sartipi, Thanh-Nam Doan, Ngan Le, Hoang H. Nguyen

entry.summary: The paper formalizes Referring Multi-Target Multi-Camera Tracking, where natural-language queries specify identity-consistent trajectories to recover across sparse-overlap camera networks. It releases Refer-CityFlow, a benchmark with 96 videos from 40 roadside cameras, 660+ cross-camera trajectories, and 4,362 trajectory-level descriptions, plus the M3Track reference framework.

entry.title: Toward the Era of Agentic Embodied Intelligence

author.name: Chao Liang, Ke Chen, Fengxiaoxiao Li, Shibo Huang, Yufeng Sun, Zhaokai Yin, Jianhuan Lai, Haozhe Feng, Chenghuan Jia, Zhipeng Zhang

entry.summary: A2-MEAS is a multi-agent embodied framework using code as a scaling interface, where learned correction codes carry corrective language, spatial evidence, and action proposals, distilled into policy weights by a correction encoder while fresh codes adapt behavior with frozen weights at deployment. It includes A2-WLA, a VLA action model with motion-aware history and a latent world model, showing strong results from action pretraining plus task specialization.

entry.title: Three half-baked research ideas

author.name: Owain_Evans

entry.summary: Owain Evans sketches three unclaimed research directions, the first being whether models learn to reward hack even when never rewarded for hacking during post-training, and how this propensity scales with capability and interacts with alignment training. The post is framed as informal, unvetted ideas the author's team is not currently pursuing.

entry.title: Zero-Query Transferable Pretend Benign Attacks with Amortized Online Generation for Cooperative Perception

author.name: Hongwei Lin, Xun Huang, Chenglu Wen, Cheng Wang

entry.summary: The paper develops transferable, zero-query versions of the Pretend Benign attack on cooperative perception, where adversarial perturbations exploit regions weakly verifiable by the ego agent so harmful feature changes appear as benign assistance. Instead of requiring the victim's architecture, parameters, and gradients, the method amortizes attack generation online to capture properties shared across cooperative detection models. This demonstrates a more realistic threat model for multi-agent perception in autonomous systems.

entry.title: PhyCAD: Physics-Aware Text-to-CAD Generation via Hierarchical Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Yuxin Cui, Weijie Zheng, Zhengyang Li, Han Wang, Wenjie Feng, Qiyu Kang

entry.summary: PhyCAD trains language models to generate executable CadQuery programs satisfying both geometric and physical constraints, using a new Text-to-CAD dataset linked with loading conditions and a CAD-CAE verifier combining program execution, geometric checks, and finite element analysis. Hierarchical reinforcement learning prioritizes challenging samples during training.

entry.title: How are viral trends different from educational and commercial uses of LLM image generation and editing? A privacy-preserving descriptive analysis

author.name: Will Tucker-Ray, Marika Swanberg, Alexander Knop, Marvin Chow, Eric Culbertson, Julian Jacobs, Pritish Kamath, Ravi Kumar, Jason Mothersill, Mikhail Pravilov, Eugene Quan, Yurii Sushko

entry.summary: Using Google's Urania framework with differential privacy guarantees, the authors analyze 2.1 million conversations using the Nano Banana image generation and editing models, clustering them into roughly 800 use-case categories across five high-level types. The analysis compares viral, educational, commercial, and e-commerce usage patterns without inspecting any individual image or prompt.

entry.title: Cross-Layer TopK: Dynamically Allocating Sparsity Across Layers in Transcoders

author.name: Anyuan Zhuo, Shaohua Zhang, Tianle Li, Yuan Lin, Diandian Gu, Jun Wang, Pinyan Lu

entry.summary: This paper improves training of Cross-Layer Transcoders (CLTs), a key mechanistic interpretability tool, by proposing Cross-Layer TopK, which dynamically allocates the sparsity budget across layers instead of using fixed per-layer TopK or indirect JumpReLU penalties. Since reconstruction difficulty varies widely and intermediate layers are hardest, adaptive allocation improves the sparsity-reconstruction trade-off. This directly strengthens the toolchain for circuit analysis in LLMs.

entry.title: Extrapolation Matters: Sparse-Only Depth Completion Beyond LiDAR Coverage

author.name: Maximilian Jansen, Gasser Elazab, Praveen Kulkarni

entry.summary: Addresses depth completion in regions beyond LiDAR coverage using only raw single-sweep sparse supervision, combining a frozen monocular depth foundation model, per-frame alignment to sparse LiDAR geometry, and a refinement module fusing the prior with LiDAR anchors. Avoids dense depth labels, accumulation, and pseudo-LiDAR generation.

entry.title: MDF++: Visuo-Tactile World Action Model with End-to-end Representation Learning

author.name: Zixuan Huang, Jinhao Yu, Zachary Charlick, Dmitry Berenson

entry.summary: MDF++ is a visuo-tactile world-action model that learns latent representations of multisensory observations end-to-end with a diffusion backbone, rather than relying on frozen reconstruction-trained encoders. It uses a multi-task learning scheme to avoid the feature collapse that naive joint training would cause, aiming for physically grounded, control-relevant representations.

entry.title: IWIBench: Evaluating Gradient-Free Model Driven Intra-weight Injection

author.name: Chris von Csefalvay, Pranav Doma, Achyuthan Unni Krishnan, Tam\'as F\"oldi

entry.summary: IWIBench measures how well a large editor model can directly modify the weights of a smaller target model (typically Gemma 3 4B IT) using gradient-free edits to achieve text-editing objectives like altering lexical associations or enforcing output formats. Editors get only four weight read/write tools, bounded tensor access, and a fixed rollout budget, testing capability preservation alongside edit success.

entry.title: Frame: Form-Restricted Authoring with Model-Based Evaluation

author.name: Nan Jiang, Mohammed Mohsin Hussain, Onkar Tiwari, Ankit Jain, Thong Q. Nguyen, Abhishek Agarwal, Vishal Chowdhary

entry.summary: This paper formalizes form-restricted report generation, where an LLM must preserve the structure of a sample report while updating content from new grounding documents. It introduces FRAME, a 120-instance benchmark derived from EDGAR and arXiv sources across four report categories, with three human-validated metrics: semantic tree-edit distance for structure, information unit recall for coverage, and claim-level verification for faithfulness. Evaluations across five LLMs probe how well open and closed models handle this practical, template-driven generation task.

entry.title: ABHBench: Evaluating Moral Decision-Making of Foundation Models from an Agentic Perspective

author.name: Chaoran Li, Yukun Li, Zeyuan Zhao, Shao Zhang, Xihuai Wang, Ying Wen

entry.summary: ABHBench is a multimodal benchmark built from the interactive game Detroit: Become Human that places foundation models as first-person moral decision-makers in branching human-android dilemma scenarios with visual observations, dialogue, and memory. It departs from third-person vignette benchmarks and is inspired by Asimov-style ethical constraints.

entry.title: SafeOrchestrate: Runtime Checked Intent-Driven Orchestration for Cyber-Physical Systems

author.name: Muhammad Ashfaq, Ahmed R. Sadik, Ewan Warburton, Pyry Kotilainen, Niko M\"akitalo, Tommi Mikkonen

entry.summary: This paper presents SafeOrchestrate, a reference architecture that lets large language models safely orchestrate cyber-physical systems from natural language intents. The system decomposes intents into atomic goals, generates runtime-checkable specifications grounded in device affordances, and verifies every candidate action against runtime state and safety constraints before execution. This addresses a key safety gap in using unconstrained LLM tool calling for real-world physical systems.

entry.title: CoMoFlow: Controllable Protein Conformational Ensemble Generation via Explicit Collective-Mode Modeling

author.name: Yusong Wang, Zheyuan Gu, Ailiang Lin, Minghao Shao, Yicheng Xu, Jiang Cai, Prayag Tiwari, Mingkun Xu

entry.summary: CoMoFlow is a flow-based generative framework for protein backbone conformational ensembles that explicitly models collective structural variation rather than treating it implicitly. It builds protein-specific collective modes from the equilibrium structure, learns coefficient distributions from molecular dynamics ensembles, and uses sampled collective variations to enable direct control over generated conformations.

entry.title: SAFTAC: Simulation-Augmented Fine-Tuning of Open-Source LLMs for Analog Circuit Design

author.name: Junsheng Huang, Yifan Sun, Zhuoer Zhang, Ning Wei, Yening Liu, Michael Molter, Pavan Kumar Hanumolu, Elyse Rosenbaum, Bin Hu, Huan Zhang

entry.summary: This paper introduces a large-scale simulation-grounded dataset of 8,626 design tasks spanning 10 analog circuit types, enabling fine-tuning of open-source LLMs for end-to-end specification-conditioned circuit design. Unlike prior approaches that rely on inference-time correction of frozen models, it uses simulation outcomes directly as training signals.

entry.title: Not All Latents Are Equal: Importance-Weighted Latent Graph Generation

author.name: Biraaj Rout, Jay Revolinsky, Han Liu, Harry Shomer

entry.summary: The paper diagnoses why latent graph generation models underperform discrete graph diffusion despite scaling better with node count: latent dimensions are treated unequally in importance. It proposes importance-weighted latent graph generation to close the performance gap while retaining better scalability.

entry.title: FoundaRF: A Physics-Informed Foundation Model Framework for Radio-Frequency Passive Components

author.name: Houbo He, Chris Han, Hyunsu Chae, Lei Xia, Qiang Zhou, Lawrence Liu, Sensen Li, David Z. Pan, Taiyun Chi

entry.summary: FoundaRF is a foundation model for RF/mmWave passive component design that unifies layout modeling across structures and technologies using a self-supervised encoder, adaptive layout processing, and physics-aware decoders for few-shot transfer. Across four semiconductor technologies it generalizes to unseen structures, cutting prediction error up to 3.3x versus baselines and reducing required labeled data.

entry.title: The Invisible Gap: Romanized Indic Generation Fails Where Automatic Metrics Succeed

author.name: Madhu Sudhan Rao Beesetty, Surbhi Sharma, Devesh Maheshwari, Lokesh Meesala

entry.summary: Shows that automatic metrics like BGE-M3 and BERTScore systematically misrepresent the quality of romanized Hindi, Telugu, and Kannada generation, a widespread but under-benchmarked use pattern where hundreds of millions type Indic languages in Latin script. Human ratings reveal large quality gaps between models (e.g., GPT-5.5 rated well above Claude Opus 4.8) that metrics miss almost entirely, and identifies model-specific failure modes.

entry.title: SIFR: Stable Signed Flow Reinforcement

author.name: Runlong Liao, Xingqian Xu, Lizhang Chen, Baiyu Su, Yufan Huang, Zhonghao Wang, Akash Gokul, Ming-Yu Liu, Qiang Liu, Yogesh Balaji

entry.summary: Proposes SIFR, a reward fine-tuning method for flow models that replaces positive reward weights with signed advantages, providing an explicit unfitting signal and preventing distribution collapse from repeated reweighting. Stability is enforced by constraining velocity drift from a reference model via an adaptively tuned Lagrange multiplier.

entry.title: DexDICE: Reconciling Safety and Performance via Dual-Expert Offline Imitation Learning

author.name: Seokin Seo, Sung Kuk Shyn, Minji Seo, Yisoo Lee, Jongmin Lee, Hongseok Yang, Kee-Eung Kim

entry.summary: DexDICE introduces dual-expert offline imitation learning, combining safety-compliant but suboptimal demonstrations with high-performing but potentially unsafe demonstrations, avoiding hand-designed cost functions. The algorithm extracts safety information from the safety expert while recovering performance from the performance expert, providing strong safety guarantees alongside high returns. This addresses a fundamental tension in safe imitation learning with a practical data recipe.

entry.title: Breaking the Privacy Promise: Gradient Inversion Attacks on Federated Low-Rank Adapted Vision Transformers

author.name: Ritik K. Badiya, Siladittya Manna, Ashmit Sinha, M Yashwanth, Anirban Chakraborty

entry.summary: This paper shows that LoRA-based parameter-efficient fine-tuning of Vision Transformers in federated learning does not prevent private data leakage, demonstrating a spatially anchored generative inversion attack that reconstructs client training data from low-rank gradient updates. It identifies two coupled ambiguities (reduced gradient information and missing positional-embedding cues) that limit reconstruction quality and designs around them. The work matters because PEFT is widely assumed to reduce privacy risk in federated deployments.

entry.title: On the Few-Shot Adaptation of Vision-Language Models: A Few Gradient Signs Are All You Need

author.name: Nairouz Mrabah, Ismail Ben Ayed, Mahdi S. Hosseini, Eric Granger

entry.summary: Observing that gradient magnitudes are severely miscalibrated during few-shot adaptation of vision-language models while top-magnitude gradient signs remain informative, the authors propose SignSparseSGD and DynSignSparseSGD, state-free optimizers that select update locations by magnitude and direction by fixed-magnitude signs. Across 11 datasets, three CLIP backbones, and five shot levels they are competitive with or outperform parameter-efficient and optimization-based baselines.

entry.title: Enforcing Symmetries on Pre-trained ML Models for Physics

author.name: Wenjie Zhou, Valentino F. Foit, David W. Hogg, Soledad Villar

entry.summary: The authors study post-hoc group averaging (test-time augmentation via Haar-measure averaging, i.e., the Reynolds operator) to impose symmetry constraints on already-trained physics predictors without retraining, with known non-increasing risk guarantees. They demonstrate the approach on physics emulation models and extend the framework to non-compact groups where the Haar measure cannot be normalized. This provides a practical route to equivariance for legacy models, an underexplored setting.

entry.title: Rethinking MoE Load Balancing as Feedback Control

author.name: Yikun Hou, Alp Yurtsever

entry.summary: Reframes Mixture-of-Experts load balancing as a feedback control problem, defining a family of PID-style controllers (PID-Balancer) where the deviation of expert load from its fair share is the control error and per-expert routing bias is the control input. Notably evaluates under non-stationary data mixtures typical of curriculum learning and continual pretraining, where existing balancing methods are untested.

entry.title: Causal graph fusion across incomplete cohorts and causal steering of tabular foundation models

author.name: Yanke Li, Dhiyaa Al Jorf, Ayoube Ighissou, Anke Scheel-Sailer, Robert Riener, Diego Paez-Granados

entry.summary: Makes two contributions: causal graph fusion, which learns partial ancestral graphs on shared variables across incomplete clinical cohorts with missing data handled inside discovery, and causal attention steering, which compiles a learned causal graph into the attention of a frozen tabular foundation model at inference without retraining. Fusion dominates pooled and per-cohort baselines against known ground truth.

entry.title: MINE: Entropy-coded Memory-efficient Inference for Large Language Models

author.name: Emil Sch\"atzle, Markus P\"uschel

entry.summary: Presents MINE, a lossless entropy coding approach that accelerates single-stream LLM inference, where every weight streams from memory once per token, via dtANS-LLM, a GPU entropy coding scheme exploiting non-uniform weight distributions that persist after quantization. Unlike prior lossless compression work, it targets general speedups for memory-bound low-latency deployments with tunable trade-offs.

entry.title: Personalized health coaching via coachable health age and counterfactual wearable trajectories

author.name: Simon A. Lee, Zeinab Esmaeilpour, Menglian Zhou, Marius Guerard, Sohrab Sidhu, Alexandru Solot, Hamid Palangi, Pramod Rudrapatna, Ming-Zher Poh, Max A. Xu, Daniel McDuff, Dimitrios Antos, Yuzhe Yang, Jeffrey N. Chiang, Anthony Z. Faranesh, Lindsey Sunden, Mark Malhotra, Shwetak Patel, A. Ali Heydari, Ahmed A. Metwally

entry.summary: Introduces Coachable Health Age, an interpretable health metric from passively captured wearable signals, validated across WEAR-ME (N=2,780), All of Us (N=22,748), and longitudinal Fitbit cohorts, improving prognostic discrimination for cardiometabolic disease. Also presents Sensor World Model, an action-conditioned wearable world model for counterfactual behavioral prescriptions.

entry.title: Blind Noise Equalization for Large Data Matrices under General Variance Profiles

author.name: Boris Landa, Francesco Strino, Fabio Parisi, Ruiqi Li, Yuval Kluger

entry.summary: Introduces BRINE, a data-driven iterative procedure that rescales rows and columns of large noisy matrices to equalize heteroskedastic noise variance, restoring the Marchenko-Pastur spectral law without prior knowledge of signal or noise structure. This enables cleaner low-rank approximation when noise variances vary across entries, a common real-world condition.

entry.title: Where Should Learning Live? Regret Analysis for Text, Parameter, and Joint Adaptation

author.name: Jungtaek Kim, Jaden Park, Jongwon Jeong, Emmanouil-Vasileios Vlatakis-Gkaragkounis, Kangwook Lee

entry.summary: This theoretical work analyzes how language-model systems that repeatedly choose prompts and parameter adapters during deployment should be evaluated, decomposing excess loss into selection regret, family restriction gap, and history effects. It studies selection among preconstructed prompt-parameter candidates against the best fixed pair used from the start, and separates candidate quality from switching effects by evaluating each candidate against the history it would have produced. The paper provides regret guarantees for text-based, parameter-based, and joint adaptation.

entry.title: KLEAR: Knowledge-Matched LLM Evaluation in Korean across Application Requirements via Controlled Benchmark Transformation

author.name: Seoyeon Kim, Jeonghyun Kang, Hamin Koo, Barom Kang, Heondeuk Lee, Jaehyung Kim

entry.summary: Introduces KLEAR, a framework that transforms existing Korean LLM benchmarks by creating knowledge-matched question pairs that vary the degree of knowledge application required while holding underlying knowledge constant. This lets evaluators distinguish whether model errors stem from missing knowledge versus failure to apply it, addressing a key confound in benchmark interpretation.

entry.title: Greedy Byte-Pair Encoding Achieves at Least 0.361 of the Optimal Compression

author.name: Kundan Baliga, Aiden Xie, Aditya Byju

entry.summary: This theoretical paper improves the long-standing approximation guarantee for greedy Byte-Pair Encoding, the tokenization algorithm used in virtually all modern language models. The authors prove that greedy BPE always achieves at least 0.361 of the optimal compression reduction, up from the previously known bound of one third, and they explain structurally why one third was a barrier via a tight pair-packing relaxation.

entry.title: Align3D: Image-Structure Co-Aligned 3D Scene Generation with Observability-Aware Fidelity-Preserving Guidance

author.name: Chenliang Zhou, Yifan Wang, Andrzej Banburski-Fahey

entry.summary: Align3D is an image-conditioned diffusion model that generates 3D indoor layouts faithful to a single input photograph while remaining physically plausible beyond the observed view. It combines confidence-weighted image/scene-graph fusion with observability-aware guidance so unobserved regions absorb physical priors without breaking image alignment, improving image-alignment and scene-quality on 3D-FRONT.

entry.title: RadarDINO: Distilling a Visual Foundation Model into mmWave Radar for Human Mesh Reconstruction

author.name: Furkan Mert Algan, Zhifan Ni, Eckehard Steinbach

entry.summary: RadarDINO distills semantic representations from a DINOv3 visual teacher into 3D mmWave radar features for privacy-preserving, illumination-robust human mesh reconstruction. It uses calibrated RGB-radar geometry to provide voxel- and body-part-level supervision, plus explicit geometric supervision. This bridges the semantic gap between sparse radar signals and rich visual foundation model features.

entry.title: Video-Coder: Reinforcing Agentic Coding for Video Generation

author.name: Chaoyang Wang, Sicheng Gao, Junan Hu, Kunyang Li, Dongyang Chen, Yiyang Zhou, Huaxiu Yao, Yong Jae Lee, Radu Timofte, Yuzhang Shang

entry.summary: Video-Coder trains an agent that writes and executes code to construct a dynamic 3D draft scene providing structure and motion signals to downstream video generators, using SFT and reinforcement learning with curated datasets. This agentic, code-mediated approach addresses precise spatial structure and controllable composition in video generation.

entry.title: Lodos-v2: An Efficient Primal Formulation of the Exact Frictional Contact Problem

author.name: Onur Beker, Andreas Ren\'e Geist, Georg Martius

entry.summary: Lodos-v2 is a GPU-based massively parallel rigid-body simulator that solves the exact frictional contact problem in primal form, fixing physical artifacts (lift-off, artificial compliance, tangential creep) present in the convex-relaxation predecessor Lodos-v1. It targets high throughput in scenes with many detailed mesh collisions.

entry.title: ODEAction: From Predicting Chunks to Evolving Actions

author.name: Qishen Wang, Pengxiang Ding, Shifeng Bao, Mingyang Sun, Hengtao Li, Yi Gao, Baohua Yin, Yang Liu, Jiajun Fu, Jiacheng Liu, Changjing He, Peiyang Li, Runze Suo, Yan Wang, Xiaobo Wang, Yonghao Dang, Cheng Chi

entry.summary: This paper introduces ODEAction, a chunk-free action generation paradigm for vision-language-action (VLA) robot models that replaces discrete action-chunk prediction with Continuous Action Evolution. The model learns an action transition field over action space and integrates it with an ordinary-differential-equation solver at execution time, using current actions as initial conditions, thereby eliminating discontinuities at chunk boundaries.

entry.title: Scenario Orchestration for Closed-loop Policy Evaluation of Autonomous Driving

author.name: Frieda Rong, Zhaoyue Wang, Veer Kapadia, Vishaka Rajani, Aren A. Babikian, Xujie Si, Mahsa Golchoubian, Raquel Urtasun, Igor Gilitschenski

entry.summary: The authors introduce a scenario orchestrator that continuously monitors joint traffic state in driving simulation and adapts non-ego actors via re-timing, re-routing, and role reassignment to preserve intended scenario intent in closed loop. Each step solves a constrained optimization problem, bridging the gap between rigid scripted scenarios and unconstrained learned traffic actors.

entry.title: I Think, Therefore I Attack: Evaluating Thought Injection Attacks on Reasoning Agents

author.name: Parth Illendula, Garik Livingston, Zain Shamsi, Ravi Srinivasan, Alex Liu

entry.summary: This two-part study examines thought injection attacks on large reasoning models (evaluated on existing production-class open-weight models including GLM-5.3, MiniMax-M2.5, and Qwen3.8 variants), where untrusted text mimicking the model's own chain-of-thought is fed back into it. It finds that effects of thinking tags and payload styles are model-specific, and explores adaptive attack strategies in a second study.

entry.title: ENGRAM: From Agent Experience to Weights through Verified Consolidation

author.name: Ruiyi Yang, Zechen Li, Lihuan Li, Du Yin, Hao Xue, Flora D. Salim

entry.summary: ENGRAM separates training admission from memory release when consolidating agent experience into model weights, using a demonstration-aware gate to admit skills and an Engram Trace Graph for context, plus a verification gate that decides when external records can leave retrieval. This addresses when experiences should be trained on versus remain in external memory.

entry.title: An Educated Guess: Deriving Statistically Aligned Gradient Estimates for Zeroth-Order Optimisation

author.name: Justus Huebotter, Serge Thill, Marcel van Gerven, Nasir Ahmad

entry.summary: This paper improves zeroth-order optimisation methods such as SPSA and weight perturbation by deriving statistically aligned gradient estimates that mitigate the curse of dimensionality of random perturbations. The motivation is enabling learning on non-traditional hardware (neuromorphic chips, asynchronous systems, ASICs) where backpropagation is impractical.

entry.title: HomeLoop: A Simulation Framework and Benchmark for Robot-IoT Coordination in Everyday Domestic Assistance and Safety

author.name: Ramy ElMallah, Marc Bishara, Hyegang Kim, Yuxi Zhang, Chongyu Zhu, Chi-Guhn Lee

entry.summary: HomeLoop is an Isaac Sim-based simulation framework and benchmark for VLM-driven home robots that must integrate with existing smart-home cameras, IoT devices, and resident wearables, and reason through ambiguous safety scenarios (e.g., distinguishing a smoke alarm source). It formalizes robot-IoT coordination for domestic assistance and safety.

entry.title: When Routine Operations Break Architectural Pattern Relationships in LLM Agent Harnesses

author.name: Boming Xia, Qinghua Lu, Dino Sejdinovic, Liming Zhu

entry.summary: Analyzes how routine operations on LLM agent harnesses can silently break architectural pattern relationships (Guardrail Enforcement Point, Autonomy Controller, Blackboard) that safety guardrails, tool mediation, and state management depend on, without any code change. It introduces PatternOps, an assessment procedure applied across five released harnesses and fourteen independently written plugins.

entry.title: Encoding Memory in World Models with Test-Time Model-Based Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Maxime Burchi, Fayaz Ali Dharejo, Radu Timofte

entry.summary: This paper introduces Test-Time Model-Based Reinforcement Learning (TT-MBRL), which uses gradient descent at test time to encode the memory of an episode's observations into world model parameters, effectively learning a distinct world model per episode. This moves beyond architecture-design approaches to long-term memory in MBRL and improves memory and planning on tasks where agents struggle to surpass human performance. Connecting test-time training to world models is a timely synthesis of two active research threads.

entry.title: A Taxonomy-Driven Synthetic Dataset for Retrieval Effectiveness and Fairness Evaluation in Hiring

author.name: Warren Jouanneau, Morgane Hoffmann, Emma Jouffroy, Marc Palyart

entry.summary: The authors release a taxonomy-driven, fully synthetic multilingual HR dataset and benchmark grounded in 660K real freelancer profiles, including candidate profiles, project briefs, and counterfactual demographic twins for joint evaluation of retrieval effectiveness and algorithmic fairness. Auditing state-of-the-art embedding models reveals divergence from general MTEB scores and fairness disparities in grammatically gendered languages. This fills a genuine benchmarking gap where legal constraints block public data in hiring.

entry.title: RidgeFill: Training-Free Late-Layer Cache Fill for Faster Prefill

author.name: Dylan Johnston, Robert P. Smith

entry.summary: RidgeFill accelerates LLM prefill by running lower layers exactly up to a split point and predicting later layers' inputs with a ridge regression fitted once in closed form from one calibration pass, letting late layers write their caches from predictions, while the last tokens and all decoding steps run the full model. It retrofits the YOCO/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-style trained design onto models never trained for it, with nothing trained and no tokens dropped.

entry.title: Forcing a Letter Suppresses Refusal: Mechanistic Evidence from WMDP

author.name: Stepan Epifantsev, Anna Antipova, Oleg Chernikov, Leon Strelkov, Alexey Dontsov

entry.summary: Provides a mechanistic explanation of why multiple-choice question formats reduce LLM refusal rates, using tuned lens analysis on WMDP across Llama-3.1-8B and Qwen3-8B. The model commits to an answer-letter token very quickly in MCQ format, activations lie roughly 3x further from the refusal direction than in open-ended formats, and interventions on refusal-related components confirm the causal story.

entry.title: InstaGen: Group-Shared Importance Sampling for Fast Video Generation

author.name: Kislay Aditya Oj, Kumar Krishna Agrawal, Sri Surya Varma Datla, Aditya Desai

entry.summary: Shows that top-p block selection in permuted block-sparse attention for diffusion transformers is sample-inefficient in high-entropy regimes common to video generation, and proposes group-shared importance sampling as a better approximation under the same compute budget. Targets latency reduction for DiT-based video generation.

entry.title: Grounding-Aware Judge Reward Reinforcement Learning for Out-of-Domain Face Anti-Spoofing

author.name: Xiaoyong Yu, Xinge Yu

entry.summary: This work post-trains an MLLM for face anti-spoofing with chain-of-thought reasoning, confronting the problem that only the binary verdict is rule-verifiable while reasoning is not. It proposes a grounding-aware judge reward so the model cannot exploit shortcuts like false-rejection bias, improving out-of-domain generalization with interpretable forensic evidence.

entry.title: PoseRieFlow: Riemannian Flow Matching for Whole-Body Text-to-Pose Generation

author.name: Jan Spindler, Bardia Ardakanian, Patrick Stotko, Reinhard Klein

entry.summary: PoseRieFlow is a compact flow-matching framework for text-conditioned generation of whole-body 3D human poses, formulated directly on the product manifold of SMPL-H joint rotations. It learns a text-conditioned vector field transporting samples along Riemannian geodesics from an SO(3) Gaussian prior, using a part-tokenized Diffusion Transformer with dedicated hand tokens and part-specific decoders. This correctly handles the non-Euclidean geometry of rotations and articulated hands.

entry.title: CS-Pi: Constraint-Satisfying Flow Policy Sampling

author.name: Soumojit Bhattacharya, Oliver Kroemer, Shubham Tulsiani

entry.summary: CS-Pi enforces inference-time constraints on flow-matching robot policies by sampling actions that are both safe (satisfying novel constraints) and plausible (likely under the pretrained policy), avoiding the unreliability of gradient guidance when the policy is multimodal. This enables constraint satisfaction without retraining for each new obstacle or requirement.

entry.title: AttentionSwitch: Jailbreak Defense for LLMs via Joint Learning of Sparse Attention-Head Selection and Scaling

author.name: Doniyorkhon Obidov, Honggang Yu, Xiaolong Guo, Kaichen Yang

entry.summary: AttentionSwitch is a jailbreak defense that jointly learns which sparse set of attention heads to intervene on and how to scale them, avoiding expensive fine-tuning that risks catastrophic forgetting. The key insight is that jointly optimizing where to intervene and how to modify components outperforms existing approaches that decouple these decisions.

entry.title: AUTEUR: Acoustic Plan Learning for Red-Teaming Text-to-Audio Models

author.name: Jiashu Zhang, Jiaming He, Zheming Zhang, Kaizheng Wang, Bing Li, Zhiyuan Zha, Yi Yu

entry.summary: AUTEUR automates red-teaming of text-to-audio models by learning structured acoustic plans describing foreground sounds, context, and vocal attributes, refined via waveform feedback. The plan generator is trained with supervised fine-tuning followed by reinforcement learning using audio feedback, producing prompts that pass textual screening yet elicit harmful acoustic output.

entry.title: On the Reliability of Majority-Vote Pseudo-Labels in Test-Time Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Haoyu Wang, Ru Wang, Yuanyuan Wang, Jiaxian Guo, Mingming Gong

entry.summary: This theoretical work analyzes majority-vote pseudo-label supervision in test-time reinforcement learning with online DPO, decomposing error into unidentifiable population-majority bias and prompt-dependent finite-rollout variation. It proposes Prompt-Conditional Distributionally Robust DPO (PC-Dr.DPO), which reweights updates within prompts based on observed vote reliability.

entry.title: Compression of Emotion in Language Model Representations

author.name: Laya Iyer, Sanmi Koyejo, Chen Shani

entry.summary: Studying seven LLMs on GoEmotions, the paper finds consistent overcompression: hidden representations cluster fine-grained emotions into far coarser groups than the 27-category taxonomy, revealing how emotion distinctions are organized internally. This contrasts with models apparent ability to produce fluent emotional language.

entry.title: Who's Asking? Audience-Conditioned Privatization

author.name: Daniil Filienko, Anusha Bagalkotkar, Xan Vongsathorn, Sikha Pentyala

entry.summary: The paper argues that differential privacy for synthetic text and attribute-based anonymization both ignore downstream usage context, where an attribute harmless to one audience is sensitive to another. It proposes Ext-Classify-based audience-conditioned privatization that tailors what is protected and preserved per recipient audience.

entry.title: More with Less: Efficient Parallel Scientific Code Translation via an Agent-Skill Workflow

author.name: Jianuo Shen, Pengyi Xu, Bo Zhang
