entry.summary: The paper presents a multi-agent framework for translating parallel scientific codes between HPC programming frameworks, separating translation, compilation diagnosis, and execution validation into autonomous agents coordinated by a verdict-driven orchestrator that routes failures to targeted repair skills. It adds output checking for self-correction and offline LLM verification to catch false positives that escape compiler and runtime checks.

entry.title: UniRGBA: Unifying RGB and Alpha in Pretrained Video Diffusion Models

author.name: Lei Xu, Zhuo Li, Yongyi Jin, Aoyu Wang

entry.summary: Introduces UniRGBA, a framework for generating videos with a native alpha channel by minimally extending an existing causal video VAE and diffusion model with zero-initialized 4-channel expansion rather than dedicated alpha encoders. This improves generalization to visual-effect content with non-local, non-elliptical semi-transparency where matting-style RGBA approaches degrade.

entry.title: RPEG: Training Reasoning Language Models Scalably and Cost-Effectively

author.name: Maciej Besta, Leonard Schmidt, Pierre Pang, Patrik Okanovic, Robert Gerstenberger, Torsten Hoefler

entry.summary: Introduces RPEG, a data-centric graph intermediate representation for reinforcement-learning pipelines used to train reasoning language models, jointly optimizing pipeline structure (bounded asynchrony, actor-critic sharing) and execution (stage fusion, fine-grained scheduling, parallelism). It targets the cost and complexity of RL steps that couple multiple large models and asynchronous dependencies.

entry.title: Logit Laundering: Evading Data-Use Auditing in Large Language Models

author.name: Ruihan Hu, Wei Luo, Yu-Ming Shang, Jiakai Wang, Chuxuan Zhang, Mei Li, Xi Zhang, Meikang Qiu

entry.summary: This paper studies data-use auditing in LLMs from an adversarial perspective, proposing Logit Laundering, a framework that lets non-compliant providers trained on watermarked copyrighted data evade watermark-based detection. By systematically demonstrating that a dominant class of auditing methods can be circumvented, the work exposes a critical gap in data-ownership safeguards. It is valuable as both an attack and a stress test that should drive more robust auditing research.

entry.title: ICare-DT: a digital twin for continuous forecasting of intensive care patients

author.name: Yanke Li, Yahang Qi, Yumi Kim, Diego Paez-Granados

entry.summary: ICare-DT is a Transformer-based digital twin that updates a latent patient state hourly from routine ICU measurements without retraining, trained on 140,473 eICU-CRD stays to forecast vital-sign crossings. Later forecasts beat the model's own earlier forecasts of the same windows across all 12 settings, and ablations confirm the gain comes from new patient data; the model also transfers to a second database without refitting. This demonstrates that routine records support continuous, adaptive patient forecasting.

entry.title: On Differentially Private Mechanisms for Linear Regression

author.name: Bardiya Aryanfard, Monika Henzinger, Farhood Rostamkhani

entry.summary: The paper studies differentially private least-squares linear regression in batch and continual observation settings, introducing ContinualAdaSSP, the first mechanism for unconstrained linear regression under continual DP with update time polynomial in d rather than n. This fills a gap where prior continual-setting work was restricted to constrained regression and polynomial-in-n runtime.

entry.title: ResQAdam: Residual-Preserving Adaptive Optimization for Memory-Efficient Quantization Aware Training

author.name: Liqun Ma, Shengkun Tang, Liangyu Wang, Lin Zhao, Wei Luo, Xinjun Niu, Spandan Tiwari, Ashish Sirasao, Kun Zhang, Zhiqiang Shen

entry.summary: ResQAdam improves memory-efficient quantization-aware training of LLMs by showing that projection-based low-rank optimizers like GaLore discard useful QAT momentum outside the top-r singular subspace. It keeps a single BF16 momentum, applies Adam only to principal-subspace coordinates, and adds a normalized sign update from the residual, maintaining accuracy with reduced memory.

entry.title: KnowEvo: Knowledge Evolution for Protein Optimization

author.name: Zijie Xing, Xingyue Liu, Runze Wang, Luoming Hu, Yanming Shen

entry.summary: KnowEvo is a framework for LLM-driven scientific discovery that treats externalized, modular knowledge itself as the optimization target rather than relying only on parameter updates or prompt refinement. It aims to make accumulated scientific expertise inspectable, evaluable, and refinable across problem-solving episodes, demonstrated on protein optimization. This speaks to a core limitation of current LLM agents for science.

entry.title: Marginal-Nonuniform Multiclass Learning

author.name: Nataly Brukhim, Steve Hanneke, Amirreza Shaeiri, Maximilian Thiessen

entry.summary: Studies multiclass classification under marginal-nonuniform learning, where rate constants may depend on the unknown marginal but not the target concept, interpolating between PAC and universal learning. Provides a complete characterization of optimal rates via a trichotomy (exponential, linear, arbitrarily slow) witnessed by a new combinatorial dimension, the uncentered DS dimension.

entry.title: High-Dimensional Off-Policy Evaluation without Sample Splitting using an Onsager Correction

author.name: Saksham Jain, Guillaume Braun, Masaaki Imaizumi

entry.summary: Develops an Onsager-corrected, target-policy-weighted criterion for off-policy evaluation that estimates the full-data reward model's out-of-sample risk using only training observations, avoiding the suboptimality of held-out selection when model rankings change after full-data refitting. Relevant to reward model selection in high-dimensional settings.

entry.title: Region-aware error triage for medical image segmentation with groupwise conformal risk control

author.name: Nishi Kanta Paul, Md Shihabul Islam Shovo, Hoileong Lee

entry.summary: RACE-Triage is a post-hoc framework that flags where segmentation masks are likely wrong without modifying the mask, applying conformal risk control separately to boundary bands and non-boundary regions. This region-aware grouping avoids under-flagging errors far from the predicted contour and provides statistical guarantees on missed-error rates for clinical review workflows.

entry.title: A Bridge from Paste to Place: Physics-Guided One-Step Image Composition via Object-Scene Interaction

author.name: Hongzhen Li, Youwei Pan, Yingfang Zhu, Sen Zhu, Fengjie Zhu, Leilei Cao

entry.summary: Paste2Place is an end-to-end physics-guided flow-based model that turns pasted-object inputs into realistic composites in a single step, guided by explicit albedo-shading-residual decomposition. The authors also build a Blender-based rendering pipeline for training and evaluation. It unifies object insertion, harmonization, and shadow synthesis in one efficient framework.

entry.title: Video2Asset: Online Construction of Persistent 3D Street-Scene Assets

author.name: Zihan Zheng, Chunlei Cai, Zhenlong Wu, Linjun Li, Yichen Gong, Xiaoyun Zhang, Qiang Hu

entry.summary: Video2Asset is an online framework that converts multi-view street video into a persistent scene of independently editable 3D objects, using occupancy as an intermediate representation. Historical Carrier Guidance and an identity encoder handle intermittent observations under motion and occlusion, while Accumulated-Evidence Association maintains object identities without fragmenting or mixing evidence. It supports continual, editable 3D scene reconstruction.

entry.title: Dynamic GPU Voxel Grids and Voxel-sequential Processing in NanoVDB

author.name: Eftychios Sifakis, Francis Williams, Christopher Horvath, Rohan Sawhney, Mark Harris, Jonathan Swartz, Ken Museth

entry.summary: The authors extend the NanoVDB sparse voxel data structure with dynamic GPU-native topology updates and a voxel-sequential access paradigm that accelerates point-wise and stencil-based operators. This removes the prior static-topology limitation, enabling use in simulation and dynamic geometry for ML workloads.

entry.title: TPS-A*: Path Planning for Any-Shape Vehicles with Certified Collision Checking in Trajectory Parameter Space

author.name: Jose Luis Blanco-Claraco, Shravan S. Rai, Fernando Ca\~nadas-Ar\'anega, Jos\'e Luis Torres-Moreno, Jos\'e Carlos Moreno-\'Ubeda

entry.summary: TPS-A* is a lattice planner whose edges are kinematically feasible trajectories with certified collision checking in trajectory parameter space; a precomputed footprint grid returns certified free distances for all candidate trajectories in one pass over local obstacles. The paper proves the grid never overestimates free distance of the continuously swept, possibly non-convex footprint.

entry.title: Aspect-wise Pairwise Tournaments for Test-Time Selection

author.name: Hannah Guan, Yilun Du

entry.summary: The paper introduces Aspect-wise Pairwise Tournaments (APT), a test-time compute method that selects among best-of-n candidates by comparing pairs of solutions on individual aspects rather than judging each in isolation. This mirrors human decision-making and aims to improve selection quality in LLM reasoning pipelines.

entry.title: MeshRT: Compile-Time Governed Wafer-Scale Runtime for Low-Latency High-Throughput Inference

author.name: Congjie He, Le Xu, Zhan Lu, Yeqi Huang, Haocheng Xiao, Cheng Deng, Lingxiao Ma, Ziming Miao, Fan Yang, Luo Mai

entry.summary: MeshRT is a wafer-scale runtime that achieves both ultra-low latency and high throughput for LLM inference by handling the runtime dynamism of batching and MoE that existing wafer-scale stacks cannot support efficiently, using compile-time governance to schedule dynamic workloads. It targets the cost premium of low-latency serving on wafer-scale accelerators.

entry.title: JEPAhead: From Inpainting to Causal Forecasting for Urban Driving

author.name: Daniel G. P. Petrini, Davi Pincinato, Fabio Grassiotto, Pedro L. F. Prado, Alexandre F. S. Osorio, Raphael V. Ramos, Felipe Pamboukian

entry.summary: The authors fine-tune a pre-trained V-JEPA1 predictor from bidirectional latent inpainting to action-free causal forecasting in urban driving, keeping the encoder frozen and forecasting sixteen future frames in one forward pass. On CARLA it retrieves the correct future among 591 candidates 69.0% of the time versus 55.3% for persistence, and predicted features are shown to encode driving-relevant semantics via linear probes.

entry.title: MotionDecipher: LLM-Assisted Clinical Interpretation of Human Motion Signals for Efficient Gait Analysis

author.name: Mingrui Ma, Tian Tan, Jinsi Guo, Jessica Rose, Yiwen Dong

entry.summary: MotionDecipher is a framework that bridges continuous human motion signals and LLM-based clinical reasoning, producing gait-analysis reports of the kind experts write manually for neurological disorder patients. It addresses the context-quality problem that limits LLM reasoning over raw motion data.

entry.title: On the Limits of Execution Traces for Repairing Assertion Failures in LLM-Generated Code

author.name: Muntasir Adnan, Carlos C. N. Kuhn

entry.summary: Shows that after iterative LLM-based program repair, residual failures are mostly assertion failures (79% on BigCodeBench with Qwen2.5 models), and argues via an information-theoretic view that assertion messages carry little fault-localization information. It proposes Breakpoint Debugging, which annotates the failed program inline with runtime variable values, outperforming resampling on hard residual failures.

entry.title: TopoSHAP: Shapley for Explainable and Efficient Topological Deep Learning

author.name: Mathilde Papillon, Nina Miolane

entry.summary: TopoSHAP assigns Shapley values to topological data cells (rings, higher-order structures) and to architectural components in topological deep learning models. Explanations match or outperform graph-based counterparts on GraphXAI benchmarks while running up to 112x faster, and reveal which architectural components drive performance.

entry.title: Deep Learning Theory through the Lens of Statistical Physics: A Topical Review

author.name: Wei Huang, Youjin Deng

entry.summary: This topical review surveys deep learning theory through statistical physics concepts including mean-field theory, phase transitions, energy landscapes, kernel and Gaussian-process limits, random-matrix tools, and Fokker-Planck formalisms. It frames foundation-model learning and generalization as high-dimensional, strongly coupled systems amenable to physics-style universality and scaling analysis. A timely synthesis given the persistent gap between deep learning practice and theory.

entry.title: Topology as a Design Variable: Joint Architecture-Sizing Optimization for SRAM

author.name: Can Wang, Junhao Ma, Yikai Wang, Shan Shen, Wei W. Xing

entry.summary: Presents OpenYieldV2, an open-source SRAM design tool that treats bitcell topology (6T vs 10T) as an optimizable discrete variable alongside continuous transistor sizing, using a fully parameterized macro compiler and a few-shot TabPFN surrogate for topology-aware optimization. This fills a real gap, since prior open tools either performed no optimization or fixed the topology.

entry.title: The Multiscale Single-Index Model: An MSE Analysis of Online SGD Dynamics

author.name: Gordon Dai, Joan Bruna

entry.summary: Analyzes the Multiscale Single-Index Model (MSIM) as a stylized setting for hierarchical feature learning with scale separation, proving that joint online spherical SGD under MSE loss for the two-hidden-layer case achieves weak recovery from random initialization in O(d log^2 d) samples. Provides tractable theory for how deep architectures learn local multiscale representations.

entry.title: Optimal Regret for Profit Maximization in Bilateral Trade

author.name: Matteo Castiglioni, Anna Lunghi, Alberto Marchesi

entry.summary: Studies repeated bilateral trade where an intermediary posts prices to a buyer and seller with only binary trade feedback, and shows learning both sides of the market is no harder in regret than learning one side. Designs an algorithm achieving optimal tilde-O(T^(2/3)) regret without observing either valuation.

entry.title: Machine learning for lattice QCD

author.name: Gurtej Kanwar, Scott Lawrence, Alessandro Nada, Phiala Shanahan

entry.summary: A survey chapter for the Lattice QCD at 50 Years volume summarizing established uses of machine learning to optimize lattice field theory calculations without introducing uncontrolled approximations. It covers the state of the field as of late 2025, authored by leading researchers including Phiala Shanahan.

entry.title: InstantHMR : Real-Time Human Mesh Recovery on Your Phone

author.name: Mohamed Adjel (LAAS-GEPETTO), Kahina Chalabi (LAAS-GEPETTO), Vincent Bonnet (LAAS-GEPETTO)

entry.summary: InstantHMR is a family of open-source single-image human mesh recovery regressors designed for mobile inference, based on the Momentum Human Rig and trained on public SAM 3D Body dataset annotations. It recovers a 6,890-vertex mesh in 5.5 ms per person on a Samsung Galaxy S23 NPU and 0.98 ms on an RTX 4070, surpassing existing methods in speed while maintaining accuracy.

entry.title: BEV3SR: Evidence-Aware 3D Spatial Reasoning from Video

author.name: Fan Zhu, Rui Yu

entry.summary: BEV3SR is a training-free, backbone-agnostic framework that turns RGB-D video into a queryable metric bird's-eye-view scene memory for 3D spatial reasoning with vision-language models. A Spatial Task Formalizer structures each query's reference frame, constraints, objective, and evidence needs, addressing viewpoint mismatch and sparse or occluded cues. It enables answering perspective-specified spatial questions from video.

entry.title: Confirming Claims of Superposition and Adversarial Examples in Vision Transformers

author.name: Xijia Che

entry.summary: A replication of the vision transformer experiments from the paper on adversarial attacks leveraging interference between features in superposition, completed under the Second Look Summer Fellowship. The author confirms that increased superposition yields adversarial attacks aligned with class-vector geometry, and extends the work by showing input/classification-head coupling is attack-method-independent and that adversarial training improves robustness without measurable geometry changes.

entry.title: Cancellation Is Not Enough: What Retries Leave Behind in an Overloaded LLM Engine

author.name: Xindan Zhang, Fei Wang

entry.summary: Through overload experiments on vLLM with three open models and detailed scheduler traces, the paper shows that propagating cancellation alone cannot restore service after transient overload when clients retry, with only 12-38% of post-overload calls delivered. The traces reveal that retried requests typically begin prefill very late, leaving the engine computing for departed clients.

entry.title: LEMMO: A Large Electromagnetic Model leveraging Pretrained LLMs for Million-Sample Signal Understanding

author.name: Mingkai Li, Jiajun Wu, Yihan Mao, Zilin Sang, Taosong Yu, Yuan Ma, Minghe Liu, Qianqian Yang, Zhiguo Shi

entry.summary: LEMMO is a large electromagnetic model for instruction-driven recognition and description of long raw IQ recordings, combining a linear-attention EM encoder with anti-aliased temporal resampling to process up to eight million complex samples. An EM-text interaction module uses instruction-conditioned learnable queries to bridge waveform and language modalities.

entry.title: Subliminal Learning in Vision-Language Models

author.name: Arman Hatami, Romina Aalishah, Ilya E. Monosov

entry.summary: The authors extend the subliminal learning phenomenon, where a teacher transmits hidden preferences to a student through unrelated training data, from LLMs to vision-language models. Finetuning teacher VLMs on animal or facial-attribute preferences and training students on the teachers' number outputs for an unrelated geometric task shows these preferences transfer across VLMs from 2B to 7B parameters.

entry.title: CascadeRec: Deployed Adaptive LLM Compute Allocation for Multi-Tenant Content Recommendation

author.name: Kai Zhao, Guilin Zhang, Xiang Cheng, Xiquan Cui, Henry Heng, Xu Chu, Alet Blanken

entry.summary: CascadeRec describes a two-tier LLM reranking cascade deployed in production at a financial planning SaaS provider, where a lightweight Tier-1 model handles most requests and a router escalates only promising cases to expensive Tier-2 inference procedures. It reports results from an extended production A/B experiment on AWS infrastructure.

entry.title: ProtoCouncil: Multi-Encoder Anatomical Prototypes for Prostate Cancer Detection in Micro-Ultrasound

author.name: Mohammad Mahdi Abootorabi, Nooshin Maghsoodi, Armin Saadat, Obed Dzikunu, Zhuoxin Guo, Hannes Cash, Ferdinand Luger, Adam Kinnaird, Brian Wodlinger, Parvin Mousavi, Purang Abolmaesumi

entry.summary: Presents ProtoCouncil, a prostate cancer detection framework for micro-ultrasound that fuses prototype learning from three foundation encoders (MedSAM, DINOv3, V-JEPA 2.1) at three anatomical levels, producing traceable, uncertainty-flagged decisions. Prototype logits decompose exactly into bias plus prototype similarities, enabling clinical interpretability.

entry.title: BOXBOX: Recursive Harness Self-Improvement for Long-Running Performance Optimization

author.name: Yuhao Tan, Hanyun Jiang, Fangkai Yang, Yuan Yao, Taolue Chen, Bo Qiao, Yu Kang, Lu Wang, Pu Zhao, Xiaoxing Ma, Qingwei Lin

entry.summary: Introduces PerfRace, a benchmark for long-running software performance optimization, and BOXBOX, a system enabling agents to recursively revise their own harnesses mid-task via kernel-managed hot reloading while preserving execution consistency. This extends harness optimization beyond offline settings with reference answers to open-ended, evolving tasks.

entry.title: DataHelix: A CPU-GPU Co-Scheduling Data Plane for Multimodal Model Training

author.name: Yuanhe Li, Jiazhen Wu, Dian Ding, Guangtao Xue, Yiming Zhang

entry.summary: DataHelix is a systems contribution addressing pipeline stalls in multimodal model training caused by heterogeneous decoding costs and tensor sizes across data-parallel ranks. It presents a metadata-first CPU-GPU co-scheduling data plane that jointly optimizes preprocessing and GPU execution rather than treating them in isolation, eliminating pipeline bubbles. This matters because data loading increasingly bottlenecks large multimodal training runs.

entry.title: Composable Causality: A Toolkit for Systematic Time-Series Causal Discovery and Treatment-Effect Benchmarking

author.name: Muhammad Hasan Ferdous, Md Osman Gani

entry.summary: DTCD is a dataset-and-toolkit enabling composable synthetic generation of multivariate time series where mechanism, confounding, sparsity, noise, and missingness can be varied independently with ground-truth causal structure, including counterfactual treatment-effect evaluation. It addresses the fixed-dataset and hardcoded-simulator limitations of existing causal benchmarking tools.

entry.title: BrainCoT: A Multi-Task Zero-Shot Brain Signal Foundation Model with Neurometric-Anchored Chain-of-Thought Reasoning

author.name: Yiyu Gui, Mingzhi Chen, Guibo Luo, Yuchao Yang

entry.summary: BrainCoT is a brain signal foundation model unifying heterogeneous tasks into an instruction-driven format with multi-task zero-shot capability, augmented by neurometric-anchored chain-of-thought reasoning that provides verifiable evidence for predictions. It targets multi-center heterogeneity and inter-subject variability that limit current brain-signal foundation models requiring task-specific supervised adaptation. This could improve clinical and research deployment of neural decoding models.

entry.title: Controllable Molecule Generation via Sparse Representation Editing: An Interpretability-Driven Perspective

author.name: Zhuoran Li, Xu Sun, Chang Wen Chen, Wanyu Lin

entry.summary: SpaRE is an interpretability-driven framework for controllable LLM-based molecule generation that learns an overcomplete sparse feature space disentangling LLM representations into concept-aligned latent features corresponding to chemically meaningful substructures and properties. Editing these sparse features enables fine-grained, precise control over generated molecules, addressing the entanglement of dense LLM representations. This connects sparse-dictionary interpretability methods to practical generative control in chemistry.

entry.title: TimeOmni-Live: Continuous & Live Time Series Understanding with Long-Term Memory

author.name: Tong Guan, Alexander Chemeris, Yiqing Guo, Warren Jin, Zhao Li, Shirui Pan, Ming Jin

entry.summary: Introduces Continuous and Live Time Series Understanding (CL-TSU), a paradigm for time series language models that maintains persistent, stateful understanding over open-ended streams instead of offline one-shot processing, along with LiveTS-Suite, a benchmark suite for data generation, training, and evaluation of this setting. Bridges the gap between static time series models and real-world streaming applications.

entry.title: Fifty-Two Shades of Pig: What the UCR Archive Really Asks Classifiers to Do

author.name: Omar Swelam, Jaris K\"uken, Shi Bin Hoo, Frank Hutter, Lennart Purucker

entry.summary: Critically audits the UCR Time Series Classification Archive, showing several datasets are repurposed from their original tasks, built from toy setups, or have flawed test splits, exemplified by PigAirwayPressure asking which of 52 pigs produced a trace. The paper questions how representative the de facto TSC benchmark is of real time series problems.

entry.title: BEVCast: Path-Adaptive BEV for Efficient End-to-End Autonomous Driving

author.name: Qiren Wang, Mingyu Guo, Zixuan Wang, Weisong Shi

entry.summary: Presents BEVCast, a two-stage bird's-eye-view model for camera-based driving that refines only high-heat cells along the predicted path to fine resolution while keeping the rest coarse, eliminating uniform dense computation. Requires no HD map or navigation command and covers the whole scene in a mixed-resolution BEV.

entry.title: FANO: Anchored Forward-Noise Optimization for Diffusion Inverse Problems

author.name: Shilong Han, Hongxia Wang

entry.summary: FANO improves zero-shot diffusion solvers for image inverse problems by diagnosing radial drift: annealed methods optimizing the denoiser input push the noise-component norm out of its typical range, degrading reconstruction. The method anchors the previous estimate and optimizes only the forward noise with a known distribution, improving performance on nonlinear tasks.

entry.title: Decoupled Mode Connectivity for Base-to-Novel Generalization in Vision-Language Models

author.name: Imad Eddine Marouf, Khalid Oublal, Enzo Tartaglione, St\'ephane Lathuili\`ere

entry.summary: The paper shows that prompt learning for CLIP suffers gradient conflict between base-class specialization and zero-shot generalization when both objectives share one prompt, and that no single-prompt loss design clearly helps. Decoupled Mode Connectivity gives each objective its own prompt and merges text features at test time at no extra inference cost. This simple decoupling improves base-to-novel generalization.

entry.title: EGT: Execution-Grounded Traversability through Learned Closed-Loop Trajectory Distributions

author.name: Chinmay Mundane, Amith Manoharan, Arun Kumar Singh

entry.summary: EGT redefines rough-terrain traversability as the probability that a vehicle-controller pair can execute a candidate path while meeting trajectory-level tracking and progress requirements, estimated via a latent-space flow matching model conditioned on terrain features and vehicle state. This accounts for terrain disturbances and controller corrections that point-wise roll/pitch metrics ignore.

entry.title: Debate to Deceive: Poisoning LLM's Fact-Checking via Game-Theoretic Multi-Agent Debate

author.name: Liting Huang, Huizhi Liang, Yi Lei, Xingjun Ma, Varun Ojha

entry.summary: The paper presents Debate-to-Deceive (D2D), a multi-agent attack framework that uses game-theoretic, rhetorically structured debate (logos, pathos, ethos strategies evolving as an evolutionary game) to generate adversarial passages that poison LLM fact-checking judgments. It improves on adversarial suffix attacks and single-agent self-reflection by producing semantically coherent, defense-resistant content.

entry.title: Nudging Decision Models: Do Digital Nudges Steer Fast, Generation-Free AI Agents?

author.name: Sascha Kaltenpoth, Haya Halimeh, Kevin B\"osch, Oliver M\"uller

entry.summary: This empirical study examines whether decision models, a new class of generation-free AI agents that select among options without text generation, can be steered by digital nudges. Adapting an online shopping experiment previously run with humans and LLM agents, the authors test three decision models across 600 runs each, finding defaults chosen 97.5-99.9% of the time and social-influence products 75-96% versus 47-49% in control. Results support dual-process theory predictions that automatic nudges affect these fast System One-style models.

entry.title: KineCouple: Substrate-conditioned residual readout for enzyme kinetic prediction

author.name: Chun Kang, Yunbo Zhang, Fanhu Zeng, Jian Liu, Siwei Deng, Lei Sha

entry.summary: KineCouple improves enzyme kinetic parameter prediction by using substrate-conditioned cross-attention over residue-level protein features instead of substrate-independent pooling, allowing residue weighting to adapt to the specific enzyme-substrate pair. This supports enzyme engineering and metabolic modeling.

entry.title: Can Agentic Systems Close the Gap in Radiology with Production AI Tools?

author.name: Aubin Charley, Julien Khlaut, Charles Corbi\`ere, Pierre Manceron, Corentin Dancette, L\'eo Machado

entry.summary: The authors present a modality-agnostic radiology agentic framework where an orchestrator calls modular tools, including those from FDA-cleared radiology AI devices, to produce structured reports. Simulation over a large multi-modality report corpus measures what such systems can achieve with production-grade tools, probing whether agents can bridge the specialist-generalist gap in radiology AI.

entry.title: LEF-JEPA: Denoising-Trained Latent Energy Fields for Spatial Representation Learning

author.name: Zhiyuan Liu, Zhihao Xu, Sicheng Liu, Huanhuan Huang

entry.summary: LEF-JEPA strengthens spatial structure in JEPA-style latent representations — which struggle to capture object shapes and boundaries when prediction supervision applies only at masked positions — via target-guided latent recovery and denoising-trained latent energy fields. The goal is to improve representations suited to prediction and action without over-encoding texture and color detail.

entry.title: AdaAlloc: Adaptive Visual Token Allocation for Long-Video Question Answering

author.name: Joungbin An, Kristen Grauman

entry.summary: Recasts long-video QA as a visual-token allocation problem, proposing AdaAlloc, a training-free inference framework that adaptively splits a fixed token budget between global context and high-resolution local evidence and chooses where in the video to draw local evidence from. This improves on uniform sampling and caption- or similarity-based retrieval, which miss motion and state changes.

entry.title: Learning Generative Dynamics for 3D Molecule Generation via Sequential Neuro-Symbolic Constraints

author.name: Zhuoran Li, Xu Sun, Chang Wen Chen, Wanyu Lin

entry.summary: Proposes SensDiff, a neuro-symbolic diffusion framework for 3D molecule generation that injects symbolic physicochemical rules into the generative process at staged points along the coarse-to-fine diffusion trajectory. This makes models internalize scientific priors during training, producing chemically valid molecules rather than merely statistically plausible ones.

entry.title: From LoRA to Language: Recovering Skill Documents from Adapters

author.name: Saranya Dintakurthy Swadha, Pavan C Shekar, Arpit Jain, Aswanth Krishnan

entry.summary: This paper asks whether a skill document (instructional text compiled into a LoRA adapter) can be recovered from the adapter weights and frozen base model. Direct weight-reading approaches recovered little, but the proposed Executing Writer - a small writer trained on execution traces - substantially improves recovery of key instructions. This has implications for auditing, portability, and transparency of compiled agent skills.

entry.title: Verifier Noise Is a Temperature: Testing Tilt Predictions in Finite-Budget LLM-Guided Search

author.name: Xiaomeng Li

entry.summary: This theoretical paper models LLM-guided search loops (propose, score, keep-if-better) as reversible Markov chains or diffusion limits, showing that verifier noise acts as an effective temperature parameterizing an exponential tilt of the mutation equilibrium, with the temperature scaling with verifier noise and minibatch size. It empirically tests these tilt predictions on LLM-guided program search. This provides a rare principled theory connecting verifier reliability to search dynamics.

entry.title: Benchmarking Machine Learning for Chaotic Three-Body Dynamics in Astrophysics

author.name: Sheng Wan, Pavan Vynatheya, Duo Xu, Li Kevin Wenliang, Ye Zhu

entry.summary: This paper constructs a hierarchy of learning tasks from chaotic gravitational three-body systems, covering stability classification and exact trajectory prediction near the stable/unstable boundary. It benchmarks general-purpose prediction algorithms and approaches building on physics foundation models using simulated triple-system trajectories.

entry.title: Accuracy Is Not Value: Choosing Weak Supervisors by What the Student Inherits

author.name: Romano Li, Xunfan Cai

entry.summary: The paper proves theoretically that a weak supervisor's value is determined by its errors after passing through the student's learning operator, so weighting supervisors by raw error inner products can be arbitrarily worse than optimal in relative excess risk. It identifies small finite-dimensional projections of the target that decide when training on weak aggregates helps and how to weight supervisors.

entry.title: Augmentron: Scalable Multi-View Visual Augmentation for Robot Learning

author.name: Tanay Tandon, Aseem Doriwala, Jade Choghari, Catherine Weaver, Pragna Mannam

entry.summary: Augmentron is a geometry-aware augmentation pipeline for robot learning that builds reusable scene representations and re-renders them through recorded camera poses, producing temporally and multi-view consistent visual variations while preserving the robot, task objects, and annotations. Replacing half of real training data across three physical manipulation tasks shows policy robustness gains. This addresses the inconsistency problems of naive per-frame generative augmentation in robotics.

entry.title: Calibrated Uncertainty Quantification on TDC ADMET: What Can Be Resolved Across 22 Datasets?

author.name: Laurits Fredsgaard, Michael Riis Andersen, Mikkel N. Schmidt

entry.summary: Systematically compares eleven calibrated uncertainty-quantification pipelines on the 22 Therapeutics Data Commons ADMET datasets using nested cross-validation across ten chemical partitions and five seeds, finding ensemble MC dropout best on average rank for performance, Brier score, and interval score. Provides practical guidance for ADMET modeling where predictions gate experimental testing.

entry.title: Representational drift in a code model: behaviour settles, which neurons carry it does not

author.name: Piotr Wilam

entry.summary: Measures an analogue of neuroscience representational drift in OpenCoder-1.5B during pretraining across two trillion tokens, finding that for grammar-fixed constructs the loss floors within the first 4% of training while reliance on specific neurons grows throughout and the identity of carrying neurons never settles. Uses ablation-based noise units at fine checkpoint granularity.

entry.title: From Procedures to Permissions: Learning Precise Subagent Authorization from Agent Skills

author.name: Wenkai Yu, Ning Ding, Wentao Zhang, Yehui Tang

entry.summary: The paper proposes learning fine-grained tool and workspace permissions for delegated subagents from Agent Skills, which encode the procedural operations, tools, and files needed at each step. This addresses the gap that existing multi-agent systems lack direct specification of the resources each subtask requires, using skills as supervision for authorization.

entry.title: Compaction, decay and reinforcement in a two-tier conversational memory: a paired evaluation against retrieval-augmented generation

author.name: Osamudiamen Edogun, Joshua Obigwe, Irfan Mehmood

entry.summary: Rigorously compares compacting conversation turns into atomic facts against transcript-based RAG on LoCoMo, using a paired design over 1,985 questions that enables McNemar's exact test. Compaction leads by 6.8 points on four comparable categories with 34% fewer prompt tokens, though the lead narrows to a non-significant 2.0 points on the full five-category set.

entry.title: Left-Right-Consistent Iterative Stereo Matching via Cross-Injection

author.name: Manuel Knott, Diogo Luvizon, Daniel Scharstein, Elias Vansteenkiste

entry.summary: The paper introduces cross-injection (CI), a lightweight add-on for pretrained left-only iterative stereo matching models that couples left and right disparity passes so the two maps agree. This addresses applications like per-eye AR/VR rendering and novel view synthesis where independent predictions are inconsistent, especially at occlusions and textureless regions. It can be applied to any pretrained iterative matcher.

entry.title: VICTR: Value-Informed In-Context Learning for Vision-Language-Action Models

author.name: Luca Macesanu, Tianluo Zhang, Aditya Patil, Archit Sharma, Kevin Angers, Christopher M. Clark, Chen Feng, Juexiao Zhang

entry.summary: VICTR enables in-context learning in vision-language-action models by retrieving demonstrations based on task progress rather than visual similarity alone, built around an In-Context Value Function Estimator. This improves the relevance of retrieved context for adapting robot behavior without fine-tuning.

entry.title: RevoSim: Scalable Multimodal Tactile Simulation for Dexterous Manipulation

author.name: Ke Zhang, Lixin Xu, Ziyi Wang, Xiyue Dong, Jie Tan, Lianghu Shao, Xianpeng Wang, Chuanyu Li, Renjing Xu

entry.summary: RevoSim is a high-fidelity multimodal tactile simulator for the BrainCo Revo3 hand that jointly models 285 piezoresistive taxels and five visuotactile fingertips, generating synchronized pressure, depth, RGB, and marker-displacement observations. It supports up to 4,096 parallel environments on a single RTX 5090 and trains in-hand manipulation and grasping policies entirely in simulation.

entry.title: Autonomous Whole-body Loco-manipulation Using a Snake Robot

author.name: Adarsh Salagame, Henry Noyes, Haroon Hublikar, Alireza Ramezani

entry.summary: This work demonstrates closed-loop loco-manipulation with the COBRA snake robot without decoupling locomotion and manipulation, allowing any part of the hyper-redundant body to make contact. It develops a contact-implicit dynamic model within a Moreau-Jean time-stepping framework and formulates a trajectory optimization approach.

entry.title: Pdb or Not to Be: Comparing Debugging Interfaces With Pass$_{X}$@$k$

author.name: Ryan Magnuson, Ellie Kitanidis, Ariel Lee

entry.summary: This study compares a debugger-only coding agent against a bash-only agent across all 500 SWE-bench Verified instances, holding the rest of the scaffold fixed to isolate the debugger's contribution. It introduces Pass_X@k evaluation metrics to assess whether interactive debugger access, which exposes live runtime state, improves agentic software engineering performance.

entry.title: CARGO: Causal Attribution and Responsibility-Guided Preventive Safe Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning for Cooperative Driving

author.name: Jingjia Teng, Yang Li, Wenjie Huang

entry.summary: CARGO is a multi-agent reinforcement learning framework for cooperative on-ramp merging in mixed traffic that estimates directed behavioral influence via a shared latent-context posterior, propagating uncertainty into interaction-edge selection. It combines signed influence with marginal team utility for reward shaping, assigns responsibility from excess tail risk relative to a safe reference policy, and uses conditional diffusion to generate future responses for risk estimation. Responsibility-guided preventive optimization then calibrates agent-specific risk reduction.

entry.title: Ontology-Driven Control of Conversational Agents with a Use-Case for Job Interview Practice

author.name: Barbara Gendron (LORIA, UL), Ga\"el Guibon (LIPN, LORIA), Mathieu D'aquin (LORIA, UL)

entry.summary: This paper proposes an ontology-based approach for designing conversational strategies in LLM-driven agents, controlling both response-level characteristics like tone and global conversational strategy. It demonstrates the method in a job interview practice use case, aiming to replace ad hoc, non-reusable adaptation techniques with transparent, structured control.

entry.title: Intent-Aware Caching for Efficient LLM Serving

author.name: Kazi Hasan Ibn Arif, JinYi Yoon, Dimitrios S. Nikolopoulos, Hans Vandierendonck, Deepu John, Bo Ji

entry.summary: This work observes that user intent predicts conversation continuation probability and inter-turn delay in multi-turn LLM workloads, and proposes Intent-Aware Caching (IAC), an online KV-cache eviction policy that classifies requests by intent. IAC improves cache hit rates and reduces redundant prefill computation in serving systems.

entry.title: PINNeval: A Comprehensive Evaluation Standard for Physics-Informed Neural Networks

author.name: Kevin von Bargen, Hamid Ebrahimy, Tim R\"omer

entry.summary: PINNeval proposes an integrated evaluation protocol for physics-informed neural networks, treating four pipeline components (domain adaptation, loss balancing, architecture, optimization) as a system rather than in isolation. It addresses the problem that many existing benchmarks use minimal defaults unrepresentative of current best practice.

entry.title: Goals as a Representational Layer for Human-AI Collaboration

author.name: Gaia Molinaro, Lev Tankelevitch, Sean Rintel, Scott Counts

entry.summary: This position paper argues that goals should become an explicit representational layer mediating interactions among people, AI systems, and organizations, since prompts rarely capture why a task is being pursued. It outlines requirements for such a layer: multidimensional, grounded in human articulation and inferred evidence, and continuously updated given goals' hierarchical and evolving nature.

entry.title: Ordered Policy Optimization

author.name: Dongkyu Derek Cho, Pan Xu

entry.summary: Ordered Policy Optimization (OPO) improves on PPO's fixed importance-ratio clipping by adapting the clipping radius to the reliability of the induced ratio distribution, controlling statistically harmful extreme ratios rather than checking each ratio against a fixed interval. The paper presents the method alongside a case study motivating distribution-level rather than sample-level ratio control.

entry.title: Failure Profiling and Reachable Trajectory Selection for Reasoning Distillation

author.name: Yijun Zhu, Jianxin Wang, Chengchao Shen

entry.summary: Proposes FPRT, a method for reasoning distillation that selects training trajectories jointly based on failure profiles and what a student model can actually reach, addressing overfitting to a teacher's output distribution. It argues that corrective trajectories reflecting teacher reasoning patterns fail to resolve the train-inference distribution mismatch.

entry.title: A Stochastic Latent Variable Generalization of Joint-Embedding Predictive Architectures

author.name: Nikos Giakoumoglou, Paschalis Giakoumoglou, Tania Stathaki

entry.summary: Presents S-JEPA, which realizes the auxiliary conditioning variable z in JEPA as a proper stochastic latent variable rather than a fixed deterministic token, using a learned posterior during training and a context-conditioned prior at inference to capture the multimodal distribution over plausible completions. The approach requires no decoders and no reconstruction.

entry.title: Robust Deep Prototype Classifiers via Lipschitz Training

author.name: Adia Khalid Khan, Lukas Gehring, Benjamin Paa{\ss}en

entry.summary: This paper addresses the problem that deep prototype-based classifiers (like Generalized Learning Vector Quantization) lose their closed-form robustness certificates when shallow prototypes are combined with deep embedding networks. The authors propose a Lipschitz-based training method to restore certified robustness while retaining the interpretability of prototype-based decisions. This matters because it reconnects interpretability and formal robustness guarantees, which typically trade off.

entry.title: Rethinking Data Selection as Distribution Matching on Semantic Manifolds

author.name: Peng Sun, Yi Yang, Mingshuo Chen, Chunxiao Li, Yao Zhu, Huawen Shen, Tianfan Fu

entry.summary: QMAC formulates instruction-tuning data selection as joint distribution matching and quality filtering, matching the empirical characteristic functions of the selected subset to the full dataset on semantic manifolds rather than relying on heuristic diversity/importance scores. This reduces cost and noise in fine-tuning LLMs and large vision-language models. Reframing data selection as distribution matching is a cleaner formulation than prevailing heuristics.

entry.title: Interpretable Multifidelity Learning with Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks for Spatiotemporal Nuclear Reactor Flow Modeling

author.name: Meredith Eaheart, Majdi I. Radaideh

entry.summary: The paper compares black-box multifidelity neural networks with interpretable multifidelity Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks (MFKANs) for predicting spatiotemporal mass flow across all 193 fuel assemblies of a pressurized water reactor core. It explores how much expensive high-fidelity CFD data can be replaced by low-fidelity data in a challenging weak-correlation regime.

entry.title: MotionBench-XAI: Benchmarking What Shapes Shapley Explanations in Spatiotemporal Machine Learning

author.name: Mathilde Papillon, Louisa Cornelis, Nina Miolane

entry.summary: This benchmark systematically studies how methodological choices in Shapley computation — what counts as a player, imputation of absent players, and game evaluation — affect explanation quality for spatiotemporal models, using synthetic data with ground-truth attributions and applications such as Parkinson's severity from human motion.

entry.title: Action-Centered Causal Bandits for Budget-Constrained Promotion Targeting

author.name: Yifan Lin, Kaixu Yang, Di Mo

entry.summary: This paper formulates platform promotion targeting as a budget-constrained contextual bandit with heterogeneous treatment effects and proposes DR-CATE-CBwK, an action-centered causal bandit that learns treatment contrasts directly. It combines an offline doubly robust learner for warm-starting with an online sequential contrast estimator whose update remains valid even under baseline-model misspecification. This matters for practitioners allocating costly interventions across users under global budget constraints.

entry.title: Practical Non-Stationary Graph Gaussian Processes

author.name: K. S. Sesh Kumar, Viacheslav Borovitskiy

entry.summary: Introduces Variance-Coupled Gaussian Processes (VCGPs) for graphs, where a positive auxiliary signal modulates node interactions via a single learned coupling exponent, controlling whether high-variability nodes propagate or attenuate information, with a cluster-wise extension for heterogeneous regimes. This offers a principled, parameter-efficient way to model non-stationary network data with uncertainty estimation.

entry.title: Future-Informed Actor-Critic

author.name: Samy Mokeddem, Gaspard Lambrechts, Adrien Bolland, Damien Ernst

entry.summary: Extends actor-critic methods by introducing the future-informed value function, which can be conditioned on both exogenous and endogenous features of future states, actions, and rewards, unlike prior work restricted to action-independent features. Derives the future-informed policy gradient and builds an actor-critic algorithm aiming to improve sample efficiency and credit assignment.

entry.title: Solver-Free Decision-Focused Learning via Neural Optimization Layers for Edge Selection

author.name: Xinda Zheng, Frits de Nijs, Edward Lam

entry.summary: Proposes a solver-free decision-focused learning framework for NP-hard edge-selection problems under uncertain objective/constraint parameters, training a neural optimization layer without solution labels and then freezing it to train a prediction model through its continuous output. Avoids the costly solver calls and optimal-solution labels required by many decision-focused approaches.

entry.title: One Run Is Not Enough: A Monte Carlo Protocol for Evaluating LLM Reliability on Data Science Tasks

author.name: Wenqi Ni, Ozan Evkaya, Miguel de Carvalho

entry.summary: Introduces DS-QA, a benchmark of 100 data science and statistics questions drawn from UK university courses, spanning 16 datasets and three difficulty levels, plus a three-layer evaluation framework. The protocol emphasizes reliability across repeated runs, task types, and difficulty levels rather than single-run accuracy, addressing an underexplored consistency dimension in LLM evaluation.

entry.title: Extending Grid Foundation Models for Phasor-Domain Dynamic Simulation

author.name: Boyang Zhao, Yifan Zhou, Alban Puech, Tilman Bockhacker, Hendrik Hamann

entry.summary: Introduces DynGridFM, extending grid foundation models from steady-state analysis to dynamic power grid simulation using component-wise tokenization and a structured latent operator, with transfer to unseen grids. Achieves 924x-1232x speedup over numerical simulators and strong few-shot adaptation on a held-out 48-machine grid.

entry.title: Coresets for Capacitated Clustering via Dual Concentration

author.name: Milind Prabhu, Chris Schwiegelshohn, Sudarshan Shyam, Erik Waingarten

entry.summary: This theory paper studies coresets for capacitated k-median and k-means clustering, where cluster-size constraints must be respected. The authors derive optimal-size coresets for finite metric spaces, matching known bounds and advancing the understanding of coreset complexity in the capacitated setting.

entry.title: Multilingual Artificial Datasets for AI-Driven Cardiology: the CliTe and ParaCliTe corpora

author.name: Lorenzo Pratesi, Eulalia Farre-Maduell, Machteld Boonstra, Michele Miranda, Jonas Mack, Eduard Rodenas-Alesina, Jonathan Kossoff, Corinne Allaart, S\'ebastien Brati\`eres, Manuela-Daniela Danu, Isabella Fumarulo, Milou Gamage, Antonio Iaconelli, Pavel Leinveber, Felix Lindberg, Pavel Mach\'a\v{c}, Vladim\'ira Mac\'ikov\'a, Gianluigi Savarese, Raffaele Scorza, Bram van Es, Emma Weiss, Andrea Guala, Martin Krallinger, the DataTools4Heart NLP group

entry.summary: Releases three multilingual artificial cardiology corpora (CliTe and ParaCliTe) created by cardiologists at 7 European hospitals in 7 languages, following privacy-safe corpus construction guidelines. Provides clinically validated, sex-balanced clinical records to enable trustworthy NLP for cardiology where real data is hard to share.

entry.title: The APL Doesn't Fall Far From The Tree: Unsupervised Artefact Prototype Learning in Histopathology

author.name: Emilia Agasi, Charlie Gourley, C. Simon Herrington, Robert L. Hollis, T. Ian Simpson

entry.summary: Artefact Prototype Learning (APL) detects technical artefacts in histopathology whole-slide images by exploiting the geometry of pre-trained embedding spaces without manual labels or fine-tuning. It computes prototypes of out-of-distribution patches to separate artefact patterns from tissue, outperforming GrandQC and HistoART on artefacts like blur and pen marks while struggling with tissue-like artefacts.

entry.title: UniMore: Fine-Grained Supervision for Unified Understanding and Generation

author.name: Haoyue Bai, Yinyi Luo, Yicheng He, Qingsong Wen, Sharon Li, Jindong Wang

entry.summary: UniMore is a post-training method for unified multimodal models that exploits paired image-text supervision to fix a loss of specificity: generated images with wrong attributes and captions lacking distinguishing details. It derives complementary fine-grained learning tasks for both understanding and generation directions.

entry.title: Lodos: A Lightweight Simulator Designed for Contact-Rich Interactions with Detailed Meshes

author.name: Onur Beker, Andreas Ren\'e Geist, Georg Martius

entry.summary: Lodos is a massively parallel rigid-body simulator focused on contact-rich interactions using detailed mesh-mesh collisions rather than coarse primitive approximations, supporting RL, stochastic optimal control, and trajectory optimization research. It is the predecessor system that Lodos-v2 improves upon.

entry.title: Extended Model-Based Learned Inertial Odometry

author.name: Sasanka Kuruppu Arachchige, Joni-Kristian K\"am\"ar\"ainen

entry.summary: The authors improve learned inertial odometry for agile quadrotor flight by adopting a body-frame representation and incorporating body-frame torque dynamics, addressing poor generalization to unseen trajectories. A learned model predicts short-horizon relative displacements that are fused with IMU measurements in an Extended Kalman Filter.

entry.title: What do LLMs Really Learn About Model Weights? A Stratification Approach to Examine Weight Space Programming

author.name: CCaptainX

entry.summary: The author replicates Takehi et al's 2026 weight-space programming result with two reasoning models, GPT-6 Astra and DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, asking them to identify a trained model's task from its weights, then applies stratification tests (removing channel labels, using only the first layer, or small random weight subsets) to distinguish genuine weight-reading from metadata shortcuts. Astra's performance survives stratification while Flash's degrades sharply, suggesting Flash relies on prompt metadata.

entry.title: AlterNet: Adaptive-Depth Mixture-of-Experts with Learned Halting for Elastic Inference

author.name: Alexander Kastius

entry.summary: AlterNet combines Mixture-of-Experts with shallow experts and a dynamic-depth mechanism using learned halting, letting a model decide how much compute each forward pass needs and scale compute down after training without retraining. It introduces sequence-level depth routing, a depth encoding for tracking progress, and regularization to support elastic inference.

entry.title: RAG-Enhanced LLMs for Interactive Explainability in Clinical Decision Support Systems

author.name: Lorenzo Mannocci, Francesca Naretto, Lucia Passaro, Anna Monreale

entry.summary: This paper proposes a clinical decision support framework combining RAG-enhanced LLMs with XAI methods to produce natural-language explanations with source traceability, addressing hallucination and unverifiable explanations in high-stakes healthcare settings. The system bridges complex predictive models and domain experts through interactive, grounded explanations. Evaluation focuses on explanation quality and faithfulness to retrieved sources.

entry.title: Relic and Gumi: Governing Memory, Safety, and Continuity in Diegetic Relational Agents

author.name: Daniele Veri'

entry.summary: The paper presents Relic, a governance architecture for longitudinal relational (companion) agents, and Gumi, a subject-specific companion governed through it. Relic separates observability, researcher review, agent memory, and agent output, representing sensitive safety signals as researcher-facing governance objects and organizing shared continuity memory around subject-confirmed wording and corrections.

entry.title: FoleyForge: Free-form, Controllable, Rectified-flow Editing of Sound Effects

author.name: Giovana Morais, Hugo Flores Garc\'ia, Prem Seetharaman, Johannes Imort, Justin Salamon, Magdalena Fuentes, Oriol Nieto

entry.summary: FoleyForge is a generative model for instruction-based editing of sound effects, handling semantic, stylistic, and DSP-like edits from free-form instructions while preserving input identity. It addresses the audio editing data gap with an automated pipeline for authoring training edits and fine-tunes a rectified-flow audio model with tunable attribute controls.

entry.title: FondueQA: A Benchmark for Evaluating Parametric Compensation in Multi-Hop QA

author.name: Laurin Schmid, Suman Navaratnarajah, Koel Dutta Chowdhury, Steffen Eger, Josif Grabocka, Christian Frey

entry.summary: Introduces FondueQA, a multi-hop QA benchmark where each required fact is uniquely localized to designated evidence, enabling controlled study of how models compensate for incomplete retrieval with parametric knowledge while controlling for benchmark contamination and memorization. It distinguishes genuine parametric knowledge from memorized benchmark instances.

entry.title: Not All Entropy Is Equal: Reward-Conditioned Entropy Allocation in Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards

author.name: Song Yu, Li Li, Zhenming Wu

entry.summary: This paper argues that global token entropy is an ambiguous diagnostic for RLVR because it conflates uncertainty in successful versus failed trajectories, diversity across correct strategies, and variation among realizations of one strategy. It introduces Reward-Conditioned Entropy Allocation (RCEA), a hierarchical diagnostic framework that separates trajectory from token entropy and conditions uncertainty on verifier outcomes. This provides sharper tools for understanding exploration and collapse in reasoning RL.

entry.title: V-STORM: A Structure-Aware Grounded Chain of Thought Dataset for Faithful and Fine-Grained Spatio-Temporal Video Reasoning

author.name: Dian Jiao, Yuqian Yuan, Jiaqi Zhu, Mingjian Gao, Siwen Tan, Yunqi Cao, Jinhui Li, Sijing Li, Zhenxuan Fan, Haoyang Wang, Wenqiao Zhang, Siliang Tang

entry.summary: V-STORM presents a framework that transforms videos into Spatio-Temporal Scene Graphs and derives grounded chains of thought from validated evidence paths, making each reasoning step traceable to verifiable spatio-temporal evidence. This provides granular, verifiable supervision for fine-grained video reasoning where multimodal LLMs currently struggle with when-and-where grounding. As a dataset and pipeline contribution it could become a useful resource for training and evaluating video reasoning models.

entry.title: MEDALLION: Manifold Embedding Distillation and Attributions for Low-dimensional Latent InterpretatiON

author.name: Vicky Jung, Claire M. He, Irene Chang, Genevera I. Allen

entry.summary: MEDALLION interprets black-box dimensionality reduction embeddings such as t-SNE and UMAP by distilling them into a neural encoder and applying feature attribution methods to identify which original features drive low-dimensional structure. Demonstrations on MNIST and single-cell transcriptomics show practical value for scientific discovery workflows.

entry.title: StreamTab: Training-Free Temporal Link Prediction with Tabular Foundation Models

author.name: Mingqi Yang, Renqi Wu

entry.summary: StreamTab is a training-free framework for temporal link prediction built on a frozen tabular foundation model pretrained on synthetic tables. It represents candidate node pairs via statistics of past interactions and in-context recent observations, avoiding per-graph training required by temporal GNNs. This demonstrates that tabular foundation models can transfer to temporal graph tasks without fine-tuning.

entry.title: The Cost of Coverage: Conformalising Native Forecast Uncertainty for GB Wind Power

author.name: Carl Somers

entry.summary: Applies conformal prediction to native wind-power forecast uncertainty bands at two Great Britain wind farms, comparing six forecasters from ARIMA to a tabular foundation model. It shows calibration repairs marginal coverage cheaply but masks under-coverage in high winds, and regime-wise calibration cuts day-ahead out-of-band volume in high winds by over 40 percent.

entry.title: Finite-sample Calibration Guarantees for Binary Segmentation

author.name: Bruno Viti, Martin Holler

entry.summary: Develops a post-hoc calibration method for binary segmentation with formal finite-sample calibration guarantees derived from concentration inequalities, addressing the miscalibration common in high-stakes applications like medical imaging. Provides high-probability bounds on calibration error rather than empirical calibration alone.

entry.title: MARS: Training Multilingual Search Agents for Retriever-Free Evidence Acquisition

author.name: Rui Qi, Yunlong Liang, Yufeng Chen, Jinan Xu, Fandong Meng, Kaiyu Huang

entry.summary: MARS trains a multilingual search agent via reinforcement learning to interact directly with raw corpora through executable shell commands, removing dependence on learned retrievers and similarity ranking. It introduces corpus-interaction-aware supervision to address sensitivity of exact search to entity surface forms and the weak guidance of outcome-only rewards in multi-turn search.

entry.title: On Seeding Watermarks to Detect Verbatim LLM Copy-Paste Responses

author.name: Aizierjiang Aiersilan, Artin Yousefi, Robert Pless

entry.summary: Proposes an input-side watermark where educators embed invisible instructions in assignment prompts so verbatim LLM answers can be detected, avoiding unreliable post-hoc AI-text detectors and the need for model-provider cooperation. Directly targets the common academic case of students submitting chatbot replies unmodified.

entry.title: MetricPose: Flexible 3D Human Pose Estimation with Depth and Geometric Cues

author.name: Shifan Zhu, Sabad Modi, Hang Yang, Arushi Agrawal, Steven Gao, Meghan Huber, Nathan Wycoff, Donghyun Kim

entry.summary: MetricPose predicts metrically accurate 3D human joint positions in camera coordinates by combining learned RGB priors, direct depth measurements, and geometric constraints like ground contact to resolve the scale-distance ambiguity inherent in monocular images. It extends a pretrained full-body estimator with optional depth and geometry-processing modules.

entry.title: Keyline Detection with YOLO: Runway Perception for Vision-Based Aircraft Landing

author.name: Leander Fritsch, David R\"ugamer, Alexej Klushyn

entry.summary: The paper proposes object keyline detection, a new task of predicting a semantically ordered set of infinite lines per object instance, more robust to occlusion and truncation than keypoints. The authors extend YOLO with keyline prediction parameterized in Hesse-normal form and apply it to runway perception for vision-based aircraft landing. This line-level analog of keypoints offers a complementary geometric representation for safety-critical perception.

entry.title: Seeing What Matters: Benchmarking Task-Conditioned Actionable Spatial Belief for Manipulation

author.name: Yina Jian, Mingkun Xu

entry.summary: This benchmark evaluates whether embodied agents acquire the specific visual evidence needed to execute a manipulation command, rather than merely describing scenes, across three simulated tabletop domains with 860 frozen evaluation cases and over 115,000 evaluator episodes. It formalizes task-conditioned actionable spatial belief as a distinct capability from generic spatial reasoning.

entry.title: HOC2R: Hand-Object Contact Trajectories for Human-to-Robot Motion Transfer

author.name: Hongkun Yu, Francisco M. L\'opez, Francisco Cruz

entry.summary: HOC2R extracts hand-object contact trajectories from human videos to enable robot motion transfer, combining frozen DINOv3 and SAM 2.1 features with learned heads for hand-object association and contact localization. It offers count-aware automation for untrimmed videos and a fixed-two mode for two-finger grippers, improving contact-count accuracy from 58.1% to 71.4% over an adapted VRB2 baseline.

entry.title: Locating Contact on Tendon-Driven Continuum Robots From Tendon Measurements Alone via Constrained Moving Horizon Estimation

author.name: Haitham El-Hussieny

entry.summary: The paper proves that external contact along a tendon-driven continuum robot is fundamentally unobservable from motor-side tendon measurements alone, since the contact-to-measurement map has a null space of dimension at least seven. It then shows that with known obstacle geometry, non-penetration and complementarity conditions restore local identifiability, and presents a real-time constrained moving horizon estimator that exploits these constraints to locate contact.

entry.title: Decision Context: Persistent Behavioral Learning for AI Agents

author.name: Nima Vahdat, Pashootan Vaezipoor

entry.summary: Forge Decision Context (forge_dc) is a system that lets LLM agents learn from user corrections and self-assessed tool-call failures across sessions by compiling behavioral signals into imperative RULE directives injected at relevant decision points. It is evaluated on DC-Bench, a new 71-scenario benchmark built from real agent traces in a deterministic mocked-tool environment, against four predecessor approaches.

entry.title: Learning Whom to Trust About the Unseen: Source Credibility and Reliability Transfer in Language Models

author.name: Ruijia Guan

entry.summary: Three behavioral studies across six models investigate how far demonstrated source reliability transfers in language models when new claims cannot be verified, adapting human cognitive-science paradigms like the Einstein effect. Notably, models favor a spiritual leader over a scientist for obscure statements - unlike humans - with preferences shifting dramatically when statements are reworded in physics vocabulary, though they reproduce some human domain asymmetries.

entry.title: Model-based learning for DoA estimation and array calibration via continuous sparse recovery

author.name: Baptiste Chatelier (IETR, INSA Rennes), Jos\'e Miguel Mateos-Ramos (MERCE-France), Vincent Corlay (MERCE-France), Matthieu Crussi\`ere (INSA Rennes, IETR), Christian H\"ager (BGU), Henk Wymeersch (BGU), Nir Shlezinger (BGU), Luc Le Magoarou (INSA Rennes, IETR)

entry.summary: The paper introduces a joint array calibration and direction-of-arrival estimation method based on simultaneous orthogonal matching pursuit, following the model-based machine learning paradigm for ISAC systems. It calibrates antenna arrays with severe gain-phase and antenna location impairments using projected gradient updates within a continuous sparse recovery formulation. This addresses hardware impairments long neglected in classical DoA estimation but critical for integrated sensing and communication.

entry.title: Challenges, Opportunities, and Misconceptions in Neurosymbolic AI

author.name: Giuseppe Marra (LPI), Pierre Genev\`es (CNRS, LIG, TYREX), Meghyn Bienvenu (LaBRI), Thomas Schiex (MIAT INRAE), Sylvie Thi\'ebaux (Comue de Toulouse, ANU), Silviu Maniu (SLIDE, LIG)

entry.summary: This position paper examines the future of neurosymbolic AI as neural models grow more capable, focusing on efficiency, safety, and interpretability. It identifies semantic alignment between neural and symbolic components and the cost of symbolic inference as core challenges, and debunks misconceptions about differentiability, independence assumptions, and scalability.

entry.title: Atik: A Shared-Mesh Transformer Accelerator for RISC-V

author.name: Ahmed Zeer, Erkan Uslu

entry.summary: Atik is an open-source RoCC accelerator for RocketChip that executes matrix multiplication and dense attention on a single shared fixed-point MAC mesh with a streaming online-softmax schedule that avoids materializing the full score matrix. It is validated cycle-by-cycle on FireSim across 137 tests with zero output mismatches and reports Sky130 physical-design area.

entry.title: What to Delegate, What to Preserve: Human Preferences for Agentic AI Across Everyday Life and Work

author.name: Sarah Wheeler, Veronica Rammouz, Yaoyao Qian, Zexuan Liu, Mengyi Wei, Anthony Rios, Tianzhi He, Kyrie Zhou

entry.summary: A scenario-based survey of 289 U.S. adults across 45 use cases in nine life domains measuring automation preference, trust, collaboration, privacy concern, and willingness to pay for AI agents. Findings show trust, desired AI leadership, prior AI use, and anticipated savings predict delegation preference, while concerns over replacing human judgment suppress it, with large variation across domains.

entry.title: VoluCompose: Constructing Compact Volumetric Visual Representations for Medical Image Understanding

author.name: Zanting Ye, Yunrui Lin, Shengyuan Liu, Jing Hao, Chen Hu, Yefeng Zheng, Lijun Lu

entry.summary: VoluCompose is a training-free, model-agnostic framework that compresses volumetric medical images for vision-language models by decoupling content selection from token budget allocation. It uses a hyperbolic token composition module with Lorentz distance to group contiguous slices and allocate tokens, reducing redundancy from hundreds of slices.

entry.title: Training-Free Active Test-Time Adaptation for Vision-Language Models

author.name: Jihwan Bang, Sumyeong Ahn, Hwanjun Song, Jae-Gil Lee

entry.summary: Studies an intermediate regime between fully unsupervised and supervised test-time adaptation for vision-language models, where a fixed labeling budget can be spent on selected test samples while predictions must be emitted before labels arrive. The method is training-free, sidestepping the restriction that models must repair their own uncertain predictions without external evidence.

entry.title: AudioSphere: Towards Self-Supervised Spatial Audio Representation Models

author.name: Goksenin Yuksel, Marcel van Gerven, Kiki van der Heijden

entry.summary: Introduces AudioSphere, a multi-channel masked autoencoder trained on Ambisonics recordings that learns joint acoustic and spatial features via patch-level spatial self-supervision, reconstructing both spectral content and directional cues. It bridges the gap between audio embedding models blind to spatial structure and spatial audio models unsuited to frame-level tasks like sound event detection and localization.

entry.title: HiMEM: Hippocampus-Inspired Memory Consolidation, Pruning, and Composition for Vision-Language-Action Models in 3D Scenes

author.name: Boran Zhao, Yanbin Hu, Jun Ye, Zhenxian Hu, Yuxin Zhai, Jin Cui, Pengju Ren

entry.summary: HiMEM introduces a hippocampus-inspired memory mechanism for vision-language-action models in 3D scenes, consolidating noisy episodic memories into compact semantic memories that capture generalizable manipulation principles. This enables better long-horizon task execution and cross-task generalization by pruning redundant scene- and robot-specific details. The bio-inspired framing applied to robot memory systems is a creative contribution to embodied AI.

entry.title: ROSE: Risk-Aware Orthogonal Subspace Navigation for Lifelong Knowledge Editing in Multimodal Large Language Models

author.name: Lingyun Song, Ziyao Chen, Kang Pan, Xiaolin Han, Yifei Zhang, Xiaoqi Wang, Yudai Pan, Xuequn Shang

entry.summary: ROSE is a framework for lifelong knowledge editing in multimodal LLMs that restricts sequential edits to the orthogonal complement of previously edited subspaces and uses a dynamically computed risk mask to protect specific factual parameters. This targets the twin problems of locality erosion and catastrophic forgetting in continual model updating. It matters because keeping deployed multimodal models factually current without degrading capabilities is a pressing practical need.

entry.title: How Small Can We Go? Calibrating Activation-Cache Compression for SAE Training

author.name: Abraham Yeung

entry.summary: This paper empirically studies how compressing the massive activation caches needed to train sparse autoencoders affects resulting features, using a frozen-SAE test and a retraining test. Findings are striking: on a GPT-2 cache, fp16 rounding retains 60.6% of features while a perturbation eight orders of magnitude smaller retains only 70.5%, indicating no clear retention scale.

entry.title: Global Solar Siting from Geospatial Embeddings

author.name: Abdullah Rehman, Quentin Paletta, Rui Song

entry.summary: The paper uses geospatial foundation model embeddings to learn latent solar site suitability from 38,591 existing solar installations, replacing hand-picked geophysical layers used in multi-criteria decision analysis. This offers a geographically transferable approach to global solar plant siting with implications for renewable energy planning.

entry.title: Learning to Restart: Differentiable Restart Policies for Optimization Dynamics

author.name: Yiman Fong, Zhonglin Xie, Zaiwen Wen

entry.summary: The paper develops a differentiable framework for learning adaptive restart policies in accelerated first-order optimization, overcoming the non-differentiability of discrete restart events via their continuous-time limit and surrogate gradients. This replaces hand-designed restart rules with learned ones.

entry.title: When Can You Trust Neural Critics? Auditing Mutual Information Estimates of Higher-Order Epistasis in Protein Language Models

author.name: Maryam Rahimimovassagh, Waldemar Karwowski, Niloofar Yousefi

entry.summary: This audit examines a prior neural mutual-information study of epistasis in ESM-2 on the GB1 protein landscape, finding run-to-run differences comparable to ordinary seed variability and substantial sensitivity to evaluation pairing schemes. It evaluates alternative estimator families for stability and uses synthetic calibrations across representation dimensionalities. The work provides important methodological scrutiny of variational MI estimation in probing neural representations.

entry.title: Safety-Focused Reinforcement Learning Using Risk-Sensitive Coupled Control

author.name: Jiabin Lin, Shana Moothedath, Vivek S. Borkar

entry.summary: Proposes a coupled control approach to safe reinforcement learning that transforms constrained optimization into a risk-sensitive problem with an average reward criterion, preventing entry into unsafe states while optimizing average cost. A two-timescale Q-learning algorithm is derived to solve the reformulated problem.

entry.title: k-Volume: a Unified Active Learning Strategy

author.name: Eliot Tron, Alain Celisse, Christophe Denis, Alice Le Brigant

entry.summary: Introduces k-Volume, an active learning strategy for classification that samples according to the volume of the smallest ball containing a point's k nearest neighbors, unifying density, diversity, and uncertainty properties depending on input/output space use. Proves asymptotic equivalence to uniform sampling over the data support and validates on synthetic and real tabular data.

entry.title: Coordinatewise Epsilon for Adam under Heavy-Tailed Noise

author.name: Jeonseong Kim, Chenglin Fan

entry.summary: Analyzes how Adam's shared scalar epsilon affects convergence when noise and curvature vary across coordinates, showing that coordinatewise epsilon choices attain the optimal heavy-tailed l1-stationarity rate O(T^-(p-1)/(3p-2)), while any predictable shared epsilon admits a lower bound of order Omega(T^-(p-1)/(2p)). Provides theory directly relevant to the ubiquitous Adam optimizer.

entry.title: Online Causal Configuration for Networked Systems via Doubly Robust Steady-State Learning

author.name: Yuli Liu, Zhiheng Zhang

entry.summary: Introduces CAUSAL-UCB, which selects configurations of networked systems using optimistic bounds on target causal values, recognizing that exploratory rewards may fail to identify a configuration's no-exploration value due to action-law mismatch and steady-state context shifts. An interference-aware clipped doubly robust evaluator yields predecision certificates separating statistical variation from identification, transport, and temporal-dependence errors.

entry.title: Fixed-point acceleration on Neural Wasserstein manifolds

author.name: Vitalii Aksenov, Sebastian Gutierrez Hernandez

entry.summary: Proposes fixed-point acceleration for optimization over probability measures represented as neural pushforwards, interpreting natural gradient descent on the induced pullback Wasserstein metric as a fixed-point iteration and accelerating it with Riemannian Anderson mixing that approximates second-order information without Hessians. Applicable to a range of ML problems involving optimization over distributions.

entry.title: GenStrain: Multi-Conditional Generative Diffusion Model To Synthesize High-quality Motion and Strain Maps From Cardiac Magnetic Resonance Images

author.name: Rishov Paul, Sona Ghadimi, Cristiane C. Singulane, Amit R. Patel, Frederick H. Epstein, Miaomiao Zhang

entry.summary: Presents GenStrain, a conditional diffusion model synthesizing cardiac strain maps from routinely collected cine CMR images, avoiding both the sparse-feature limits of registration-based motion estimation and the extra acquisitions required by DENSE CMR. This could bring gold-standard strain assessment into standard clinical workflows.

entry.title: Enabling Retraining-Free Accurate Inference in Analog Compute in Memory Accelerators

author.name: George Karfakis, Puneet Gupta

entry.summary: Enables pretrained models to run accurately on analog compute-in-memory accelerators without costly hardware-aware retraining, exploiting the fact that layer representation on the array can be changed offline without changing the computation. Input centering and Hadamard rotations designed for analog arrays mitigate converter and device errors under shared calibration.

entry.title: VLA Handover: Failure-Prediction-Based Switching from On-Robot to Server VLA Models

author.name: Takayuki Nishio

entry.summary: Proposes VLA handover: a robot runs a small VLA locally and switches to a large server-side VLA only when local failure is predicted, formulated as cost minimization under a required success probability with a heuristic that retrains neither model. Demonstrated in simulation with SmolVLA and pi-0.5 on LIBERO tasks.

entry.title: GeoJeV: Unified Spatial Probability for Training-Free Efficient Evidence Acquisition in Ultra-High-Resolution Remote Sensing

author.name: Xinyi Niu, Lingfeng Chen, Jiehua Zhang, Panhe Hu, Li Liu, Zhen Liu, Yongxiang Liu

entry.summary: GeoJeV is a training-free method that reformulates evidence acquisition in ultra-high-resolution remote sensing as spatial probability-driven region selection, avoiding reliance on generative MLLM search control and repeated autoregressive decoding. This yields faster and more relevant region-level evidence for multimodal understanding of large remote sensing images.

entry.title: CoMET: Tracking the Shared Pose Error of Roadside Messages for Asynchronous Vehicle-Infrastructure Cooperative 3D Detection

author.name: Shuwei Sun, Jian Huang, Hui Cao

entry.summary: CoMET estimates shared translation errors in roadside-to-vehicle cooperative 3D detection using only decision-time information, per-sender Kalman filtering over matched vehicle-roadside detection pairs. It handles the substantial fraction of messages (38% at zero added delay) with no matched pairs by tracking the common-mode pose offset over time on V2X-Seq.

entry.title: Video Stitching from Multiple Moving Cameras

author.name: Shira Ifergane, Roy Amoyal, Shahar Benishay, Oren Freifeld

entry.summary: MViS is a lightweight test-time optimization framework for joint geometric alignment of video from multiple freely moving cameras with temporal consistency, removing the two-camera or fixed-ordering restrictions of prior stitching methods. It uses a spatial-transformer-inspired network to predict per-view, per-time homographies, optimized in geometry-guided and appearance-based stages. This generalizes video stitching to unconstrained multi-camera settings.

entry.title: AnimWeb-Bench: Benchmarking Animated Webpage Code Generation from Videos

author.name: Zhongyi Zhang, Jingyu Xiao, Shuqing Li, Michael R. Lyu

entry.summary: AnimWeb-Bench is the first benchmark for generating animated webpage code from videos, comprising 124 real-world webpages across 7 domains and 33 animation types, with a human-aligned evaluation metric. It fills a gap left by static-screenshot code generation benchmarks and tests MLLMs and coding agents on a pervasive but unstudied capability.

entry.title: Horizon-Coupled Obstacle Guidance for Relative-Action Diffusion Policies

author.name: Guangyuan Wang, Haishan Xia, Zitao Zhang, Kejia Chen, Yuanchen Sun, Zhenguo Sun, Donghao Zhang, Yu Zhang, Alois Knoll
