Using a pre-registered protocol with CMA-ES and random search over 1,560 PPO runs plus 340 evaluation runs, the authors show a searched reward generalizes to a held-out task and beats task-only PPO, episodic novelty, and random-search baselines, while also probing its vulnerability to tampering exploits. The pre-registration and scale of the study are notable for RL reward-search research.

entry.title: Positional Encoding is All You Need for Scalable Equivariance Constraint Relaxation

author.name: Hagay Michaeli, Haggai Maron, Daniel Soudry

entry.summary: The paper shows that equivariance constraint relaxation, previously done with costly non-equivariant dense layers, can be achieved simply by relaxing positional encoding. This avoids the significant computational overhead of dense relaxation layers while retaining the optimization benefits and test-time strict equivariance.

entry.title: Empirical Bayes Flow Matching for Continuous Cryo-EM Heterogeneity

author.name: Daniel Aibinder, Azmi Haider, Dan Rosenbaum

entry.summary: EB-FM learns a flow matching generative prior over 3D molecular structures directly from noisy 2D cryo-EM projection images, using a Monte Carlo stochastic approximation EM framework that alternates guided flow-based posterior sampling with prior updates. It targets continuous heterogeneity, where structures are never directly observed.

entry.title: PianoBench: Evaluating Musical Perception and Reasoning in Language Models

author.name: Louis Bradshaw, Irmak Bukey, Daniel Chenyu Lin, John Thickstun, Chris Donahue

entry.summary: PianoBench evaluates whether multimodal language models can perceive and reason about specific musical features, testing models on congruent acoustic and symbolic representations of piano performances. It is derived from a new 20,000-hour dataset of interleaved transcripts of music and spoken commentary from instructional piano videos. Results show open-weight audio-language models reach at most 52.8% accuracy, barely above a no-audio control, while frontier chain-of-thought models do substantially better, revealing a large perception gap.

entry.title: What Remains in Sight? Autoregressive Video Decoding as Representation-Guided Context Rewriting

author.name: Lixuan He, Jihyeon Je, Yang You, Leonidas Guibas

entry.summary: The paper proposes ReCR, a training-free method that makes context selection in autoregressive video generation an explicit test-time decision, treating decoding as representation-guided context rewriting. Rather than relying on fixed windows or compressed caches, ReCR decides which past frames or segments the decoder should see at each step.

entry.title: Feeling of Knowing in Large Language Models

author.name: Zichuan Fu, Xian Wu, Jingtong Gao, Wenlin Zhang, Jiaxuan Li, Binhao Wang, Yimin Deng, Guojing Li, Xiaopeng Li, Derong Xu, Yefeng Zheng, Xiangyu Zhao

entry.summary: Studies knowledge-judgment desynchronization after post-training updates in LLMs through a functional feeling-of-knowing (FoK) channel that judges the model's current knowledge state without implying subjective experience. It proposes training a knowledge channel and a FoK channel via on-policy SFT, knowledge-delta FoK training across intermediate knowledge states, and FoK-guided policy optimization to support selective generation, retrieval triggering, and model routing.

entry.title: Regret-based Characterization, Information Limits, and the Sample Complexity of Auditing Adaptive Policies

author.name: Irene Aldridge

entry.summary: This paper decomposes the value of adaptivity in MDPs as a sum of covariances between Q-values and action distributions, showing that an MDP's adaptivity gap is bounded by the information its policy uses. It derives information-theoretic limits and sample complexity results for auditing adaptive policies from bandit-feedback logs, and warns that audits based on immediate costs alone can have the wrong sign.

entry.title: Holistic Parallel Supervision for Expressive Speech to Speech Translation

author.name: Hao Zhang, Ismail Rasim Ulgen, Bismarck Bamfo Odoom, Rui Liu, Zihan Zhang, Berrak Sisman, Philipp Koehn

entry.summary: The paper introduces a training-data construction strategy for expressive speech-to-speech translation that combines professional dubbing, aligning content, prosody, timing, and speaker identity, with multilingual voice conversion to reduce speaker mismatch. It also presents DirectS2ST, an end-to-end model predicting complete target-speech representations directly from source speech. This addresses a genuine data bottleneck for expressive S2ST.

entry.title: CRESiST: Self-Enhancing Explorative Policy Learning for Simultaneous Speech Translation

author.name: Chenyang Le, Pei Zhang, Yuxiang Chen, Bing Han, Derek F. Wong, Baosong Yang, Yanmin Qian

entry.summary: CRESiST proposes an end-to-end interleaved read-write framework for simultaneous speech translation built on an omni-modal LLM, achieving full KV cache reuse and segmentation-free infinite-stream inference without external voice activity detection. It learns streaming policies via explorative policy learning rather than rigid offline alignment. A solid systems contribution to low-latency speech translation.

entry.title: Who Pays for the Knowledge Models Copy? Model Collapse as Rogers' Paradox

author.name: Nam H. Le

entry.summary: This theoretical paper reframes model collapse through cultural evolution theory, specifically Rogers' paradox: populations relying on copying end up no better off unless some members keep learning independently, since copied knowledge goes stale. It shows Rogers' model fitted to synthetic training predicts collapse magnitude within a few percentage points and argues the information supply entering the loop is the core problem. A conceptually rich synthesis connecting generative-model degradation with evolutionary theory.

entry.title: Turns Matter: Advancing Streaming Video RL via Turn-Level Credit

author.name: Shuai Dong, Kanghui Tian, Linghan Chen, Wenqi Shao, Hongrui Wu, Haowen Hou, Yongfu Zhu, Xuehui Wang, Ziyue Wang, Wenpu Liu, Weichu Xie, Yuqi Xu, Congcong Wang, Kaiwen Tuo, Caoyuan Ma, Taiqiang Wu, Ji Zhao, Wenzheng Chang, Dianyi Wang, Siyuan Wang, Zhongyu Wei, Yu Qiao, Jiaqi Wang

entry.summary: TurnWise is a turn-level GRPO framework for streaming video understanding, where models must decide when to respond versus keep observing. It addresses the mismatch between trajectory-level advantages and turn-level decisions, which currently causes redundant replies after early successes and suppressed follow-ups after failures. Turn-level credit assignment promotes informative responses and reduces redundancy.

entry.title: Feature Puzzles: Single-Image Supervision for Multi-View 3D-Aware Segmentation

author.name: Jiahao Ma, Qiang Zhang, Miaomiao Liu, David Ahmedt-Aristizabal, Chuong Nguyen

entry.summary: Feature Puzzles learns multi-view-consistent 3D-aware segmentation using only single-image semantic segmentation supervision, constructing consistent pseudo-labels via cropping and geometric transformations. A lightweight plug-and-play network leverages these labels, avoiding costly video or calibrated multi-view capture requirements.

entry.title: MotoVerse: A Benchmark for Predictive Perception of Motorized Two-Wheelers in Dense Unstructured Traffic

author.name: Varun A. Paturkar, Shankar Gangisetty, C. V. Jawahar

entry.summary: MotoVerse is a benchmark for ego-centric predictive perception from motorized two-wheelers, with 949 maneuver clips from dense unstructured traffic and trajectory annotations for over 31,000 road agents including 16,000+ MTWs. It supports maneuver anticipation and trajectory prediction tasks with an MTW-specific challenge taxonomy.

entry.title: ReactWorld: Structuring Interaction Responses for Embodied Video Generation

author.name: Hanwei Liu, Huijia Zhang, Hanzhang Wang, Guangyu Liu, Hanbei Zhan, Linjie Hu, Bin Xiao, Xuan Zhou, Dong Zhang

entry.summary: ReactWorld is an embodied video world model that predicts scene changes from robot actions using structured interaction anticipation: an interaction response field predictor describes participant roles, future motion intensity, and local motion changes in feature space, with a response feedback adapter refining object features. It is inspired by chain-of-thought reasoning.

entry.title: CrossPressor: Scalable Cross-View Fusion for Feed-Forward 3D Gaussian Splatting

author.name: Yuxi Hu, Wenhao Dong, Jun Zhang, Friedrich Fraundorfer

entry.summary: CrossPressor is a training-free method for scaling anchor-based feed-forward 3D Gaussian Splatting to long multi-view sequences, addressing a representation-fusion mismatch where fixed anchors must aggregate ever more support views. It uses coverage-cycled evidence routing to distribute spatial evidence across support views and fusion layers while preserving decoder-facing anchor queries.

entry.title: BudgetSplat: Budget-Controllable Generalizable Gaussian Splatting

author.name: Yuxi Hu, Jun Zhang, Wei Mao, Yuchen Rao, Friedrich Fraundorfer

entry.summary: BudgetSplat reformulates Gaussian primitive compaction in feed-forward 3D Gaussian Splatting as a joint optimization of importance, spatial coverage, and cross-view redundancy, allowing the final representation to fit a user-specified preservation ratio. A single trained model supports varying view counts and multiple test-time budgets without retraining. This addresses the redundancy-driven cost blowup of pixel-aligned methods.

entry.title: Same Layout, Different Count: What Number Words Do Past Ten in Text-to-Image Models

author.name: Liang Yue, Eric A. Vance

entry.summary: This controlled study examines how number words behave in text-to-image generation beyond about ten objects across five open models, holding objects and starting noise fixed and using 3,088 blind human counts. All models follow numbers for small counts but diverge past their reach; SD3.5-M and FLUX.1-dev fail soon after ten while FLUX.2 klein and Qwen-Image loosely follow up to twenty-five. Beyond reach, the coarse noise structure drives layout, not the number word.

entry.title: When can multi-fragment 2D/3D registration be trusted? Calibrated certification and uncertainty-driven view planning for pelvic fracture fluoroscopy

author.name: Bowen Xiang, Michael I. Miga

entry.summary: The paper presents a closed-loop system for CT-to-fluoroscopy registration in pelvic fracture surgery that bounds registration errors with calibrated sandwich covariance, flags unreliable fragments, and plans the next X-ray view accordingly. Simulated experiments on 60 fracture CTs show 95 percent bounds covering 83 percent of unflagged fragments, with an exploratory AUC of 0.94 for a view-shift feature predicting tightly bounded failures.

entry.title: Contact-Implicit Whole-Body Trajectory Optimization for Dynamic Humanoid Locomotion on Parameterizable Uneven Terrain

author.name: Roberto Mauceri, Stefano Dafarra, Giulio Romualdi, Marco Gabiccini, Daniele Pucci

entry.summary: The paper presents a contact-implicit whole-body trajectory planner for humanoid robots on parameterizable uneven terrain, generating feasible dynamic motions without predefined contact sequences by solving nonlinear programs with full dynamics. A smooth-surface ground approximation and novel contact constraints extend applicability from flat ground to arbitrary smooth surfaces such as steps and ramps.

entry.title: Diversity-Aware Experience Replay via Statistical Leverage Scores

author.name: Shaifalee Saxena, Alexander Scheinker

entry.summary: The authors propose scoring stored transitions in off-policy RL replay buffers by statistical leverage, a label-free measure of how unusual each transition is relative to the buffer, and sampling mini-batches from a mixture of leverage-based and uniform distributions. This targets a key problem in real-robot RL where replay buffers are dominated by routine near-identical transitions while rare informative events are undersampled. The approach requires no rewards, labels, or value networks.

entry.title: Robocasa-Mem: Benchmarking Environment and Process Memory in Long-Horizon Mobile Manipulation

author.name: Sihang Chen, Chen Ye, Wei Chen, Xiaohan Lei, Zhipeng Tang, Sha Zhang, Yuan Zhang, Zixuan Chen, Jiajun Deng, Houqiang Li, Yanyong Zhang

entry.summary: RoboCasa-Mem is a new benchmark of nine mobile manipulation tasks that require agents to use interaction history at key decision points, organized around two memory categories: environment memory (spatial locations, object attributes, relationships) and process memory (task progress, multi-task scheduling). It fills an evaluation gap for memory-dependent decision-making in mobile manipulation. Benchmarks like this enable systematic comparison of memory architectures for embodied agents.

entry.title: Flexible Intensities Matter: A Comprehensive Re-evaluation of Hawkes Processes and Neural Temporal Point Processes

author.name: Hendrik Mehrtens, Florian Buettner, Oliver Stegle

entry.summary: This systematic re-evaluation compares flexible classical Poisson and Hawkes processes against neural temporal point processes on five benchmarks plus two large-scale medical datasets from UK Biobank and MIMIC-IV. The study challenges prior claims of neural dominance, arguing earlier comparisons pitted flexible neural models against overly restricted classical baselines and neglected medical data.

entry.title: AGORA: Reliability-Aware Aggregation of LLM Judges via Item-Response Theory

author.name: Junhyung Ahn

entry.summary: AGORA applies item-response theory to aggregate multiple LLM judges, placing items on a latent quality scale and describing each judge by sensitivity and ordered rating thresholds so reliability is learned from all items. This addresses the failure of simple averaging and Dawid-Skene models when human-labeled validation sets are small.

entry.title: RECAP: Context-Aware Prediction Recycling with Request-Local and Persistent Memories for Multimodal Speculative Decoding

author.name: Hengjie Zhu, Dayan Wu, Xinze Liu, Peng Fu, Zheng Lin, Weiping Wang

entry.summary: RECAP improves training-free speculative decoding in vision-language models by storing target-model predictions under multi-token keys, separating request-local contextual memory from persistent token-level memory to avoid aliasing predictions across different images and prefixes. Entropy-confidence weighting fuses retrieved predictions at lookup. It addresses a concrete failure mode in prediction-recycling accelerators.

entry.title: Reasoning-Trace Overflow in Code Generation: An Empirical Study of Explicit Reasoning Models

author.name: Lukas Twist, Helen Yannakoudakis, Jie M. Zhang

entry.summary: The study measures reasoning-trace overflow in small open-weight reasoning models for code generation: models spending so much of a fixed 32k-token output budget on reasoning that usable code is never produced. Across seven models and six benchmarks, overflow is rare on simple tasks but common on harder ones, and the value of reasoning is highly conditional. Lightweight inference-time controls are evaluated as mitigations.

entry.title: Using Experience Twice: Dynamic Process Rubrics for Privileged Token-Level Credit Assignment

author.name: Shumao Wu, Kongcheng Zhang, Jianqiang Huang, Baisheng Lai

entry.summary: Proposes Online Rubric Self-Distillation, which distills distinctions among on-policy agent trajectories into natural-language process rubrics used as dense token-level supervision to augment sparse outcome-reward RL. The policy generates multiple rubric bundles per step, enabling credit assignment for critical decisions within trajectories.

entry.title: Do agents need to sleep?

author.name: Ido Haber, Giulio Tononi

entry.summary: Drawing on the selectionist ringing-resonance-renormalization account of sleep from neuroscience (co-authored by Giulio Tononi), the paper maps sleep-like consolidation operations onto digital memory architectures for persistent LLM agents suffering semantic drift, error propagation, and memory saturation. It derives the falsifiable prediction that selectionist consolidation will outperform alternative memory-management schemes. It is a conceptually rich bridge between sleep theory and agent memory engineering.

entry.title: Hybrid LLM-Deterministic Pipelines for Enterprise-Scale Code Migration at Bloomberg

author.name: Mario Corchero, David Williams, Laszlo Kiss Kollar, Haowen Liu, Shivam Bairoliya, Gala Malbasic, Serkan Kirbas, Federica Sarro

entry.summary: An industrial experience report on Bloomberg's Automated Uplift initiative, applying hybrid LLM-deterministic migration pipelines across thousands of repositories in two production campaigns: a Python packaging migration (~1,900 repos) and a C++ build system migration (~6,700 repos). Together these produced 2,333 pull requests and 729 successful migrations.

entry.title: CoSafe: Cooperative Runtime Safety Assurance for Mixed-Traffic Autonomous Driving

author.name: Dingji Wang, You Lu, Haowen Jiang, Yanggang Chen, Yuyang Bi, Bihuan Chen, Shenglin Bao, Xin Peng

entry.summary: CoSafe is a runtime safety assurance framework for autonomous driving in mixed traffic, where violations can arise from locally reasonable but jointly incompatible decisions among autonomous vehicles, human-driven vehicles, cyclists, and pedestrians. It continuously monitors hazards and coordinates across participants, going beyond ego-centric assurance approaches.

entry.title: Mixture of Wide Experts: Sparse Routing for Interpretable Native Coordinates

author.name: Tavish Mankash, Vardhaman Kalloli, Keshava Prasad, Deepan Muthirayan

entry.summary: Mixture of Wide Experts (MoWE) is a sparse feed-forward layer in which selected experts read the full representation but write to fixed, disjoint output coordinates, aiming to make models learn interpretable features natively rather than requiring post-hoc sparse autoencoders. On a controlled task with known hidden causes, MoWE preserves predictive performance while localizing causes more clearly than dense and standard MoE models, demonstrated with two 19-layer runs at approximately matched compute trained on 10 billion tokens. This connects architectural sparsity with interpretability.

entry.title: Language Models Can Benefit from Domain-Specific Inductive Biases

author.name: Damien Teney, Liangze Jiang, Zachary Shinnick, Hemanth Saratchandran, Simon Lucey

entry.summary: This work trains small language models from scratch on domain-specific subsets of pretraining data (web, code, math) and introduces transformer variants where standard activations are replaced with learned splines tuned per dataset. It evaluates cross-domain transfer to determine whether architectures refined for general-purpose learning are equally effective on data subsets, finding measurable benefits from domain-matched inductive biases.

entry.title: Finite-Sample Convergence in Networked Average Reward MARL: Decentralization Pitfalls and Entropy Remedies

author.name: Yizhou Zhang, Yashaswini Murthy, Laixi Shi, Adam Vierman

entry.summary: Studies networked average-reward MARL where agents update with k-hop neighborhood information, proving impossibility results for convergence to globally optimal joint policies under multiagency and partial observability. The paper then proposes remedies, apparently involving entropy regularization, with finite-sample convergence guarantees.

entry.title: Sample-Grained Approximate Unlearning with Provable Per-Sample Bounds

author.name: Yaxin Xiao, Yulin Jin, Li Tang, Haoyang LI, Huadi Zheng, Qingqing Ye, Haibo Hu

entry.summary: The paper introduces SALA, a plug-in optimization framework for machine unlearning that operates at the level of individual samples, steering each forget-set example toward its correct target distribution rather than relying on dataset-level aggregate metrics. It provides provable per-sample bounds on unlearning effectiveness, addressing how aggregate metrics can mask sample-level deviations from full retraining. This improves both the evaluation and practice of approximate unlearning.

entry.title: Beyond Foundation Models: PFN Priors Improve Tabular Hyperparameter Optimization

author.name: Artem Chistyakov, Renat Sergazinov, Artem Babenko

entry.summary: PriorTune meta-tunes hyperparameter configurations for conventional from-scratch tabular models using only synthetic datasets sampled from published PFN priors, greedily selecting a high-winrate configuration subset offline. Online, new datasets fit only the selected configurations, so gains come at no extra cost, with observed equal scaling from more configurations and synthetic datasets.

entry.title: AlgoPilot: Cross-Paradigm Reasoning in Language Models via Strategy Selection and Guidance

author.name: Yilun Hao, Ruixiao Yang, Hudson Hilal, Yongchao Chen, Kaizhi Qian, Yada Zhu, Yang Zhang, Chuchu Fan

entry.summary: AlgoPilot is a framework enabling LLMs to select an appropriate solving paradigm (program synthesis, symbolic reasoning, planning, optimization) and formulate problems before execution. It uses a SteerLM trained with SFT and RL to choose strategies, paired with structured guidance modules for each paradigm.

entry.title: A Universal Raw-IQ Radar Encoder for Cross-Sensor Human Sensing

author.name: Jonas Leo Mueller, Dario Zanca, Sebastian Hoefler, Jan Petermann, Thomas Altstidl, Naga Venkata Sai Jitin Jami, Emmanuelle Salin, Bjoern M. Eskofier

entry.summary: Argues that micro-Doppler spectrograms are a poor transfer basis for radar sensing and instead pretrains a convolutional beta-VAE on raw radar IQ measurements from four platforms spanning 60 and 77 GHz, aligned via a unified spectral interpolation grid. The frozen encoder transfers to downstream human sensing benchmarks across unseen users, tasks, and hardware with only small heads trained.

entry.title: Can saliency maps flag chest radiograph classifier errors at a new hospital? An external validation study

author.name: Aashish Chapagai, Angad Singh Gurtatta, Erik Cambria

entry.summary: Tests whether saliency maps detect individual errors of chest X-ray classifiers at external hospitals, evaluating over 300,000 decisions per model (CNN and ViT trained on NIH ChestX-ray14) at two external sites with radiologist-consensus labels. Grad-CAM localized findings far less often than radiologists (hit rate at most 0.575 versus 0.888), and anatomical enrichment adds only limited incremental error-detection value beyond model confidence.

entry.title: Conformal Prediction at Performative Equilibrium: The Price of Performativity

author.name: Ahmed Mahrous, Roberto Di Pietro

entry.summary: This work studies conformal prediction when deployed predictors change the data distribution, seeking coverage guarantees valid at performative equilibrium rather than under exchangeability. It proves a phase transition at distribution-map sensitivity L=1: for L>=1 no procedure can guarantee both equilibrium coverage and nontrivial sets, while for L<1 the minimax excess miscoverage is characterized.

entry.title: Zuse: A Decision Model for European Languages

author.name: Umair Mehmood Imam

entry.summary: Zuse comprises three decision models (4B, 9B, 27B) trained as low-rank adapters with pointer heads on frozen open-weight bases, targeting classification-style decisions over 27 European languages. The 27B model reaches 87.5% accuracy with low calibration error across a broad 11-source, 9-task-group European suite. It extends the emerging decision-model paradigm beyond English for the first time.

entry.title: Modality-Aware Expert Pruning for MoE-Based Multimodal Large Language Models

author.name: Donggeun Kim

entry.summary: MAEP is a training-free framework for pruning mixture-of-experts experts in multimodal LLMs that decomposes expert importance by modality (vision versus language) in a single forward pass, rather than aggregating importance uniformly across tokens. It targets the dominant memory cost of MoE-MLLMs, where experts exceed 90% of parameters in models like InternVL3.5-30B-A3B and Qwen3-VL-30B-A3B (existing models, analyzed rather than newly released). Practical compression contribution for deployed multimodal systems.

entry.title: From Activation to Intervention: Interpreting Sparse Visual Features through Reconstruction

author.name: Jianyang Gu, Jacob Beattie, Mridul Khurana, Julia Chae, Xi Xiao, Cheng Zhang, Anuj Karpatne, Wei-Lun Chao, Sara Beery, Tanya Berger-Wolf

entry.summary: RecSAEI shifts sparse autoencoder feature interpretation in vision models from passive observation of maximally activating images to active intervention: features are modified along SAE decoder directions and the visual output is reconstructed as direct causal evidence of feature meaning. This resolves ambiguity when multiple features activate in the same locations, such as texture and color. An interpretability-by-reconstruction framework for visual representations.

entry.title: FedIA: Instance-Aware Cross-Modal Representations for Federated Prompt Learning

author.name: Xuanjing Zhang, Qi Guo, Yanan Qiao, Yong Han, Junge Bo

entry.summary: FedIA improves federated prompt learning of vision-language models by making personalization instance-aware rather than client-level, adjusting the balance between globally shared and local prompts per input. This addresses visual variation among samples within a client that fixed, input-agnostic prompt combinations overlook.

entry.title: ChanSFormer: A Channel Agnostic Vision Transformer for Multi-Channel Cell Painting Images

author.name: Jingwei Zhang, Srinivasan Sivanandan, Dimitris Samaras

entry.summary: ChanSFormer is a vision transformer for heterogeneous multi-channel imaging (e.g., Cell Painting assays) that remains channel-agnostic as experimental configurations evolve, preserving cross-channel interactions without learnable per-channel embeddings. It replaces global self-attention-based channel handling that requires prior knowledge of channels.

entry.title: DSRS: Teaching MLLMs to Perceive, Reason, and Segment in Complex Driving Scenes

author.name: Sicen Guo, Zhengfei Song, Kuanhsun Chen, Xu Huang, Ping Zhong, Wei Ye, Shaoyi Du, Rui Fan

entry.summary: DSRS introduces driving scene reasoning segmentation, a task requiring multimodal LLMs to interpret implicit instructions, infer spatial relations, detect risks, and apply traffic rules to produce accurate segmentation masks. The authors contribute a benchmark dataset and DSRS-Net, a new framework for the task.

entry.title: LungMend: A Healthy-Only Latent Diffusion Shape Prior for Lung Mask Correction in Severe Tuberculosis CT

author.name: Rezkellah Noureddine Khiat, Pierre-Yves Brillet, Catalin Fetita

entry.summary: LungMend is a latent diffusion post-processing model trained only on healthy lungs that corrects lung segmentation masks on severe tuberculosis CT scans, recovering cavities and consolidations that standard models like R231 miss. By learning to complete lungs from faulty masks and bone anatomy, it avoids requiring pathological training data or CT intensities. It improves accuracy on expert-annotated slices.

entry.title: Time-to-Goal: Learned Temporal Metrics for Long-Horizon Planning with JEPA World Models

author.name: Ruilong Yu, Fei Ye

entry.summary: The paper identifies a flaw in JEPA-based planning: prediction and regularization objectives do not guarantee that latent states closer in time to a goal receive lower costs, so temporal ordering is weakened at long horizons. The authors propose Time-to-Goal, a lightweight learned metric over latent trajectories that restores this ordering and improves long-horizon planning in flat JEPA world models.

entry.title: Rethinking Self-Repair in Code-as-Policy Agents: What Drives Retry Success?

author.name: Siddharth Aphale, Ayushman Singh

entry.summary: This controlled study in simulated manipulation disentangles the sources of retry success in code-as-policy agents, finding that a frozen Qwen2.5-Coder-7B recovers 85.3% of failures within five retries using feedback, versus 68.3% from pure resampling. Notably, failure-specific feedback offers little advantage over feedback from unrelated episodes or fixed task guidance, challenging assumptions about why self-repair works.

entry.title: TestBED: An Open-Source Toolkit for Bayesian Experimental Design

author.name: Gavin Kerrigan, Marcel Hedman, Sahel Iqbal, Tom Rainforth

entry.summary: TestBED is a general-purpose open-source toolkit for Bayesian experimental design that decomposes the BED pipeline into modular, reusable components covering tasks, objectives, training mechanisms, policy architectures, and evaluation, with scalable implementations. It addresses the fragmentation of bespoke BED codebases that hinders comparison and adoption of methods.

entry.title: Challenge-Aware Knowledge Recruitment with Meta-Agent Supervision for Medical Multi-Agent Reasoning

author.name: Riccardo Riccio, Haitz S\'aez de Oc\'ariz Borde, Pietro Li\`o

entry.summary: The paper proposes challenge-aware adaptive recruitment for medical multi-agent reasoning, where a CHALLENGER agent inspects the evolving reasoning trace and triggers targeted knowledge retrieval or mid-discussion specialist recruitment. On a hard subset of MEDAGENTSBENCH spanning nine biomedical datasets, this gap-driven approach outperforms upfront retrieval and standard multi-agent debate.

entry.title: Split-KV: Efficient Context Parallelism for Training Diffusion Drafters

author.name: Geng Zhang, Fangzhao Zhang, Cong Xie, Tiantian Fan, Yang You

entry.summary: Split-KV is an exact context-parallelism method for training diffusion drafters used in speculative decoding, exploiting the empirically established asymmetry between short draft queries and long contexts while handling the sample-dependent load balancing induced by anchor sampling. It keeps key/value sharded to enable efficient training. Targets scalability of a promising decoding-acceleration technique.

entry.title: HarnessFlow: MCTS-Guided Harness Optimization for LLM Agents

author.name: Zhi Hong, Qianlong Wang, Hongchen Wei, Aidan Wu, Daohong Ying, Mingze Kong, Bei Liu, Chong Luo

entry.summary: Presents HarnessFlow, a framework that automatically optimizes executable agent harnesses under a limited evaluation budget using Monte Carlo Tree Search over a refinement tree of candidate harnesses. A coding agent refines harnesses using archived code, execution feedback, and evaluation histories while the model and environment stay fixed.

entry.title: LIBRA: Programmatic Induction of Executable Tool Libraries

author.name: Zekai Li, Zhenke Liu, Yonghao Li, Junhan Liu, Xulong Xiao, Jiapeng Zhang

entry.summary: LIBRA converts flat LLM agent tool catalogs into executable tool libraries by having an LLM propose per-tool contracts (invocations, reusable outputs, state changes, success conditions) and then validating compositions in a sandbox before user queries arrive. This captures workflow dependencies that per-tool similarity retrieval misses in multi-tool tasks.

entry.title: Generative AI for urban planning: synthesizing land-use maps with satellite imagery via DualControlNet

author.name: Qingqi Song, Yuzhou Chen, Lingqian Hu, Shenhao Wang

entry.summary: DualControlNet is a generative land-use model that jointly synthesizes high-resolution land-use maps and satellite imagery from simple text prompts, adding multimodality, controllability, and domain-specific verification to urban planning generation. It was trained on over 40,000 paired tiles from Orlando and Chicago and evaluated with land-use-specific metrics rather than generic image quality. This moves generative AI in urban systems from unimodal prediction toward controlled scenario synthesis.

entry.title: Model Merging Does Not Require Uniform LoRA Ranks

author.name: Zirong Xie, Zainab Afolabi, Nikita Kozodoi, Jack Butler

entry.summary: This paper challenges the standard practice of training all experts at the same LoRA rank before model merging, showing the coupling is a property of specific merge methods rather than of merging itself. Across 36 experts, three domains, four ranks, and three model scales, per-domain best ranks improve averaging and utility-based selection by up to 1.8 points while conflict-resolution methods can lose up to 4 points.

entry.title: Dexterous Robotic Hands in the Foundation-Model Era: A Full-Stack Survey of Hardware, Data, Cross-Embodiment Transfer, Learning, and Evaluation

author.name: Ji Pei

entry.summary: This survey organizes the literature on dexterous robotic hands from January 2024 to early November 2026 into five interdependent layers: hardware, data collection and curation, cross-embodiment transfer, learning and foundation models, and evaluation. It provides a system-level architecture, comparative tables, and case analyses connecting design choices across layers, plus cross-cutting perspectives on human hand-object understanding and tactile sensing. It fills a need for integrated assessment of a field usually evaluated piecewise.

entry.title: Structure, Dimensionality, and Distribution Shape - What Makes Pretraining Data Transferable, and Why the Input Pipeline Decides Which

author.name: Sangyoon Bae, Jiook Cha

entry.summary: Proposes the Transfer-Invariance Principle: whether a corpus property (structure, dimensionality, distribution shape) matters for transfer depends on the model's input transform rather than the modality. Introduces TransferForge, a controllable synthetic corpus generator, and shows empirically that e.g. PatchTST window standardization makes distribution shape inert while Chronos-style priors cannot express certain structures.

entry.title: SKILL2STEER: One-Pass Hypernetwork for Mapping Natural-Language Skills to Low-Rank Post-Block Activation Shifts

author.name: Ran Li, Lei Chen

entry.summary: The paper investigates whether compiled skill artifacts injected into model activations actually carry skill content, testing this assumption via controls on a retrieval agent. Surprisingly, a wrong skill document performs on par with the correct one and a single averaged bundle matches per-skill routing, indicating compiled shifts encode a domain-general behavioral prior rather than skill content — though same-norm random directions collapse to baseline. The work tempers expectations for prompt-to-parameters skill compilation.

entry.title: Contextual Linear Activation Steering of Language Models

author.name: Brandon Hsu, Daniel Beaglehole, Adityanarayanan Radhakrishnan, Mikhail Belkin

entry.summary: CLAS decomposes activation steering into a fixed interpretable direction plus a context-dependent coefficient, allowing steering strength to adapt per input and enabling selective steering of multiple behaviors in different parts of a single generation. This improves on fixed-strength linear steering methods for controlling and specializing LLMs. It has implications for interpretability and lightweight model control.

entry.title: Phonological Knowledge of Chinese Characters in Language Models

author.name: Xiaozhe Ji, Renfen Hu, Hai Hu

entry.summary: The authors introduce PinyinBench, a controlled benchmark for homophones, phonological features, and polyphonic Chinese characters, and probe 17 text-only and multimodal LMs via behavioral testing, layer-wise probing, and activation steering. A frontier model (DS-v4-flash) exceeds 90% on homophone judgment but drops to 72% when characters differ only in tone, revealing systematic gaps. This provides insight into how linguistic knowledge is represented inside LMs.

entry.title: SAUCE: Summary Analysis Using Conversation Entailment

author.name: Man-Ling Sung, Hemanth Kandula, Jeff Ma, William Hartmann, Matthew Snover

entry.summary: SAUCE is a reference-free, entailment-based evaluation pipeline for cross-lingual conversational speech summarization that measures accuracy and fact coverage by checking entailment between conversation and summary. Unlike black-box LLM judges or embedding metrics, it is explainable, mapping summary claims to sources and capturing information loss from transcription and translation errors. Addresses a real gap in evaluating an increasingly commercial capability.

entry.title: Chronos: Sequential Identity-Preserving Video Generation by Temporal Anchoring

author.name: Mengqi Huang, Wenchuan Wang, Zhendong Mao, Yijing Tu, Zhike Liu, Luoni Wang, Ning Tong, Xiaoxiao Sheng, Tianyu Huang, Xuecheng Qi, Yongdong Zhang

entry.summary: Chronos addresses the tension between identity fidelity and temporal controllability in identity-preserving video generation, unifying single-segment facial identity preservation with multi-segment sequential action generation via temporal anchoring. It targets identity drift and motion suppression under large pose variations.

entry.title: USI-Brain: Enhancing Underwater Spatial Intelligence via Spatial Data-Driven Vision-Language Modeling

author.name: Zhiliang Zhu, Zhiqiang Zhao, Xie'an Jiang, Yingxin Lai, Kangye Zheng, Dawei Zhao

entry.summary: The paper presents a spatial data engine producing 4.27M QA pairs linking underwater visual appearance with object-level geometry, used to train USI-Brain, a vision-language model with an Underwater Prior-guided Rectifier for gated visual feature corrections. It also introduces USI-Bench with 6,525 samples for evaluating underwater spatial reasoning.

entry.title: RDT-3D: Resolution-Decoupled Training for High-Fidelity 3D Geometry Generation

author.name: Jiale Zhang, Yang Liu, Chengyang Li, Jin Yuan, Qianxi Jia, Taicheng Huang

entry.summary: RDT-3D identifies a training-inference resolution discrepancy in coarse-to-fine 3D generation pipelines that use RoPE conditioning, and proposes anchoring coordinate guidance at 512 resolution while supervising geometry at 1536 to enable robust detail extrapolation. Additional mechanisms address remaining fidelity issues.

entry.title: Entropogram-guided Visual Realignment Decoding: Capturing the Rhythm of Multimodal Reasoning

author.name: Jiaqi Deng, Zhe Fu, Yakun Chen, Dichang Zhang, Zonghan Wu, Xiaoshui Huang, Huan Huo, Guandong Xu

entry.summary: This work analyzes MLLM hallucination through decoding-time entropy dynamics, identifying two characteristic entropy patterns linked to premature convergence and abrupt local transitions, and proposes an entropogram-guided realignment decoding method to correct reasoning in progress. It treats entropy as a structured signal of modality integration rather than static uncertainty.

entry.title: Benchmarking Fine-Grained Visual Reasoning for Remote Sensing in Urban Management

author.name: Jiawei Zhang, Rizhao Cai, Dayan Guan

entry.summary: UMBench is a fine-grained urban remote sensing benchmark built from UAV images spanning traffic monitoring, construction, environmental quality, and disaster warning tasks. Evaluations show current multimodal LLMs rely on scene-level priors rather than fine-grained visual evidence. The authors also propose a training-free evidence-first chain-of-thought prompting method that improves fine-grained reasoning.

entry.title: Dual Flow: Joint Image-Measurement Flow for Inverse Problems

author.name: Sevket Ege Yesilyurt, Figen S. Oktem

entry.summary: Dual Flow introduces a coupled flow-matching framework for linear inverse problems that jointly estimates the clean image and its noise-free measurement, rather than only conditioning image sampling on the observation. The noisy measurement merely initializes the measurement state; thereafter, both states are updated jointly, coupling reconstruction and measurement denoising.

entry.title: GRASP: Gradient-Guided Sampling for Contact-Rich Physics-Based Motion Retargeting

author.name: Yang Liu, Tong Wang, Yiming Bao, Heng Yang

entry.summary: GRASP combines sampling-based exploration with gradient-guided refinement for physics-based retargeting of human demonstrations to robots, without requiring a differentiable simulator. GRASP-TO extends tempered sequential Monte Carlo with local quadratic cost models fit to archived rollouts guiding MCMC rejuvenation (with Metropolis-Hastings correction), and GRASP-MPC scales the approach to longer-horizon problems.

entry.title: Scale Anchoring via Implicit Semantics and Sequence-Consistent Loop Closure for VGGT-Based SLAM

author.name: Ziyi Jin, Kangjin Yu, Beichen Wang, Can Jiang, Zhongpu Xia, Jie Xu

entry.summary: Building on VGGT-SLAM 2.0, this work tackles scale drift in feed-forward monocular geometric foundation models by anchoring submap scales via joint VGGT inference that exploits learned implicit semantic-geometric cues, plus short-sequence-assisted direct loop connections with consistency checks and translation-scale alignment. Each accepted loop candidate contributes robust constraints across submaps. This improves global consistency of calibration-free dense monocular SLAM.

entry.title: Near-Minimax Sample Complexity for Multi-Objective Reinforcement Learning under Generative Models

author.name: Yue Wang

entry.summary: The paper establishes the constant-confidence minimax sample complexity for finite discounted MDPs with multiple reward functions, where one dataset must support epsilon-optimal policies for all convex combinations of rewards. The resulting tight characterization clarifies how the number of objectives affects sample requirements, including the regime where additional objectives are essentially free.

entry.title: Regression with Many Generated Controls

author.name: Timothy Christensen, Daniel Vebman

entry.summary: This paper analyzes linear regression when a latent control variable is proxied by many AI/ML-generated imputations, deriving the implicit estimand targeted by each practical strategy (including all proxies, factors, IV, and nonlinear variants). It determines when these estimands recover the parameter of interest and offers practical recommendations for the increasingly common AI-proxy setting.

entry.title: Hybrid Spark: Adaptive Speculative Decoding That Lets the Content Choose the Drafter

author.name: Ekagra Ranjan, Bharat Venkitesh

entry.summary: Hybrid Spark introduces adaptive speculative decoding that selects between model-based drafters and cheap model-free drafters like n-gram lookup based on content, allowing model-free drafters to participate in batch-wide verification budget allocation. This avoids forcing deployments to fix one drafter or split GPUs between drafting approaches.

entry.title: Reglos: A Self-Evolving Personal Memory Agent with Recursive Self-Improvement

author.name: Sen Yang, Jiaduo Lin, Zehong Huang, Wen Liu

entry.summary: Reglos is a training-free personal memory agent whose memory record evolves append-only as new preferences supersede old ones, and whose context-construction harness improves via recursive self-improvement, with the key safeguard that harness changes are tested to confirm benefit beyond the specific failures they targeted. This addresses overfitting risk in self-modifying agent systems. It combines personalization with a self-improvement safety check.

entry.title: Behavior Graphs: Unsupervised Graph Structures for Interpreting Robot Deployment Data

author.name: Erik Bauer, Jakob Thumm, Christopher Agia, Rohan Sinha, Chen Xu, Haruki Nishimura, Jeannette Bohg, Marco Pavone, Masha Itkina

entry.summary: Behavior graphs compress large volumes of robot policy rollouts into a single interpretable directed graph by learning behavior-mode similarity, linking behaviors temporally, and tying them to outcomes. A user study across three real-world settings shows the graphs help analysts ground data-collection decisions. This operationalizes the data-flywheel idea for robotics deployment.

entry.title: How Finely Can Vision-Language Models See Biology? Bio-VQA: A Benchmark for Taxonomic, Morphological, Spatial and Individual Reasoning

author.name: S M Rayeed, Qian Ma, Charles V. Stewart, Yao Ma

entry.summary: Bio-VQA is the largest biological visual question answering benchmark, with 1.86M questions over 217K images from 11 public datasets, spanning taxonomic reasoning, fine-grained attribute grounding, spatial reasoning, and individual re-identification. It substantially extends beyond prior benchmarks focused on species identification in a few groups, probing what VLMs can actually perceive in biodiversity imagery.

entry.title: Readable Is Not Steerable: Pre-Registered Tests of Physical Structure in Learned Fluid Representations

author.name: Manvendra Modgil

entry.summary: Three pre-registered studies test whether self-supervised world models organize latents around physical quantities in 2D Navier-Stokes flow, finding that a JEPA trained on the flow fails the pre-registered criteria and does no better than an untrained network, while plain autoencoders that render the field make enstrophy prominent in slow latent directions. The results challenge common claims that predictive world models naturally encode physical structure.

entry.title: DARE: Difficulty Analysis for Repair Enhancement

author.name: Jikwang Lee, Seungwook Jung, Jaechang Nam

entry.summary: DARE addresses the problem that solve-rate metrics for LLM coding agents hide task difficulty differences across benchmarks. It defines continuous task difficulty as observed failure rate across multiple agents and integrates difficulty prediction, feature-group contribution analysis, and task-specific repair support without costly repeated agent runs. This yields richer evaluation signal and targeted support for coding agents.

entry.title: Learning Pseudo-Riemannian Manifolds for Heterophilic Graphs via Graph Signature

author.name: Yun Young Choi, Asung Kil, Sun Woo Park, Minho Lee, Seokhwan Kim

entry.summary: The paper argues that positive-definite geometric priors common in GNNs fundamentally mismatch heterophilic graphs where edges encode dissimilarity, and introduces the Graph Signature Index, an inertia of a class-compatibility matrix computable from label topology alone. It shows no positive-definite form can represent the needed negative squared distances and proposes pseudo-Riemannian manifolds as an alternative.

entry.title: Message-passing graph persistence

author.name: Jorge Luiz Franco, Arthur Queiroz Moura, Moacir Ponti, Amauri Souza

entry.summary: This paper introduces Message-Passing Graph Persistence (MGP), a family of topological descriptors that integrates message passing into graph filtrations, updating node embeddings at each filtration step and tying them to persistence events. The authors prove invariance properties and show that MGP can complement or exceed the expressivity limits of standard message-passing GNNs, which are bounded by the one-dimensional Weisfeiler-Leman test. This bridges persistent homology and GNN representation learning more tightly than prior work.

entry.title: Dr. No: Feature Steering for Abstention in Vision-Language Models

author.name: Farid Hasanov, Riccardo Renzulli, Bahram Zonooz, Mykola Pechenizkiy, Decebal Constantin Mocanu

entry.summary: Dr. No identifies sparse autoencoder features associated with abstention and commitment behavior and modulates a small set of them during the prefill pass at inference time, without retraining the base model. Evaluated on LLaVA-1.6 Mistral 7B across multimodal abstention benchmarks, it enables controlled refusal when evidence is insufficient.

entry.title: TB-Transolver: Parallelized and Coherent Long-Horizon Rollouts via Temporal Bundling for Time-Dependent PDEs

author.name: Sidharth S. Menon, Ameya D. Jagtap

entry.summary: Extends the Transolver neural PDE solver with temporal bundling so that time-dependent problems can be rolled out in parallel rather than sequentially, removing the linear cost scaling with temporal horizon while preserving coherence of long-horizon predictions. Targets unstructured mesh physics simulation at scale.

entry.title: Separating Common and Unique Directions for Model Merging

author.name: Shiting Wang, Yingjie Zou, Ke Li

entry.summary: Finds a consistent two-regime structure in task vectors within a shared directional basis - a low-dispersion common bulk and a high-dispersion task-dominated tail - and proposes CUSD, a data-free pre-merging method that separates common and unique components and merges each with a domain-appropriate rule. Improves on single element-wise merge rules.

entry.title: Self-Privileged Fine-Tuning

author.name: Yangrong Hu, Xueyu Zhou, Yue Wu, Jian Huang

entry.summary: The paper analyzes token-level weighting schemes used to improve supervised fine-tuning of language models, theoretically characterizing the target distributions they induce. It shows dynamic weighting methods like Dynamic Fine-Tuning induce heavily sharpened target distributions, while static weighting fits flatter distributions, and builds on this analysis to propose self-privileged fine-tuning. This provides principled understanding of a commonly used but under-theorized component of LLM post-training.

entry.title: Finite Spectral Depth Controls Gaussian Entrance Rank and Avoidance of the First Gradient-Flow Saddle

author.name: Yanlin Long

entry.summary: Analyzing matrix factorization dynamics under small initialization, the paper shows that applying a finite number of Newton-Schulz iterations (the Muon optimizer's core step) to the normalized gradient changes the rank selected early in training and can bypass the first nonzero stationary point of gradient flow. Under a residual-inertia condition, bypass is guaranteed for sufficiently large spectral depth.

entry.title: LoopVQ: Sub 1-bit KV Cache Quantization for Looped Transformers

author.name: Minsoo Cheong, Sungjoo Yoo

entry.summary: LoopVQ targets the KV cache memory bottleneck in looped transformers, exploiting redundancy along the loop axis and differing quantization sensitivity across loop steps to compress the cache below 1 bit per element via vector quantization. This complements parameter savings of looped architectures by addressing inference memory. It matters for deploying parameter-efficient language models at scale.

entry.title: Do We Still Need Rotation-Invariant Architectures? A Statistical Robustness Benchmark for Point Cloud Classification

author.name: Abdulla Nasir Chowdhury, Gulpi Qorik Oktagalu Pratamasunu, Kazuhiro Fukui

entry.summary: The paper benchmarks 10 point cloud architectures, including rotation-invariant and equivariant designs, across 5 domains under pose, noise, and occlusion using confirmatory hypothesis tests. It finds RI architectures achieve the best pose robustness but rank near the bottom on noise robustness, and shows a simple invariance loss on the embedding can close much of the gap without built-in invariance.

entry.title: Spin Spherical Fourier Neural Operators: Efficient Equivariant Learning for Vector and Spin Fields on the Sphere

author.name: Kevin Mulder, Matthew A. Price, Eirini Leftaki, Jason D. McEwen

entry.summary: The authors extend spherical Fourier neural operators to spin fields (fields whose values change phase under local frame rotation) via lifted spherical convolutions that are exactly rotationally equivariant. Computation exploits harmonic representations and sampling theorems on the sphere and rotation group, targeting applications like wind, CMB polarization, and weak lensing.

entry.title: Physics-informed traditional and generative Mori-Zwanzig-reduced models for multiscale systems

author.name: Emily Williams, Saad Qadeer, Amanda Howard, Panos Stinis

entry.summary: This work extends the Mori-Zwanzig formalism for model reduction to bases discovered by physics-informed machine learning, using the fluctuation-dissipation theorem to close the resulting non-Markovian dynamics. A complementary generative closure is introduced, and both approaches substantially improve filtered-state predictions over Markovian dynamics alone.

entry.title: Replicability, Reproducibility, and Robustness in Political and Social Science Research with Large Language Models

author.name: Joan C. Timoneda, Sebasti\'an Vallejo Vera

entry.summary: This chapter tackles the reproducibility crisis in LLM-assisted social science, distinguishing replicability, reproducibility, and robustness, and proposing a probabilistic standard based on result distributions rather than identical outputs. It shows measurement choices can reverse the sign of downstream regression coefficients, a striking methodological warning. Important guidance for the growing practice of using LLMs as social-science instruments.

entry.title: ChangeJEPA: Predict Before You Compare for Remote Sensing Change Detection

author.name: Buddhi Wijenayake, Dhananjaya Jayasundara, Vishal M. Patel

entry.summary: ChangeJEPA reformulates remote sensing change detection as latent post-state prediction within a joint-embedding predictive architecture rather than Siamese feature comparison. Given a pre-change image and partial post-change evidence, it predicts the full post-change representation under both a prior hypothesis and an updated hypothesis, filtering nuisance variations like illumination and seasonality. This predict-before-compare design improves discrimination of true change.

entry.title: ReTailor: A Residual Feature Tailoring Framework for Real-Time Cross-Sensor Pansharpening Adaptation

author.name: Jing-Ze Liang, Wei-Jie Xiao, Zi-Han Cao, Yang-Dong Li, Tian-Yi Hu, Liang-Jian Deng

entry.summary: ReTailor enables real-time adaptation of pansharpening models to unseen satellite sensors by optimizing only a lightweight residual Feature Tailor under self-supervised, physics-aware constraints, avoiding target-sensor retraining or expensive per-image zero-shot optimization. This corrects cross-sensor shifts without disturbing the learned fusion prior.

entry.title: RouTex: Multi-reference 3D Texture Generation by Reprogramming Rotary Position Encoding

author.name: Chengyang Li, Yang Liu, Jiale Zhang, Qiang Rao, Wei Zhang, Taicheng Huang

entry.summary: RouTex conditions 3D texture generation on multi-view reference images using an in-context diffusion transformer, introducing Positional Routing to reprogram 3D RoPE along spatial and semantic dimensions for explicit reference-to-view correspondence without extra parameters. It targets ambiguity resolution in unobserved surface regions.

entry.title: CAPE-JEPA - Cross-modal Adversarial Probabilistic Embedding JEPA

author.name: Aniket Junghare, Biplab Banerjee

entry.summary: CAPE-JEPA extends JEPA-style predictive self-supervised learning for cross-modal remote sensing retrieval (SAR and multispectral) by replacing deterministic latent forecasting with a probabilistic cross-attentional Gaussian predictor outputting per-patch parameters, plus adversarial components for distributional alignment. It addresses the assumption of uniform patch predictability in prior work like X-JEPA.

entry.title: Agent-Driven Generative Priors for Pathology Image Synthesis and Segmentation

author.name: Sicheng Yang, Rui Tang, Haipeng Zhou, Hongqiu Wang, Zhaohu Xing, Jianda Ma, Lie Dai, Guang Yang, Lei Zhu

entry.summary: This work proposes a three-stage pathology pipeline: an agent system screens image quality to build TCGA-200K (217,030 curated patches), a generative model is trained on screened data for synthesis and segmentation-friendly representations, and the outputs are adapted to downstream tasks. It links automated data curation, generation, and analysis rather than treating synthetic data as an isolated step.

entry.title: UniLoop: Unified Loop Closure Detection from Retrieval to Geometric Verification and Relative Pose Estimation

author.name: Jingwen Yu, Pengyu Wang, Jin Wu, Weinan Chen, Ping Tan, Hong Zhang

entry.summary: UniLoop unifies loop closure detection for SLAM by reusing hierarchical features of a pretrained geometric foundation model across retrieval, geometric verification, and relative pose estimation, replacing the usual cascade of separate models. A shared encoder produces global descriptors, a cross-view decoder performs pairwise verification, and native geometric predictions supply pose constraints for pose-graph optimization.

entry.title: ZipDrift: Generating Multimodal Short-Horizon MPC Costs with One-Step Drifting Models

author.name: Ke Zhang

entry.summary: ZipDrift addresses the observation that optimal short-horizon MPC cost corrections are often multimodal (e.g., passing an obstacle on either side), where deterministic regression averages modes. It trains a one-step diffusion-style generator over cost corrections, tilted toward low closed-loop cost and learned only from cost evaluations without differentiating through the optimizer.

entry.title: Online Adaptation to Latent Physical Properties for Learning from Demonstration

author.name: Kotaro Kajitsuka, Masaki Murooka, Fumio Kanehiro

entry.summary: The authors tackle manipulation of visually identical objects with different physical properties, proposing a learning-from-demonstration method that jointly learns a dynamics model and latent representations of physical properties from adaptive demonstrations. The policy is conditioned on online latent estimates acquired through interaction, enabling actions like regrasping and contact relocation. This addresses a practical gap where appearance-based policies fail on objects that look identical but behave differently.

entry.title: H^2MARL: Hierarchical Heterogeneous Multi-agent Reinforcement Learning for Humanoid Robot Control

author.name: Xuemin Hu, Kaixin Li, Qingqing Xia, Yuxin Wang, Wei Xie, Bo Tang, Long Chen

entry.summary: H2MARL formulates humanoid whole-body control as a multi-agent RL problem at the joint-degree-of-freedom level with a physical-heterogeneity-aware policy factorization, where each torque-actuated joint is treated as an agent with its own characteristics. Combined with a hierarchical structure coordinating high-level and low-level control, this addresses the coupled dynamics and heterogeneous actuation of humanoid bodies. The framework aims to produce better-coordinated whole-body motion than existing partition-based MARL or independently optimized hierarchical controllers.

entry.title: Generative Modeling for Cascading Extremes via Autoregressive Transformers

author.name: Miguel de Carvalho, Myung Won Lee, Jordan Richards, Sotirios Sabanis

entry.summary: The paper introduces an extremal token representation encoding multivariate observations as categorical sequences—using a quiet token for non-exceedances—enabling decoder-only transformers to model history-dependent dependence among extreme events like earthquake-tsunami cascades. The representation is invariant to monotone transformations and preserves the ordering of dominant exceedances.

entry.title: Prior-data fitted networks for variable selection

author.name: Omar Melikechi

entry.summary: This paper extends prior-data fitted networks (PFNs) to Bayesian variable selection, introducing CD-PFN for conditional dependencies and PC-PFN for parent-child identification in causal graphs. Both networks estimate posterior inclusion probabilities in a single forward pass without posterior sampling, and often outperform existing methods on semi-synthetic and real data.

entry.title: Can Large Language Models Review the Scientific Literature? A Test Against a 102-Article Benchmark

author.name: Abdullah Al Kalbani, David M. Schultz, Alexandra K. Anderson-Frey, Zhonghua Zheng, Catherine McGuire

entry.summary: This study evaluates six AI tools, including tools built on Claude Code and Codex, across four stages of literature review against a published 102-article review corpus on the Spanish plume weather pattern. It finds significant gaps in article discovery that institutional library access partially closes, and reports mixed accuracy in interpretation, synthesis, and future-work proposal.

entry.title: Route to Remember: Adaptive Memory Selection for LLM Agents

author.name: Zeyu Fang, Jun Yin, Yongsheng Mei, Xu Han, Chaitali Joshi, Zhongkai Sun, Jie Hao, Bin Guo, Chengyuan Ma, Benjamin Z. Yao, Chenlei Guo

entry.summary: This paper proposes routing between text-based memory retrieval and weight memory that internalizes episodic and semantic knowledge like user-specific facts into parameters, answering without context cost. It aims to close the recall-precision gap of earlier weight-memory attempts while avoiding unbounded context growth in production agents.

entry.title: How Do Artificial Agents Make Decisions in Light of Visual Data?

author.name: Keyty Loza, Shayan Monadjemi

entry.summary: This study examines how vision-language model agents perceive and quantify uncertainty in visualizations and make decisions under uncertainty. It builds on prior work in visualization literacy and decision theory through two complementary empirical studies. The work matters because it probes a gap between VLMs' visual reasoning capabilities and their decision-making reliability.

entry.title: UniCompress: From Multi-LoRA Experts to One Compact Model for Edge Intelligence

author.name: Mingkang Liu, Peipei Jiao, Weiming Meng, Tianyuan Liu, Lichen Pang, Junyan Li

entry.summary: UniCompress converts multi-task LoRA expertise from a Qwen3-VL-4B teacher into a single compact adapter-free student via asymmetric INT2 quantization with GPTQ initialization and teacher-guided recovery, jointly compressing the vision encoder and language backbone. It targets memory-constrained embodied and edge deployments of VLMs. Note that Qwen3-VL is an established model family, not a new release.

entry.title: Beyond Risk Cues: A Mechanism-Level Benchmark and Verifiable Debate for Scam Video Detection on the Web

author.name: Yifan Wang, Junyu Lu, Shun Zhang, Chaozhuo Li, Fanliang Bu, Rong Yin, Lingbin Bu, Changrong Min, Peng Chen

entry.summary: Introduces MechScam, a benchmark of 6,614 videos annotated with scam mechanisms, evidence-supported explanations, and confusable non-scam categories like advertisements. It also proposes a verifiable debate framework for detection reasoning and tests robustness against misleading arguments, moving beyond binary scam classification.

entry.title: SUMONE: A Simple and Efficient Summarizer for Plug-and-Play Agent Memory

author.name: Jizhe Zhang, Ang Li, Chenheng Zhang, Yisen Wang

entry.summary: Presents SumOne, a standalone agent-memory summarizer trained via masked trajectory reconstruction with a frozen reconstructor, using reconstruction quality plus a length penalty as a task-agnostic GRPO reward. This self-supervised approach decouples memory compaction from specific downstream tasks or agents.

entry.title: BEAKER: An Expert-Curated Benchmark for Embodied Brains in Self-Driving Chemical Laboratories

author.name: Fei Lin, Tengchao Zhang, Ziyang Gong, Xiaotong Yu, Bohan Zhang, Yifan Zhou, Qihao Yang, Ji Dai, Dong Li, Yining Jiang, Qinghua Ni, Jun Huang, Qiang Zhang, Yue Zhou, Zhihang Zhong, Yonglin Tian, Fei-Yue Wang, Xue Yang

entry.summary: BEAKER is an expert-curated benchmark of 1,000 question-answer samples evaluating multimodal LLMs as embodied brains for self-driving chemical laboratories, covering perception, reasoning, and action under physical, procedural, and safety constraints. It fills a gap left by prior benchmarks focused on safety or general scientific understanding. It targets execution-oriented embodied capabilities in autonomous chemistry.

entry.title: PEEK: One-Step-Look-Ahead Exposure Bias Correction for Diffusion Sampling

author.name: Yunwei Bai, Ying Kiat Tan, Tsuhan Chen

entry.summary: PEEK is a training-free deterministic sampler plugin that corrects exposure bias in diffusion image generation by performing a provisional one-step update, evaluating the denoiser at the look-ahead state, and interpolating predictions. This reduces the train-test mismatch between denoiser training assumptions and sampler conditions.

entry.title: BobFlow: Towards Human-Agent Collaborative Data Science Using Dataflows

author.name: Jiadong Bai, Yicong Huang, Chen Li

entry.summary: BobFlow is a system that uses dataflows as a shared computational abstraction for human-agent collaboration in data science, combining the dataflow representation with the ReAct paradigm so agents can iteratively construct and execute analyses. It aims to give agents a structure they can reason about while allowing human analysts to understand, guide, and modify the analysis, addressing the opacity of script-based agent outputs.

entry.title: Confucius4-R2T2: A Stable-Prefix Streaming ASR Model for Real Real-Time Transcription

author.name: Daniel Huang, Qi He, Shaoxiong Duan, Yingjie Li, Qiao Cheng, Yitao Duan

entry.summary: Confucius4-R2T2 is a streaming ASR model built by post-training Qwen3-ASR-1.7B on 1,500 hours of Chinese and English audio so that it never revises earlier output tokens, which matters for machine consumers like voice agents. The authors introduce the Longest Stable Prefix notion, proving monotonicity and consistency properties that underpin the training approach.

entry.title: Touch\'{e}World tech report : Towards Online Unified Camera--Hand Exploration in Generative Worlds

author.name: Jiaao Yu, Yanjian Zhang, Haoyang Jiang, Guillaume Wisniewski, Nadi Tomeh, Shijie Jia

entry.summary: TouchéWorld extends camera-controlled video world models by adding gesture-driven hand interaction, letting users explore generated environments while simultaneously manipulating objects and people via temporally aligned camera and hand controls. The authors build joint camera-hand training data from heterogeneous egocentric videos using annotation completion, consistency-based filtering, and temporal alignment, then fine-tune a pretrained world model to accept both action channels. This points toward richer, embodied-style interaction in generative worlds beyond passive navigation.

entry.title: Conformal Prediction for Distribution-to-Distribution Regression

author.name: Trung-Khang Tran, Tuan A. Hoang, Viet-Hoang Tran, Tan M. Nguyen

entry.summary: This paper extends Split Conformal Prediction to distribution-to-distribution regression, where inputs and outputs are distributions. The authors show naive applications produce marginally valid but practically non-interpretable prediction sets, and propose methods yielding sets with well-defined volume and tractable sampling while retaining coverage guarantees.

entry.title: Don't Replace, Complement: A Detector-Agnostic Subspace Signal for Near-OOD Detection

author.name: Wonseok Shin, Songkuk Kim

entry.summary: This paper introduces PLUS, a per-class low-dimensional subspace signal designed specifically for near-OOD detection, arguing that far-OOD and near-OOD settings require fundamentally different signals because near-OOD inputs activate class-characteristic feature directions much like in-distribution samples. Rather than replacing existing detectors, PLUS is positioned as a complementary signal that can be added to detectors that already saturate far-OOD performance. This addresses a well-known weakness in post-hoc OOD detection.

entry.title: Probabilistic Steering of Generative Priors for Lab-in-the-Loop Antibody Optimization

author.name: Anisha Parsan, Sebastian Ober, Calvin McCarter, Nick Bhattacharya, Hunter Elliott

entry.summary: This work unifies the discovery and optimization stages of therapeutic antibody development by smoothly transitioning a generative structure model into probabilistic black-box optimization, with the handoff guided by posterior uncertainty of a probabilistic surrogate. The approach improves optimization efficiency in the low-data (low-N) regime relevant to wet-lab-in-the-loop settings.

entry.title: Decision Transformer with Task-Aware Representations for Offline Meta-Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Xinbo Zhao, Yuhang Liu, Xin Zhang, Lei Le, Zhaohan Xi, Yingxue Zhang

entry.summary: Proposes CoTA-DT, a Decision Transformer framework for offline meta-RL that learns latent task representations by combining contrastive learning from trajectories, alignment with natural-language task descriptions, task-conditioned world-model supervision, and Q-function supervision. The representations guide policy generation for better generalization across tasks.

entry.title: CANDO: Conservative Action-Noise Directional Optimization for Residual Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Zeyu Gao, Chengkai Hou, Chaoyue Li, Zhuangzhe Wu, Jiaming Liu, Yao Mu, Peng Jia, Li Zhang, Shanghang Zhang

entry.summary: CANDO is a noise-space residual RL method for adapting frozen generative policies (e.g., for robot control) without destroying structure learned from offline demonstrations. Unlike existing noise-space methods with fixed latent feasible regions, CANDO uses conservative directional optimization of noise edits, combining the preservation benefits of noise-space residual methods with improved sample efficiency. The work targets the important problem of fine-tuning pretrained generative policies for robotics.

entry.title: Does LinUCB Need Valid Confidence Sets?

author.name: Ahmed Ben Yahmed, Marc Abeille, David Janz, Cl\'ement Calauz\`enes

entry.summary: The paper proves that replacing LinUCB's confidence width with any fixed positive constant preserves sublinear regret when the action set is smooth and strongly convex, showing valid confidence sets are not necessary for LinUCB's success. The mechanism is that action-set curvature drives exploration in all directions even without guaranteed optimism, analyzed via a novel logarithmically capped spectral potential yielding eigenvalue lower bounds on the design matrix. This reframes why contextual bandit algorithms work.

entry.title: Surrogate Models for Stochastic Al-Cu Phase-Field Solidification

author.name: Simon Savukoski, Tatu Pinomaa

entry.summary: The paper introduces a variance-preserving denoising diffusion bridge model (VP-DDBM) as a surrogate for autoregressive prediction of 2D Al-Cu alloy solidification microstructure, conditioned on phase, concentration, and temperature fields. Across held-out thermal gradients it outperforms deterministic U-Net and SI-ConvNeXt baselines on long-horizon errors and preserves fine dendritic structure. It enables stochastic ensembles and long trajectories that are computationally prohibitive with direct phase-field simulation.

entry.title: Density-Aware Reward Scaling: A Reinforcement Learning Framework for Reward-Proportional Sampling

author.name: Ria Shekhawat, Abhijeet Sinha, Yingtao Zhu, Dianbo Liu

entry.summary: This paper introduces Density-Aware Reward Scaling (DARS), a reward-processing mechanism that promotes reward-proportional sampling in continuous outcome spaces by inversely scaling rewards according to local outcome density estimated within on-policy rollout groups. The method preserves standard policy-gradient training and requires no learned density model, critic, or auxiliary objective. Experiments on multimodal navigation tasks show DARS-GRPO avoids collapsing onto a single high-reward solution.

entry.title: Exact Selective Inference for Spectral Clustering via Piecewise-Constant Graph Perturbation

author.name: Naotoshi Nakamura

entry.summary: This paper develops exact selective inference for spectral clustering on epsilon- and k-nearest-neighbor graphs, showing that along the one-dimensional perturbation of the truncated-chi selective test, graph changes occur only at finitely many roots. This makes conditioning on the clustering event tractable, yielding valid p-values that correct for the double use of data in clustering and testing.

entry.title: Fairness Metrics based on the AUC in Clinical Predictive AI

author.name: Jo\~ao Matos, Ben Van Calster, Richard D. Riley, Paula Dhiman, Gary S. Collins

entry.summary: This paper examines eight AUC-based fairness metrics used to evaluate clinical prediction models, highlighting that the AUC is non-collapsible so subgroup and overall values are not directly comparable as often assumed. It provides guidance on how these fairness metrics should be interpreted in clinical AI settings. This matters because flawed fairness assessments can lead to misleading conclusions about model equity in healthcare.

entry.title: De Rham cohomological architectures for PINNs and PDEs with topological holes

author.name: Andrew Gracyk

entry.summary: This paper addresses failure modes of physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) in domains with topological pathologies such as holes, punctures, and poles. The author proposes Hodge-de Rham PINNs, which parameterize 1-forms using the Hodge-Morrey-Friedrichs decomposition for manifolds with boundary, connecting the architecture to de Rham cohomology to handle discontinuous interfaces and path-dependent integration errors. This brings differential-geometric structure into scientific machine learning, potentially improving PDE solvers on multiply-connected domains.

entry.title: From Forecasting to Feedback: Evaluating Learned Dynamics for Tokamak Control

author.name: Guoyang Shi, Siqi Ding, Xuanhe Wang, Pei Guo, Changquan Yu, Jiale Hu, Jiayi Zhi, Zhengyuan Chen, Jianguo Chen, Tianyuan Liu

entry.summary: This paper studies the gap between offline forecasting accuracy and closed-loop control performance for learned dynamics models in tokamak magnetic control. Using a calibrated free-boundary Grad-Shafranov solver, the authors generate four datasets and train 16 action-conditioned Transformers at varying rollout budgets, then evaluate PPO policies optimized in the learned surrogates on unseen reference scenarios. The work highlights how feedback loops can amplify surrogate model errors in high-stakes physical control settings.

entry.title: Learning Almost Complex and Complex Structures

author.name: Edward Hirst, Tancredi Schettini Gherardini, Tom\'as S. R. Silva, Jakob Stein

entry.summary: The authors use neural networks and polynomial features, trained without target supervision, to numerically construct almost complex and complex structures on spheres and sphere products up to dimension six. Their approach passes admissibility checks on all nine admissible examples and correctly rejects the topologically obstructed S^4, demonstrating ML as a discovery tool in differential geometry.

entry.title: Language Model Augmented Decision Transformer for Multi-Task Offline Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Xinbo Zhao, Yuhang Liu, Xin Zhang, Lei Le, Zhaohan Xi, Yu Yang, Yingxue Zhang

entry.summary: LaMA-DT is a unified sequence-modeling framework that uses a single LLM for both trajectory augmentation and multi-task policy learning in offline multi-task RL, guided by natural-language task descriptions. It employs supervised generation and alignment objectives plus a scoring-and-filtering mechanism to address per-task data scarcity and cross-task generalization.

entry.title: Forgetting to Improve: Principled Data Removal in Active Learning

author.name: Manuel Wendl, Erik Englesson, Andreas Krause, Carl Henrik Ek

entry.summary: The authors propose a method that incorporates the downstream task into Gaussian process modeling by principled removal of data that harms the model under mismatch conditions. They derive an influence function for GP models enabling task-aware data deletion, challenging the assumption that more data always helps aleatoric/epistemic uncertainty quantification.

entry.title: SWAP-INR: Implicit Neural Representation with Switchable Attention Paths for Time-varying Multivariate Scientific Data Compression

author.name: Hyunsoo Son, Jeonghyun Noh, Chaoli Wang, Won-Ki Jeong

entry.summary: Proposes SWAP-INR, an implicit neural representation architecture for high-fidelity lossy compression of large multivariate, time-varying scientific simulation data. It introduces a switchable attention path module that explicitly models cross-variable interactions and adapts to diverse spectral characteristics of physical variables, addressing storage bottlenecks in high-performance computing.

entry.title: MiCaDe: Online LiDAR-Camera Miscalibration Change Detection for Autonomous Driving

author.name: Carlo Sgaravatti, Riccardo Pieroni, Matteo Corno, Sergio M. Savaresi, Luca Magri, Giacomo Boracchi

entry.summary: Proposes MiCaDe, an online method that detects when extrinsic LiDAR-camera calibration has drifted using sequential change detection on discrepancies between 3D and 2D bounding boxes, requiring no calibration targets or changes to the perception stack. It achieves low false-alarm rates with negligible computational overhead, addressing safety-critical calibration drift in long-term autonomous vehicle deployments.

entry.title: Perturb, Repair, Verify: Self-Play Vision-Language Verifiers for Compositional Understanding

author.name: Zijun Huang, Yingjun Du, Cees G. M. Snoek

entry.summary: PROVE is a self-play framework that trains vision-language verifiers through a closed perturb-verify-repair-verify loop, eliminating dependence on external teacher judges or curated hard negatives. A mutator injects typed errors into correct image-caption pairs over objects, attributes, counts, and relations, and the verifier learns to detect and explain them.

entry.title: Rewrite, Then Veto: Rewriter-Agnostic Edit Gating for LLM-Based Post-OCR Correction

author.name: Jorge Ram\'on Fonseca Cacho

entry.summary: This paper introduces EditVeto, a small 0.6B-parameter gate that vets edits proposed by a full-context LLM rewrite of noisy OCR transcripts, keeping or reverting character-aligned edit blocks. Oracle analysis shows vetoing a full rewrite beats per-span generation given true error locations, and the frozen gate improves all five tested rewriters, including two unseen during training, on eight HIPE-OCRepair-2026 test sets. It matters because it offers a rewriter-agnostic safeguard against LLM overcorrection of historical text.

entry.title: Where Should a KV-Cache Repair Budget Go? Distractor Structure and Contextual Compatibility in Non-Prefix Reuse

author.name: Yuxing Peng, Zhiqing Tang, Weijia Jia

entry.summary: The paper analyzes when non-prefix KV-cache reuse fails, showing it loses 19-100% of context-dependent questions answerable by full prefill, with larger losses when surrounding chunks resemble the target. Because recoverable damage spreads across distractor chunks, a small repair budget is best spent recomputing the answer-bearing target against the reused cache. This yields actionable guidance for cache-reuse efficiency in RAG-style serving.

entry.title: LibriSpeech-Real-QA: A Benchmark for Streaming Question Answering

author.name: Zewen Zhan, Hui Lu, Xueyuan Chen, Huimeng Wang, Yikai Huang, Xixin Wu, Shiyin Kang, Bin Xia, Zhiyong Wu

entry.summary: This work presents a benchmark for real-time streaming speech interaction, where models must answer questions from continuously arriving audio chunks rather than complete recordings. It exposes that most speech LLMs operate offline and lack evaluation protocols for genuine streaming QA. Useful for the development of voice assistants and live transcription-interaction systems, an area where major labs are actively shipping products.

entry.title: SpecCompact: Accelerating LLM Agent Context Compaction with Slot-Parallel Semantic Speculative Verification

author.name: Yulu An, Yifei Feng, Xiangyang Yin
