entry.summary: SpecCompact accelerates agent context compaction using slot-parallel semantic speculation: a small fine-tuned drafter generates structured summary slots in parallel, which the target model verifies and repairs, cutting latency while retaining information. This targets a real latency bottleneck as agent histories grow. Useful systems work complementary to the growing compaction literature.

entry.title: From Tokens to Trajectories: Parameter-Efficient Continuous Adaptation of Unified Multimodal Models

author.name: Gayatri Deshmukh, Onkar Susladkar, Adheesh Juvekar, Halil Kilicoglu, Ismini Lourentzou

entry.summary: FlowShift is a parameter-efficient post-training framework that converts pre-trained unified multimodal models from discrete tokenization to continuous rectified-flow generators, bypassing the quantization bottleneck that degrades fine visual detail. It retains the backbone's semantic priors via LoRA on attention layers with continuous latent projections, and uses Dual-Objective Velocity Vector Distillation to boost visual quality without semantic drift.

entry.title: C-WFDM: A ControlNet-Guided Wavelet-Fusion Diffusion Model for Multimodal Brain MRI Completion

author.name: Muhammad Nabi Yasinzai, Remika Mito, Mangor Pedersen

entry.summary: C-WFDM synthesizes missing brain MRI modalities (T2w, FLAIR, T1Gd) from available contrasts using a ControlNet-guided diffusion model with wavelet fusion. It targets the uneven modality availability across pooled neuroimaging datasets that hampers downstream AI applications.

entry.title: Spatially and Compositionally Controlled Multimodal Glioblastoma MRI Synthesis with Latent Diffusion

author.name: Steven Glass, Max Van Puyvelde, Marija Pizurica, Mia Meyer, Olivier Gevaert, Willie Brink

entry.summary: This paper proposes a two-stage latent diffusion framework for generating controllable glioblastoma MRI scans: one model creates tumor segmentation maps conditioned on location and composition, and a second modality-conditioned diffusion model with ControlNet renders consistent T1, T1Gd, T2, and FLAIR images. The approach addresses dataset imbalance in clinical neuro-oncology imaging. Generated segmentations show low centroid and subregion proportion errors on held-out data.

entry.title: Semantic Residual Vector Quantization for Sign Language Generation

author.name: Chang Liu, Ke Han, Niccol\`o Biondi, Gloria Isotton, Elisa Ricci, Davide Talon, Nicu Sebe

entry.summary: SRVQ frames sign language generation as a two-level process from semantics to kinematics, using a semantic residual vector quantizer to give the generator an explicit text-aligned intermediate target for what to sign before refining how to sign it. This disentangles lexical content from fine articulation such as handshape, trajectory, and facial expression, which prior pose-based and reconstruction-only tokenizers entangle.

entry.title: AgentCount: An Agentic Workflow for Traceable Colony Counting and Insight Generation from Agar Plate Images

author.name: Zhuosheng Liu, Austin E. Weber

entry.summary: AgentCount is an open-source agentic pipeline for automated colony counting from agar plate images, using seven specialized agents for quality control, plate localization, colony detection (via SAM 3), counting, CFU calculation, validation, and reporting. Its key contribution is traceability: the final count keeps a record of which objects were included, addressing a major reproducibility gap in manual microbiology workflows.

entry.title: Closed-Loop Adaptive Sampling on a Generative Ocean Model

author.name: Shayesteh Hafezi, Alan Papalia

entry.summary: The paper develops a multi-robot closed-loop adaptive sampling framework that uses learned generative ocean models, which produce fast high-resolution forecasts and ensembles but lack the explicit uncertainty representations assumed by classical informative planning. The work bridges this gap to direct mobile robots toward maximally informative measurements of an evolving ocean environment.

entry.title: FWIK: Multi-Waypoint IK Selection via Lookahead Graph Search

author.name: Jinglan Cao, Guohui Zhong, Chengwei Zhang

entry.summary: This paper introduces Future-Window Inverse Kinematics (FWIK), an online method for selecting inverse kinematics solutions for redundant robot arms by considering a window of future waypoints rather than optimizing one waypoint at a time. It builds a layered joint-space graph of IK candidates, ranks paths with motion-time estimates, and uses a learned model to prune self-collision-prone transitions. This matters because myopic IK selection can increase motion time or cause downstream planning failures in multi-waypoint tasks.

entry.title: Dynamic Shape Control of Soft Trunk Robots

author.name: Hehui Zheng, Marc Stampanoni, Roshan S. Kaundinya, Ronan Hinchet, George Haller, Robert K. Katzschmann

entry.summary: The authors extend adiabatic spectral submanifold (aSSM) model-based control to whole-shape-profile control of helicoid soft trunk robots, learning an aSSM model to handle the high nonlinearity of these compliant manipulators. Whereas prior aSSM work achieved accurate end-effector tracking, this enables control of the full shape profile, expanding workspace access in complex regions. The combination of structured control theory with learned models for soft robots is the core contribution.

entry.title: When to Ask for Help: Uncertainty-Triggered Aerial Refinement for Off-Road Navigation

author.name: Pranay Samineni, Adam Thorpe, John Chubick, Anand Balakrishnan, Christian Ellis, Swarat Chaudhuri, Ufuk Topcu

entry.summary: The paper introduces a planner-conditioned air-ground assistance method where a UGV's MPPI rollouts determine when aerial sensing is needed and which map layer a UAV should measure. By scoring rollouts under resolved map hypotheses and requesting the highest-utility aerial measurement, the system avoids fixed support roles and improves off-road navigation in heterogeneous air-ground teams.

entry.title: A Unified Framework for Training-Dataset Aggregation and Exact Machine Unlearning via Gibbs Probability Measures

author.name: Yaiza Bermudez, Samir M. Perlaza, I\~naki Esnaola

entry.summary: The authors study renormalization, normalized log-linear combination, and nesting of Gibbs probability measures, showing the results are themselves Gibbs measures and characterizing them as solutions to entropy-regularized optimization problems. A central result applies these operations to give a unified treatment of dataset aggregation and exact machine unlearning, with geometric interpretations via Pythagorean identities.

entry.title: Discovering like a scientist: Literature-informed dimensionless learning for physical closure of data-driven equations

author.name: Hao Xu, Tianhao Wu, Dongxiao Zhang

entry.summary: This paper introduces pi-former, a knowledge-guided transformer trained on 1,288 established dimensionless groups that learns variable association and exponent assignment patterns to propose interpretable dimensionless groups under exact dimensional constraints. The framework explains how data-driven equation coefficients vary across operating conditions and identifies predictive dimensionless numbers across seven physical problems.

entry.title: Ai2 and Google collaborate on a new generation of climate models

author.name: Unknown

entry.summary: Ai2 announces a partnership funded by Google.org with technical support from Google Research to develop NeuralGCM+, an open-source model combining physics-based simulation with AI to jointly model atmosphere and ocean for faster, more reliable long-term climate projections. Open sourcing is positioned as a way to broaden access to climate modeling capability.

entry.title: Iterated creation, grading, and revision of data science projects by language models

author.name: Rohan Alexander

entry.summary: This empirical study has writer models create complete data science projects that are graded and revised over three rounds across 49 writer-grader pairs from seven models from five developers including Anthropic, OpenAI, Google, DeepSeek, and Z.AI. Of 147 initial submissions only 107 ran and rendered, and average scores improved with iterative feedback.

entry.title: Autonomous agents for electricity-system planning

author.name: Yoon Pyo Lee, Samrendra Roy, Jay Phil Yoo, Kazuma Kobayashi, Souvik Chakraborty, Syed Bahauddin Alam

entry.summary: The paper presents an autonomous agent framework for electricity-system planning that loops through proposal, numerical evaluation, feedback interpretation, redesign, and final selection, automatically executing investment-and-dispatch optimizations and feeder verification with fixed acceptance criteria. It evaluates forty carbon-constrained planning trajectories. It demonstrates agentic workflows applied to a substantive real-world engineering domain.

entry.title: EnzymeRSI: A dual-loop recursive self-improvement system for enzyme design

author.name: Genoria AI Team, Yuejie Hou, Lixiang Yang, Yisi Liu, Weiting Tang, Yueyuxiao Yang, Meng Yang

entry.summary: Presents EnzymeRSI, a dual-loop recursive self-improvement system for enzyme engineering where an outer loop evolves harness assets without weight updates and an inner loop develops prediction algorithms, with a cloud lab specified to close the physical loop. The outer loop improved mean Spearman correlation on ProteinGym by 0.044 across five tasks.

entry.title: Objective-Conditioned Active Preference Learning for Multi-Objective Alignment

author.name: Duc Anh Vu, Thong Nguyen, Hoang Pham, Ponhvoan Srey, Luu Anh Tuan

entry.summary: OGC-DPO is an active learning framework for multi-objective LLM alignment that treats each (response pair, objective) combination as a separate query and uses gradient coverage to select maximally informative comparisons, reducing annotation cost that otherwise grows linearly with the number of objectives. It also treats conflicting preferences as informative rather than discarding them.

entry.title: Pairing Expert Critique with LLM-Driven Refinement: An Iterative Approach for Curating Quality AI Evaluation Datasets

author.name: Honson Ling, Kidus Admassu, Stephanie Rosenthal

entry.summary: The paper presents SME-C, a human-AI workflow where subject matter experts give lightweight critiques of candidate LLM responses and an LLM iteratively refines datasets and evaluation rubrics from that feedback. It is validated in financial business briefs with 3,853 critiques from 411 finance professionals across two survey rounds. This addresses the bottleneck of expensive expert authoring for high-quality evaluation data.

entry.title: Traffic-VL: Reinforced Vision-Language Models for Generalizable End-to-End Traffic Signal Control

author.name: Xingchen Zou, Maonan Wang, Kemou Jiang, Jie Li, Yiqi Chen, Xi Chen, Hai Yang, Yuxuan Liang

entry.summary: The paper introduces SynTra-V, a pipeline converting physics-based traffic simulations into photorealistic multi-view surveillance imagery with semantic auditing, and Traffic-VL, a vision-language model trained with reinforcement learning for end-to-end traffic signal control from raw camera views. This bridges the gap between perception and control decisions without idealized intermediate representations.

entry.title: TailSteer: Trajectory-Tail Steering for Drift-Resistant Multi-turn Image Editing

author.name: Ruikang Li, Zixuan Chen, Jiarui Wu, Mingde Yao, Yiyuan Zhang, Yujin Wang, Hanming Deng, Lewei Lu, Tianfan Xue

entry.summary: TailSteer is a final-stage training framework that improves multi-turn image editing robustness by preventing small unintended changes from accumulating into severe visual drift across turns. The method keeps early denoising dynamics close to the base model while concentrating preservation efforts in the final stage, avoiding costly multi-turn retraining or hard-to-scale inference mechanisms. This targets a real reliability gap in foundation image-editing models.

entry.title: RAPID: Increasing Efficiency of Internal Distillation via Randomized Methods

author.name: Ryan Swift, Konstantinos Psounis

entry.summary: Tackles the inefficiency in internal (activation-level) knowledge distillation caused by learnable projection matrices that map teacher representations into smaller student spaces and are discarded after training. RAPID replaces these with randomized projection methods, reducing training cost while preserving distillation quality.

entry.title: Policy Network Diffusion

author.name: Jiate Liu, Deheng Ye

entry.summary: The paper explores whether diffusion models can generate the parameters of reinforcement learning policy networks, proposing DPPG: a Transformer-based autoencoder that compresses patchified network parameters plus a task-conditioned diffusion model that generates parameters for different environments. Experiments suggest a single unified generator can produce policy networks that generalize across tasks. This connects generative modeling to zero-shot policy synthesis.

entry.title: Sheaf-MPNN: A Library for Sheaf Neural Networks as Message Passing

author.name: Alessio Borgi, Mario Severino, Luke Braithwaite, Steve Azzolin, R\'emi Bourgerie, Olga Zaghen, Emanuele Mule, Riccardo Ali, Leo Minh Kustermann, Edoardo Coppola, Antonio Purificato, Stefano Fiorini, Christopher Irwin, Filippo Spiga, Fabrizio Silvestri, Michael Bronstein, Pietro Li\`o

entry.summary: Sheaf-MPNN is a PyTorch Geometric library that reformulates sheaf neural network diffusion as local, incidence-wise message passing instead of explicitly assembling a global sparse sheaf Laplacian block matrix. This removes memory and computational overheads that hinder scalability of existing sheaf implementations while retaining the ability to learn per-node/edge feature spaces and restriction maps. A credible author team (including Bronstein and Liò) contributes an engineering contribution likely to accelerate adoption of sheaf-based GNNs.

entry.title: Deep Neural Operator Learning for stochastic heat equations and applications

author.name: Hengrong Du, Qi Feng, Weinan Wang

entry.summary: The paper proves a universal approximation theorem for solution operators of semilinear stochastic heat equations in dimension d at least 2, extending neural operator approximation theory to SPDEs with distribution-valued Gaussian forcing. A Fourier cutoff reduces the forcing to finitely many measurements, with Besov and Schauder estimates controlling solution error, and ReLU branch networks with grid-based trunk functions approximate the finite-dimensional solution map with explicit bounds. For linear cases the reduction matches Wiener chaos truncation.

entry.title: Towards an Optimal Control Foundation of Early Exits - Turnpikes and ResNets

author.name: Jens P\"uttschneider, Simon Heilig, Asja Fischer, Timm Faulwasser

entry.summary: Using optimal control theory, the paper proves that ResNets trained with joint output and intermediate-layer losses exhibit the turnpike phenomenon: the layers needed to reach a prescribed loss level are bounded independently of network depth. This yields structural similarity across internal representations and provides a principled foundation for early-exit inference.

entry.title: NovoCRF: Globally Normalized De Novo Peptide Sequencing on a Prefix-Mass Lattice

author.name: Rui Qiao, Lei Xin, Baozhen Shan

entry.summary: NovoCRF formulates de novo peptide sequencing as a conditional random field over a prefix-mass lattice, so its paths exactly correspond to peptides within the precursor mass tolerance, trained with global normalization over all mass-feasible peptides. It claims to be the first de novo method with exact normalization and uses a modular three-component software design. This offers an interpretable, principled alternative to end-to-end transformers in proteomics.

entry.title: Where Do Distilled Students Store Thinking?

author.name: Taeyeong Kim, Jaemin Jung, Ahhyun Kim, Unggi Lee

entry.summary: This paper investigates how reasoning behavior is stored in weight-space when small student models are distilled from long-reasoning teachers with interpolated solution lengths. Analyzing LoRA adapter subspaces across multiple teacher-student pairs, it identifies a shared subspace tied to thinking-like behavior (reflective markers, monologue format, long solutions) and locates where adapter updates shift when teachers stop thinking.

entry.title: GSBR: Geometric Support Behavior Regularization for Online RL

author.name: Charles Xu, Jacob Berg, Liyiming Ke, Sergey Levine

entry.summary: GSBR is a regularizer for online reinforcement learning that anchors behavior to a pretrained diffusion or flow-matching base policy using a geometric support constraint that is neither as restrictive as behavioral cloning nor as blunt as hard support limits. It aims to preserve the sample-efficiency benefits of regularization while allowing the policy to improve beyond suboptimal base-policy modes.

entry.title: When Every Choice Is Correct: A Causal Study of Numerical Preference in Language Models

author.name: Hongnian Huang, Hongliang Liu

entry.summary: Using numerical choice among equally valid integers as a probe, this study traces how preference is processed across layers and tokens via perturbation probing, gradient attribution, and activation interventions in Qwen3-4B. Interventions show pre-answer edits shift the selected number and attention-head replacements trace continuing influence on subsequent digit emission. It offers a clean causal lens on internal preference formation.

entry.title: How Far Can You Steer? Behavior-Capability Frontiers in Contrastive Activation Addition

author.name: Deepanshu Raj

entry.summary: This paper studies Contrastive Activation Addition (CAA) steering through a behavior-capability frontier, selecting interventions that maximize behavioral change subject to explicit bounds on capability degradation (1-5 percentage points) across four instruction-tuned models and seven behaviors. It finds validation-selected steering effects generalize strongly, framing usability of steering in terms of capability cost. A useful quantitative lens on activation steering safety and practicality.

entry.title: Lesion Overlap Ranks PET Segmentation Models but Does Not Certify Patient-Level Tumor Burden

author.name: Tushar Kataria, Gerald Sabin, Ponnuswamy Sadayappan, Shireen Y. Elhabian

entry.summary: This study examines whether Dice-style overlap metrics reliably certify patient-level metabolic tumor volume (MTV) estimates from automated PET segmentation, using 1,014 autoPET FDG PET/CT studies plus PSMA validation. Interestingly, rankings by mean Dice exactly match rankings by lower relative MTV error, yet overlap performance does not guarantee individual-patient burden reliability. The work calls for burden-oriented evaluation in clinical deployment.

entry.title: DualCast: Dual-Image Conditioned Diffusion Transformers for Digital Human E-Commerce Video Generation

author.name: Lifan Jiang, Yibo Zhao, Senlin Cheng, Bolei Xu, Xiaobo Li, Can Ye, Dehai Zhao, Deng Cai, Boxi Wu

entry.summary: DualCast is a role-addressed dual-image conditioning framework for digital human e-commerce video generation that explicitly separates the roles of product reference and human presenter. This reduces role ambiguity, product distortion, identity drift, and single-reference collapse in diffusion-transformer video generation.

entry.title: CLEAR: Color-Texture Latent Alignment for Single Image Reflection Removal

author.name: Tu Vo, Sheir A. Zaheer, Chan Y. Park

entry.summary: CLEAR is a diffusion-based single-image reflection removal method that avoids reusing degraded-input skip connections, since reflections form a second structured layer whose edges re-enter the output through naive high-frequency feature reuse. It uses color-texture latent alignment to mitigate color drift and detail loss.

entry.title: Coupled Scene Graph Anticipation: When With-Constraint Recall Hides Structural Inconsistency

author.name: Zeno Nongmaithem, Anushttha Srivastava, Anshit Sinha, Apoorv Sisodia, Suman Chowdhury, Prerana Mukherjee, Rajesh P. Barnwal

entry.summary: CoupledSGA links subject-object relationships through a Relationship Interaction Graph with graph attention inside the Neural ODE vector field and adds a structural consistency loss over mutually exclusive predicates, preventing contradictory predictions like simultaneous sitting on and standing on. The paper also exposes a flaw in the standard with-constraint evaluation protocol that can hide structural inconsistency.

entry.title: OUCH: Objective, Uniform, Controlled Haptic Stimulation for Automated Neurological Assessment

author.name: Sherry Choi, Sitao Sunny Li, Joseph Romero, Lillian Chin, Ashwin G. Ramayya, Allison M. Okamura, Ava Chen

entry.summary: OUCH is a wrist-worn pneumatic device delivering standardized noxious mechanical stimuli for neurological assessment of patients with disorders of consciousness, replacing highly variable manual bedside stimulation. The device uses stacked pneumatic pouch actuators with a buckling compliant spacer so the indenter contacts skin only during actuation, characterized via blocked force tests, clinician evaluation, and finite element analysis.

entry.title: LumiTac: Compact, High-Rate Six-Axis Optical Tactile Sensing for Human-Robot Interaction

author.name: Hao Wu, Haotian Guo, Yu Feng, Yutong Wang, Jianshu Zhou

entry.summary: LumiTac is a camera-free optoelectronic tactile sensor that measures six-axis loads (force and torque) using five photoemitters and five RGBW photoreceivers coupled through translucent silicone, with spectral encoding of the light field. The sensing head is 12 mm in diameter, under 2 g, and costs roughly 7 USD, with a small MLP performing online reconstruction. This offers a low-cost, compact route to six-axis tactile feedback for human-robot interaction.

entry.title: Detecting Silent Action-Interface Mismatch with Calibrated Relational World Models

author.name: Rui Zhu, Xurui Li, Haixu Tang

entry.summary: This paper studies offline detection of silent robot action-interface mismatches—permuted axes, inverted signs, rescaled rotations, reversed gripper polarity—using learned state-action-effect relations as calibrated contracts. Clean held-out transitions calibrate alarms at a controlled false-positive rate, and a fixed inverse vocabulary supports closed-set localization of the mismatched field. On LIBERO Spatial tasks, a conditional Gaussian-mixture score achieves 65.7% recall at a 2.5% false-positive rate, outperforming simpler residual scores.

entry.title: Balance-Guided Forest for Causal Effect Estimation

author.name: Feiyang Yi, Jelena Bradic

entry.summary: Balance-Guided Forest (BGF) improves forest-kernel balancing for causal effect estimation by using current balancing weights to guide subsequent tree construction, via a splitting score combining residual imbalance with outcome contrast. This avoids wasting tree capacity on already well-balanced features, a mismatch in prior two-stage approaches.

entry.title: Separation Is a Riesz Energy: How Many Environments Does ICA Need?

author.name: Yuda Bi, Yubo Guo, Jiaxiao Cai, Xiaonai Li, Zhuolin Li, Vince D. Calhoun

entry.summary: This work shows that Gaussian independent components can be recovered when their variances vary across environments, and quantifies the cost: separating component j requires sample size scaling with the Riesz 2-energy of its variance signature across environments. The authors prove minimax lower bounds for joint diagonalization of K covariances and give a spectral estimator achieving these rates.

entry.title: Uncertainty-Aware Resource Orchestration for Agentic AI Systems

author.name: Masoud Shokrnezhad, Tarik Taleb

entry.summary: This work addresses the fact that LLM agent pipelines have unpredictable, heavy-tailed compute, bandwidth, and latency demands that emerge only at runtime, creating a provisioning dilemma. It proposes an uncertainty-aware orchestration framework for allocating resources to agentic workloads whose structure differs fundamentally from fixed classical workflow graphs.

entry.title: EchoKV: Self-Corrective KV Cache Eviction via Iterative Query Feedback

author.name: JianKun Zou, Tongtong Yuan

entry.summary: EchoKV identifies a failure mode in KV cache eviction where early workspace errors distort subsequent eviction queries, and introduces iterative self-correction using decode-generated queries to recover the workspace before remaining lookahead steps. It matches the forward-pass budget of prior methods (LAQ) while adding tensor re-scoring. Targeted at long-context inference efficiency.

entry.title: A Systematic Benchmark for Evaluating Multimodal Personalized Reasoning of Vision-Language Models

author.name: Dohyun Kim, Junyong Lhim, Kwanyong Park

entry.summary: Introduces MPRBench, a benchmark with 12 sub-tasks for evaluating multimodal personalized reasoning in vision-language models, reasoning over heterogeneous personal information with interpretable error analysis. Experiments show current personalized MLLMs struggle with accurate recognition of personal details and holistic reasoning.

entry.title: MA-Mesh: Resilient Multi-Agent Collaboration via Role-based Self-Healing

author.name: JunYong Lee, Woo Kyung Kim, Honguk Woo

entry.summary: Introduces MA-Mesh, a framework adding a role-based self-healing layer to multi-agent collaboration, generating resilience-aware specifications compiled into executable policy code. It includes cross-agent reflection, where agents evaluate each other's outputs, for systematic runtime robustness management.

entry.title: On Turn-Level Best-of-N Sampling for Scaling LLM Agents

author.name: Jalaj Bhandari, Dhawal Gupta, Hongli Zhan, Zhenting Wang, Varad Pimpalkhute, Zhengzhong Liu, Eric Xing, Rupesh Srivastava

entry.summary: The paper evaluates turn-level best-of-N sampling for LLM agents on long-horizon tasks using a generator-selector framework where a selector model picks among N candidate actions each turn. It tests whether off-the-shelf open-weight LLMs can compare candidate actions directly, distinguishing itself from prior critic-guided search work. It offers practical insights into inference-time scaling for agents.

entry.title: CAST-Bench: Tracing Every Sound to Its Source in Multi-Shot Audio-Video Generation

author.name: Yucong Liu, Qi Tian, Shuyuan Tu, Kaihang Pan, Weijie Kong, Chao Pan

entry.summary: CAST-Bench formulates text-to-audio-video generation correctness as an audiovisual contract requiring each requested sound to be emitted by the right source, synchronized with the visual action, in multi-shot generation. It enables diagnosing missing sounds, wrong-source attribution, and cross-shot sound loss, which prior benchmarks do not separate.

entry.title: Discarded or Unreachable? Diagnosing and Repairing Spatial Relation Failure in Vision--Language Similarity

author.name: Mahdi Mostajabdaveh, Zirui Zhou

entry.summary: This diagnostic study shows that near-chance left/right relation scores in contrastive vision-language models have two distinct causes calling for opposite fixes: pooling may discard the relation while dense features retain it, or the relation may be linearly decodable in the pooled vector yet unreachable by native similarity scoring. Across ten encoders, lateral polarity is decodable at 0.77-0.99 while nine of ten remain at chance under native scoring on a million-caption search.

entry.title: BAM: Bivariate Additive Models for Interpretable Tabular Prediction

author.name: Atsushi Koike

entry.summary: BAM is a class of generalized additive models with pairwise interactions in which each pairwise shape function is constrained to a simple parametric form, ensuring shape functions are genuinely interpretable and auditable against domain knowledge, unlike the irregular contours produced by EBM or NODE-GAM. The paper argues that such simplification can match standard GAM accuracy if the right feature pairs are captured. This raises the bar for glass-box interpretability in tabular prediction.

entry.title: Editing Large Language Models with Geometry-Aware Regularization

author.name: Bingqing Liu, Wei Liu, Jun Wang, Xiaobo Sun, Yuhua Li, Ruixuan Li

entry.summary: GEdit is a knowledge editing framework built on a Low-Rank Plus Diagonal factorization of Transformer FFN representations that uses geometry to distinguish core knowledge to preserve and hard edits to handle. Its low-rank regularization protects a core knowledge subspace while a complementary mechanism addresses difficult edits.

entry.title: Quo Vadis, Driving Scene Reconstruction? Occlusion-Aware Gaussian Densification

author.name: Dung Do Tien, Kien Nguyen Do Trung, Kiet Dang Vu, Trung Thai Tran, Duc Dung Nguyen

entry.summary: OccSplat is a feed-forward 3D Gaussian Splatting framework for driving scene reconstruction that explicitly predicts new Gaussian primitives for regions occluded in the input view, completing missing scene geometry in 3D rather than inpainting missing pixels. This targets a fundamental weakness of single-observation feed-forward reconstruction for novel-view synthesis.

entry.title: IDSISA: Influence-Distilled Sharded Training for Efficient Machine Unlearning

author.name: Deeraj SK, Sadhana Devarajan, Tanmoy Hazra, Anupam Shukla

entry.summary: IDSISA improves SISA-based machine unlearning by using influence functions to concentrate forget-prone samples into few shards and distillation from unaffected shards to recover utility lost to isolated retraining. The method retains SISA's certified deletion guarantee while reducing shard spread and utility degradation.

entry.title: Four Extensions of the Universal Law of Robustness: Log-Concave Covariates, Heterogeneous Mixtures, Vector-Valued Predictors, and Markovian Data

author.name: Tobias J. Peter (ZHAW Zurich University of Applied Sciences)

entry.summary: This paper extends Bubeck and Sellke's universal law of robustness, which relates overparameterization, noise level, and Lipschitz constants, by relaxing each of its major hypotheses: Gaussian concentration to exponential concentration (covering log-concave covariates), homogeneous covariate laws to heterogeneous mixtures, scalar to vector-valued predictors, and independent to Markovian samples. The results are stated at matching rates, with necessity results for some conditions. This strengthens the theoretical foundations connecting overparameterization and robust interpolation.

entry.title: Honest Small Decision Models for Finance: Scale, Specialization Collapse, and Mixed-Corpus Remediation

author.name: Ajitabh Kumar

entry.summary: The paper trains small System-1 decision models (0.8B-32B parameters) across two families including Qwen3.5/3.8, fine-tuned with a frozen LoRA recipe on finance decision corpora including a programmatic-gold policy corpus and a reality-labeled outcome corpus with walk-forward splits and a sealed 2026 test set. It quantifies specialization collapse, showing narrow fine-tuning costs 9-45 percentage points of general decision competence, and studies mixed-corpus remediation.

entry.title: The role of injected noise in diffusion model generalization

author.name: Vincent Emmerling, Felix G\"unther, David Kappel

entry.summary: The paper investigates why diffusion models trained on different datasets produce similar samples from the same initial noise, showing that noise injected during sampling is critical to this apparent generalization effect. It finds the impact of injected noise is largest in the intermediate sampling regime where broad structure exists but sample identity is not yet determined.

entry.title: StreamLTT: Risk Certification for Policy Selection under Stream Dependence

author.name: Jinwen Xu, Qin Lu

entry.summary: Extends the Learn-then-Test (LTT) risk-certification framework to sequential settings where losses are dependent and nonstationary, by certifying average predictable risk conditioned on observed history. Conditional centering converts empirical deviations into a martingale sum, enabling variance-adaptive tests and finite-sample Hoeffding guarantees.

entry.title: Decomposing Rank Reversals under Temporal Nonstationarity: Alignment, Aggressiveness, and Instability

author.name: Deying Song, Xueying Ding

entry.summary: Provides a model-agnostic decomposition of out-of-sample R2 under temporal drift into target alignment, miscalibrated aggressiveness, and predictive instability, explaining why performance rankings reverse across training horizons. Derives complexity phase boundaries and closed-form optimal-memory equations for ridge regression, extending guarantees to complex architectures.

entry.title: Proper Agnostic Learning of Affine Halfspaces under Log-Concave Marginals

author.name: Zhijie Zheng

entry.summary: The paper gives a proper constant-factor agnostic learner for affine halfspaces under full-dimensional log-concave marginals, returning a single halfspace with error at most C*OPT plus epsilon for arbitrary binary labels. Sample and computation complexity are polynomial in dimension and inverse accuracy, without requiring knowledge of the marginal mean or covariance. The key geometric result compares global disagreement with disagreement on a balanced restriction for minority halfspaces.

entry.title: What Does It Mean to Remove an Edge? Intervention-Aware Fidelity for Graph Neural Network Explanations

author.name: Rocco Mattia Di Mauro, Marco Grassia, Giuseppe Mangioni

entry.summary: This work formalizes an ambiguity in GNN explanation evaluation: deletion fidelity can mean structural edge deletion (recomputing normalization and attention) or message suppression (blocking the message while keeping structure). The authors derive sufficient conditions under which the two interventions coincide, notably for additive message passing. The analysis improves the interpretability and rigor of how GNN explanations are benchmarked.

entry.title: Cool Graphs: Active Property Search Towards Quantum Nano-Refrigerators

author.name: Sofia Blyufer, Amir Kleiner, Uri Peskin

entry.summary: This paper couples a Graph Variational Autoencoder with an uncertainty-driven active learning loop to search exponentially large configuration spaces of quantum nano-refrigerators, identifying energy-absorbing configurations in electronic junctions. The GVAE maps physical parameters such as site energies and couplings into a latent space that separates cooling from dissipative regimes, drastically reducing the number of expensive quantum-chemical computations needed. It demonstrates ML-guided discovery in quantum thermodynamics.

entry.title: Molecular Prior Networks

author.name: Pawel Gomoluch, Anthony Bradley

entry.summary: The paper applies prior-data fitted networks (PFNs) to drug-target affinity prediction, where wet-lab costs limit datasets to tens to hundreds of molecules. By amortizing learning over a corpus of synthetic or prior molecular tasks, a transformer can perform affinity prediction in a single forward pass for new small-data drug discovery projects.

entry.title: We Ran a Research Sprint With AI. The AI Worked. The Research Didn't

author.name: Anush Sankaran, Arijit Banerjee

entry.summary: This position paper reports a 100-minute AI-assisted research sprint with twelve researchers in three teams, finding that personal AI tools can create a consumption bottleneck and AI-induced research silos that displace shared decision-making. Of 33 logged AI interactions, only one was accepted outright and 27 lacked evaluation, arguing that how AI use is structured matters as much as access.

entry.title: Co-Occurrence Priors Override Visual Spatial Evidence: Understanding False Alarms in Vision-Language Models for Construction Struck-By Hazard Detection

author.name: Xiaoshan Zhou

entry.summary: This study dissects why vision-language models produce false struck-by hazard alarms in construction monitoring, testing whether failures stem from object recognition, spatial encoding, or co-occurrence priors. Using counterfactual worker-excavator scenes with existing models Qwen2.5-VL-7B and InternVL3.5-8B, it shows via probing and causal interventions that hazard decisions are dominated by learned co-occurrence priors despite correct spatial encoding.

entry.title: Point interpolation and distributional universality in flow-based generative models

author.name: Antonio \'Alvarez-L\'opez, Jingpu Cheng, Liyan Zhang, Qianxiao Li

entry.summary: The paper provides quantitative theory for the expressive power of flow-based generative models, relating finite-sample point interpolation to distributional approximation in Wasserstein and total variation distances. It proves universality criteria for parameterized Lipschitz vector-field families and shows coordinate-wise dynamics are insufficient in dimensions of two or more.

entry.title: E2I-Flow: EEG-to-Image Reconstruction via Wavelet-Temporal Cross-Attention and Conditional Flow Matching

author.name: Haowei Pan, Hwa Hui Tew, Junn Yong Loo, Fuad Noman, Hernando Ombao, Chee-Ming Ting

entry.summary: Proposes E2I-Flow, a framework for reconstructing perceived images from non-invasive EEG signals, combining a stationary-wavelet frequency branch and temporal-mixing branch via bidirectional cross-attention, with conditional flow matching as the image decoder. This addresses the complex time-frequency structure of EEG and limitations of discrete denoising decoders in neural decoding.

entry.title: DenseTwins: Dense Modality Decoupling for Multimodal Self-Supervision

author.name: Carlo Sgaravatti, Daniele Kopyshevskiy, Davide Secco, Giacomo Boracchi

entry.summary: Proposes DenseTwins, a multimodal self-supervised framework that learns dense representations by explicitly decoupling feature space into shared and modality-specific components, combining dense cross-modal correspondences with separate modeling of modality-unique information. This addresses limitations of prior methods that either collapse modality-specific information or learn only global features, with relevance to robotics and autonomous driving.

entry.title: Ablating Design Choices for Protein Ensemble Generators Across Structural Regimes

author.name: Eoin Quinn, Oliver Bent

entry.summary: Ablates architecture, sequence conditioning, rigid-body alignment, and training-source choices in a minimal C-alpha flow-matching model for protein conformational ensemble generation, evaluating variants against experimental SAXS and NMR data across ordered, disordered, multi-domain, and transitional proteins. Findings include that mixture-of-experts routing and static pair representations have no detectable effect, while smaller protein language models hurt ordered proteins more.

entry.title: Learning Behaviorally Relevant Dynamics in Multimodal Neural Recordings

author.name: Parastoo Azizeddin, Eray Erturk, Maryam M. Shanechi

entry.summary: BREM-NET is a nonlinear multimodal dynamical model that fuses behavior with multiple neural modalities such as spiking and local field potentials, each with distinct statistics and temporal resolutions. It provides a unified brain-behavior representation where prior source-separation models relied on a single neural modality.

entry.title: TandemBench: Benchmarking Decision Models for Multi-Agent Collaboration

author.name: Baohang Li, Xiaocheng Feng, Bing Qin

entry.summary: TandemBench is a 1,200-question benchmark of multi-agent cooking scenarios where decision models choose team plans affecting goal completion, with reference answers established via execution and exact search. It evaluates 40 native decision models against 10 general-purpose LMs on plan selection and on judging whether better arrangements exist. The benchmark addresses an emerging class of models and their coordination capabilities.

entry.title: A Framework for Context Enrichment and Selective Robustness in LLM Social Agents

author.name: Mattia Greiche, Reihaneh Rabbany, Maximilian Puelma Touzel

entry.summary: This work studies brittleness of LLM agents in social simulations under meaning-preserving prompt variations. The authors formalize controlled context enrichment to test whether richer agent context improves robustness, defining context richness and robustness in ways that support controlled comparisons. The framework helps validate whether simulation results reflect genuine grounding or prompt artifacts.

entry.title: ME^2FDiff: Multiscale Expert Enhancing Feature Diffusion in Residual Network for Brain Tumor Segmentation

author.name: Afrida Rahman, Bijoy Kundu

entry.summary: ME^2FDiff is a single-model architecture for post-treatment glioma segmentation from MRI that uses attention-conditioned spectral diffusion in the encoder bottleneck and iterative refinement rather than a single forward pass. It addresses the mismatch of one bottleneck representation for varying sub-regions and the lack of refinement mechanisms.

entry.title: 3D Banff Glomerulitis Scoring for Kidney Transplant Pathology: Feasibility Study for Volumetric Quantification

author.name: Yanfan Zhu, Junchao Zhu, Ruining Deng, Shilin Zhao, Yu Wang, Yaohong Wang, Yuechen Yang, Chongyu Qu, Zhengyi Lu, Juming Xiong, Mengmeng Yin, Yihan Wang, Andrew J. Rauch, Haichun Yang, Yuankai Huo

entry.summary: A feasibility study extending the Banff scoring system for kidney transplant glomerulitis from single 2D sections to 3D, aligning serial sections, reconstructing glomerular identities across depth, and integrating inflammatory-cell counts under Compatible, Volumetric, and Deduplicated Volumetric strategies. It examines both technical feasibility and clinical relevance.

entry.title: Unaligned Image Guided Denoising via Cross-modal Conditional Flow Matching

author.name: Runmin Zhang, Linshan Li, Si-Yuan Cao, Zhu Yu, Lingyu Zhu, Huaqi Zhang, Hui-Liang Shen

entry.summary: UGD-FM formulates guided image denoising as a progressive cross-modal conditional flow matching process that handles severe noise combined with large-range 2D cross-modal misalignment, letting restoration and guidance aggregation mutually reinforce each other. A stage-focused, inference-consistent training strategy enables efficient few-step inference.

entry.title: Uncertainty-Driven Efficient Communication for UAV-Based Collaborative Perception

author.name: Jiuwu Hao, Yuting Wan, Liguo Sun, Zao Zhang, Yueyang Wu, Pin Lv

entry.summary: The authors propose UCP, an uncertainty-driven framework for UAV collaborative perception that selects what to communicate by combining observational uncertainty (sensor-limited regions) and discriminative uncertainty (model ambiguity near decision boundaries), addressing both missed and false detections under tight bandwidth. This departs from prior foreground-only spatial selection methods.

entry.title: Neural networks and games

author.name: Philip R. Neary

entry.summary: The paper establishes an exact equivalence between symmetric binary Hopfield networks and binary-action games admitting a quadratic potential, mapping stable network configurations to pure-strategy Nash equilibria and asynchronous updating to best-response dynamics. Memory storage and retrieval in neural networks thus correspond to the design and selection of equilibria in games.

entry.title: Generalized Hyperrectangular Prediction Sets in Multivariate Conformal Prediction

author.name: Nabil Alami, Souhaib Ben Taieb

entry.summary: The paper extends hyperrectangular conformal prediction sets to generalized hyperrectangles—Cartesian products of arbitrary one-dimensional sets—and introduces a rectangularization framework converting any continuous multivariate nonconformity score or conditional density into one yielding such sets with finite-sample coverage. This yields prediction sets that are interpretable as per-output intervals.

entry.title: Transport along Local Annealing Paths: Wasserstein Geometry and Multimodal Sampling

author.name: Han Chen, Sifan Liu

entry.summary: The paper analyzes geometric annealing paths in Wasserstein space for multimodal sampling, showing they can detour substantially when mass moves between modes, which slows transport-map learning. Motivated by this geometry, it proposes componentwise annealed transport (CAT), which reduces inter-mode mass transfer and improves multimodal sampling robustness.

entry.title: A low-rank decoder bottleneck bounds reliability in foundation-model perturbation prediction

author.name: Zheyu Zhang, Yuanhao Huang, Fan Feng, Jie Liu

entry.summary: This audit of the STATE foundation model's state-transition decoder across three encoders and four cell lines finds that its first attention layer produces a low-rank output, and projecting onto 4-32 fixed directions preserves prediction quality. The low-rank bottleneck bounds per-prediction reliability by distance to training responses, offering a practical signal for prioritizing CRISPR perturbation experiments.

entry.title: How big is the open model economy today?

author.name: Nathan Lambert

entry.summary: Nathan Lambert uses the Interconnects Dashboard, an aggregator of open model adoption and performance data, to assess how large the open-weight model inference market actually is and whether it is growing or a rounding error. He candidly discusses how imprecise existing measurements are, including noisy platform and marketing metrics, and offers current best approximations of where the open model economy stands.

entry.title: BrainBind: Bridging Synchronized EEG and fMRI through Long-Form Naturalistic Video Representations

author.name: Shixiao Wang, Rining Wu, Jian K. Liu

entry.summary: BrainBind maps synchronized EEG and fMRI recorded during long-form naturalistic video viewing into frozen video embedding spaces, treating them as shared visual-semantic references. It enables cross-modality brain decoding evaluated on CineBrain with multi-seed recall metrics across video anchors and system configurations.

entry.title: CHARM+: Cross-Hardware Attention with Re-Merge Multistream Mechanism

author.name: Xinhang Zhang, Boning Zhang, Chengchun Liu, Chunpu Li, Lei Sun, Weifeng Zhang, Limin Xiao

entry.summary: CHARM+ improves distributed attention for long sequences by reorganizing sequential Ring-Attention-style communications into hierarchical levels with intra-level parallelism and computation overlap, and by decoupling cross-hardware communication to handle NUMA/node bandwidth imbalance. It targets GPU utilization in cross-hardware LLM inference. This is a systems-level efficiency contribution.

entry.title: AmbiHTMLBench: A Benchmark for HTML-based Visually Rich Document parsing

author.name: Boyu Niu, Yingjie Xiong, Shurui Li, Linhan Pang, Yuntong Zhang, Han Wang, Hao Wu, Kai Zuo, Xu Tang, Xuanhe Zhou, Fan Wu

entry.summary: Introduces AmbiHTMLBench, a benchmark of 1,115 pages for document parsing into executable HTML rather than Markdown, preserving spatial structure, table geometry, visual hierarchy, and rendering semantics. It supports both objective and alternative evaluation protocols for layout-sensitive, editable document representations.

entry.title: TSFM Meets LLM: Context as Covariates

author.name: Hemanth Ram, Sai Shankar Narasimhan, Shubhankar Agarwal, Sandeep Chinchali

entry.summary: CoCo is a forecasting framework where an LLM distills textual context (news, reports, annotations) into covariates for time series foundation models, bridging the numerical precision of TSFMs and the text reasoning of LLMs. The paper also provides a scalable method for generating paired multimodal datasets by annotating real-world time series with LLMs.

entry.title: VIPBench: A Human-Aligned Benchmark for Voice Identity Perception in the Age of Voice Cloning

author.name: Xudong Tang, Matthew Groh

entry.summary: VIPBench contains 124,876 same-or-different voice judgments from 1,290 listeners on 9,800 recording pairs of 100 public figures, including real recordings, TTS voice clones, and speaker morphs. It reframes voice identity evaluation around human perception rather than speaker-label recovery, with implications for intellectual property, cybersecurity, and voice cloning detection.

entry.title: MonoLaDN: Language-Guided DeNoising for Monocular 3D Object Detection

author.name: Kiet Dang Vu, Cao Le Minh Khoa, Nguyen Viet Tri Pham, An Nguyen Gia, Tam Le Thuc Ho, Duc Dung Nguyen

entry.summary: MonoLaDN transfers the geometric reasoning of a frozen vision-language model into a monocular 3D detector via a language-guided denoising training framework, keeping the deployed detector purely vision-based and free of VLM inference cost. This injects high-level semantic priors into a fundamentally ill-posed depth-from-single-view task.

entry.title: EmoReward: Self-Evolving Reward Calibration for Emotional Video Generation RL

author.name: Mingzhe Zheng, Yue Wu, Jing Tan, Chang Zou, Dengyang Jiang, Zeyue Tian, Xuanhua He, Ryan Xu, Yunyang Ge, Sihui Ji, Yunlong Lin, Kaihang Pan, Hongru Yan, Sixiang Chen, Dianyi Wang, Julian Zhang, Weijie Kong, Changlin Li, Lanqing Guo, Zhao Zhong, Qifeng Chen, Harry Yang

entry.summary: EmoReward is a self-evolving reward mechanism for RL post-training of emotional video generation, addressing reward hacking and poor capture of emotional intent by fixed quality rewards. It distills evidence reliability from reward traces to calibrate facial, motion, and chromatic cues across narrative contexts, extending GRPO-style training beyond verifiable domains.

entry.title: Does the Trust Boundary Hold over Time? A Long-Horizon Benchmark for Receiver-Directed Federated Learning

author.name: Ting Xu, Henry Leung

entry.summary: This paper introduces a long-horizon benchmark for receiver-directed federated learning, where each site admits, rejects, or abstains on incoming model transfers based on its own data, testing whether such trust boundaries remain sound over hundreds of rounds. With thirteen semi-synthetic sites, an exact oracle, an attack protocol, and fourteen methods evaluated over 600 rounds (plus Qwen3-1.7B LoRA sites over 500), it finds that gates judging against a fixed reference admit 29% of transfers harmful to the site's current model. This exposes real vulnerabilities in transfer-based FL defenses at scale.

entry.title: Graph-Localized Coverage for Conformal Prediction on Inductive Graphs

author.name: Jinwen Xu, Qin Lu, Georgios B. Giannakis

entry.summary: Introduces GLocalCP, an online conformal prediction framework for inductive node classification and edge prediction that combines marginal and graph-local calibration with uncertainty-adaptive prediction sets. It uses an MI-based nonconformity score from MC dropout and kernel-based local corrections to control where errors occur on the graph, not just aggregate coverage.

entry.title: LoopKV: Loop-Aware KV Cache Compression for Serving Looped Transformers

author.name: Tianle Zhou, Yang Zhang, Tianyu Wu, Zhuohan Wang, William Nixon, Juncheng Yang

entry.summary: Targets KV cache memory limits in looped transformers like Ouro, where separate caches per loop constrain batch size. LoopKV allocates quantization precision and cache sharing per (loop, layer) cell based on measured sensitivity, since uniform-bit or fixed-rule approaches misallocate; later loops tolerate sharing better, which the method exploits.

entry.title: ZEMA: confidence-calibrated signed descent with only one state

author.name: Ali Dadsetan, Domenic Rosati, Frank Rudzicz

entry.summary: Building on the view of Adam as sign descent modulated by gradient uncertainty, ZEMA measures per-coordinate support for the gradient sign using z-scores from per-example gradients, converts this into a sign probability, and smooths updates with a single exponential moving average. Because probability is formed before smoothing rather than after, ZEMA keeps one state per parameter instead of Adam's two, with modest per-step overhead. This yields a memory-lighter optimizer with confidence-calibrated updates.

entry.title: Ensembles of Random Partition-Based Models under Covariate Shift

author.name: Mary Versa Clemens-Sewall, Eliza O'Reilly

entry.summary: This work extends covariate shift severity theory from single models to ensembles of random partition-based estimators, introducing new discrepancy measures of shift. It shows that with sufficient ensemble size, such models achieve minimax-optimal risk convergence rates under covariate shift, formalizing empirical observations that ensembles are more robust to shift.

entry.title: Aero-VPA: Few-Step Flow-Matching Control over Non-Reconstructive JEPA Latents for Agile Flight on Edge Hardware

author.name: Yeonseok Lee

entry.summary: Aero-VPA is a lightweight Vision-Predictor-Action architecture for 3D drone navigation on edge hardware, forecasting latent states with an RGB-D ViT and ensemble predictor without pixel reconstruction, and generating action chunks via conditional flow matching in two Euler steps. Ensemble dispersion provides an uncertainty-based fallback, cutting sequential network evaluations to five per decision.

entry.title: Adapting Qwen3 to Tajik from 0.6B to 8B: Lower Text Loss Did Not Mean Better Understanding

author.name: Tohir Saidzoda, Madina Abdusalomzoda, Nasimjon Rajabov, Akhrorkhon Ikromov, Komron Giyosiev, Abubakr Abdullozoda, Amin Jalilov, Jonibek Kishvarov, Rahmonali Sharipov, Mariyamkhon Shodyeva

entry.summary: This paper systematically adapts Qwen3 models (0.6B to 8B) to Tajik with LoRA adapters and continued pretraining, showing that lower Tajik text loss did not translate into better reading comprehension on Belebele at most scales. Continued pretraining on roughly 375M tokens plus supervised fine-tuning yielded a model 11.4 points above Qwen3-8B on Belebele, though with English capability costs. It is a valuable empirical caution for language-adaptation practice.

entry.title: Whose Values Are Generated? Measuring Visual Value Leakage in Multilingual Text-to-Image Generation

author.name: Zucan Lyu, Binwei Yao, Rheeya Uppaal, Jing Yao, Xiaoyuan Yi, Junjie Hu

entry.summary: VisionValueBench is a multilingual benchmark operationalizing six Hofstede cultural value dimensions to measure how text-to-image systems frame neutral social situations through particular cultural orientations. The authors find that value-neutral prompts nonetheless yield images favoring specific value orientations, a phenomenon they call visual value leakage. This extends cultural evaluation of T2I beyond landmarks and clothing to underlying values.

entry.title: A Feasibility Condition for Confidence-Gated Tiered LLM Inference

author.name: Sumit P. Ahuja

entry.summary: This paper derives a closed-form condition determining when confidence-gated tiered LLM inference cascades are worthwhile compared to routing all queries to a datacenter backstop. Modeling routing as a binary test with an architecture cost ratio, it gives practitioners a principled way to know when tiered serving cannot deliver savings regardless of threshold choice.

entry.title: Whose Transparency is it Anyway? Understanding Generative AI Transparency Needs and Gaps Across Stakeholders

author.name: Genevieve Smith, Sahiba Chopra, Natalia Luka, Min Kyung Lee

entry.summary: Drawing on a global survey of 400 end-users, AI builders, and policymakers plus focus groups, this study examines how different stakeholders understand transparency in generative AI. Findings indicate shared understandings of what transparency should afford, but systematic gaps in who is actually served by current transparency practice, with end-users most underserved.

entry.title: Self-Supervised Pretraining for Label-Efficient Facial Expression Recognition using Smart Glasses

author.name: Zhengtao Gao, Francesco Bombassei De Bona, Leonardo Alchieri, Ivana Kiprijanovska, Simon Stankoski, Bojan Sofronievski, Hristijan Gjoreski, Marc Langheinrich, Martin Gjoreski

entry.summary: The paper applies masked-autoencoder self-supervised pretraining on optomyographic signals from smart glasses for camera-free, privacy-preserving facial expression recognition, finetuning under personalized few-label settings. It shows SSL can reduce dependence on costly labelled expression data. Relevant to wearable health and affective computing applications.

entry.title: From Handcrafted to Generative: RLVR-Optimized Icon Generation for Alexa+

author.name: Rohan Sequeira, Matthew Rosenberg, Amin Mahmoudabadbozchelou, Oleg Poliannikov, Jonathan Rubin

entry.summary: Describes a production pipeline from Amazon that automatically generates vectorized animated icons for Alexa+ devices from text descriptions, replacing hand-drawn assets. The pipeline stages include image generation, semantic decomposition, vectorisation, styling, and animation, with quality optimized via RL with verifiable rewards.

entry.title: EviSeek: An Evidence-Centric Agentic Framework for Embodied Active Information Seeking

author.name: Jintao Li, Zhiyong Cao, Baihua Xiao, Yu Bai, B\"orje F. Karlsson

entry.summary: Introduces EviSeek, a training-free framework for embodied question answering that makes question-derived evidence demands explicit acquisition objectives, linking actions and retained evidence to the information sought. It improves accuracy by 7.1 percentage points on 3,436 ESI-Bench questions with Qwen3 models.

entry.title: Rules, Traces and Routing Statistics: Training and Calibration Data for Open Models on ARC-AGI-2

author.name: Nguyen Minh Thang, Trinh Thi Phuong

entry.summary: The authors build a large corpus of executable rules and curated tasks for the NVARC Qwen3-4B grid model and study which training and calibration data improve ARC-AGI-2 performance under a constrained offline compute budget of four L4 GPUs for 12 hours. Continued fine-tuning raised the semi-private score from 28.96 to 33.06 across 189 runs on 120 hidden tasks. It is a careful empirical study of data curation for abstract reasoning.

entry.title: Hallucination Is Linearly Decodable from Mid-Layer Hidden States in Quantized LLMs

author.name: Aizierjiang Aiersilan

entry.summary: The paper shows that a linear probe on a single mid-network layer of 4-bit quantized 7B-8B open models (Llama-3.1-8B, Mistral-7B, Qwen2.5-7B) detects hallucination with 0.904-1.000 AUROC, far exceeding sampling-based detectors capped at 0.541. It characterizes where truthfulness signals are linearly decodable in quantized models across four hallucination benchmarks. This supports cheap, internal hallucination detection for deployed models.

entry.title: Constraint-Preserving Flow Matching for Spectral Graph Generation

author.name: Anita Yang, Ken-ichi Kawarabayashi, Yohan Jung

entry.summary: LaSFM formulates flow matching on the Stiefel manifold to generate spectral graph representations that provably preserve Laplacian structure: eigenvector orthonormality, positive eigenvalues, and the nullspace constraint that prior methods ignore. This yields eigensystems consistent with actual graph Laplacians.

entry.title: Whiel: A Neurosymbolic Platform for Certified Relational Program Verification

author.name: Jesse Comer, Fangzhu Shen, Shuo Zhang, Mayur Naik, Sudeepa Roy, Val Tannen

entry.summary: Whiel is a Lean-certified system for reasoning about imperative relational programs, encoding containment and equivalence problems for Datalog, extensions with negation, and graph query languages, plus optimized or incremental evaluation algorithms. Its states are database instances, enabling compositional Hoare-style reasoning with first-order relational specifications using prophecy variables.

entry.title: Text-Only Domain Adaptation for Low-Resource Medical ASR: Shallow Fusion and Density Ratio Rescoring for Hausa

author.name: Oche David Ankeli, Hassan Adelani Luqman, Theodora Ngozi Egbunike, Joshua Gottschalk, Bonaventure F. P. Dossou

entry.summary: This paper adapts a fixed MMS-1B-FL102 acoustic model to Hausa medical speech recognition using only text data, comparing shallow fusion and density ratio rescoring with KenLM language models built from medical and general-domain corpora. Evaluation uses physician-reviewed recordings from ten speakers across six northern Nigerian states under prompt-disjoint cross-validation. It demonstrates a practical recipe for low-resource, domain-specific ASR without new speech data collection.

entry.title: Clips2Story: Training-Free Video Storyboarding and Editing Using Multimodal Retrieval-Embedded Generation

author.name: Junnuo Wang, Weihan Xu, Hao-Wen Dong

entry.summary: This paper introduces Clips2Story, a training-free pipeline that creates keyword-specified short videos from unordered pools of clips by extracting multimodal text descriptors, retrieving relevant clips, and using an LLM to select and arrange them into a coherent narrative. It addresses a real gap, since most video editing tools assume a single temporally ordered source video.

entry.title: Today's Work, Tomorrow's Workforce: Incentivizing Learning in AI-Assisted Work

author.name: Moritz Diener, Daniel Hendriks, Philipp Spitzer, Gerhard Satzger, Joshua Holstein, Wei Sun

entry.summary: This paper models how AI assistance affects worker skill formation over a sequence of accept-or-solve tasks, comparing myopic workers who maximize immediate utility with strategic workers who value future skills. It shows novices can become trapped in AI reliance, with implications for skill acquisition, retention, and the ability to oversee AI.

entry.title: Noise-regularized training of quantum circuit Born machines under a finite shot budget

author.name: Hoang M. Ngo, Quan Nguyen, Jung Taek Seo, Wanli Xing, My T. Thai

entry.summary: This paper bounds the generalization gap of quantum circuit Born machines by the complexity of distributions reachable under noise, showing scrambled local Pauli noise contracts this complexity and acts as a regularizer with an intermediate optimal strength. It proposes GENIE, a framework realizing a chosen noise level with capped error mitigation and selecting it during training from held-out data.

entry.title: Route First, See Later: Enabling Vision Agents to Reason Scientifically by Separating Routing Policy from Action Spaces

author.name: Shubhabrata Mukherjee, Jeffrey Donatelli, Daniela Ushizima

entry.summary: The paper introduces ZETA, an agent architecture for scientific image analysis that decouples intent interpretation (routing) from visual tool execution, making failures auditable as either misrouting or failed perception. Measurement is treated as a deterministic operation grounded in explicit geometry rather than generative output, improving reliability for high-stakes scientific automation. This addresses the lack of auditability in current multi-tool vision agent architectures.

entry.title: CounterFactual Retrieval for Evidence-Aware Individual Animal Identification

author.name: Ankit K. Upadhyay, Aleksandr Algasov, Ekaterina Nepovinnykh, Fedor Zolotarev, Tuomas Eerola, Heikki K\"alvi\"ainen, Charles V. Stewart, Lukas Picek

entry.summary: The paper proposes Counterfactual Forensic Retrieval (CFR), an evidence-aware evaluation protocol for individual animal identification that tests the same query-gallery task under full-image, foreground-only, and shortcut-only views. This reveals whether high retrieval accuracy reflects genuine animal features or identity-correlated shortcuts, addressing a blind spot as wildlife re-identification moves to shared benchmarks and foundation models. It is a methodological contribution to evaluation rigor in computer vision for conservation.

entry.title: The Information Limits of Neural Controlled Differential Equations Under Sparse Observations

author.name: Rostislav Gusev, Evgenia Romanenkova, Alexey Zaytsev

entry.summary: This theoretical work characterizes the fundamental ambiguity in Neural CDE predictions under sparse observations: different admissible interpolation paths consistent with the same data can yield different terminal states. It derives a zonotopic approximation of the set of compatible terminal states using signed areas and Lie brackets, yielding a computable ambiguity certificate and analysis of measurement requirements.

entry.title: P$^2$-MOPD: Accelerating Multi-Teacher On-Policy Distillation via Parameter Priors

author.name: Sinuo Wang, Jiacheng Lu, Zeyu Zhang, Maojia Song, Rui Sun, Beidi Luan, Yutong Xie, Jing Li, Daxin Jiang, Qi Wu, Zuo Bai

entry.summary: P2-MOPD treats the linear combination of student and expert parameters as a single differentiable model, jointly optimizing mixing coefficients and student weights under the same on-policy distillation objective. Unlike pure task arithmetic, the student remains trainable so experts act as parameter priors rather than constraining the solution to the span of frozen parameters, with gains across four domains at 1.7B and 4B scales.

entry.title: One Mistake, Three Layers: Persistence Rules Under Depth Correlation

author.name: Maryam Rahimimovassagh, Michael Brown, Sanjeda Sara Jennifer, Niloofar Yousefi

entry.summary: This paper shows that the common persistence rule for reading probing depth curves (requiring a threshold crossing for three consecutive layers) can report signal onset up to nineteen stages early on synthetic curves due to correlation between neighboring layers, a hazard familiar from neuroimaging but unexamined for probing. It proposes a calibrated estimator using label-permutation null trajectories with controlled error rates.

entry.title: Structured Priors: Towards an algebra of component priors for prior-data fitted networks

author.name: Thomas Bartz-Beielstein

entry.summary: Replaces hand-built synthetic data generators for prior-data fitted networks (like TabPFN) with a structured prior algebra of named component priors linked by formally proven operators (mixture, convolution, amplitude scaling, local transform, projection) within a measure-theoretic framework. This makes the effect of prior composition on trained networks more predictable and validated.

entry.title: When Strong Reasoners Join the Pool: Small Union Premiums and Costly Runaway Generations in LLM Routing

author.name: Teng-Ruei Chen

entry.summary: Measures the union premium in LLM routing benchmarks - the gap between a single-model clairvoyant ceiling and an any-model-correct oracle - using pre-committed fixed-protocol generation of 30 seeded samples per MATH-500 problem for modern reasoning models (Llama-3.3-70B, Nemotron Nano 9B v2). Finds the premium shrinks with strong reasoners while runaway multi-sample generations are costly.

entry.title: Deep Learning Compilers: Architecture, Optimization, and Empirical Characterization

author.name: Jinghao Wen, Ruixuan Wang, Xun Jiao

entry.summary: A systematic survey of deep learning compilers covering their architectural evolution across frontend, middle-end, and backend stages, optimization techniques, and empirical characterization of representative compilers. It matters because efficient compilation is central to deploying increasingly complex models on heterogeneous hardware. The paper also outlines emerging research directions in the field.

entry.title: CAPSkip: Cancellation-Aware Prefix Skipping for Selective Backpropagation

author.name: Heejin Choi

entry.summary: CAPSkip improves selective backpropagation by accounting for cancellation between per-example gradients, which scalar scores like loss or gradient magnitude ignore. Among correctly classified examples, it skips the longest prefix in increasing last-layer gradient-norm order whose vector sum stays within a relative budget of the batch gradient, bounding the change to the raw final-layer gradient in exact arithmetic. This enables cheaper training with a controlled effect on the update.

entry.title: Leakage-free evaluation of residual graph convolutional networks for network intrusion detection

author.name: Zahid Iqbal

entry.summary: This paper audits common data-leakage pitfalls in graph-based network intrusion detection, where test flows contaminate the training graph, duplicates straddle splits, and only single splits are reported. After rigorous label-aware deduplication (removing 69% of flows in NF-UNSW-NB15-v2) and train-only graph construction, a two-layer residual GCN is compared against simpler baselines. The work matters because it quantifies how much of the reported advantage of GNNs in this domain may be evaluation optimism rather than genuine capability.

entry.title: TAPES: Task-Aligned Joint Predictive Pretraining for Transaction Event Sequences

author.name: Ruobing Zuo, Weiyu Han, Huilin He, Haoyu Jiang, Ze Zhao, Jie Sheng, Xiao Tan, Shuai Chen, Tianyi Zhang

entry.summary: TAPES is a pretraining framework for transaction event sequences in online commerce and financial services that constructs candidate target sets from admissible field-operator combinations and performs task-aligned joint prediction, explicitly modeling conditional co-occurrence among prediction targets. This addresses the mismatch between generic predictive pretraining objectives and the diverse downstream semantics (values, changes, relations) of real transaction tasks. It could improve representation quality for industrial sequence models.

entry.title: Attending to Memory Writes Reduces Seed Variability in Recurrent Length Generalization

author.name: Sungwoo Goo, Hwi-yeol Yun, Sangkeun Jung

entry.summary: The paper studies bounded delta attention in recurrent memory models, implemented in TraceRelay with additive phase recurrence and attention computed before a parallel scan. On prefix-supervised modulo-5 tasks trained at lengths 1-40 and tested at length 80, upper delta attention achieves similar mean accuracy to a local-attention recurrent baseline but with dramatically reduced seed variance (a 63 percent reduction in standard deviation). The findings suggest attending to memory writes stabilizes length generalization.

entry.title: DRAP: Dynamics-Risk Adaptive Plasticity for Continual Learning in Physical AI

author.name: Oswaldo Ludwig

entry.summary: DRAP is a replay-free continual learning method for physical AI that estimates per-parameter importance from action gradients weighted by a Lyapunov-inspired trajectory-amplification risk, addressing error accumulation in closed-loop control. A ridge-regularized local model fitted to expert transitions yields a policy-independent stability estimate used to modulate plasticity.

entry.title: Going Deeper With Memories

author.name: Afshin Khadangi

entry.summary: DeepMem is a causal multiscale byte-level language model that separates semantic compression from exact byte preservation using an invertible subband transform, fast-weight memory blocks, and an attention-based super-resolution decoder. It reportedly outperforms a matched byte-level Transformer on FineWeb-Edu while avoiding tokenizer dependence. This is a novel architecture addressing the cost of full-resolution byte processing.

entry.title: Aligning Language Models with General Preferences: An Empirical Study of Direct Nash Optimization

author.name: Austin Tsai, Saurav Nanda, Ganapathy Parthasarathy, Bhuvnesh Kumar, Parivesh Choudhary

entry.summary: The authors independently re-implement Direct Nash Optimization (DNO-Prct), an alignment method that finds Nash equilibria of preference games via on-policy sampling, LLM rating, and DPO-style updates, and evaluate it on Llama 3.1 8B Instruct and Mistral 7B Instruct with GPT-4o as annotator. Three iterations raise AlpacaEval 2.0 length-controlled win rates substantially for both models. This provides a useful empirical validation and characterization of a Nash-based alternative to RLHF/DPO pipelines.

entry.title: Complete Donor-Set Guidance for Frozen Diffusion Docking Models

author.name: Hyunwoo Kim, Insoo Park, Ziseok Lee, Wooyeol Lee, Yoorim Gang, Kyungsu Kim

entry.summary: The paper proposes Complete-Identity Contract Guidance (CICG) and Historical Contract Transfer (HCT) to inject metal-coordination donor-set constraints into already-trained general-purpose diffusion docking models without retraining. By applying translation, rotation, and torsion updates guided by a supplied complete donor set, the method corrects metal-donor geometry errors in ligand pose predictions for metalloproteins. This offers a training-free route to metal-aware molecular docking.

entry.title: LaplaceDiag: Fault Diagnosis through Changes in Learned Actuator Effects

author.name: Oliver Niggemann

entry.summary: This paper introduces LaplaceDiag, a data-driven fault diagnosis method that learns a healthy plant model using LaplaceNet, a neural network operating in Laplace space. It explicitly separates nonlinear history-based prediction from an interpretable matrix describing how actuator values influence sensors, allowing changed actuator effects to narrow the search for faulty components without requiring detailed component models or labeled fault data.

entry.title: The Complexity of ReLU Network Synthesis from a Parameter Multiset

author.name: Dimitrios Myrisiotis

entry.summary: The paper studies the computational complexity of constructing a ReLU network when its parameter values are given as a multiset of rationals and only the architecture may be chosen. It proves that exact matching of two examples is NP-complete, while agreement with a Boolean circuit on all inputs is Sigma-2-P-complete even with four neurons, separating the roles of weights and architecture.

entry.title: How Risky Is Your Data-Driven Policy?

author.name: Omar Besbes, Alon Rieger

entry.summary: This paper quantifies the tail risk of data-driven policies using conditional value-at-risk over training samples, policy randomization, and future outcomes. It decomposes regret against a distribution-knowing oracle into expected post-sample regret and a sample-risk premium capturing tail risk omitted by average-case analysis.

entry.title: One-shot Distributed Learning via Weighted Averaging with Server-side Information

author.name: Pavle Tepav\v{c}evi\'{c}, Du\v{s}an Jakoveti\'{c}, Milo\v{s} Savi\'{c}

entry.summary: Studies one-shot distributed learning where workers fit local models that the server aggregates, and proposes weighted averaging schemes incorporating server-side data to preserve the pooled-data MSE order even when the number of workers grows quickly relative to local sample sizes and local estimation bias is nonzero. This reduces communication relative to iterative distributed training.

entry.title: Hybrid acoustic and pretrained embedding feature fusion for unmanned aerial vehicle detection using stacking ensemble learning under a leakage-aware evaluation protocol

author.name: Zahid Iqbal

entry.summary: Re-evaluates acoustic drone detection on the public DroneAudioDataset under a grouped, source-disjoint evaluation protocol, revealing that widely reported high accuracies partly reflect data leakage from random clip-level splits of recordings derived from few sources. It also proposes a stacking ensemble fusing acoustic features with pretrained embeddings, comparing performance under leakage-free versus random splits.

entry.title: Post-stratified importance sampling

author.name: Yuling Yao, Sergei Tikhonov

entry.summary: Motivated by multilevel regression and poststratification from survey statistics, the authors propose post-stratified importance sampling (PIS), which recasts high-dimensional importance weighting into two one-dimensional modeling problems: regression on importance ratios and density estimation of those ratios. This addresses the high or infinite variance and unreliable uncertainty quantification that plague standard importance sampling.

entry.title: A simple adaptive accelerated optimistic dual averaging method for unconstrained convex optimization in $p$-norm geometry

author.name: Bowen Li, Danqing Zhou, Chuan He

entry.summary: This paper introduces A2ODA, an adaptive accelerated optimistic dual averaging method for unconstrained convex optimization that uses low-cost preconditioning in p-norm geometry for p in [2, infinity]. The method is line-search-free, employs a new stepsize selection technique based on an aggregated affine lower model, and provides convergence bounds under a generalized local smoothness condition that separate constant and gap-dependent curvature effects. It matters because efficient preconditioning is critical for large-scale first-order optimization used in machine learning.

entry.title: GUILD: Guided Iterative Data Collection for Imitation Learning

author.name: Shivin Dass, Kevin Nguyen, Rohan Yelandur, Junhong Xu, Roberto Mart\'in-Mart\'in

entry.summary: GUILD is a guided data collection method for imitation learning that actively reasons about which data to collect next to maximize downstream policy performance, rather than filtering an already-collected unguided dataset. It alternates between iterative collection and policy training, targeting the costly real-world teleoperation bottleneck in robot learning.

entry.title: Information-Matched Auditing of Conversational Emotion-Shift Forecasting: A Leakage-Safe Evaluation Protocol

author.name: Bin Wen, Dai-Qiao Zhang, Tien-Ping Tan

entry.summary: The paper presents an information-matched, leakage-safe auditing protocol for conversational emotion-shift forecasting, with an explicit commitment point, executable causality tests, equal hyperparameter searches, and seed-dialogue-aware inference. Applied to six causal model families across four corpora, it shows a deployable train-only current-emotion classifier changes conclusions versus flawed baselines. It matters as a rigorous methodological corrective for a subfield prone to leakage-distorted comparisons.

entry.title: Ruby-OPD: Enhancing Pronunciation Controllability and Accuracy for Flow-Matching Text-to-Speech via On-Policy Distillation

author.name: Rui Hu, Xiaolong Lin, Zhenpeng Zhan

entry.summary: Ruby-OPD is a two-stage framework for Japanese flow-matching TTS that uses Ruby text representations to preserve lexical and prosodic cues while controlling polyphonic readings, combined with on-policy distillation. It targets the long-standing trade-off between cascaded front-end controllability and end-to-end naturalness in Japanese, an unsegmented script with extensive polyphony. It advances pronunciation controllability in TTS for a hard script type.

entry.title: When Do Summaries Become Instructions? Unsupported Policy in LLM Agents' Self-Written Handoff Summaries

author.name: Wenhui Chu

entry.summary: This single-author study examines whether context-compaction handoff summaries written by LLM agents contain unsupported restrictions or authorizations not backed by the underlying record, using synthetic tool-use tasks with ground-truth permission ledgers. It finds low rates of unsupported policy (roughly 0.1-2.4% of summaries) and mixed evidence that these sentences change successor behavior. A careful, safety-relevant probe of an emergent failure mode in long-running agents.

entry.title: SVGFaith: A Two-Layer Meta-Evaluation of Faithfulness Metrics for Text-to-SVG Generation

author.name: Guotao Liang, Haitao Zhou, Biao Liu, Huanxuan Liao, Lingfeng Qiao, Qian-Wen Zhang, Qian Yu, Di Yin, Xing Sun

entry.summary: SVGFaith is a meta-evaluation framework for text-to-SVG faithfulness metrics, with 1,842 controlled contrastive pairs across eight capability axes and 1,327 human-annotated comparisons of real generator outputs.
