It shows that CLIP and related image-text embedding metrics fail to capture fine-grained prompt faithfulness. Valuable for correcting evaluation practice in an active generative area.

entry.title: Beyond accuracy: what AI assurance needs to establish in public services

author.name: Louise Yorke

entry.summary: This study examines reliability of AI-produced evidence in public services by evaluating eight GPT-4o configurations classifying 1,200 UK Prime Minister's Questions into 21 policy topics against human-coded labels. It finds accuracy in the 68-70% range but substantial output instability across unchanged repeats, and combines technical evaluation with governance and measurement-theory analysis. The work argues AI assurance in government needs both output testing and organizational sufficiency criteria.

entry.title: GaussianRenderFormer: Transformer-based Rendering of 3D Gaussian Splats

author.name: Shahaf Valencia Levy, Sagie Benaim

entry.summary: GaussianRenderFormer is a transformer that learns to render 3D Gaussian splats directly, with each Gaussian a token in a view-independent encoder and a view-dependent decoder turning camera ray patches into pixels, requiring no rasterizer. Trained on roughly 20,000 Objaverse objects, it renders unseen objects at 38.08 dB PSNR versus 44.02 dB for rasterizing the same pruned input. Diagnostics point to a view-decoder bottleneck as the limiting factor.

entry.title: Navigational Safety of Marine Surface Vehicles in Restricted Visibility: From Intelligent Vision to Vision-Centered Multi-Sensor Fusion

author.name: Ryan Wen Liu, Fengchuan Song, Tianxiang Wang, Guobei Peng, Youngrong Kim, Xian Zhong, Hooi-Siang Kang, Maohan Liang, Junzhi Yu, Shanliang Yao

entry.summary: A survey-style paper on perception for marine surface vehicles under degraded visual conditions, covering vision-based detection and recognition challenges and vision-centered fusion with complementary sensors such as AIS, radar, and LiDAR. It aims to improve situational awareness and navigation safety for maritime autonomy.

entry.title: STARE: Scene Text-Aware multimodal Retrieval for Everyday objects

author.name: Kento Tokura, Ryosuke Korekata, Daichi Yashima, Kei Katsumata, Kanon Amemiya, Miyu Goko, Komei Sugiura

entry.summary: STARE tackles service robots retrieving everyday objects from free-form instructions that reference visual features and scene text, introducing a Crosslingual Visual Prompt for scene-text interpretation and modeling of named-entity-to-object relationships. Evaluation uses two novel benchmarks for this task.

entry.title: FlashRelight: Portrait Video Relighting with Dynamic Lighting

author.name: Jiahui Sheng, Le Li, Limin Lin, Jiahao Li, Wansen Feng, Hong Gu, Shuhan Chen, Xiaorun Li, Rui Hu

entry.summary: FlashRelight is a two-stage framework for portrait video relighting under dynamic lighting, first suppressing source illumination then synthesizing target lighting on an illumination-neutral video. It supports envmap sequences, semantic lighting text prompts, and lighting reference videos as control modalities.

entry.title: Learning to Track Cells from Sparse Annotations in 3D Time-Lapse Microscopy

author.name: Yusuke Uchida

entry.summary: This paper presents a cell tracking pipeline for 3D time-lapse microscopy that works with sparse annotations, combining 2.5D and 3D detectors trained to suppress erroneous background supervision, calibrating link and division probabilities from motion and appearance features, and jointly selecting lineage graph events. It addresses the common failure mode where unannotated cells are treated as background.

entry.title: PixelSpline: Continuous Space-Time Video Super-Resolution via Endpoint-Anchored Shared Pixel Trajectories

author.name: Wanqi Yuan, Nianyi Li

entry.summary: This paper presents a continuous space-time video super-resolution framework combining long-context encoding, continuous HR feature lifting, and PixelSpline, which models each pixel's motion as a single continuous trajectory shared by both endpoint frames instead of independent directional flows. This reduces ambiguous correspondence and inconsistent trajectories in joint temporal and spatial upsampling.

entry.title: TOP: Transmission-Oriented Remote Sensing Pansharpening

author.name: Zi-Han Cao, Jing-Ze Liang, Shao-Jie Wu, Jin-Cheng Di, Liang-Jian Deng, Gemine Vivone

entry.summary: TOP is presented as the first transmission-oriented pansharpening framework, unifying compact binary latent coding, onboard satellite pansharpening, and efficient downlink in one satellite-to-ground pipeline. It addresses the unexamined assumption in prior work that high-resolution data arrive losslessly, making fusion quality robust to compression perturbations introduced during downlink.

entry.title: $\mathcal{C}^\infty$ Smooth Trajectory Planning with Application to Soft Robots

author.name: Reinhard M. Grassmann, Abdulaziz Y. Alkayas, Lingyun Chen, Sami Haddadin

entry.summary: The paper introduces a C-infinity smooth trajectory generator that satisfies kinematic constraints while achieving smoothness orders beyond previously used standards (C4 for collaborative robots, C5 for drones), motivated by the unknown and potentially much higher smoothness requirements of soft continuum robots. The method targets high motion performance and vibration suppression for complex, flexible systems.

entry.title: The Effectiveness of Sliding Mode Control for Robust Vision Stabilization under the Plant-Binding Condition

author.name: Sooyeun Yang, Jongseong Brad Choi, Seung Bok choi

entry.summary: This paper rigorously characterizes when sliding mode control (SMC) actually outperforms simpler baselines like low-pass filtering and PID for vision stabilization, identifying the plant-binding condition (disturbance velocity near actuator slew limits) as the deciding factor. Through two independent vision domains including handheld video and virtual PTZ plants, the authors show SMC and LPF are statistically indistinguishable outside the binding regime. This is a valuable negative-result-adjacent analysis that disciplines when complex controllers are justified.

entry.title: Risk-Sensitive Non-Parametric and Kernel Bandits

author.name: Devdan Dey, Sujoy Bhore, Avishek Ghosh

entry.summary: This work studies non-parametric bandits where arms are evaluated under Cumulative Prospect Theory rather than expected reward, proposing NPCB, an optimistic algorithm decoupling mean estimation from CPT-based decisions. It proves regret matching classical non-parametric bandits order-wise, showing risk sensitivity in the CPT sense incurs no additional cost.

entry.title: Exact signal recovery from generative priors with sigmoid output activation

author.name: Matthew S. Scott, Yaniv Plan, \"Ozg\"ur Y{\i}lmaz

entry.summary: The paper proves exact uniform signal recovery in generative compressed sensing for ReLU networks with a final sigmoid activation, without assuming expansivity, provided the input layer is the narrowest layer. The required number of measurements scales with depth and geometric mean layer widths via k(d log(K/k) + log-log terms), with entries of the signal bounded away from saturation.

entry.title: Towards the Query Complexity of Sampling under Strong Log-Concavity and Log-Sobolev Inequalities

author.name: Huanjian Zhou, Taiji Suzuki

entry.summary: The authors prove query complexity lower bounds for sampling from smooth distributions using first-order oracles, showing that any randomized sampler for strongly log-concave targets requires exp(Omega(log^{1/3} d)) queries even from a warm start, and an Omega(kappa) lower bound for log-Sobolev targets. These results rule out polylogarithmic dimension dependence and formally separate log-Sobolev sampling from strongly log-concave and Gaussian sampling.

entry.title: Fun toy result: a subliminal-learning effect via on-policy distillation

author.name: shawnghu

entry.summary: The author demonstrates a subliminal learning variant where a student is trained via on-policy distillation from a preference-prompted teacher on sequences generated by an unprompted model, producing an 82% cat-preference transfer. The effect persists even when loss is masked to number-related tokens only, suggesting transmission is not mediated by preference-related token logit mass.

entry.title: VirtualTrialHarness: Coordinating Agentic Operationalization of Virtual Trial Protocols Across Complex Clinical Schemas

author.name: Pengze Li, Jingna Feng, Yue Yu, Yining Wu, Xinyue Hu, Jie Lin, Avanti Bhandarkar, Cui Tao

entry.summary: VTHarness is an agent framework that translates virtual clinical trial protocols into executable analyses by selecting reusable procedural skills per workflow stage and using explicit contracts to keep study decisions consistent. It addresses real operationalization challenges like patient identity, linkage, and temporal interpretation across complex clinical schemas.

entry.title: FlyHash for LLM Agent Memory: An Empirical Validation and a New Application

author.name: Mohan Bheemadolu, Chrisogonas O. Odhiambo

entry.summary: The paper applies FlyHash, a sparse random-projection with winner-take-all hashing inspired by the fruit fly olfactory circuit, to LLM agent external memory retrieval for the first time. It empirically validates the scheme against dense embedding plus ANN baselines on practitioner-relevant questions. This bridges computational neuroscience insights with agent memory systems.

entry.title: LegalEvolver: Agentic Legal Judgment Prediction via Rubric-Guided Self-Evolution

author.name: Xinyu Yang, Jiejun Tan, Chenlong Deng, Chenghao Zhang, Tongyu Wen, Zhicheng Dou

entry.summary: Proposes LegalEvolver, a rubric-guided self-evolution framework that optimizes retrieval queries for legal judgment prediction, moving beyond direct query formulation from user requests to capture latent legal issues. It samples high-quality optimized queries and search trajectories to improve LLM-agent legal retrieval.

entry.title: Jev with Foresight: Safe Language-Guided Autonomous Driving via a Language World Model

author.name: Yansong Qu, Jiancong Chen, Samuel Labi

entry.summary: Jev-AD pairs a typed decision model that outputs probabilities over predefined questions with a language world model that predicts how nearby vehicles will move over the next two seconds for each candidate action. In simulated highway merging, this foresight mechanism cuts the same decision model's collision rate from 26.0% to 2.4% at 0.25 seconds per decision.

entry.title: Do Language Models Know Which Constraints Belong Together?

author.name: Junbo Jacob Lian, Kaixuan Chen, Hanzhang Qin, Huiling Chen, Chaoyu Zhang, Chung-Piaw Teo

entry.summary: The paper proves information-theoretic lower bounds showing that when a Dantzig-Wolfe reformulation requires a hidden group of w constraint families that only strengthen the bound together, any method observing only bounds needs on the order of k^w evaluations to find the group. It then examines whether LLMs can predict such constraint groupings for mixed-integer programs, where these zero-marginal groups arise in lot sizing, network design, and facility location.

entry.title: GREP: Grounding Generated Room Evaluation in Principles

author.name: Mohan Cao, Yongsen Mao, Chucheng Xiang, Zhongyuan Liu, Zhihang Zhong, Haiping Wang, Yuan Liu

entry.summary: GREP introduces a three-tier evaluation philosophy for LLM-generated furnished rooms: physical validity, visual coherence, and human-use logic, shifting from predefined questions to principle-guided assessment. An evaluation agent autonomously and adaptively identifies issues in generated indoor scenes according to these principles. This fills a gap in holistic scene-quality evaluation for generative interior layout systems.

entry.title: A Bag of Tricks for Defending Deep Learning-based Face Recognition Pipelines against Backdoor Attacks

author.name: Quentin Le Roux, Marti Jimenez, Yannick Teglia, Philippe Loubet Moundi

entry.summary: This technical report presents three practical defenses against data-poisoning backdoor attacks on industrial face recognition systems, targeting the realistic threat of compromised third-party training data. One defense operates at training time to detect poisoned identities and two at inference time to filter suspicious inputs, each with algorithms and computational cost analysis.

entry.title: FedFiOT: Fisher-Weighted Optimal Transport for Model Merging in One-Shot and Few-Round Federated Learning

author.name: Quan Minh Nguyen, Hoang M. Ngo, Bhakti Chowkwale, Yasaman Keshtkarjahromi, My T. Thai

entry.summary: FedFiOT is a Fisher-weighted optimal transport framework for merging client models in one-shot and few-round federated learning, tackling neuron misalignment from client drift and importance-weighting under data heterogeneity. By combining optimal transport-based neuron matching with Fisher information weighting, it aims to close the performance gap with conventional multi-round FL while preserving communication savings. This is a targeted fix for a known bottleneck in communication-efficient FL.

entry.title: Stacking-Based Weighting for Large Language Bayes in M-Open Settings

author.name: Anant Bhide, Akarsh Gupta, Edmond Cunningham, Justin Domke

entry.summary: The paper proposes stacking-based aggregation for Large Language Bayes, which generates candidate probabilistic programs from a natural language description, replacing likelihood-based Bayesian model averaging with weights optimized for predictive performance. This addresses model misspecification and uncertainty under-representation when averaging concentrates on a single model in M-open settings.

entry.title: LIRA: A More Interpretable Dynamic Loss-Informed Rank Allocation for Low-Rank Adaptation

author.name: Sihao Wang, Bozheng Li, Xuemiao Xu, Haoxin Yang, Yujie Xu, Jie Tang

entry.summary: Proposes LIRA, a dynamic-rank LoRA method that scores each layer by the estimated magnitude of the local loss perturbation associated with reallocation, aiming to make online rank reallocation more interpretable than heuristic or first-order-signal approaches used in prior adaptive-rank variants.

entry.title: Variational Learning with Lie Group Exponential Families

author.name: Eren Mehmet K{\i}ral, Thomas M\"ollenhoff, Koichi Tojo, Mohammad Emtiyaz Khan, Kenichi Bannai

entry.summary: The paper extends a Lie-group framework for variational Bayesian learning to arbitrary general Lie groups, building on prior work on multiplicative and affine groups that naturally handles parameter constraints and low-variance gradient estimation. It establishes an explicit relation to standard natural-gradient variational methods such as Bayesian learning rule. This generalizes a growing line of work on geometry-aware variational inference for neural networks.

entry.title: Exploiting Biases in Attention for Transformers

author.name: Charles Herr, Gabriele Spadaro, Enzo Tartaglione

entry.summary: The paper analyzes attention sparsity in vision transformers, showing that attention-matrix columns have unequal relevance to the final computation, with this effect growing with depth — implying tokens have query-independent absolute importance. The authors reformulate attention with an explicit input-dependent bias term on the query-key dot product, whose scalar value per token serves as a proxy for anticipated token influence and can guide attention-map pruning. This enables efficient attention pruning across multiple models.

entry.title: Non-Interfering Asymmetric AdamW Updates for Constrained Exploration of Equifinality in Hybrid Models

author.name: Ekaterina Gikalo, Zavud Baghirov, Christian Reimers, Markus Reichstein, Martin Jung, Marco K\"orner

entry.summary: The paper studies equifinality in hybrid process-based/neural models, where observations constrain aggregate fluxes but not internal partitioning, using evapotranspiration as the motivating case. The authors propose deliberately producing ensemble spread via auxiliary repulsion on transpiration using non-interfering asymmetric AdamW updates, instead of relying on random seeds alone, which spans only a narrow band of admissible partitionings. This is a creative contribution to uncertainty exploration in scientific hybrid modeling.

entry.title: Fusing Earth observation embeddings and spaceborne terrain with meteorological forcing for flood peak depth prediction from high-water marks

author.name: Wen Zhou, Shaowen Wang, Upmanu Lall, Venkatesh Merwade, Dingqi Ye

entry.summary: The paper trains deep learning models to predict flood peak depth from field high-water mark surveys (5689 USGS surveys across 39 events), using spaceborne terrain, geospatial foundation-model embeddings, and antecedent meteorological forcing. Unlike prior work trained on hydrodynamic simulations, it learns directly from observations and predicts before peak arrival.

entry.title: On Discovering Algorithms for Adversarial Imitation Learning

author.name: Shashank Reddy Chirra, Jayden Teoh, Praveen Paruchuri, Pradeep Varakantham

entry.summary: The paper analyzes adversarial imitation learning by decomposing it into density ratio estimation and reward assignment, then uses algorithm discovery (learned/searched design choices) to find improved reward assignment functions, an under-explored component affecting training stability. This reframes AIL design as a searchable space rather than fixing hand-derived reward transforms. The result is more stable and performant imitation learning with limited demonstrations.

entry.title: HyVox: Rethinking Low-Power Voice Intelligence towards Neuromorphic-von Neumann Edge Computing

author.name: Snehasis Addy, Eduardo Calle Ortiz, Prashant Shenoy, Phuc Nguyen

entry.summary: HyVox is a hybrid neuromorphic-von Neumann system for low-energy open-set speaker identification, splitting work so a spiking neural network on a neuromorphic processor produces speech embeddings while a microcontroller maintains the speaker gallery and makes enrollment/rejection decisions without weight updates. The SNN backbone uses a hierarchical temporal abstraction with learned per-neuron time constants across fast, medium, and slow timescales. The design targets always-on voice intelligence under tight energy budgets.

entry.title: Nonparametric GARCH: An Iterated Neural Estimator

author.name: Ruizhi Deng, Guohao Shen, Ngai Hang Chan

entry.summary: The authors propose an iterated neural estimator for nonparametric estimation and forecasting of GARCH-type volatility processes, alternating between estimating the recursion map and updating latent conditional variances. They prove finite-sample bounds and minimax rate-optimal guarantees up to logarithmic factors, with rates robust to lag-order overspecification.

entry.title: Sparse Internal Control of Language Models

author.name: Xizhe Zhang

entry.summary: This paper introduces sparse internal control, a framework for steering frozen language model behavior via inference-time interventions on a small set of internal nodes. It provides a local target-controllability formulation characterizing candidate site-direction pairs with constraints on target recovery, off-target preservation, and intervention cost.

entry.title: Same Origin, Different Verdicts: Text Production Conditions Confound Machine-Generated Text Detection in Russian

author.name: Stanislav Kirichenko

entry.summary: This study shows that text production conditions confound machine-generated text detection, holding origin fixed while varying generation conditions across a Russian corpus of 1882 documents from four generation channels and annotated archival human texts. It finds that production conditions push text in the same direction as the generative signature detectors look for, undermining detector reliability where verdicts carry consequences.

entry.title: Selective, Risk-Controlled Emotion Forecasting in Conversation: From a Persistence Barrier to Departure Detection with Conformal Guarantees

author.name: Bin Wen, Dai-Qiao Zhang, Tien-Ping Tan

entry.summary: This paper shows next-state emotion value prediction faces a persistence barrier: repeating a speaker's previous state is nearly unbeatable by frozen-encoder corrections in a state-observed testbed. What remains learnable is the timing of departure from persistence, formalized with conformal risk guarantees and learnable on three of four corpora. The honest negative result and principled reformulation are valuable for affective forecasting research.

entry.title: CAPTOR: text-encoder-free grounding by counting caption co-occurrence over the visual words of a frozen encoder

author.name: Elad Yoshai, Natan T. Shaked

entry.summary: CAPTOR enables text grounding in images without a text encoder, useful for image encoders trained without paired captions, such as histopathology models. It clusters frozen image-encoder patch tokens into visual words, derives term signatures from caption co-occurrence statistics, and factorizes the term-patch score matrix into a query-independent image factor and a term-by-word table so new queries are cheap. This enables grounding over any frozen encoder with captioned data.

entry.title: Semantic Prior-Guided Incomplete Cross-Modal Retrieval with Noisy Labels

author.name: Jiali Chen, Ruitao Pu, Yingke Chen, Dezhong Peng

entry.summary: SPIRN addresses incomplete cross-modal retrieval when labels are noisy, using fixed semantic priors as a consistent reference for robust representation learning instead of relying on categorical annotations. This departs from the label-driven paradigm of prior incomplete retrieval methods.

entry.title: CardioDrift: Automatic Cardiac Motion Tracking on a 3D Atlas Mesh via Shape-aware Coherent Point Drift with Slice Shift Correction

author.name: Reza Akbari Movahed, Abuzar Rezaee, Shatha Alamri, Edmond S. L. Ho, Fani Deligianni, Ali Gooya

entry.summary: CardioDrift is a fully automatic atlas-based probabilistic framework that tracks cardiac motion from cine CMR on a 3D atlas mesh with globally corresponding points, using shape-aware coherent point drift and slice shift correction. It avoids the time-consuming semi-automatic atlas fitting required by correspondence-based alternatives while enabling inter-subject motion comparison. This targets quantification of myocardial motion abnormalities.

entry.title: Adaptive Multi Mode: Budget-Aware Routing of Optimizers By Online Landscape Probes

author.name: Benjamin Jacob Bodner

entry.summary: AMM routes a known optimization budget among quasi-Newton, trust-region, coordinate, multistart, and evolution-strategy engines using online probes of landscape properties such as curvature, plateaus, separability, and fractal structure, each with cost and validity ranges. Developed with a pre-registered loop on BBOB (32 of 36 predictions held), it was then tested once on held-out problems.

entry.title: SCRUB: Contact-Based Surface-Frame Estimation for Force-Motion Control with an Armless Quadruped

author.name: Sourav Selvaraj, Juan Pablo Espinosa Chessal, Mahdi Agheli

entry.summary: SCRUB enables an armless quadruped to slide a body-mounted tool along near-vertical surfaces with controlled force, estimating the surface normal on unmapped surfaces via a Kalman filter combining force cues and velocity information. Existing normal estimators rely on friction models or assume tool velocity lies along the surface, which walking violates. A predictive controller uses the estimate to press and slide the tool for wiping, sanding, and inspection tasks.

entry.title: Support Vector Machines Directly Minimise KL Divergence

author.name: Ivan Silajev

entry.summary: This paper proves that the dual objectives of support vector classification and regression are exact, constrained KL divergence minimization problems between two Gaussian measures, giving SVMs a probabilistic interpretation that also recovers kernel ridge regression under relaxed constraints. This bridges the geometric margin view of SVMs with probabilistic machine learning.

entry.title: Anduin: A sybil-resistant agentic marketplace reputation system

author.name: Reza Ramji, Preston Vander Vos, Ziming Zeng, Duc V. Le

entry.summary: Anduin evaluates whether onchain payment histories can yield Sybil-attack-resistant provider ratings for autonomous AI agents in permissionless markets. Using a 157-day dataset of 66M agentic transactions worth $6.1M across 16 blockchains, it models payment flows as a bipartite graph and proposes three Sybil-resistant rating algorithms.

entry.title: Which One Is Sounding? Binaural Sounding Instance Disambiguation for Audio-Visual Segmentation

author.name: Haoze Ma, Yidi Li, Yu Ma, Pengyuan Zhao, Yi Shi, Bin Ren, Yanwen Guo, Dimitrios Kanoulas

entry.summary: BiSID-AVS uses binaural audio's interaural differences as spatial constraints to identify which same-class instance is sounding in audio-visual segmentation, refining beyond motion-based instance association that fails under sparse or inconspicuous movement. It introduces a novel sensing modality into the AVS task. Relevant to robotics and embodied perception.

entry.title: SurgTransfer: Multi-Step Latent Action Modeling for Action Transfer in Surgical World Model

author.name: Saurabh Koju, Love Panta, Deepak Thapa, Rudra P. K. Poudel, Prajwal Ghimire, Angus Watson, Yash Raj Shrestha, Prashnna Kumar Gyawali, Binod Bhattarai

entry.summary: SurgTransfer adapts latent action learning from unlabeled videos to surgical world models, arguing that single-step latent action paradigms are too short-sighted for surgery and modeling multi-step latent actions instead. The goal is transferring expert surgical maneuvers without reliance on ground-truth kinematics or task-specific annotations.

entry.title: Multimodal Fusion Methods for Whole-Slide Images and Clinical Data in Inflammatory Bowel Disease

author.name: Ankana Banerjee (University of Stavanger, Norway), Mark van der Giezen (University of Stavanger, Norway), Ole Gunnar Aasprong (Stavanger University Hospital, Norway), Emiel A. M. Janssen (University of Stavanger, Norway), {\O}yvind Steinsb{\o} (Stavanger University Hospital, Norway), Tore Grimstad (Stavanger University Hospital, Norway), Kjersti Engan (University of Stavanger, Norway)

entry.summary: A modular computational pathology framework that trains an attention-based aggregator over patch embeddings from a frozen foundation model and combines slide-level and clinical embeddings through 15 interchangeable fusion methods under identical conditions, predicting STRIDE-II-aligned remission outcomes in a prospective inflammatory bowel disease cohort. The best fusion method reached strong performance, enabling like-for-like comparison across fusion strategies.

entry.title: How Well Can Large Language Models Impersonate Individual Authors? A Comparative Evaluation

author.name: Harshit Gupta, Shunichi Ishihara

entry.summary: This study evaluates authorship impersonation by six existing widely used LLMs (Gemini 3 Pro, Claude Opus, GPT-5.2, GPT-5.2 Pro, DeepSeek 3.2, and Grok 4.1 Fast) on short product reviews using two in-context prompt types, including one with explicit stylometric guidance. It measures mimicry with a cosine distance metric and embedding distribution analysis, finding impersonation remains challenging for most models with Gemini showing a comparative edge. All evaluated models are long-established, so this is an analysis of existing systems rather than new releases.

entry.title: AgentTrustCI: Build-Time Policy, Grounding, and Trajectory Tests for Java LLM Agents

author.name: Sachin Gupta

entry.summary: AgentTrustCI is a Java/JUnit 5 framework that expresses application-layer agent expectations—tool selection policies, answer grounding, and workflow trajectories—as build-time tests over deterministically replayed traces, with a judge interface for optional semantic checks. On 55 synthetic enterprise cases it correctly classifies all 30 injected faults and 25 controls, including designated critical cases.

entry.title: Towards Automatic Heart Murmur Characterization from Multi-spot Phonocardiograms

author.name: Marcelo Nogueira, Jorge H. Oliveira, Carlos G. Ferreira, Miguel T. Coimbra, Al\'ipio M. Jorge

entry.summary: The paper formulates automatic heart murmur characterization as five patient-level classification tasks covering timing, shape, pitch, quality, and grade, going beyond the usual binary murmur detection. It compares three multi-spot strategies for combining recordings from four auscultation locations, including independent per-location classifiers with late fusion and a synchronous multi-input CNN. This advances clinical phonocardiogram analysis toward clinician-grade diagnostic richness.

entry.title: When Latent Dynamics Meet Data Assimilation: A Benchmark of Koopman-Type Representations

author.name: Zhiwei Zhang, Wenxuan Yuan, Xiaoyuan Cheng, Pouria Behnoudfar, Chuanqi Chen, Charlotte Moser, Yuta Tarumi, Jin-Long Wu, Rossella Arcucci, Takemasa Miyoshi, Nan Chen, Marc Bocquet, Sibo Cheng

entry.summary: A systematic benchmark comparing seven Koopman-type representation methods plus baselines across five dynamical systems ranging from periodic to strongly chaotic, within deep latent data assimilation. The study evaluates forecast and assimilation accuracy, physical state recovery, and dynamical consistency, revealing trade-offs between Koopman linearity and assimilation performance.

entry.title: ScaleTraj: Scale-Decomposed Human Trajectory Generation

author.name: Yulin Zeng, Yiheng Zhao, Jun Yan, Yuhong Liu

entry.summary: Identifies the Population-Level Displacement Gap, where bottom-up mobility generators fail to reproduce the heavy-tailed (truncated power law) displacement distribution after aggregation, and proposes ScaleTraj, a scale-decomposed trajectory generator that reconciles individual-level realism with population-level statistical fidelity.

entry.title: The Price of List Replicability: Tight Bounds for Bias Estimation

author.name: Michael Chen, Atieh Bastan, A. Pavan, N. V. Vinodchandran

entry.summary: The paper studies list-replicable algorithms for estimating the biases of d coins, establishing the first nontrivial sample complexity lower bounds for this replicability notion, matching prior upper bounds up to logarithmic factors. List replicability requires the algorithm's output to fall in a small per-input set of valid answers, a weaker but natural relaxation of exact replicability. This tightens the understanding of the statistical cost of reproducibility in estimation problems.

entry.title: Rethinking GA2Ms: performance and out-of-distribution generalisation

author.name: George Dimitriadis, Damian Machlanski, Paul Clarke, Spyridon Samothrakis

entry.summary: The paper proposes CoGA2M, a multi-resolution higher-order composite generalized additive model, and benchmarks spline-based GAMs on the TALENT large-scale tabular suite. It shows interpretable additive models rank in the top third against strong baselines and examines their robustness under distribution shift.

entry.title: Mapping urban heat from citizen-collected data: a scalable Gaussian process approach to correcting for preferential sampling

author.name: Ellie K. Kim, Zachary D. Calhoun, Michael H. Bergin, David E. Carlson

entry.summary: The paper introduces two scalable Gaussian process frameworks that correct for preferential sampling and sensor bias in crowdsourced weather station data, enabling high-resolution statewide urban heat island temperature mapping. This addresses the sparse-monitoring problem in intra-city heat assessment relevant to public health. The work combines spatial statistics with an important applied environmental problem.

entry.title: Nearly Linear-Time Follow-the-Perturbed-Leader for Weakly Observable Graph Bandits

author.name: Jongyeong Lee, Hyundam Yoo

entry.summary: The authors propose an FTPL policy for online learning with directed weakly observable feedback graphs achieving best-of-both-worlds guarantees with nearly linear expected runtime. A novel graph-based loss estimator combining forced exploration, conditional geometric resampling, and adaptive learning rates yields near-optimal regret in both adversarial and stochastic regimes.

entry.title: Data informed Ansatz Selection for Variational Quantum Circuits

author.name: Manav Seksaria, Advith Desu, Anil Prabhakar

entry.summary: Provides three training-free rules for selecting variational quantum circuit ansatz and depth from data and gate set alone: SVD of dataset Fourier coefficients indicates whether entanglement is needed and which qubits it connects; quantum Fisher information rank growth with depth follows a law fixing circuit depth; and additional analysis guides readout. This avoids costly train-and-compare searches over candidate circuits.

entry.title: When Does Better Confidence Improve a Knowledge-Graph Audit?

author.name: Zehao Lin, Kai Chen, Xixuan Hao, Erenkai Zhu, Chunyu Li, Helan Hu

entry.summary: This theoretical and empirical study examines when improved confidence estimates actually help human auditing of LLM-built knowledge graphs, using repairability, selection headroom, and label validity, and modeling non-adaptive auditing as budgeted covering. It bounds regret of first-order planning by a structural mass quantity and validates on Re-DocRED across extraction configurations and cross-document graphs. The work clarifies the gap between better error prediction and real audit gains.

entry.title: SO(3)-Equivariant Learning on CAD Boundary Representations

author.name: Matteo Ballegeer, Dries F. Benoit

entry.summary: SO3brep is an SO(3)-equivariant graph neural network for CAD boundary representations (B-reps) that maintains robustness to part pose without the information loss of local-frame methods. Node features computed in local frames are mapped to a shared frame via Wigner D-matrices, and Clebsch-Gordan tensor products couple features with inter-face directions so relative orientations are preserved. This addresses rotation sensitivity in existing B-rep networks.

entry.title: Many Pixels, One Composition: Self-Supervised Spectra for Specimen-Level Prediction

author.name: Eleftheria Tetoula-Tsonga, George Arvanitakis, Theodoros Giannakas

entry.summary: This paper predicts elemental composition of physical specimens from hyperspectral imaging by training a pixel-level self-supervised encoder, then attaching a lightweight attention-based regression head that aggregates many pixel representations per specimen. It outperforms spectral matching, unmixing, and supervised baselines on test specimens.

entry.title: Does RRT* Work on Uneven Terrain Meshes?

author.name: Otobong Jerome, Tiago Nascimento

entry.summary: The paper rigorously analyzes whether RRT* retains its asymptotic optimality guarantees on triangle-mesh terrains, showing the original algorithm cannot even run on a zero-volume surface and that a naive mesh reformulation minimizes the wrong objective (chord length rather than surface geodesic cost). The analysis clarifies what a correct mesh-based RRT* formulation would require.

entry.title: FOSCo-Net: Ego-centric Voxel Completion for Forest LiDAR Occlusions

author.name: Iman Esfandiyar, Dominik Belter

entry.summary: FOSCo-Net is a self-supervised voxel completion framework that reconstructs LiDAR geometry occluded by tree trunks from a single scan, using temporally accumulated observations as automatic supervision without manual labels. The authors evaluate ego-centric cylindrical and Cartesian grid representations with multiple decoder designs, finding a gated skip decoder most reliable. This improves traversability estimation and reduces false obstacle predictions for ground robots in forests.

entry.title: Towards Efficient Whole Page Ranking with One-Pass Inference

author.name: Qi Xu, Zhigang Hua, Zijie Lei, Yan Xie, Jizhe Zhang, Lynn Lu, Delun Du, Sha Hua, Ren Mao, Ke Pan, Haomin Yu, Sandeep Pandey, Luke Simon

entry.summary: This industrial paper proposes Multi-Item Scoring (MIS), a prefix-aware non-autoregressive framework for whole-page ranking that incorporates sequential conditioning while avoiding the inference overhead of autoregressive generation. It balances ad and organic content under layout and business constraints at large scale.

entry.title: From Type to Token: Petri Nets, Individual Token Philosophy, and Individualized Causal Effects

author.name: Fernando Delbianco, Fernando Tohm\'e, Gustavo Bodanza

entry.summary: The paper argues that structural causal models and Bayesian networks capture only type-level causation, which collapses under unbounded treatment-effect heterogeneity, and proposes Petri Nets under an individual token philosophy as the natural token-level causal representation. It develops a formal translation from Bayesian networks to Petri nets providing a two-layer account of individualized causality. This is a theoretical contribution to causal inference formalism.

entry.title: CARM: Conformal Adaptive Risk Masking for Reliable Scientific Super-Resolution

author.name: Guangtao Zhang, Haonan Wu, Junxuan Gao, Zhengyang Liu, Zhaoxi Zeng, Zhihao Li, Jianguo Huang, Zhiqiang Liu

entry.summary: Proposes CARM, a conformal risk control framework that adapts spatial trust masks for Earth-observation super-resolution under temporal distribution shift, maintaining heterogeneous experts over data streams. It addresses miscalibration of fixed thresholds caused by seasonality and episodic events.

entry.title: Corralling AI Risks with Grassroots Contracts

author.name: Ehud Shapiro

entry.summary: A position-style paper by Ehud Shapiro proposing grassroots contracts as a governance mechanism against three major platform AI risks: AI control of global platforms, unaccountable anonymous AI agents operating alongside humans, and unattributed deepfakes. It argues for bottom-up contractual accountability structures rather than top-down regulation alone.

entry.title: One Scale, Four Texts: Gaps, Overlaps and Silent Repairs in Published Grading Schemes

author.name: Elisa Rovai, Fabio Rovai

entry.summary: This paper formalizes four published versions of a diabetic retinopathy grading scale into a rule language over 24 finding variables and exhaustively enumerates over 1.4 billion finding profiles with SMT and OWL verification. It shows every action-assigning text leaves some cases uncategorized, revealing gaps, overlaps, and tacit reader repairs in clinical category systems. It matters as a rigorous case study in specification ambiguity in high-stakes classification schemes.

entry.title: Task-Efficient Agent Evaluation Using Cached Traces

author.name: Ben Johnson, Hayden Helm

entry.summary: The paper proposes efficient benchmarking of agentic systems by representing execution traces as LLM-generated structured summaries embedded with a text encoder, enabling performance estimation from few task executions. The representations preserve correctness and task signal while suppressing system-identity and harness-related signals. This reduces the cost of evaluating agents on expensive benchmarks.

entry.title: LLM-based NPCs in Video Games: A Systematic Mapping Study

author.name: Dilan Mian, Jeremy Bradbury, Yann-Ga\"el Gu\'eh\'eneuc, Fabio Petrillo, Cristiano Politowski

entry.summary: A systematic mapping study of LLM-based game non-player characters, filtering 377 papers to 42 analyzed across four thematic axes covering components, latency, and safety coverage. It provides the first quantitative picture of what has been built in this emerging area, its effectiveness, and its costs.

entry.title: TACT: A Pragmatic Approach to Qualitative Analysis with an AI Council

author.name: Rudrajit Choudhuri, Christian Bird, Carmen Badea, Anita Sarma

entry.summary: TACT (Traceable AI Council for Thematic analysis) enables large-scale AI-assisted qualitative analysis while keeping human teams in control of interpretation, via an AI council procedure with two variants: TACT-Lite and TACT-Full, which adds adversarial critics from other model families. It targets software teams analyzing stakeholder feedback at scale.

entry.title: A Hybrid Approach for Automated Security Pattern Recovery

author.name: Anh Minh Nguyen, Tuan Dat Tran, Alzubair Hassan, Liliana Pasquale

entry.summary: SecPatRec is a hybrid approach for automatically recovering security pattern implementations from source code, treating a pattern as a reference architecture and recovery as a deductive task: identifying which prescribed roles are present, grounding them in code entities, and recovering interaction sequences. This supports security-by-design auditing of existing software. It combines deductive reasoning with learned components to handle the abstraction and variability of pattern implementations.

entry.title: SysPilot: Cross-Library Performance Autotuning via Library Performance Contracts

author.name: Yineng Yan, Haowei Chen, Christopher J. Rossbach

entry.summary: SysPilot is a cross-library performance autotuning system targeting resource contention when independently developed ML and scientific libraries co-run and oversubscribe shared CPUs, GPUs, and memory bandwidth. It introduces Library Performance Contracts that characterize shared-resource behavior and runtime signals correlated with interference, enabling efficient cross-boundary configuration search.

entry.title: From Admission to Retention: Predicting Durable Offspring in Quality-Diversity Search

author.name: Corrado Calamita, Matteo Mendicini, Luca Ferrari, Riccardo Bertamini

entry.summary: This paper studies credit assignment in unstructured Quality-Diversity search, asking whether signals observable before an individual reproduces can predict not just archive entry but long-term retention of its offspring across generations. Experiments on a planar-arm benchmark and two robotic-locomotion tasks reveal that the same lineage signals often correlate with entry and persistence in opposite directions, offering insight into how automated failure discovery allocates search effort.

entry.title: From Reconstruction to Imputation: Test-Time Optimization for Missing Time-Series Channels

author.name: Bj\"orn Ludwig, Alexander Windmann, Ren\'e Heesch, Oliver Niggemann

entry.summary: This work converts a frozen sequence reconstructor—trained without mask augmentation—into a time-series imputer at inference time by treating missing channel entries as optimization variables and backpropagating to minimize reconstruction error on observed coordinates. The observed-self-consistency objective avoids per-failure-pattern imputer training and artificial masking.

entry.title: Occlusion for Free: Detecting Occlusion from the Disagreement Between Two Monocular Distance Cues

author.name: Chibueze Praise Onyenweaku, Toyibat Adele, Sikirulahi Opeyemi Abdulkareem, Obed Honour Eje

entry.summary: This paper shows that pedestrian occlusion can be detected without occlusion annotations by comparing two distance cues a camera-only pipeline already computes: apparent height (unchanged by occlusion) and monocular metric depth (pulled toward the occluder). Only the ordering of the two cues matters, so no calibration of focal length, stature, or depth scale is needed. This is an elegant, label-free signal useful for robotics and autonomous driving safety.

entry.title: Learning Directional Randers Geometry for Latent-Space Exploration

author.name: Th\'eau Blanchard (HeKA | U1346, GE Healthcare), St\'ephanie Allassonni\`ere (CMAP)

entry.summary: The authors show that asymmetry, not curvature, is the key geometric property needed for realistic latent-space interpolation in irreversible processes such as disease progression, where certain transitions are impossible. They learn a directional Randers (Finsler-type) geometry for latent spaces, capturing asymmetric transition costs that symmetric Riemannian metrics cannot model. Applications include tumor growth dynamics and cognitive decline trajectories.

entry.title: Minimal Superior Penalties: Characterising and Calibrating Decision-Aware Proper Scoring Rules

author.name: Rouhollah Ahmadian

entry.summary: This paper studies proper scoring rules used as validation metrics for classifier training and identifies a 'superiority' property: every correctly classified forecast should score better than every incorrectly classified one. The authors derive closed-form expressions for the separation between best-case correct and worst-case incorrect scores, define an infimal penalty as the minimum correction needed, and show standard Brier and log scores fail this property without adjustment.

entry.title: RGDM: Robust Graph Diffusion Model

author.name: Yancheng Wang, Ping Li, Dongfang Sun, Yingzhen Yang

entry.summary: Introduces the Robust Graph Diffusion Model, combining a Robust Graph Autoencoder with a Latent Diffusion Model to generate labeled synthetic nodes and edges from adversarially corrupted graphs. An edge selection mechanism and low-rank latent regularization enable robust generation that integrates into a given graph.

entry.title: Reciprocity Can Erase Direction:tructural Boundaries and Controlled Utility of Magnetic Graph Networks

author.name: Dawei Han, Zicheng Wang, Yaoxing Ren, Yi Lv, Rongqian Wu, Fumin Wang

entry.summary: This paper characterizes when magnetic graph networks, which encode edge direction through phase, can lose their directional signal before prediction occurs. The authors derive exact identities linking imaginary energy to amplitude-weighted reciprocity, prove collapse conditions for top-k selection, and construct paired examples with identical features but opposite labels showing provable chance-level performance for direction-erasing representations. Experiments confirm support-phase variants can achieve perfect AUROC in controlled fits.

entry.title: SaMA: Morpho Adaptation via Asymmetric Expansion of Kronecker Product

author.name: An Nguyen, Anh Tong

entry.summary: SaMA is a parameter-efficient fine-tuning method that generalizes the Kronecker product by relaxing the shared-block constraint in perfect-shuffle factorization, addressing two LoRA limitations: flat directions in the loss landscape and effective rank that scales only linearly with parameter budget. SaMA's practical rank scales quadratically with parameters, up to full rank, while retaining PEFT efficiency. The method aims to improve optimization behavior of adaptive optimizers under low-rank constraints.

entry.title: Ground-Wing: A Parametric 3D Wing-in-Ground-Effect Dataset for Benchmarking Neural Surrogate Models

author.name: Andrea Cenzato, Lukas Karch, Andre Luckow, Yoran Pichon, Francesco Pasqua, Abouzar Ghasemi, Rishikesh Ranade, Ira Shokar, Julia Kowalski

entry.summary: The paper presents a CFD dataset of 770 RANS simulations across 194 unique parametrized 3D wing configurations in ground effect, motivated by motorsport aerodynamics. It benchmarks six neural surrogate architectures spanning convolutional, graph-based, transformer-based, and JEPA-based paradigms on surface pressure and field prediction. This provides a standardized benchmark for neural operators in an industrially relevant aerodynamic regime.

entry.title: On the Complexity of Finite-Sum Nonconvex-Strongly-Concave Minimax Optimization with Exact Proximal Oracles

author.name: Yuxing Peng, Zhiqing Tang, Weijia Jia

entry.summary: This theory paper establishes lower bounds for finite-sum nonconvex-strongly-concave minimax optimization, showing that neither unrestricted adaptivity nor exact component proximal oracle access improves polynomial complexity. The results cover settings relevant to adversarial training and distributionally robust learning, extending prior lower bounds beyond linear-span and zero-respecting algorithms. It provides explicit complexity bounds parameterized by smoothness, condition number, and initial gap.

entry.title: DLER: Dual-Logit Experience Replay for Online Continual Learning

author.name: Huiwei Lin, Shanshan Feng, Kong Aik Lee

entry.summary: DLER decomposes dot-product logits into angle and norm factors for online continual learning, showing the angle factor captures novel knowledge but is prone to prediction bias while the norm factor preserves historical knowledge. Building on this analysis, the method uses dual-logit experience replay to counteract the imbalance between current and replayed samples in a single-pass streaming setting. Experiments indicate improved handling of catastrophic forgetting versus bias-correction baselines.

entry.title: Auditing Multi-Proxy Explanations of Web User Preferences: Identification Boundaries and Abstention

author.name: Yu Zhang, Zhihan Wang, Yuhang Lu, Shuai Li

entry.summary: The paper builds an audit framework for explanations of web user preference proxies (behavior, ratings, LLM profiles), distinguishing point identification, partial identification, and principled abstention. It proves a sharp majority threshold for uncontaminated proxy attributions under which the coordinatewise median recovers latent attribution support and direction, with sharp minimax error guarantees.

entry.title: Federated Transfer Learning for Medical Image Classification under Mixed Skew

author.name: Alexandre G. Leclercq, S\'ebastien Bougleux, Aur\'elien Corroyer-Dulmont, Romain H\'erault

entry.summary: This paper proposes a personalized federated learning method for medical imaging that handles mixed skew (feature, label, concept, and quantity shifts) across centers while starting from pretrained models rather than training from scratch. It addresses the realistic constraint that limited patient data precludes from-scratch federated training.

entry.title: Post-Inference Model Chaining: A Problem Statement and a Model-based Bootstrap for Training End-to-End Digital Twins

author.name: Lukas Madenach, Timo Bailer, Tobias Eilert

entry.summary: The authors analyze the statistical properties of chaining separately trained stage models into end-to-end digital twins, showing that forwarding predictive draws through chains produces persistent coverage inflation and input-dependent bias. They propose a diagnostic using error-free latents and a model-based bootstrap to address these distortions. This formalizes a previously under-examined problem in multi-stage industrial simulation pipelines.

entry.title: CATF: A Manager-Worker Framework for Context-Aware Time-Series Forecasting

author.name: Yueqiao Chen, Dongyu Liu

entry.summary: CATF is a context-aware time-series forecasting framework using a Manager-Worker architecture, where a Transformer-based Manager performs hard routing of each input to a single specialized Worker model based on contextual signals like weather and calendar information. Hard routing during both training and inference avoids the inference cost and interpretability problems of soft-routing Mixture-of-Experts approaches and removes the need for manual data partitioning. This offers a practical middle ground between single monolithic forecasters and costly ensembles.

entry.title: A local orchestration harness for molecular design with foundation models

author.name: Sakib Mostafa, Md Atik Ahamed, James Zou, Lei Xing, Md Tauhidul Islam

entry.summary: MolCrew is a locally deployable system that coordinates four separately trained molecular specialist models (structure generation, description, endpoint prediction, edit proposal) with a language-model orchestrator and RDKit verification, retaining local data control and enforcing chemical constraints. It addresses practical integration challenges in molecular design workflows. The work is relevant to privacy-preserving, tool-augmented LLM systems for science.

entry.title: All Paths All at Once: A Quantum Monte Carlo and Neural Committor Approach to Reaction Pathway Search

author.name: Chien-Chai Chang

entry.summary: The paper introduces tReax_expedition, an energy-only method combining Monte Carlo exploration, stochastic quench labeling, and restrained continuation to find competing reaction pathways without potential-energy gradients. Benchmarks on 2D potentials and nine gas-phase reactions recover intermediates and saddle energies within 0.76 kJ/mol of independently refined values, with alanine dipeptide revealing limits from incomplete conformational relaxation.

entry.title: CORA: Teacher-Guided Causal O-RAN Adaptation for Jamming Detection

author.name: Sneihil Gopal, Richard A. Rouil

entry.summary: CORA is a teacher-guided reinforcement learning framework that transfers the hindsight of a retrospective KPI detector to a causal, streaming jamming detector without any labeled attack data. Offline, the retrospective detector on unlabeled logs defines a recall-weighted reward for a controller that adapts sensitivity, persistence, and grace parameters of the causal detector.

entry.title: KeyWise: Efficient Video-Only Piano Transcription with a Lightweight Per-Key Architecture

author.name: Anastasios Chatzigiannis, Natalia Panagou, Maria Koziri

entry.summary: Introduces KeyWise, a lightweight architecture for transcribing piano from top-view video alone by exploiting known keyboard geometry: the rectified keyboard is divided into 88 tiles, each tracked over time by a small shared recurrent network. It matches state-of-the-art onset accuracy on PianoVAM while being efficient and robust to pedal and audio noise issues.

entry.title: Conditional independence and graphical models for rankings

author.name: Aritz P\'erez

entry.summary: Introduces relative rank models, a probabilistic framework based on structured coarsenings of the ranking space that relax mutual-exclusivity constraints while preserving relative order information. This enables a well-defined notion of conditional independence for rankings, supporting tractable graphical models for preference learning and decision-making.

entry.title: Estimating "Realized" Skewness using Convolutional Neural Network

author.name: Haozhe Jiang, Ostap Okhrin, Michael Rockinger

entry.summary: Proposes a CNN-MLP estimator of monthly skewness from 5-minute high-frequency financial data via a direct functional mapping, showing in Monte Carlo experiments with stochastic volatility models that it reduces finite-sample bias versus existing realized-skewness estimators. The paper also characterizes the finite-sample bias of plug-in estimators and establishes risk consistency properties, with favorable empirical portfolio results.

entry.title: PolicyIK: High-Precision Inverse Kinematics for Robot Arms with Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Yuhan Liu, Xinqi Liu, Zixuan Dong, Keith W. Ross, Shenji Wan

entry.summary: PolicyIK trains a goal-conditioned RL policy for high-precision inverse kinematics on robot arms, updating joint-position references from pose feedback while retaining controller offsets at rest. Design choices like two-scale pose errors with error-dependent action gains address redundancy, singularities, and cross-embodiment transfer needs of VLA policies.

entry.title: CARTBench: Rubric-Based Evaluation of Shopping Advice for Complex and Ambiguous Requests with Timelines

author.name: Yuqin Dai, Zhanwei Zhang, Honghui Yang, Zhouheng Yao, Yueqi Zhang, Jingyu He, Chaoyang Shi, Fanding Wei, Boyuan Pan, Kai Xu, Yao Hu, Yongliang Shen

entry.summary: CARTBench is a benchmark for evaluating LLM shopping assistants on complex, ambiguous requests with timelines, built from real commercial needs across 17 retail domains with timestamped dialogues and 1,603 product records. It introduces case-specific rubrics distilled from successful orders via Ideal Response Principles, plus a structured prompting strategy. It addresses evaluation data scarcity and standardization for a commercially important use case.

entry.title: Balancing hierarchical representation and quantization: A performance trade-off in text embeddings

author.name: Kai Ponel, Marco Polignano, Erasmo Purificato, Aylin Julia Temizkan, Marco Levantesi, Giovanni Semeraro, Ernesto William De Luca

entry.summary: This empirical benchmark study evaluates how hierarchical variable-length embeddings interact with quantization, running 168 configurations per task across four embedding models on 38 MTEB tasks. It finds int8 quantization is statistically indistinguishable from full precision, providing practical guidance for efficient embedding deployment. Thorough and useful, though confirmatory rather than novel in technique.

entry.title: BiCG-Net: Target-Specific Image Quality Assessment via Observation Modeling and In-Image Differencing

author.name: Yibu Yang, Tingqiong Cui, Liming Lei, Hao Xiong, Jun Xu, Siyuan Liu, Guanghui Huang

entry.summary: BiCG-Net estimates quality of a specific target region rather than a whole image, using nested patch sampling expanding outward from the target box and an in-image differencing mechanism that provably cancels background influence. A student network distills an 11-teacher ensemble through a linear observation model, addressing the lack of target-level human MOS benchmarks.

entry.title: SpikePose: Lightweight Video Human Pose Estimation

author.name: Yunhao Huang, Kaushik Bhargav Sivangi, Tianyi Yu, Fani Deligianni

entry.summary: SpikePose pairs a frame-reset single-step spiking neural network encoder with a motion-aligned heatmap memory module for lightweight video pose estimation, keeping temporal reasoning outside the spiking backbone. It improves joint localization and motion consistency on MPII and related datasets while reporting lower estimated arithmetic energy. The work helps close the gap between spiking and conventional networks on non-event-driven video.

entry.title: Object-independent evaluation of small-data astronomical image classifiers: architecture, representation, and acquisition shortcuts

author.name: Eraldo Pereira Marinho

entry.summary: This study shows that reported performance on small astronomical image datasets can reflect object reuse, field-of-view differences, acquisition settings, and catalogue-derived shortcuts rather than true morphology. Using a curated four-class dataset with 370 physical objects and group-constrained splits, the authors compare CNN-Transformer, ResNet-50, and ViT-B/16 models across multiple field-of-view representations to isolate shortcut effects.

entry.title: Reflection-Robust Stereo Visual-Inertial Odometry via Kalman-Filtered Ground-Height Estimation

author.name: Uihyun Hwang, Sungjae Shin, Dongjae Kim, Hyun Myung

entry.summary: This work addresses a specific failure mode of visual-inertial odometry in reflective indoor environments, where specular floor reflections produce virtual features below the ground plane and corrupt state estimation. The method estimates ground height in real time with a Kalman filter and rejects only feature candidates whose inferred 3D positions lie below the estimated ground, restricted to reflection-prone floor regions. This preserves more valid features than blanket floor masking.

entry.title: Corridor-Based Monitoring and Emergency Braking Decision for Automated Vehicle Safety

author.name: Junnan Pan, Vladislav Nenchev, Mohak Mansharamani, Prodromos Sotiriadis, Ferdinand Englberger

entry.summary: The paper describes a redundant safety channel for automated vehicles that decides emergency braking from lidar data under tight embedded compute constraints. It uses a predicted motion corridor, curvature-aware of the planned path and vehicle geometry, to filter lidar measurements, plus a decision method that evaluates objects inside the swept-body boundary. This targets the critical safety problem of independent fallback braking systems.

entry.title: Tight Lower Bounds under Matched High-Order H\"older Smoothness and Uniform Convexity

author.name: Cedar Site Bai

entry.summary: This optimization theory paper establishes tight lower bounds for deterministic algorithms minimizing functions that are simultaneously high-order Holder-smooth and uniformly convex when the smoothness and convexity orders match (q = p + nu). It proves that any algorithm using derivatives up to order p requires Omega((H/sigma)^(2/(3(p+nu)-2)) * log(Delta_0/epsilon)) oracle calls to reduce the optimality gap to epsilon, matching the known upper bound. This resolves the complexity picture for this class of higher-order uniformly convex optimization problems.

entry.title: Offline Learning of Reserve Prices from Censored Bids

author.name: Lavanya Marla, Yunzong Xu, Boxuan Zhou

entry.summary: The paper studies how a seller can learn an optimal reserve price for second-price auctions from censored historical bids, characterizing exactly when an optimal reserve is identifiable under a monotone hazard rate assumption. When identification fails, the authors derive the minimax-regret-optimal reserve over distributions consistent with the observed data.

entry.title: Assurance-Conditioned Continuous Authorization for Autonomous AI Agents

author.name: Mehdi Shajari

entry.summary: ACCA proposes harness-independent continuous authorization for autonomous agents that act through tools, delegate, and change models or environments while earlier authorizations remain in flight. It maintains an effective-authority envelope via typed dependency graphs enabling selective re-evaluation when authorization-relevant conditions change.

entry.title: When to Ask, When to Answer: Strategic Clarification for Ambiguous Reference Resolution in Dialogue

author.name: Ibrahim Khebour, Nikhil Krishnaswamy

entry.summary: The paper studies strategic clarification in dialogue: asking questions only when answers will narrow the candidate referent set, using a controlled test environment built from SIMMC 2.1 that measures how many questions each ambiguous reference requires. It examines how baseline LLMs and common post-training methods behave, documenting LLM bias toward premature answering.

entry.title: Drift-adaptive Representation Preservation for Domain-Incremental Learning

author.name: Hyunmin Kong, Gyutae Oh, Jitae Shin

entry.summary: The paper tackles domain-incremental learning by measuring representation drift for each past domain-class concept against fixed anchors and using that measured drift both in a consolidation loss and in prototype construction to prioritize preservation of high-forgetting-risk pairs. This goes beyond uniform regularization that ignores which concepts are most at risk.

entry.title: Auditing a Model-Hub Benchmark: Data Quality, Training Budgets, and Side Information in HuggingBench

author.name: Michal Podstawski

entry.summary: The author audits HuggingBench (SIGIR 2025), a benchmark for recommending Hugging Face resources, treating it as a data product and finding that three of its four external knowledge graphs violate the item-entity identity constraint despite passing basic validation. Correcting the join improves every KG-based method in every seed, by up to 73% mean Recall@10, and reverses ten of 27 method comparisons. This demonstrates how data-quality flaws can distort benchmark conclusions.

entry.title: Quantifying out-of-distribution data severity with Wasserstein distances: benchmarking large language models for alloy property prediction

author.name: YuJie Liu, Dezhen Xue, Jun Sun, Xiangdong Ding, Zhibin Gao, Turab Lookman

entry.summary: The study benchmarks general-purpose LLMs against domain-specific materials models (SteelBERT, MatSciBERT, SciBERT) on alloy property prediction for Ti, steels, high-entropy alloys, and Al, finding general LLMs surprisingly outperform the specialized models. It proposes a hybrid approach where numerical priors from models like CatBoost are fed into reasoning LLMs to further improve predictions, and uses Wasserstein distances to quantify OOD data severity.

entry.title: LENS: Reliability-Aware Stock Prediction via LLM-Extracted Priors and News-Driven Semantic Graphs

author.name: Hao Zhou, Tiejun Ma, Luis Felipe Costa Sperb

entry.summary: Proposes LENS, a static-dynamic graph framework for stock return prediction that treats relational reliability as a first-class signal: LLM-extracted company graphs are aggregated over multiple runs with confidence weighting, and dynamic news-driven graphs carry reliability signals through the pipeline rather than treating every edge as trustworthy.

entry.title: SCANO: Restoring Boundary-Condition Completeness in Sampled Meshes with a Sliced-Cross-Attention Neural Operator for 3D Thermal Fields

author.name: Tianyu Li, Zhiwei Cao, Qingang Zhang, Ruihang Wang, Binyang Song, Yonggang Wen

entry.summary: The paper analyzes how mesh subsampling distorts boundary-condition information when training neural operators on huge meshes, identifying three distortion mechanisms including count-based rather than area-based face weighting. It proposes a sliced-cross-attention neural operator (SCANO) that restores boundary-condition completeness for 3D thermal field prediction when training on subsamples and deploying on whole meshes. The analysis yields measurable criteria for when boundary conditioning stays consistent under sampling.

entry.title: FedCSGA: Evolutionary Client Selection with Joint Statistical and System Heterogeneity in Federated Learning

author.name: Ghani Haider, Majid Kundroo, Leo Zhang, Jinchul Choi, Taehong Kim

entry.summary: FedCSGA proposes an evolutionary client selection scheme for federated learning that jointly models statistical and system heterogeneity across communication rounds, rather than treating them independently as prior methods do. By adapting subset selection to coupled heterogeneity, it aims to reduce communication cost, mitigate stragglers, and improve convergence in edge deployments. It addresses a practical bottleneck in real federated systems.

entry.title: Modulating Merging Strengths via Joint Loss Estimation for LoRA-based Continual Learning

author.name: Kun Gu, De Cheng, Zhipeng Xu, Lingfeng He, Di Xu, Nannan Wang

entry.summary: M2LE improves LoRA-based continual learning by replacing the single shared scalar that scales new LoRA updates before merging with element-wise merging strengths estimated from joint losses. The authors argue different update components affect previous and current tasks differently, so per-element modulation better balances stability and plasticity. The approach maintains a single inference model across tasks with parameter-efficient fine-tuning.

entry.title: Basin2Vec: Learning Basin-Centric Embeddings for Scalable Hydrological Modeling

author.name: Muhammad Talha, Xiaofeng Liu, Yuan Yang, Pang-Ning Tan, A. Pouyan Nejadhashemi

entry.summary: Basin2Vec is a self-supervised framework that learns compact watershed representations from hydroclimatic and physiographic data without observed streamflow, outperforming handcrafted attributes and general-purpose geospatial embeddings. It improves temporal generalization and zero-shot spatial transfer for streamflow prediction across multiple forecasting architectures.

entry.title: Impact of Input Resolution in Mammographic Mass Detection: A Controlled Multi-Architecture Study

author.name: Kaan Buyukdemirci, Emine Ulku Saritas

entry.summary: A controlled study on the VinDr-Mammo dataset isolating the effect of input resolution on mammographic mass detection, training 18 detectors across six resolutions with all other factors fixed. The design enables the first clean quantification of the accuracy-versus-compute trade-off from downsampling mammograms.

entry.title: ProcessPrefBench: Evaluating Cross-Task Transfer of Individual Process Preferences from Naturalistic Human-AI Interaction

author.name: Yiwen Yang, Guanming Liu

entry.summary: ProcessPrefBench tests whether process preferences (standards for evidence, depth, focus, procedure, delivery) revealed in one natural human-AI dialogue can shape an assistant's later answers on unstated tasks. Built from three months of dialogues from two knowledge workers, it provides 66 source-target cases and tests target-only, full-history, and distilled-preference prompting conditions. It targets personalization beyond surface style, an understudied capability.

entry.title: Visual Forensic Detection of Fabricated Bangla News Photocards using Deep Learning

author.name: Anindya Kundu, Kabya Mithun Saha, Md. Muhaiminul Islam, Fayek Ahmed, Aminul Kader Bulbul, Muhammad Ibrahim

entry.summary: This paper tackles photocard-based misinformation in Bangladesh, where fake news is embedded in image pixels mimicking news branding, invisible to text-based fact-checkers. The authors build a dataset of roughly 2,000 authentic and fabricated Bangla photocards, expanded to 32,736 samples via transformations, and recast detection as visual forgery detection. The work addresses an underrepresented language and a misinformation vector largely ignored by mainstream tools.

entry.title: Ray-Tracing-Based Dynamic Channel Sounding With Autoregressive Wi-Fi CSI Prediction

author.name: Lyutianyang Zhang, Yixin Ying, Liu Cao, Vanlin Sathya, Jinke Ren, Shuguang Cui

entry.summary: This paper develops a dynamic Wi-Fi MIMO channel sounding framework combining autoregressive CSI prediction with SINR-aware scheduling, evaluated using Sionna-based ray tracing to capture environment-specific channel dynamics under device mobility. It addresses the tradeoff between CSI accuracy and acquisition overhead, plus error accumulation in autoregressive prediction. The work supports physical AI applications that need accurate, low-overhead channel state information.

entry.title: Embedding Semantic Entropy: NLI-Free Semantic Uncertainty Estimation with Geometry-Aware Clustering

author.name: Akshiya Raveendran, Praveenasarma Baskarakurukkal, Pragatheeswaran Vipulanandan, Kamal Premaratne, Uthayasanker Thayasivam

entry.summary: The paper replaces entailment-model-based clustering in semantic entropy with K-Medoids clustering in semantic embedding space, using dynamic cluster selection based on intra-cluster compactness and inter-cluster separation. Experiments across five QA datasets and four 7B-scale models show competitive AUROC and AUARC performance without requiring NLI models.

entry.title: Fault-tolerant shallow recurrent decoders for sparse sensing with missing sensor measurements

author.name: Matteo Romilio Pasqual, Matteo Tomasetto, J. Nathan Kutz, Andrea Manzoni

entry.summary: The paper extends shallow recurrent decoders (SHRED) to handle sparse, asynchronous, noisy, and missing sensor measurements for real-time high-dimensional state estimation. The authors compare naive imputation strategies, fault-tolerant architectures, and Lagrangian-based optimization approaches to make sparse sensing robust to sensor failures and irregular sampling. This addresses a common gap where sensing strategies assume idealized, continuously active sensors.

entry.title: Explainable Anomaly Detection in 5G Networks through Continuous Time Graphs

author.name: Thomas Hoger (LAAS, LAAS-SARA, LAAS-RISC), Philippe Owezarski (LAAS, LAAS-SARA, LAAS-RISC)

entry.summary: The authors formalize 5G network exchanges as dynamic graphs and apply graph-based learning to detect anomalies at packet-level semantic granularity while capturing sequential and topological context essential for multi-stage attacks. The approach is evaluated with popular dynamic graph models and aims to provide explainable detection beyond traditional network-based methods.

entry.title: Quantifying Trait-State Hierarchy in EEG Foundation Model and Signal Processing Embeddings

author.name: Anusha Madapura, Aditya Kommineni, Shrikanth Narayanan

entry.summary: This work quantifies how EEG foundation model and classical signal-processing embeddings encode stable traits such as subject identity, age, and sex versus transient stimulus-driven states. Using a hierarchy metric and kNN purity on brain-computer interface datasets, it reveals differences in what various EEG representations capture.

entry.title: Autonomy and Coordination in Intelligent Manufacturing: A Recursive Autonomous Agent Framework

author.name: Yuning Chen, Hongda Zhang, Linqiang Hu, Ziqing Zhou, Yi Liu, Zhao Huang, Ding Zhou, Haining Xu

entry.summary: The paper analyzes intelligence in human production organizations through a complex adaptive systems lens, identifying two coupled mechanisms: individual autonomy for local decision-making and collective coordination to align decisions with shared goals and constraints. It formalizes a production-system model showing how local decision rules and coordination jointly produce system-level decisions, and proposes a recursive autonomous agent framework for intelligent manufacturing. The framework emphasizes feedback-driven continuous adjustment in production environments.

entry.title: DyPSI: Dynamic Physics Sensing via Joint Field and Sensor-Trajectory Generation

author.name: Yizhou Zhang, Panqi Chen, Lei Cheng, Ting Zhang, Jianlong Li, Jianfeng Shi, Shikai Fang

entry.summary: Proposes DyPSI, a framework that jointly generates future spatiotemporal physical fields and sensor trajectories conditioned on historical observations, lifting discrete sensor coordinates into continuous representations. It overcomes static sensing assumptions in reconstruction and sensor placement for evolving environments.

entry.title: Spatio-Temporal Multi-Order Interaction for Video Recognition

author.name: Kevin D. Nguetche, Lilian Hollard, Eric Granger, Marco Pedersoli

entry.summary: Building on MogaNet's multi-order spatial representation, the paper introduces parallel multi-order temporal processing using depthwise-only convolutions with implicit gating-based aggregation, achieving linear rather than quadratic complexity in channel count. The method balances local-order (CNN-style) and global-order (transformer-style) interactions for video recognition.

entry.title: Deep Meets Classical: A CPU-Efficient Decision-Fusion Model for Automatic Modulation Classification

author.name: Zhiyi Yin, Zhizhao Wen, Ruoxin Zhang, Chao Wang, Puyang Xu, Yifan Jiang, Yusi Gong

entry.summary: FuseAMC shows that a compact CNN on raw I/Q samples and a classical higher-order-cumulant feature classifier are complementary for automatic modulation classification, with the CNN stronger at low SNR and the cumulant classifier stronger at high SNR. It fuses their decisions in a lightweight model that runs on CPUs, targeting cognitive radio and non-cooperative signal identification. The comparative SNR-conditioned analysis is itself a useful empirical contribution.

entry.title: Human Motion Prediction via Continual Prior Compensation

author.name: Jianwei Tang, Jian-Fang Hu, Tianming Liang, Xiaotong Lin, Jiangxin Sun, Wei-Shi Zheng, Jianhuang Lai

entry.summary: The paper proposes Continual Prior Compensation (CPC), a temporal continual learning framework for human motion prediction that progressively trains models on different future time horizons rather than all moments simultaneously. This addresses the interference where short-term prediction learning is hindered by long-term prediction objectives.

entry.title: Beyond the principle-practice gap: Responsible AI as situated epistemic and ethical practice

author.name: Thao Do Ngoc, Emma Carmel

entry.summary: Based on fourteen semi-structured interviews with actors designing and governing AI-enabled anti-trafficking systems, this paper argues that the so-called principle-practice gap in Responsible AI is not merely an implementation or compliance deficit. Instead, the authors show that varied institutional and professional conditions shape which issues actors come to recognize as ethical at all. This reframes Responsible AI scholarship from a deficit model toward a situated epistemic practice perspective.

entry.title: ExaTune: Exhaustive Hyperparameter Landscape Exploration at Scale

author.name: Kevin Dick, Katie Lonsway

entry.summary: ExaTune is an open-source HPC system that exhaustively evaluates discretized hyperparameter grids via K-fold cross-validation to produce hyperparameter landscape maps, applying fitness landscape analysis methods from evolutionary computation (ruggedness indices, autocorrelation, fitness-distance correlation) to ML hyperparameter spaces for the first time at scale.

entry.title: An Information Budget for Label-Noise Memorization, and What Statistical Complexity Tracks: A Study with Multilayer Perceptrons

author.name: Nancy Baygorrea C., Ot\'avio da Fonseca Martins Gomes

entry.summary: Studies how much label noise an MLP memorizes and when, decomposing predictive information into signal, memorization, and heterogeneity terms with a Fano-type bound relating memorization to training accuracies. Across 89 MNIST runs with pre-specified hypotheses, normalized memorization information tracked memorized noise on training samples and stayed near zero on held-out data.

entry.title: Feature-Based and Deep Learning Methods for Astronomical Light Curve Classification

author.name: V. Baymakanov, Kh. Khamitov, A. Raimova, A. Isaeva, R. Taran, M. Zedan, M. Kornilov, M. Demianenko, K. Malanchev, M. Hushchyn

entry.summary: A systematic comparison of classical feature-based models versus end-to-end deep learning for variable star classification on the ZTF StarEmbed dataset of roughly 40,000 objects across seven imbalanced classes. The authors find that physically motivated features consistently beat deep models on raw light curves, attributing the gap to limited labeled data and the irregular sampling and morphological diversity of the data. It is a useful reality check for deep learning adoption in astronomy.

entry.title: Anomaly Detection on Resource-Constrained Devices with Reservoir Computing

author.name: Marco Angioli, Mathias Persson, Hiroto Tamura, Hadi Banaee, Amy Loutfi, Gouhei Tanaka, Alberto Giaretta, Denis Kleyko

entry.summary: This work adapts Mahalanobis Distance of Reservoir States (MDRS), an unsupervised time-series anomaly detection method, for edge devices with strict compute and memory budgets. Two optimizations are proposed: replacing random reservoir connectivity with a circular shift and computing anomaly scores from the final reservoir state alone, plus preprocessing that exploits the reservoir's temporal memory. The result is competitive anomaly detection with substantially lower computational cost.

entry.title: Do Ray-Traced Cities Make a Better Channel Prior for an Unseen Site? A Pre-Registered Study in Simulation, and a Test on Measured Channels that Reverses It

author.name: Krish Patel

entry.summary: This pre-registered study asks whether channel priors pooled from ray-traced city simulations outperform standard 3GPP stochastic models for estimation at unseen base station sites. Simulation suggests the pooled prior nearly matches site-trained estimators, but a test on measured real-world channels reverses the conclusion, and learned models add little over classical methods.

entry.title: Shrinkage prior for implicit generative models

author.name: Shreya Sinha-Roy, Christian P. Robert, Ritabrata Dutta

entry.summary: This work proposes a sample-efficient training mechanism for implicit generative models using shrinkage priors within a generalized Bayes framework, circumventing the intractable likelihood via a scoring-rule posterior. It adapts sparsity-inducing techniques from the high-dimensional regression setting to deep generative models. The approach could improve training efficiency when data is scarce relative to parameter dimension.
